title: RTSP parser: a single non-UTF-8 (e.g. Latin-1) byte in any header value poisons the whole session
description: Follow-up from the fss-2h5zq.32 round-4 review (r32e probe p04). The parser now poisons the session (until reset()) on invalid UTF-8 anywhere in the header block, so a camera sending e.g. 'Server: Caf\xe9' (Latin-1) kills the session. That is fail-closed and SAFE, but likely too harsh for real devices. Decide with real recorded device captures (file-ingest-first; no device I/O until an owner decision): options are (a) keep strict; (b) treat a non-UTF-8 byte in a header VALUE of a non-framing header (not Content-Length, CSeq, Transport, Session, or any credential/challenge header) as a typed recoverable per-message error that discards exactly the declared message when a single valid Content-Length is known, never lossily decoding. Never flatten or silently replace bytes; never weaken framing/poison rules for framing headers. Also noted: a '\n\r\n' header terminator is not recognized (the parser waits, then poisons as unterminated): non-standard, document it.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Documentation sub-item landed in 58a5ac0: find_header_boundary documents the deliberate non-recognition of the non-standard LF-CR-LF terminator (waits, then poisons unterminated-header-block), pinned by lf_crlf_terminator_is_not_recognized_and_poisons_unterminated_fss_0i0ue in rtsp_contract.rs (both stages: partial terminator waits; budget overrun poisons typed).\n\nThe core (a) strict vs (b) typed-recoverable-per-message decision remains BLOCKED on an owner decision backed by real recorded device captures (file-ingest-first; no device I/O until then) — the bead text itself gates the choice on that evidence.

title: Bug: leftover atomic-writer temp files are listed in release package checksums
description: Found by the independent confirmation of fss-xhxwh (8fa1a64). scripts/release_artifacts.py package() builds <target>.sha256sums.txt and receipts/ARTIFACT_SHA256SUMS.txt from normalized_files(ctx.artifacts) (~453-455), which uses rglob("*") and includes dotfiles (~58-65). Since release JSON assets are now written through the atomic writer, a run killed mid-write can leave a .<name>.tmp.* file in the artifacts directory; the next package run lists it in both checksum receipts, and an upload of that directory may ship it. Confirmed with a probe (scratchpad/probe_leftover.py): the output lists .fss-x.sbom.spdx.json.tmp.abc123 next to fss-x.tar.xz. Fix: normalized_files must skip, or better fail closed with a typed error on, names matching the writer's temp pattern (.*.tmp.*) in the artifacts directory. Test: make_input, create artifacts/.fss-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.sbom.spdx.json.tmp.stale, run package, assert no checksum line contains '.tmp.' (or a typed refusal). Informational: qualification_receipt.py:114 uses BaseException.add_note (Python >= 3.11); declare the minimum Python version or guard it.
notes: [FoggyBass 16:28 EDT] REOPENED per FuchsiaMountain review-749 #1, verified at eecebd6: scripts/release_artifacts.py still lists the stage with normalized_files(ctx.stage) in verify_stage (line 116) and in the package stage_files (line 353), so a leftover atomic-writer temp in the stage (e.g. stage/.fss.tmp.killed) is hashed into verification.json and STAGE_SHA256SUMS.txt and packaged into the .tar.xz/.zip. My close reason scoped the stage out ('not written by the atomic writer'), but a leftover temp of any origin must not ship. Fix: apply the same refusal (release_artifact_files) to the stage and receipts listings, with failing-first tests for each.
close_reason: Reopened stage/receipts gap fixed in b05a28e (FuchsiaMountain). Orchestrator verification, independent of the author: red on 08912e4 with b05a28e's test file: 3 failures (test_verify_refuses_leftover_atomic_writer_temp_file_in_stage, test_package_refuses_leftover_atomic_writer_temp_file_in_stage, test_package_refuses_leftover_atomic_writer_temp_file_in_receipts); green on a clean checkout of b05a28e: tests/test_release_artifacts.py 9 OK, test_claim_proof_bundle_checker OK, test_slo_validate OK; no test lines removed. The diff routes verify_stage, the package stage_files listing and both receipts listings through release_artifact_files, and verify now runs inside the typed LeftoverAtomicTempFileError handler (exit 3). Adversarial probe of release_artifact_files at b05a28e: top-level leftover, nested stage subdir bin/nested/.fss-server.tmp.killed and receipts/.verification.json.tmp.x1 are all REFUSED; the clean control and a non-temp .gitkeep are accepted. No cargo-read files changed. Earlier fix 748b07d + 9867956 still applies to artifacts.

title: Bug: qualify.sh writes qualification receipts non-atomically (readers can see half-written receipts)
description: Found by the 6.11 rework (orchestrator subagent, 1a551bc/4b1ca2d): scripts/qualify.sh writes each qualification receipt in place, so a concurrent reader (e.g. scripts/claim_proof_bundle_checker.py, which now inspects receipts and treats a corrupt receipt as an error) can read a half-written receipt as corrupt. Fix: write each receipt to a temp file in the same directory, fsync it, then rename it into place (atomic within the filesystem); make the claim checker's corrupt-receipt error message name the file. Acceptance: a planted-negative test that truncates a receipt mid-write proves readers see either the old or the new complete receipt, never a partial one; policy lane green.

title: Pin authority ledger and effect-journal heads so a byte-copied fork cannot vouch for lineage or discharge
description: From the fss-mnlz1 r3 review (residual): a byte copy of the authority ledger (1.9 ms) reproduces its LedgerAnchor (incl. state_root) exactly and can record a rival child that classifies terminal; a journal fork (0.36 ms) makes a planless result terminal while the real journal holds the obligation Pending. Nothing pins the real authority: ContractBasis does not contain the ledger anchor; the external-mutation check runs only at open(); a copy is simply a new file. Fix: pin the authority and journal heads in the handoff or the contract basis (or have consumers verify the selection-witness commitments against pinned heads), so a forked store cannot vouch. Planted fork tests with exact equality.
notes:
Orchestrator: extended scope = the AUTHORITY-WRITER residual (from the fss-mnlz1 r5 review): besides byte-copied forks, a party with raw append access to the authority ledger can (R5-B) displace a lineage basis so an effect first terminal proof is downgraded (fss-mnlz1 r6 makes that visible as a typed marker) and (R5-C) plant a junk first lineage entry (raw write, no witness, junk payload) that blocks the subject first genuine record (honest callers can continue only by naming the junk digest). Durable fix: lineage writes only via record_reference_publication (the authority refuses non-API lineage batches), plus pinned heads against forks.
Orchestrator: add R7-A (from the fss-mnlz1 r7 review, executed): with raw authority-ledger write access, one raw batch holding a lineage entry X (witness P) plus a proof marker naming X satisfies first_lineage_proof same-batch rule (situation_sections.rs ~585-600); X→L (the genuine first proof) is then reported "already proved … by X" and its first terminal announcement is suppressed. Same class as R5-C; the durable fix (accept lineage/proof-marker writes only via record_reference_publication, or require the marked entry to be backed by a vouched step with a sealed proof) closes both.

comments.author: MistyRabbit
comments.text: Reconnaissance landed: the fork vector is compiled_against (situation_sections.rs:649) accepting the compile anchor at ANY batch-history position — a byte-copied ledger with a rival child appended self-vouches through lineage_step, and the journal-fork discharge works the same way via the committed-history check. Detection requires an externally pinned head (handoff capsule or contract basis binding the authority head digest + journal root at mission/compile time), which ripples into the frozen agent-abstraction registry encodings. Scope: consumer-side pinning + planted fork tests with exact equality. Not started; needs a fresh session with the registry-digest ripple budgeted.

title: CAP- Capability bridge: file-ingest-first end-to-end
description:
## Why this epic exists (read this first)

On 2026-09-13 a Phase-1 reality check (main 474931d) found the following.

FSS is a deep, carefully reviewed reference-semantics library for an evidence ledger and an
agent-facing situation model. It sits on a real, crash-tested local storage substrate
(fss-ledger, fss-object, fss-publication). It is NOT a surveillance system yet:

- No code path touches a camera, a network socket, a codec, a model weight, an alert provider or
  an archive backend.
- The workspace has zero third-party dependencies and no Asupersync.

Key findings:

1. The only runnable end-to-end demo, `fss-lab` (crates/fss-cli/src/bin/fss-lab, 2,918 lines,
   2026-08-31), is a self-contained toy. It has its own SHA-256 (digest.rs), ledger (ledger.rs),
   spool (spool.rs) and effect coordinator (effects.rs), and it imports NOTHING from fss-core,
   fss-reference, fss-ledger, fss-object or fss-publication. The one thing a user can run end to
   end does not exercise the roughly 200k lines being hardened. The real composition (fss-reference
   policy, alert and situation over ledger, object and publication) runs only inside cargo tests.
   Vision goal #40, GATE-010, is rated WRONG_APPROACH.
2. Four "island" crates have ZERO consumers:
   - fss-packet: RTP/RTCP parsing, sequence continuity, bounded H.264 NAL reconstruction from RTP.
   - fss-tensor: dtype, shape, stride, storage and view core, with no kernels.
   - fss-model-ir: frozen operator IR v1 with 22 opcodes (Add, Sub, Mul, Div, Relu, Gelu, Silu,
     Sigmoid, Tanh, MatMul, Reshape, Transpose, Squeeze, Unsqueeze, Concat, Slice, LayerNorm,
     RMSNorm, Softmax, Conv2d, MaxPool2d, Embedding), plus canonical digest and shape inference.
     No executor.
   - fss-geometry: pinhole projection, triangle-mesh ray hits, PnP from supplied correspondences,
     route forecasts.
3. No ingest of any real bytes. There is no file importer: ADP-FILE-001 (fss-x4a.30.89.2) is only
   a registry row. There is no decoder (FSS-117, fss-x4a.12.16) and no executor (FSS-139,
   fss-x4a.14.10). `fss doctor`/`fss status`/`fss capabilities` return hard-coded JSON strings
   (crates/fss-cli/src/fss_cmd.rs).
4. Governance versus product: about 87k lines of checkers, schemas and registries, against 0 lines
   that reach a sensor, codec, model, network, archive or alert provider. In the two days before
   the check, 132 of 233 commits were contract, registry or checker hardening. 75% of the ready
   queue is "Realize registry row ...". The ready frontier rewards contract work, so the swarm has
   been optimizing the verifier rather than the product.
5. Integration is not beaded. No bead covers fss-lab on the real crates, packet -> acquisition ->
   capsule, IR -> executor -> event, or geometry -> coverage. Implementing the existing beads one
   by one can leave isolated, fully "closed" crates.

Verified state on 2026-09-13:

- About 2091 tests pass and 1 fails (fss-packet wire_contract
  `source_description_must_terminate_and_match_chunk_count`).
- clippy -D warnings is red (fss-packet lints, fss-geometry missing_docs).
- The policy lane is red: fss-packet and fss-geometry are "planned" in crate_topology.json but are
  workspace members, and the MANIFEST catch-up has 71-74 findings.

## The owner's binding steering decisions (2026-09-13)

1. Build CAPABILITY, not more registry or contract hardening. In scope:
   - (a) Rebuild fss-lab on the REAL crates.
   - (b) FILE INGEST FIRST: recorded H.264 (Annex-B and recorded RTP) and MJPEG files, plus a
     sans-IO RTSP parser with NO sockets, into sensor capsules and the acquisition lifecycle, using
     fss-packet (the owner's crate; never edit crates/fss-packet/**) and fss-tensor.
   - (c) Real callers for fss-packet, fss-tensor, fss-model-ir and fss-geometry where the plan
     puts them.
   - (d) A JPEG/MJPEG decoder feeding fss-tensor and a small scalar executor over fss-model-ir.
     Pure Rust, forbid(unsafe), zero new crates.
   - (e) `fss doctor`/`fss status` that read the real ledger.
   - (f) The main-green prerequisites fss-kr9n3, fss-1bd1l and fss-lc2r1 are already tracked.
     They are referenced as dependencies, not duplicated.
2. Device I/O stays blocked. Keep forbid(unsafe) and the zero-third-party-crate rule. NO camera,
   USB or socket beads now. Networked RTSP and Asupersync (fss-x4a.8.1) remain owner decisions;
   each gets exactly one placeholder bead marked "blocked on owner decision fss-x4a.8.1".
3. Existing beads are not closed, deleted or re-prioritized here; reshaping the backlog is a
   separate owner decision. New beads cite existing ids with `related` edges and depend on them
   with `blocks` edges only where the work truly cannot proceed.

## Target end state (what "done" looks like for this epic)

A user with a recorded file can run the first-party pipeline end to end on the real crates:

    fss-lab pipeline --input tests/fixtures/media/<fixture>.mjpeg --root <dir> --json

It goes file -> bounded split -> SensorCapsules with source custody -> root-last publication ->
EvidenceDeltaBatch in the DurableReferenceLedger -> baseline-JPEG decode into a u8 HWC Tensor ->
a scalar model-IR activity graph with an invocation receipt -> reference policy (single camera,
so never corroborated) -> event revision -> prepared alert with a simulated provider ->
receipt -> SituationCapsule -> sealed handoff. After that, `fss doctor --json --root <dir>` and
`fss status --json --root <dir>` report what is really on disk, including orphaned staging,
incomplete journal tails and indeterminate obligations, when faults are injected. Every step has
a companion test bead with unit tests and an e2e script that writes structured JSON-lines logs.

## Vision-checklist goals this epic moves (numbers from the reality check)

| Goal | Status on 2026-09-13 | What this epic does |
|---|---|---|
| #1 replay adapter | PARTIAL | file roots |
| #2 recorded-file import ADP-FILE-001 | NOT_STARTED | vertical slice |
| #6 acquisition lifecycle and sensor capsules | PARTIAL, no adapter drives it | file sessions drive it |
| #7 packet kernel | no consumer | rtpdump plus continuity callers |
| #8 codec | NOT_STARTED | baseline JPEG/MJPEG |
| #15 tensor/IR | no consumer | decoder output and executor input |
| #17 model execution | NOT_STARTED | scalar executor plus receipt |
| #27 twin/geometry | no consumer | visibility for coverage |
| #28 coverage | PARTIAL | geometry-derived occlusion |
| #34 doctor/status | STUB | real |
| #40 walking skeleton | WRONG_APPROACH | fss-lab on the real crates plus a file pipeline |

## Out of scope, and why

Out of scope:
- UVC/UAC, V4L2 and USB. Safe std Rust cannot issue ioctl or mmap, and no substrate crate is
  admitted.
- Networked RTSP, ONVIF, vendor adapters, WebRTC and LL-HLS.
- Archive, encryption and ATP.
- FrankenSQLite.
- Real alert providers and PTZ.
- Detection, tracking and association beyond one first-party activity graph.

These wait on owner decisions (fss-x4a.8.1 Asupersync, an ADR for the device-I/O substrate) or
on external prerequisites (hardware, consented corpora, admitted Franken siblings).

## Structure

Tracks, with priorities:
- Foundation (e2e harness, fixture generators): P1.
- LAB: fss-lab on the real crates. P1.
- INGEST: Annex-B, MJPEG, file adapter, acquisition lifecycle, rtpdump and fss-packet, RTP
  continuity, gauntlet. P1.
- RTSP sans-IO: P2.
- DECODE: JPEG to Tensor. P2.
- EXEC: scalar executor, receipt, model package, mock-seam routing. P2.
- GEO: geometric visibility for coverage. P2.
- DOCTOR/STATUS: P2.
- CAPSTONE pipeline and qualification: P2.
- Owner and blocked placeholders: P2.

Every implementation bead has a companion "(tests)" bead. The capstone qualification bead
depends on all test beads and on the three main-green bugs.

## Refinement round 1 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
Every CAP child was re-checked against the code at 8b96911.
- The twin merge (f9004ef, f5ed038) added fss-twin, so the workspace now has 11 members. fss-twin
  is "implemented" in crate_topology.json and depends on fss-geometry.
  - fss-geometry is therefore no longer consumer-free, although the CAP path still needs its own
    caller (GEO).
  - fss-twin itself has no consumer yet. The new bead CAP- TWIN (fss-2h5zq.68, with tests fss-2h5zq.69)
    covers that; it needs an owner scope confirmation.
- The model IR has 22 opcodes. The earlier "21" was a counting error; the list is right.
- New beads:
  - CAP- DOCTOR0 (fss-2h5zq.66, with tests fss-2h5zq.67): the existing opens create directories and
    take locks, so doctor and status need a non-mutating inspection layer.
  - CAP- TWIN (fss-2h5zq.68, with tests fss-2h5zq.69), described above.
- Structural corrections:
  - LAB1 uses fss-publication's LedgeredRootPublisher.
  - The acquisition history uses the real state kinds.
  - The rtpdump path handles SequenceClass::Probation.
  - EXEC4 generalizes the MockModelResult-only policy input.
  - The ready splitters, parser and decoder no longer carry acceptance criteria that need fixtures
    they do not depend on.
- The full change list is in the bridge-plan index (scratchpad bridge-plan-2026-09-13.md, section
  "Refinement round 1").

## Refinement round 2 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
Round 2 checked the five items round 1 left unverified, plus the four round-1 beads (.66-.69).
- RtcpMode has two variants, Compound and ReducedSize. The RTSP fixture and session beads now say
  which one applies and when.
- Model IR attribute types and defaults, the dtype rules, and the a20fa6c API deltas are now in the
  EXEC beads. f32 transcendentals come from libm, so goldens that must match on every host need a
  first-party exp.
- The model_execution_receipt schema allows no placeholder strings or nulls in required digest
  fields, and no repository tool validates JSON instances. EXEC2 now defines the field mapping, the
  sentinel digests and a stdlib instance validator.
- fss-twin: brown_luma_96x96.gray is a Brown-Conrady-DISTORTED frame, so it belongs on the raw
  (rectification) path. fss-twin re-exports no fss-geometry types, so CAP- TWIN also needs the
  fss-1bd1l gate.
- DOCTOR0: a write-refusing SpoolIo cannot go through open_with_io. Each owning crate therefore
  splits a read-only classifier out of its open. fss-ledger gains a bounded read-only replay.
  Writer detection uses /proc/locks, because the LOCK files persist after a writer exits.
- New capability: an explicit, operator-driven `fss-lab recover`, the repair affordance that
  doctor names. Doctor stays read-only.
- Storage bounds: one spool object holds at most 64 MiB, and a ledger batch at most 16,384 deltas
  and 16 MiB. File custody is therefore chunked, and large imports are written as capsule batches
  plus a final manifest batch.
The full change list is in the bridge-plan index (section "Refinement round 2").

## Refinement round 3 (2026-09-13, verified against main 7168075)
Round 3 was a targeted review of the round-2 design and of the EXEC beads against main 7168075,
which includes the fss-x4a.14.8 round-5 IR changes. It found material defects:
- Recover: AppendPhase has 8 variants and only four are injectable. The in-memory simulated provider
  cannot be reconciled from a separate recover process, so it becomes durable. reconcile_verified
  needs state Observed. Repair must hold the deployment lock and refuse mid-history corruption. The
  effect journal gets its own repair action, and orphan discards are added.
- Import: every import commits at least two batches (the ledgered-root batch has a fixed one-delta
  shape). Completion is an import object moving from generation 1 to 2. Resume skips committed
  batches by deterministic id. A span may cover any number of chunks. Chunk tamper surfaces as
  CustodyUnavailable (the spool rehashes). The exact capacity check runs after hashing and before
  staging. Every staged object must be reachable from a durable ledgered root, or doctor is never
  clean.
- DOCTOR0: /proc/locks can never prove "no writer" (pid namespaces, replaced lock files), so the
  writer_state values change. inspect_linkage cannot report LedgerReconciliationRequired. The
  read-only proof needs a recording I/O capability.
- EXEC: the IR is final for now (from_u32, opaque UnsupportedVersion, free-text defaults,
  Shape-for-IntList, ONNX Reshape). The activity package needs a valid generation id
  (model:fss-activity:v1), a single weight-bundle artifact and an explicit first-party license.
  Receipt sentinels use a distinct fss-na: scheme.
- DECODE/TWIN: the luma contract is pinned. The twin identity comes from the recorded luma digest.
  The decode-vs-raw differential is bounded, not byte-equal.
- A third digest-domain count pin exists in crates/fss-model-ir/tests/model_ir_contract.rs:420.
The full change list is in the bridge-plan index (section "Refinement round 3").
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Every child bead is closed or explicitly deferred by the owner
- [ ] CAP- QUALIFY passes: green main at one sha (including doctests), all scripts/e2e/cap_*.sh exit 0 with validated logs, fss-packet/fss-tensor/fss-model-ir/fss-geometry have non-test consumers on the CAP path, and fss-twin's consumer status is recorded
- [ ] `fss-lab pipeline --input <fixture> --root <dir> --json` shows the full digest chain on the real crates; fss doctor/status read that root

title: CAP- e2e harness: scripts/e2e/lib.sh structured JSON-lines logging and runner
description:
## What and why
Every CAP- test bead must ship an end-to-end script with detailed logging. Today the repo has no
e2e script convention. It has scripts/qualify.sh lanes and about 30 Python checkers, and
fss-x4a.28.41 ("deterministic end-to-end scripts, fault matrices, standalone proof verification",
P0) is an unbuilt umbrella. This bead builds the small shared harness so the ~25 CAP e2e scripts
log uniformly and can be read by humans, agents and a later proof-bundle lane.

## Build
- `scripts/e2e/lib.sh`: bash, `set -euo pipefail`, sourced by `scripts/e2e/cap_*.sh`. Functions:
  - `e2e_init <name>`: creates `${FSS_E2E_LOG_DIR:-target/e2e-logs}/<name>/` and a run file named
    by a monotonically increasing run index. There is no wall clock in digests; a `ts` field is
    allowed in logs only.
  - `e2e_step <step> -- <cmd...>`: runs the command, captures its exit code, stdout digest (sha256
    via `sha256sum`) and a bounded stdout excerpt (first 4 KiB, secret-redacted), then appends one
    JSON line
    `{ts, script, bead, step, cmd, exit, duration_ms, stdout_sha256, stdout_excerpt,
    stderr_excerpt, verdict:"ran"}` (the full record schema is defined in "Refinement round 1" below).
  - `e2e_expect_eq <step> <expected> <observed>`, `e2e_expect_json_field <step> <file-or-var>
    <jq-free-path> <expected>`: use a tiny `python3 -c` JSON reader, because jq may be absent.
  - `e2e_expect_exit <step> <code>`.
  - `e2e_summary`: writes `{"step":"summary","verdict":...,"steps":N,"failures":[...],
    "repro":"<exact command>"}`. It exits 1 if any expectation failed and prints the log path.
  - `e2e_bin <name>`: resolves a binary. It uses `$FSS_BIN_DIR/<name>` if set, otherwise
    `target/debug/<name>`, otherwise it fails with a clear message telling the operator to build
    first via `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- cargo build -p fss-cli --bins --locked --offline`
    and set FSS_BIN_DIR. rch runs remotely, so scripts never invoke cargo implicitly.
  - `e2e_tmpdir`: creates a scoped temp root under the log dir. It is removed on success and kept
    on failure for forensics, and the kept path is logged.
- Redaction: excerpts pass through a filter that drops lines matching
  authorization|password|token|secret|cookie (case-insensitive) and replaces raw hex blobs longer
  than 64 characters with their length.
- A 4 KiB excerpt cap and a 10 MiB total log cap per run; both are enforced.

## Where it connects
Every CAP-* (tests) bead depends on this one. A later qualification lane (fss-x4a.28.41,
QL-REFERENCE-001) can consume the JSON-lines logs as proof inputs. Do not add a new qualify.sh
lane in this bead: claim lanes fail closed until scripts/lanes/<lane>.sh exists, which is a
separate decision.

## Considerations
- It must work under zsh-invoked bash on the build host.
- No network access, no sudo, and no writes outside the repo's target/ or the chosen log dir.
- Scripts are also checked by shellcheck if it is available (optional; log a skipped step if
  absent).
- Register the new paths in MANIFEST.delta.sha256. There are no Rust modules, so no
  semantic-plane rows.

## Shared rules for every CAP- bead (repeated so this bead stands alone)

Context: parent epic "CAP- Capability bridge: file-ingest-first end-to-end" (fss-2h5zq), created
2026-09-13 from the Phase-1 reality check at main 474931d and the owner's binding steering
decisions. The epic holds the full background; the essentials are repeated here.

- Constitution (AGENTS.md): Rust 2024 on nightly-2026-08-31. `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` in every
  crate, target, test, example and helper, with no exception path. Zero third-party crates: the
  dependency closure is fss-* only, and DEP-EXCEPTION-001 admits nothing. This bridge also adds
  ZERO new workspace crates. New code lands as modules in existing crates, mainly fss-reference and
  fss-cli. Moving the code into the planned L3/L4 crates (fss-codec-mjpeg, fss-container,
  fss-device-core, fss-model-runtime, fss-kernel-cpu, fss-coverage) is a later owner decision,
  because a new member trips the crate_topology and member-count pins (see fss-1bd1l).
- Do NOT edit crates/fss-packet/** (the owner's crate). Use its public API as-is:
  RtpPacket::parse, SequenceTracker, H264Depacketizer, NalUnit, SenderReportClock and
  JitterEstimator. Any change that needs fss-packet edits goes to an owner bead and is never
  assigned to an agent.
- No device I/O: no camera, USB, V4L2 or socket code; no `std::net` or `TcpStream`. Inputs are
  recorded files and recorded transcripts only. Every file read goes through an explicit I/O
  authority value, following the ReplayIoAuthority/ReplayCx pattern in
  crates/fss-reference/src/adapter_replay.rs, with cooperative cancellation checkpoints
  (request -> drain -> finalize). Asupersync `Cx` is NOT admitted yet (owner decision
  fss-x4a.8.1). Do not add Tokio or any other runtime.
- Security boundary: fixtures are synthetic and generated first-party. No third-party footage, no
  identifiable people, no captured network addresses. Never handle credentials: RTSP auth headers
  are detected and refused, never computed or stored. No scanning. Logs never contain secrets or
  private media bytes; they carry digests and byte spans only.
- Truth discipline:
  - A decoded frame is not retained evidence without source custody.
  - File import has no live continuity, so it never certifies absence. Negative reads stay
    unknown or not_observable.
  - File mtime is not capture time. Use ClockBasis::Estimated with an explicit, wide
    CaptureInterval unless the stream itself carries timing.
  - One camera's model score is never "corroborated".
  - unknown, not_observable, stale and indeterminate are never flattened to null, low confidence
    or omission.
- Registration, done in the same commit as the code:
  1. Every new .rs module under crates/fss-core or crates/fss-reference gets a
     `module_declarations` entry in architecture/semantic_plane_registry.json with its plane
     (authority | cognition | effect | support | ambiguous).
     scripts/semantic_plane_checker.py audits exactly those two crates and fails otherwise.
  2. Every new canonical digest or encoding domain tag gets a row in registries/DIGEST_DOMAINS.md
     (ID SCHEMA-DOMAIN-<NAME>-001, domain fss.<name>.v1, scope, authority, invariant rule).
     Bump ALL THREE pinned domain counts in the same commit: the two digestDomainCount
     assertions in tests/test_schema_validate.py AND the domain_count assertion (and its
     message) in crates/fss-model-ir/tests/model_ir_contract.rs:420 (45 at main 7168075;
     verified in refinement round 3). Count from the value on HEAD at commit time, because several CAP
     beads add domains in parallel.
  3. Every new or changed source path gets a row in MANIFEST.delta.sha256 per ADR-0013. Never
     edit the MANIFEST.sha256 base. Check with `python3 scripts/manifest_audit.py`.
  4. New crate dependency edges must point downward in architecture/crate_topology.json. Layers:
     L2 ledger/object/publication, L3 fss-packet, L4 tensor/model-ir/geometry, L6 fss-cli,
     L7 fss-reference. fss-cli -> fss-reference is the one waived inversion. Check with
     `python3 scripts/dependency_dag_checker.py`.
  5. New CLI error and exit identities get rows in registries/ERRORS.md, and the operation
     crosswalk (architecture/operation_crosswalk.json and crates/fss-cli/src/crosswalk.rs) stays
     consistent.
- Verification (remote only):
  - `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- cargo test -p <crate> --all-targets --no-fail-fast --locked --offline`
  - `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets --keep-going --locked --offline -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo fmt --check`

    `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- cargo test -p <crate> --doc --no-fail-fast --locked --offline`.

    output is ANSI-coloured; strip ANSI before counting diagnostics). Re-run Python checkers and
    e2e scripts on a fresh `git worktree add --detach` checkout, never only in the shared tree.

  Main is currently red for reasons outside this bead (fss-kr9n3, fss-1bd1l, fss-lc2r1). Until
  those land, report "no new findings attributable to this bead's files". Never weaken a gate.
- E2E convention: every test bead ships scripts/e2e/cap_<name>.sh using the shared helpers in
  scripts/e2e/lib.sh (see the "CAP- e2e harness" bead).

  - LocalRootPublisher::open and StagingSpool::open create directories and take exclusive lock

- Swarm hygiene:
  - One bead per commit, with the bead id in the subject.
  - Commit only files you own. Never `git add -A`. Never reset, amend or rebase main.
  - Commit only what compiles against committed HEAD, and commit type changes together with all

title: CAP- LAB ReferenceDeployment (tests): reopen, digest linkage, crash cut points, path independence, e2e
description:
## Unit and contract tests (crates/fss-reference/tests/reference_deployment_contract.rs)
- Open an empty root, run one synthetic source -> capsule -> publish -> append cycle, reopen, and
  check that the same anchor and roots are recovered.
- Path independence: the same scenario under two roots gives identical anchor, publication and
  handoff digests.
- A crash at each fss_publication::PublishCutPoint (via inject_crash_at): reopen reports
  orphaned or broken roots exactly, and nothing is published half-way.
- Journal append failure at each AppendPhase (fail_journal_after_phase): reopen with Reject
  returns the typed incomplete-tail error.
- A lost ACK leaves the effect indeterminate after reopen.
- Duplicate intent does not duplicate an effect.

## E2E (scripts/e2e/cap_reference_deployment.sh)
Run the contract test binary with `--nocapture` and a logged filter per case, then parse its
structured stdout lines into JSON log steps. The goal is a log a human can read: case, cut
point, expected state, observed state, digests.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Blocked by (must finish first):
  - fss-2h5zq.9: CAP- LAB: ReferenceDeployment composition in fss-reference (spool + root-last publication + durable ledger + effects + situation)
  - fss-2h5zq.1: CAP- e2e harness: scripts/e2e/lib.sh structured JSON-lines logging and runner
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.63: CAP- QUALIFY: whole-bridge verification on green main (rust+policy lanes, all CAP e2e scripts) and honest status/doc update

## Refinement round 1 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- Add LedgerCutPoint::AfterRootDurable to the crash cases. RootLedgerReconciliation must report the
  pending root and its guidance, never a silently visible batch.
- AppendPhase has six variants: BodyWrite, BodySync, CommitWrite, CommitSync, ReconcileRead and
  ReconcileTruncate. The last two fire only during reconciliation, so their cases exercise the
  reconciliation path and assert its typed result.
- Enumerate PublishCutPoint, LedgerCutPoint and AppendPhase with an exhaustive match that has no
  wildcard arm, so a new upstream variant breaks the test build instead of silently lacking a case.
- A second ReferenceDeployment::open on a locked root returns deployment_locked.
- Print CAPLOG lines per case; the e2e script runs through e2e_cargo_test.

## Refinement round 2 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- A second open while locked returns deployment_locked, and both journals stay byte-identical.
- LAYOUT round-trips (site_lineage, paths, limits digest). A directory without LAYOUT is
  not_a_deployment.
- Recovery actions:
  - for each AppendPhase: reopen with Reject gives the typed tail error;
    open_for_recovery(TruncateIncompleteLedgerTail) succeeds; the committed prefix and last_root are
    unchanged; a normal reopen then succeeds;
  - the same for the effect journal;
  - foreign trailing bytes: the plan from fss_ledger::doctor/plan is applied through
    ApplySealedLedgerRepair; a mismatched plan digest is refused; the quarantine sidecar exists.
- A tiny DeploymentLimits gives a typed capacity refusal that names the limit.

## Refinement round 3 (2026-09-13, verified against main 7168075)
A review of the round-2 recover design against the code corrected these test expectations:
- AppendPhase has 8 variants (error.rs:30-47): BodyWrite, BodySync, CommitWrite, CommitSync,
  ReconcileRead, ReconcileTruncate, ReconcileSync, ReconcileSeek. fail_journal_after_phase
  (durable.rs:414) injects only the first four, after the real write succeeded (journal.rs:254-272).
  The exhaustive match lists all 8. Expected results replace the round-2 "for each AppendPhase" line:
  - BodyWrite, BodySync: reopen with Reject gives the typed tail error;
    open_for_recovery(TruncateIncompleteLedgerTail) succeeds; committed_len and last_root are
    unchanged; a normal reopen then succeeds.
  - CommitWrite, CommitSync: the append returned AppendIndeterminate, yet a Reject reopen succeeds and
    the batch is visible. Retrying append_batch with the same batch_id returns the committed anchor
    (idempotent append) and appends nothing.
  - ReconcileRead, ReconcileTruncate, ReconcileSync, ReconcileSeek: asserted not_applicable with the
    reason "no injection hook in fss-ledger" (owner decision whether to add hooks).
- DurableEffectJournal has no fault hook: build its incomplete tail by writing the leading bytes of a
  valid record directly to a copy of the journal.
- New cases:
  - mid-history corruption (a bad record followed by valid ones) is refused by
    ApplySealedLedgerRepair with recover_corrupt_history, and the journal is unchanged;
  - a crash between the quarantine rename and the truncation (simulate by running apply's steps up to
    the rename on a copy): rerunning apply reuses the identical sidecar (repair.rs:885) and succeeds;
  - foreign bytes in the effect journal are repaired through ApplySealedEffectRepair;
  - a plan computed read-only while a writer holds <root>/objects/LOCK is refused at apply with the
    typed locked error, and the journal is byte-identical;
  - LAYOUT is written atomically (a leftover LAYOUT temp is ignored); a non-empty root without LAYOUT
    is not_a_deployment and open does not create LAYOUT there;
  - plan digests are excluded from the path-independence comparison (they bind path, dev and inode).
- After each clean scenario cycle, LocalRecoveryReport.unreferenced_objects is empty and
  reconcile().is_clean() holds.

## Shared rules for every CAP- bead (repeated so this bead stands alone)

Context: parent epic "CAP- Capability bridge: file-ingest-first end-to-end" (fss-2h5zq), created
2026-09-13 from the Phase-1 reality check at main 474931d and the owner's binding steering
decisions. The epic holds the full background; the essentials are repeated here.

  crate, target, test, example and helper, with no exception path. Zero third-party crates: the
  dependency closure is fss-* only, and DEP-EXCEPTION-001 admits nothing. This bridge also adds
  ZERO new workspace crates. New code lands as modules in existing crates, mainly fss-reference and
  fss-cli. Moving the code into the planned L3/L4 crates (fss-codec-mjpeg, fss-container,
  fss-device-core, fss-model-runtime, fss-kernel-cpu, fss-coverage) is a later owner decision,
  because a new member trips the crate_topology and member-count pins (see fss-1bd1l).
- Do NOT edit crates/fss-packet/** (the owner's crate). Use its public API as-is:
  RtpPacket::parse, SequenceTracker, H264Depacketizer, NalUnit, SenderReportClock and
  JitterEstimator. Any change that needs fss-packet edits goes to an owner bead and is never
  assigned to an agent.
- No device I/O: no camera, USB, V4L2 or socket code; no `std::net` or `TcpStream`. Inputs are
  recorded files and recorded transcripts only. Every file read goes through an explicit I/O
  authority value, following the ReplayIoAuthority/ReplayCx pattern in
  crates/fss-reference/src/adapter_replay.rs, with cooperative cancellation checkpoints
  (request -> drain -> finalize). Asupersync `Cx` is NOT admitted yet (owner decision
  fss-x4a.8.1). Do not add Tokio or any other runtime.
- Security boundary: fixtures are synthetic and generated first-party. No third-party footage, no
  identifiable people, no captured network addresses. Never handle credentials: RTSP auth headers
  are detected and refused, never computed or stored. No scanning. Logs never contain secrets or
  private media bytes; they carry digests and byte spans only.
- Truth discipline:
  - A decoded frame is not retained evidence without source custody.
  - File import has no live continuity, so it never certifies absence. Negative reads stay
    unknown or not_observable.
  - File mtime is not capture time. Use ClockBasis::Estimated with an explicit, wide
    CaptureInterval unless the stream itself carries timing.
  - One camera's model score is never "corroborated".
  - unknown, not_observable, stale and indeterminate are never flattened to null, low confidence
    or omission.
- Registration, done in the same commit as the code:
  1. Every new .rs module under crates/fss-core or crates/fss-reference gets a
     `module_declarations` entry in architecture/semantic_plane_registry.json with its plane
     (authority | cognition | effect | support | ambiguous).
     scripts/semantic_plane_checker.py audits exactly those two crates and fails otherwise.
  2. Every new canonical digest or encoding domain tag gets a row in registries/DIGEST_DOMAINS.md
     (ID SCHEMA-DOMAIN-<NAME>-001, domain fss.<name>.v1, scope, authority, invariant rule).
     Bump ALL THREE pinned domain counts in the same commit: the two digestDomainCount
     assertions in tests/test_schema_validate.py AND the domain_count assertion (and its
     message) in crates/fss-model-ir/tests/model_ir_contract.rs:420 (45 at main 7168075;
     verified in refinement round 3). Count from the value on HEAD at commit time, because several CAP
     beads add domains in parallel.
  3. Every new or changed source path gets a row in MANIFEST.delta.sha256 per ADR-0013. Never
     edit the MANIFEST.sha256 base. Check with `python3 scripts/manifest_audit.py`.
  4. New crate dependency edges must point downward in architecture/crate_topology.json. Layers:
     L2 ledger/object/publication, L3 fss-packet, L4 tensor/model-ir/geometry, L6 fss-cli,
     L7 fss-reference. fss-cli -> fss-reference is the one waived inversion. Check with
     `python3 scripts/dependency_dag_checker.py`.
  5. New CLI error and exit identities get rows in registries/ERRORS.md, and the operation
     crosswalk (architecture/operation_crosswalk.json and crates/fss-cli/src/crosswalk.rs) stays
     consistent.
- Verification (remote only):
  - `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- cargo test -p <crate> --all-targets --no-fail-fast --locked --offline`
  - `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets --keep-going --locked --offline -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo fmt --check`
  - `scripts/qualify.sh --lane policy`
  - `--all-targets` does NOT run doctests. When the crate has doc examples, also run
    `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- cargo test -p <crate> --doc --no-fail-fast --locked --offline`.
  - Launch rch from the repo directory with `--base <sha>`. Decide pass or fail by exit code (rch
    output is ANSI-coloured; strip ANSI before counting diagnostics). Re-run Python checkers and
    e2e scripts on a fresh `git worktree add --detach` checkout, never only in the shared tree.

  Main is currently red for reasons outside this bead (fss-kr9n3, fss-1bd1l, fss-lc2r1). Until
  those land, report "no new findings attributable to this bead's files". Never weaken a gate.
- E2E convention: every test bead ships scripts/e2e/cap_<name>.sh using the shared helpers in
  scripts/e2e/lib.sh (see the "CAP- e2e harness" bead).
  - Logs are JSON lines under ${FSS_E2E_LOG_DIR:-target/e2e-logs}/<name>/. The first record is an
    env record (git sha, bead id, binary sha256s, host triple, FSS_* settings); then one record per
    step: {ts, script, bead, step, cmd, exit, duration_ms, expected, observed, digest,
    stdout_sha256, stdout_excerpt, stderr_excerpt, verdict, repro}. Rust tests feed the log by
    printing one-line `CAPLOG {json}` records under --nocapture; lib.sh ingests them (ANSI
    stripped) through e2e_cargo_test. scripts/e2e/validate_log.py checks every record.
  - The final record is {"step":"summary","verdict":"pass"|"fail","steps":N,"failures":[...]}.
  - Scripts exit non-zero on any mismatch. They are deterministic (fixed seeds, no wall clock
    inside digests) and bounded in size, and they print a one-line reproduction command.

  - scripts/dependency_audit.py (DEP-AUD-022) scans every .rs file, tests and examples included,
    for the bare word unsafe. Comments are masked but string literals are NOT, so never put that
    word in a string literal or a guard-test pattern. The only allowed occurrence is
    #![forbid(unsafe_code)].
  - The workspace has 11 members since the twin merge (f9004ef, f5ed038). fss-twin (L4,
    "implemented") depends on fss-geometry. Treat crates/fss-twin/** and crates/fss-geometry/**
    as owner-authored upstream code, like fss-packet: use their public API and record API gaps in
    notes instead of editing them.
  - Shared hot files (edit only your own rows or lines; stage with `git add -p`):
    registries/DIGEST_DOMAINS.md, tests/test_schema_validate.py,
    crates/fss-model-ir/tests/model_ir_contract.rs (the third domain-count pin),
    architecture/semantic_plane_registry.json, MANIFEST.delta.sha256, registries/ERRORS.md,
    crates/fss-reference/src/lib.rs, crates/fss-reference/Cargo.toml and
    crates/fss-cli/src/lab_cmd.rs.

    files, so they are not read-only. Read-only inspection goes through fss-2h5zq.66.
- Swarm hygiene:
  - One bead per commit, with the bead id in the subject.
  - Commit only files you own. Never `git add -A`. Never reset, amend or rebase main.
  - Commit only what compiles against committed HEAD, and commit type changes together with all
    their users.
  - Record final paths and evidence with `br update <id> --append-notes`. Never use --notes,
    which overwrites the field.

- [ ] The lock-order, LAYOUT, recovery-action and capacity cases pass with CAPLOG lines
- [ ] AppendPhase cases follow the round-3 expectations with all 8 variants in an exhaustive match; the corrupt-history, resumed-apply, effect-journal repair, locked-apply, atomic-LAYOUT and idempotent-append cases pass; a clean cycle leaves no unreferenced objects

title: CAP- LAB: port the six fss-lab scenarios onto ReferenceDeployment (real crates) with an explicit --root and report schema v2
description:
## What and why
fss-lab has six deterministic scenarios in crates/fss-cli/src/bin/fss-lab/scenario.rs
(run_scenario, 1,000 lines): quiet, raccoon, intrusion, sneaky, lost-ack and corrupt-source. They
use two virtual cameras, cam-front (failure domain front-power-and-network) and cam-side
(side-power-and-network). On 2026-09-13 `fss-lab matrix` ran green, but entirely on private
types (SourceSpool, EvidenceLedger, EffectCoordinator, digest::sha256).

Rewrite run_scenario so every scenario drives the REAL stack through ReferenceDeployment (LAB1):
- virtual source bytes -> fss_core SensorCapsule::from_source_bytes;
- stage_and_publish;
- DurableReferenceLedger batches;
- MockModelExecutor / execute_mock_model for detections;
- evaluate_unknown_presence (independent failure domains required for corroboration);
- publish_reference_event;
- alert prepare/dispatch/observe/reconcile through the DurableEffectJournal and the simulated
  provider;
- compile_reference_situation, then seal_reference_handoff.

## Behavioural expectations per scenario (keep the semantics the toy demonstrated, now proven by the real crates)
- quiet: certified_quiet only if the real CoverageWitness certifies absence (continuous, complete
  coverage from both cameras). absence_certified=true.
- raccoon: a benign classification; no alert.
- intrusion: two independent failure domains corroborate; the alert is prepared, dispatched and
  verified.
- sneaky: a protected residual world survives, with a probe/information-gathering affordance and
  a coverage_gap warning. It must never certify absence.
- lost-ack: the effect ends transient_indeterminate with a reconcile affordance, and there is no
  blind retry.
- corrupt-source: corruption is detected by the real spool verification. The capsule is withheld
  with source_corrupt, never used as evidence.

If a real-crate result DIFFERS from the toy's, that is a finding, not something to paper over.
Record it in notes and open a bug bead. Do not tweak the real crates to match the toy.

## CLI changes (crates/fss-cli/src/lab_cmd.rs and src/bin/fss-lab/main.rs)
- `run <scenario>`, `matrix` and `replay <scenario> --repeat N` take `--root <dir>` (required).
  There are no ambient filesystem roots (crate_topology rule). `matrix` uses <dir>/<scenario>/.
  `self-test` keeps using an internal scoped temp root under the explicit --root.
- `replay --repeat N` proves byte-identical reports across N fresh roots.
- The report schema becomes `fss.lab.scenario.v2`: the v1 fields plus ledger_sequence,
  ledger_anchor_root, publication_root, situation_digest, handoff_digest, effect_state,
  obligation_state and crate_generations. The digests now come from fss_core.
- Update the strict parsing tests (crates/fss-cli/tests/cli_argument_parsing.rs, lab_cli.rs) and
  add new error identities (missing --root) to registries/ERRORS.md.

## Cargo
fss-cli currently depends on fss-core and fss-reference only. Prefer going through the
fss-reference re-exports. If direct fss-ledger/fss-object/fss-publication imports are needed, add
those downward edges (L6 -> L2) and update Cargo.lock plus its MANIFEST.delta row.

## Related
GATE-010 fss-x4a.2.2 and FSS-240 fss-x4a.24.40. Old private modules are deleted in LAB3, not
here, so this diff stays reviewable. Until LAB3 lands, the old modules may be dead code, but do
NOT add `#[allow(dead_code)]`; gate scans flag both `#![allow` and `#[allow`. Land LAB2 and LAB3
back to back, or delete within LAB2 if clippy would otherwise go red.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Blocked by (must finish first):
  - fss-2h5zq.9: CAP- LAB: ReferenceDeployment composition in fss-reference (spool + root-last publication + durable ledger + effects + situation)
- Related existing beads (context only, not blocking; this bead does not close them): fss-x4a.2.2, fss-x4a.24.40
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.12: CAP- LAB scenarios on real crates (tests): per-scenario assertions, determinism across roots, e2e matrix script
  - fss-2h5zq.13: CAP- LAB: delete fss-lab's private digest.rs, ledger.rs, spool.rs and effects.rs (no private SHA-256, ledger or spool left)
  - fss-2h5zq.15: CAP- LAB: fss-lab crash-matrix subcommand (kill at every publish cut point and journal phase, reopen, report recovery)
  - fss-2h5zq.17: CAP- LAB: `fss-lab ingest --input <file> --root <dir>` runs the file-ingest adapter on the real stack and prints an import report
  - fss-2h5zq.51: CAP- EXEC: route the fss-reference mock-model seam through the scalar executor for one lab scenario (executor-backed observations into policy)
  - fss-2h5zq.55: CAP- GEO: lab 'sneaky' scenario derives its coverage gap from geometry (occluded zone) instead of a hard-coded gap

## Refinement round 1 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- The policy input is ReferenceModelObservation::new(result: MockModelResult, failure_domain,
  interval) (policy.rs:21). The six mock scenarios therefore keep MockModelExecutor and
  execute_mock_model. The executor path is CAP- EXEC4 (fss-2h5zq.51), which generalizes that input.
- `run` and `matrix` refuse a --root that already holds a deployment or other files, with a
  registered `root_not_empty` error, so scenario histories never mix. `replay --repeat N` creates N
  fresh sub-roots under --root.
- The v2 report adds a `knowledge` object per scenario, so tests assert labels instead of parsing
  prose:
  - absence: certified | not_certifiable{reason};
  - corroboration: corroborated | single_source | not_applicable;
  - the coverage-gap zones.
- The publication lock refuses two ReferenceDeployment opens of one root (deployment_locked), so
  matrix runs its scenarios sequentially.

## Refinement round 3 (2026-09-13, verified against main 7168075)
- Every alert dispatch goes through ReferenceDeployment's single simulated-provider accessor; fss-lab
  never constructs its own ReferenceAlertProvider. fss-2h5zq.15 makes that provider durable under
  the root, so the recover command can reconcile from a separate process.
- After every scenario, LocalRecoveryReport.unreferenced_objects is empty and reconcile().is_clean()
  holds: every staged payload is reachable from a durable ledgered root (local/mod.rs:504, :514-520).
  A producer that leaves unreferenced objects is a defect to fix here, not a doctor finding.

title: CAP- LAB scenarios on real crates (tests): per-scenario assertions, determinism across roots, e2e matrix script
description:
## Integration tests (crates/fss-cli/tests/lab_real_crates.rs)
- For each scenario, spawn env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_fss-lab") with a temp --root and assert the
  disposition fields. Then open the same root with fss_ledger::inspect and the LocalRootPublisher
  from the test, and check that the ledger sequence and publication root in the report match what
  is really on disk. This check is what proves the demo uses the real crates.
- Determinism across two roots.
- Negative cases: missing --root gives the registered error id and exit code; an unknown scenario
  is rejected.

## E2E (scripts/e2e/cap_lab_real_crates.sh)
1. Resolve fss-lab via e2e_bin.
2. For each of the six scenarios, run it into its own tmp root and log disposition, digests and
   exit code, with expectations from a table in the script.
3. Rerun into fresh roots and compare stdout sha256s.
4. Run `fss-lab matrix` twice and compare.

title: CAP- LAB: delete fss-lab's private digest.rs, ledger.rs, spool.rs and effects.rs (no private SHA-256, ledger or spool left)
description:
## What and why
While private copies of SHA-256, the ledger, the spool and the effect coordinator exist, the demo
can drift back to the toy, and reviewers cannot tell which code a report came from. The reality
check's first step for gap #1 explicitly says to delete them.

## Build
- Remove crates/fss-cli/src/bin/fss-lab/digest.rs (a private SHA-256 compress function and
  CanonicalWriter), ledger.rs (EvidenceLedger, CoverageCertificate, certify_absence,
  assess_event), spool.rs (SourceSpool) and effects.rs (EffectCoordinator).
- Move any still-needed behaviour to its real owner and cite it in notes:
  - coverage certification -> fss_core CoverageWitness;
  - corroboration -> fss_core CorroborationAnalysis / fss_reference evaluate_unknown_presence;
  - the effect lifecycle -> fss_core EffectJournal / fss_reference DurableEffectJournal.
- Their in-file unit tests (for example ledger_is_append_only_and_rejects_time_reversal,
  absence_requires_complete_continuous_coverage, correlated_sources_do_not_fake_corroboration,
  lost_ack_is_indeterminate_and_blocks_blind_retry, and so on) encode useful properties. Port each
  property to a test against the REAL owner, in fss-reference or fss-core tests, if it is not
  already covered there. List the old-to-new test mapping in notes. Do not silently drop coverage.
- Remove the MANIFEST rows of the deleted files. ADR-0013 says the delta cannot delete sources, so
  follow fss-lc2r1's resolution for deletions. If none exists yet, record the needed base
  compaction in notes and coordinate on fss-lc2r1. Do not hand-edit the base.

- digest.rs: canonical_fields_are_unambiguous, domains_are_separated.
- ledger.rs: ledger_is_append_only_and_rejects_time_reversal,
  absence_requires_complete_continuous_coverage, observed_presence_blocks_absence_certificate,
  correlated_sources_do_not_fake_corroboration, independent_failure_domains_corroborate.
- spool.rs: staged_bytes_are_not_visible_before_root_publication,
  corruption_prevents_verification_and_reads, publication_is_idempotent_and_ordered,
  key_reuse_with_different_bytes_fails.
- effects.rs: exact_idempotent_prepare_returns_the_existing_operation, idempotency_drift_fails,
  obligation_cannot_drift_between_operations, lost_ack_is_indeterminate_and_blocks_blind_retry,
  reconciliation_can_prove_completion.

There is no sha256_known_vectors test. SHA-256 vectors belong to fss-core's digest tests; cite those.
main.rs declares `mod digest; mod effects; mod ledger; mod scenario; mod spool;`. Remove the four
private mods in the same commit as their files.

title: CAP- LAB: fss-lab crash-matrix subcommand (kill at every publish cut point and journal phase, reopen, report recovery)
description:
## What and why
GATE-010 (fss-x4a.2.2) pass criteria include: "every injected kill/cancel point leaves terminal
or explicitly indeterminate obligations; duplicate intent/commit does not duplicate an effect;
doctor detects staged, orphaned, and indeterminate state." Today that matrix exists only as
fss-publication's process_death_crash_harness and fss-ledger's crash tests. It is not reachable
from the runnable demo.

## Build
A subcommand, `fss-lab crash-matrix --root <dir> [--scenario intrusion] [--json]`:
- For each fault point it runs the scenario in a fresh sub-root, injects the fault, then reopens
  via ReferenceDeployment and records the recovery state. Fault points:
  - every fss_publication::PublishCutPoint (inject_crash_at);
  - every fss_ledger AppendPhase (fail_journal_after_phase);
  - an effect dispatch with a lost ACK;
  - cooperative cancellation at each ReplayCx checkpoint.
- The recovery state it records: orphaned staging count, broken roots, incomplete tail (Reject
  error), pending/indeterminate obligations, and whether a re-run after recovery duplicates any
  effect (it must not).
- Output: `fss.lab.crash_matrix.v1`, with one row per fault point: {fault, expected_class,
  observed_class, orphaned, broken_roots, tail_state, obligations:{terminal, indeterminate},
  duplicate_effects:0}. The overall verdict is pass only if every row matches its expected class.
- It runs in-process with injected faults. Real process-death is fss-publication's existing
  harness; cite it rather than duplicating it.
- The sub-roots are left on disk. They are the doctor's test corpus (see DOCTOR-T).

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Blocked by (must finish first):
  - fss-2h5zq.11: CAP- LAB: port the six fss-lab scenarios onto ReferenceDeployment (real crates) with an explicit --root and report schema v2
- Related existing beads (context only, not blocking; this bead does not close them): fss-x4a.2.2
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.16: CAP- LAB crash-matrix (tests): expected-class table, idempotency after recovery, e2e with per-fault log lines
  - fss-2h5zq.58: CAP- DOCTOR (tests): crash-matrix corpus detection, read-only proof, bounded output, exit codes, e2e

## Refinement round 1 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- Fault points at 8b96911:
  - PublishCutPoint {AfterChildrenVerified, AfterManifestBody, AfterRootTempWrite,
    AfterRootRename};
  - LedgerCutPoint {AfterRootDurable}, through LedgeredRootPublisher::inject_crash_at;
  - AppendPhase {BodyWrite, BodySync, CommitWrite, CommitSync, ReconcileRead, ReconcileTruncate};
  - a lost ACK;
  - every entry of ReferenceDeployment's DEPLOYMENT_CANCEL_STAGES.
- The ReconcileRead and ReconcileTruncate rows run through the reconciliation path with an explicit
  expected class. No row is silently skipped; a not-applicable row carries its reason.
- Sub-roots get stable slug names `<root>/<family>.<variant>/`, for example publish.after_root_rename,
  ledger.after_root_durable, append.commit_sync, effect.lost_ack and cancel.<stage>. Doctor tests
  address them by name.
- Each row also records RootLedgerReconciliation.is_clean() and its guidance. A "rerun after
  recovery" column proves that duplicate intent duplicates neither an effect nor a batch.

## Refinement round 2 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- New subcommand: `fss-lab recover --root <dir> [--truncate-incomplete-tail ledger|effects]
  [--plan-ledger-repair] [--apply-ledger-repair <plan-digest>] [--reconcile-effects] [--json]`.
  - It is the next_affordance that `fss doctor --root` names (fss-2h5zq.57). Each action is
    explicit, runs through ReferenceDeployment::open_for_recovery (fss-2h5zq.9), prints
    `fss.lab.recover_report.v1` with the typed receipt, and refuses a locked root.
  - --plan-ledger-repair prints the sealed plan and its digest and changes nothing. Only
    --apply-ledger-repair with that exact digest applies it.
  - --reconcile-effects reconciles indeterminate obligations only against the lab's simulated
    provider, a deterministic observation, through DurableEffectJournal::reconcile_verified or
    reconcile_failed. It never retries blindly, and it never touches a real provider.
  - Registered error ids: recover_root_locked, recover_nothing_to_do, recover_plan_mismatch.
- The crash matrix's "rerun after recovery" column runs exactly these actions, and each row names
  the action it applied. The matrix therefore proves the same operator path a user takes.

## Refinement round 3 (2026-09-13, verified against main 7168075)
A review of the round-2 recover design against the code found these defects; the corrections
below replace the conflicting round-2 text.
- Expected classes per slug (the round-1 slugs are kept):
  - append.body_write, append.body_sync: incomplete_tail; action --truncate-incomplete-tail ledger.
  - append.commit_write, append.commit_sync: clean with the batch committed (the caller saw
    AppendIndeterminate); action none; the rerun returns the committed anchor.
  - append.reconcile_read, _truncate, _sync, _seek: not_applicable, reason "no injection hook in
    fss-ledger" (AppendPhase has 8 variants; only four are injectable, journal.rs:254-272).
  - publish.after_children_verified, publish.after_manifest_body: unreferenced objects; action: rerun
    the producing command, which re-stages them as AlreadyPresent and publishes them, so they become
    reachable (no discard API exists for verified or held objects);
    publish.after_root_temp_write: an orphaned root temp (--discard-orphaned-temps);
    publish.after_root_rename and ledger.after_root_durable: a pending root (the slot is
    PendingLedger).
  - effect.lost_ack: indeterminate; --reconcile-effects.
  - effect.after_commit_before_dispatch (new row): Committed with no provider record (built by driving
    the journal steps without dispatching); --reconcile-effects.
  - cancel.<stage> rows before any write: recover_nothing_to_do.
  The expected-class table is written from these rules before the first run; it is never copied from
  observed output.
- The simulated provider must be durable. ReferenceAlertProvider is in-memory (alert.rs:173-178), so
  a separate `fss-lab recover` process would start empty and reconcile nothing. Add a lab-only durable
  record of the simulated provider's messages and failures under <root>/effects/ (an fss_ledger
  Journal of canonical records, appended and synced before dispatch returns, LostAck included),
  loaded on open and labelled simulated in every report. --reconcile-effects reads only that record
  and never touches a real provider.
- Effect reconciliation API (replaces the round-2 wording): reconcile_verified requires state
  Observed (fss-core effect.rs:2410), so an Indeterminate operation with a provider delivery record
  goes Indeterminate -> Observed -> reconcile_verified, exactly as reconcile_alert does
  (durable_effect.rs:716-740). A provider failure record uses reconcile_failed. No provider record:
  the operation stays Indeterminate. A Committed operation with no provider record becomes
  Indeterminate with reason restart_reconciliation_pending_observation; dispatch is never retried
  (owner decision).
- Actions and synopsis: `fss-lab recover --root <dir> [--truncate-incomplete-tail ledger|effects]
  [--plan-ledger-repair | --plan-effects-repair] [--apply-ledger-repair <digest> |
  --apply-effects-repair <digest>] [--discard-orphaned-temps] [--discard-orphaned-staging]
  [--reconcile-effects] [--json]`.
  - Every mutating action holds <root>/objects/LOCK (through LocalRootPublisher::open) for its whole
    duration; fss_ledger repair apply's own flock is on the journal file only (repair.rs:805), which
    writers never lock. A held lock gives recover_root_locked.
  - --plan-*-repair is read-only: a bounded read, fss_ledger::doctor and plan through the
    fss-2h5zq.66 path; no lock, no publisher open. Plan digests bind the canonical absolute path, dev
    and inode (repair.rs:388-411), so a plan is valid only for that file.
  - --apply-*-repair opens only its target journal, never through DurableReferenceLedger::open or
    DurableEffectJournal::open (both refuse foreign bytes). It refuses with recover_corrupt_history
    when the foreign range contains a structurally valid record header, because
    fss_ledger::doctor reports mid-history corruption as foreign bytes (repair.rs:300-360) and
    applying it would quarantine committed history. If fss-ledger has no public header probe, add a
    pure one in repair.rs with its own tests. A rerun after a completed apply returns
    recover_nothing_to_do; a crash between the quarantine rename and the truncation is finished by
    rerunning apply, which reuses the identical sidecar.
  - --discard-orphaned-temps calls LocalRootPublisher::discard_orphaned_temps (local/mod.rs:1101).
    --discard-orphaned-staging needs a new pass-through LocalRootPublisher::discard_orphaned_staging in
    fss-publication, delegating to StagingSpool::discard_orphaned_staging (fss-object
    spool/mod.rs:668), with its own test; LocalRootPublisher exposes only spool(&self).
  - Pending roots: commit_root(slot, validity) needs a CaptureInterval that a pending root does not
    carry (ledger.rs:752). Recover does not guess one: it reports the pending root and names "rerun
    the producing command" (idempotent through deterministic ids). An explicit
    --commit-pending-root <slot> --validity is an owner decision.
  - Several named actions run in a fixed order: ledger bytes, effect bytes, a normal Reject reopen
    check, orphan discards, then effect reconciliation (which may append ledger batches, so it is
    last). A crash mid-recover is resumed by rerunning the same command; completed steps report
    nothing_to_do.
  - Registered error ids add recover_corrupt_history.
- The two journals can be byte-repaired independently: a truncation drops only uncommitted bytes and
  neither journal references the other's uncommitted records. Semantic reconciliation is not
  independent, hence the fixed order.

title: CAP- LAB crash-matrix (tests): expected-class table, idempotency after recovery, e2e with per-fault log lines
description:
## Tests (crates/fss-cli/tests/lab_crash_matrix.rs)
- Run crash-matrix into a temp root and parse the JSON. Assert that the row set equals the full
  enumerations: the test lists PublishCutPoint and AppendPhase variants from the real crates, so
  adding a variant without a matrix row fails.
- Assert the expected class per row.
- Assert zero duplicate effects after re-run.
- Assert the sub-roots exist.

## E2E (scripts/e2e/cap_lab_crash_matrix.sh)
Run the matrix and emit one log step per fault row, with expected versus observed class,
orphaned and broken counts, tail state and obligations. Keep the root on failure.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Blocked by (must finish first):
  - fss-2h5zq.15: CAP- LAB: fss-lab crash-matrix subcommand (kill at every publish cut point and journal phase, reopen, report recovery)
  - fss-2h5zq.1: CAP- e2e harness: scripts/e2e/lib.sh structured JSON-lines logging and runner
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.63: CAP- QUALIFY: whole-bridge verification on green main (rust+policy lanes, all CAP e2e scripts) and honest status/doc update

## Refinement round 1 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- Enumerate the rows with an exhaustive match over the real enums (no wildcard arm). The rows
  include LedgerCutPoint and all six AppendPhase variants.
- Assert the slug names and the rerun-after-recovery column.
- Print CAPLOG lines per row; the e2e script runs through e2e_cargo_test.

## Refinement round 2 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- For each crash-matrix slug:
  - the pre-recovery state is attention-worthy;
  - the named recover action succeeds;
  - a normal ReferenceDeployment reopen then succeeds;
  - rerunning the scenario duplicates neither an effect nor a batch.
- Error cases: an --apply-ledger-repair digest that does not match gives recover_plan_mismatch;
  recover on a clean root gives recover_nothing_to_do; recover on a locked root gives
  recover_root_locked.
- The e2e script logs one recover step per slug.

## Refinement round 3 (2026-09-13, verified against main 7168075)
- Assert each slug's expected class from the round-3 table of fss-2h5zq.15; the exhaustive match
  covers all 8 AppendPhase variants and the four Reconcile* rows are asserted not_applicable with their
  reason.
- Rerun proof: the rerun skips operations already terminal (the durable simulated provider's message
  count is unchanged) and returns the original batch anchors; no new batch id appears.
- Run `fss-lab recover --reconcile-effects` as a separate process on effect.lost_ack and
  effect.after_commit_before_dispatch, then assert the resulting states (Verified from a delivery
  record; Indeterminate with restart_reconciliation_pending_observation when there is none).

title: CAP- LAB: `fss-lab ingest --input <file> --root <dir>` runs the file-ingest adapter on the real stack and prints an import report
description:
## What and why
This is the user-facing command for file-ingest-first: the first time any FSS binary accepts a
real file of media. It lives in the laboratory binary on purpose. Adding a product `fss import`
operation would require an operation-crosswalk registry row (AOP rows, crates/fss-cli/src/
crosswalk.rs); that is a separate decision. See notes for a follow-up.

## Build
`fss-lab ingest --input <path> --root <dir> [--format auto|annexb|mjpeg|jpeg|rtpdump]
[--assumed-fps <n>] [--capture-start-ns <t> --capture-uncertainty-ns <u>] [--json]`
- It calls the INGEST FileIngestAdapter (INGEST3) with explicit I/O authority (ReplayCx), a
  ReferenceDeployment at --root, and the acquisition lifecycle (INGEST4).
- It prints `fss.lab.ingest_report.v1`, which contains:
  - input_sha256 and bytes; the detected format and the detector evidence (magic bytes);
  - segment counts (access units or JPEG frames);
  - capsules[] (id, sequence, span, source_digest, capture interval, clock_basis);
  - the publication_root and ledger_sequence/anchor;
  - acquisition: the state history and terminal state;
  - continuity: "not_applicable_file" for annexb/mjpeg, or the ContinuityWitness / degradation
    summary for rtpdump;
  - knowledge: {absence: "not_certifiable_no_live_continuity"}.
- rtpdump support is enabled once INGEST5 and INGEST6 land. Until then `--format rtpdump` returns
  a typed `unsupported_until_packet_admitted` error that cites fss-1bd1l/fss-kr9n3. It must not
  panic or silently fall back.
- Assumptions (assumed fps, capture start) are recorded in the report as operator-supplied
  assumptions, never as measured facts.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Blocked by (must finish first):
  - fss-2h5zq.11: CAP- LAB: port the six fss-lab scenarios onto ReferenceDeployment (real crates) with an explicit --root and report schema v2
  - fss-2h5zq.23: CAP- INGEST: FileIngestAdapter (ADP-FILE-001 reference slice): file -> SensorCapsules with source custody -> root-last publication -> ledger batch
  - fss-2h5zq.25: CAP- INGEST: drive AcquisitionSession through a file session (request -> auth(None) -> ack -> first frame -> explicit no-continuity or continuity -> quiescence)
- Related existing beads (context only, not blocking; this bead does not close them): fss-x4a.30.89.2
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.18: CAP- LAB ingest command (tests): CLI integration per format, determinism, degraded paths, e2e ingest script
  - fss-2h5zq.36: CAP- RTSP: `fss-lab ingest --rtsp-transcript <file>` routes recorded sessions through capsules, continuity and the ledger
  - fss-2h5zq.43: CAP- DECODE: `fss-lab decode --input <mjpeg|jpeg> --root <dir>` ingests, decodes and prints per-frame tensor digests
  - fss-2h5zq.61: CAP- CAPSTONE: `fss-lab pipeline --input <file> --root <dir>`: file -> capsules -> decode -> executor -> policy -> event -> prepared alert -> receipt -> situation -> handoff

## Refinement round 1 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- CLI additions:
  - `--max-bytes <n>`, the limit knob that fss-2h5zq.18 tests;
  - `--sensor-id <id>`, default `file-import`;
  - a stream id derived deterministically from the import identity.
  Both ids are printed in the report. A --root that holds a deployment of a different site lineage
  is refused.
- Re-import semantics, decided in fss-2h5zq.23: importing the same identity into the same root
  returns the existing import-manifest root with `"import":"idempotent_existing"` and appends no
  batch.
- `acquisition.history` uses the real AcquisitionStateKind names: Requested, Authenticated,
  AdapterAccepted, FirstFrameObserved, Degraded, Cancelled (see fss-2h5zq.25).

## Refinement round 2 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- The acceptance item that referred to DOCTOR was conditional on a bead this one does not depend on.
  It is now a cross-check owned by fss-2h5zq.62, not a close condition here.
- Large inputs follow fss-2h5zq.23: chunked custody, and capsule batches plus a final manifest
  batch. The report adds custody.chunks and batches.count.

## Refinement round 3 (2026-09-13, verified against main 7168075)
- Report: import is new | resumed | idempotent_existing; batches is {count, ids};
  custody.chunks is {chunk_bytes, count, unique_count}.
- Only --max-bytes (and the spool's max_total_bytes) are checked before the read. The exact spool
  capacity refusal happens after hashing and before staging, and names the spool limit.
- Add a bounded `--chunk-bytes <n>` knob (at least 4 KiB, at most the spool's max_object_bytes,
  default 16 MiB). It is part of the import identity, so fss-2h5zq.18 can exercise multi-chunk
  imports with small fixtures.
- The "doctor reports healthy" cross-check owned by fss-2h5zq.62 relies on fss-2h5zq.23's
  reachability rule (no unreferenced objects after a complete import).

title: CAP- LAB ingest command (tests): CLI integration per format, determinism, degraded paths, e2e ingest script
description:
## Tests (crates/fss-cli/tests/lab_ingest_cli.rs)
- For every clean fixture in tests/fixtures/media/{h264,mjpeg,jpeg}: ingest, then assert the
  report against fixture_manifest.json expectations, including the counts and the span sums
  covering exactly the input bytes minus declared garbage.
- Reopen the root and cross-check that the ledger and publication state match the report.
- Degraded fixtures give typed findings and the expected exit code.
- An oversize input (a --max-bytes test knob, or a generated file above the limit) gives a typed
  limit error before any allocation.
- `--format rtpdump` before INGEST5 gives the typed unsupported error; after it, the real path.

## E2E (scripts/e2e/cap_lab_ingest.sh)
One step per fixture: command, exit code, format, capsule count versus manifest, publication
root, and a determinism rerun. Log the on-disk object count per root.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Blocked by (must finish first):
  - fss-2h5zq.17: CAP- LAB: `fss-lab ingest --input <file> --root <dir>` runs the file-ingest adapter on the real stack and prints an import report
  - fss-2h5zq.1: CAP- e2e harness: scripts/e2e/lib.sh structured JSON-lines logging and runner
  - fss-2h5zq.3: CAP- fixtures: deterministic synthetic H.264 Annex-B and rtpdump (RTP/RFC 6184) fixture generator
  - fss-2h5zq.5: CAP- fixtures: first-party deterministic baseline JPEG and MJPEG fixture encoder
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.63: CAP- QUALIFY: whole-bridge verification on green main (rust+policy lanes, all CAP e2e scripts) and honest status/doc update

## Refinement round 1 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- Test --max-bytes, idempotent_existing, the sensor-id default, and the refusal of a foreign site
  lineage.
- Assert the acquisition history uses the real state-kind names.

## Refinement round 3 (2026-09-13, verified against main 7168075)
- Multi-chunk through the CLI: `--chunk-bytes 4096` on a clean fixture gives custody.chunks.count > 1,
  the same capsule digests as the default chunk size, and a different import identity.
- Out-of-range --chunk-bytes (below 4 KiB or above the spool object limit) gives a typed usage
  error.
- A re-run into the same root prints idempotent_existing; after a simulated crash between batches, a

title: CAP- INGEST: bounded H.264 Annex-B elementary-stream splitter with exact source spans and access-unit grouping
description:
## What and why
A recorded .h264/.264 file is an Annex-B byte stream: start codes 0x000001 or 0x00000001, NAL
units, and emulation-prevention bytes. fss-packet reconstructs NALs only from RTP. Its NalUnit
has a private constructor ("reconstructed NAL bytes without an invented Annex-B start code"), and
it has no Annex-B scanner. We may not edit fss-packet, so the splitter lives in fss-reference.
The owner bead "CAP- OWNER fss-packet Annex-B/NalUnit unification" records the option to move it
later.

## Build
`crates/fss-reference/src/ingest/annexb.rs`:
- `split_annexb(bytes: &[u8], limits: AnnexBLimits, cx: &ReplayCx) -> Result<AnnexBScan,
  AnnexBError>`.
- Scan for 3-byte and 4-byte start codes. Trailing zero bytes before a start code
  (trailing_zero_8bits) belong to no NAL and are recorded as inter-NAL padding spans.
- Per NAL: span {offset, len} into the ORIGINAL bytes. Emulation-prevention bytes are kept
  because custody covers exact bytes. Also record forbidden_zero_bit (must be 0, otherwise a typed
  error), nal_ref_idc and nal_unit_type.
- Access-unit grouping per H.264 7.4.1.2.3. A new AU starts at an AUD (type 9), at SPS/PPS/SEI
  after a VCL NAL, or at a VCL NAL whose first_mb_in_slice == 0. first_mb_in_slice is decoded
  with a bounded ue(v) Exp-Golomb reader over an RBSP view that removes emulation-prevention bytes
  into a small scratch buffer, never allocating per NAL beyond the limit.
- Per AU: span, NAL indices, is_idr (type 5 present), has_sps, has_pps, slice_count.
- Limits (checked arithmetic, before any allocation): max_input_bytes (default 512 MiB), max_nal_bytes
  (default 16 MiB, matching fss-packet's H264Limits range), max_nals, max_aus.
- Cancellation checkpoint every 1 MiB scanned.
- Errors are typed and stable: EmptyInput, NoStartCode, ForbiddenBitSet{nal}, NalTooLarge,
  TooManyNals, TruncatedNal, LeadingGarbage{len}. LeadingGarbage is recorded as an omission span,
  not fatal, if under a small limit. There is no panic path; add a fuzz-ish property test in the
  companion bead.
- Output also lists SPS/PPS raw spans for later SDP cross-check (RTSP) and decode (future
  FSS-124).

## Considerations
- It must not claim decodability: an AU with slices but no preceding SPS/PPS is "undecodable
  without parameter sets", a typed flag, not an error.
- Never allocate the whole file twice; the adapter owns the single read buffer.
- Registration: module_declarations `crates/fss-reference/src/ingest/annexb.rs` -> "support"
  (parser helper). The ingest/mod.rs file needs a module_declarations entry too. MANIFEST.delta
  rows.

## Related
fss-x4a.12.12 (FSS-113, the bounded H.264 AU/SPS/PPS parser) is the eventual production owner of
full SPS/PPS parsing. This bead only parses what grouping needs. fss-x4a.30.89.2 (ADP-FILE-001).

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Related existing beads (context only, not blocking; this bead does not close them): fss-x4a.12.12, fss-x4a.30.89.2
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.20: CAP- INGEST Annex-B splitter (tests): manifest equality, malformed corpus, property/no-panic, e2e
  - fss-2h5zq.23: CAP- INGEST: FileIngestAdapter (ADP-FILE-001 reference slice): file -> SensorCapsules with source custody -> root-last publication -> ledger batch
  - fss-2h5zq.64: CAP- OWNER (needs owner, do not assign): fss-packet Annex-B byte-stream splitter and a public NalUnit-from-bytes constructor, to unify file and RTP NAL paths

## Refinement round 1 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- fss-packet's H264Limits::default() uses max_nal_bytes 8 MiB with a 16 MiB ceiling. Use the same
  default (8 MiB) and ceiling here, so the file and RTP paths agree.
- Acceptance is split to keep this bead ready while fixtures land. This bead is proven on hand-built
  byte vectors in its own unit tests:
  - 3-byte and 4-byte start codes;
  - AUD and no-AUD streams;
  - emulation prevention and trailing_zero_8bits;
  - a two-slice AU, and SPS/PPS/SEI boundaries.
  Equality with every FIXH264 manifest is proven by fss-2h5zq.20, which depends on the fixture
  generator.
- Cancellation: ReplayCx::checkpoint calls drain_and_finalize and returns
  ReplayAdapterError::CancellationRequested. Map it to a typed AnnexBError::Cancelled, and assert
  cx.is_drain_completed().
