title: CAP- e2e harness (tests): self-test script proving logging, expectations, redaction and caps
description:
## What
Prove the harness itself before 25 other beads rely on it.

## Build
`scripts/e2e/selftest.sh` sources lib.sh and runs the following. It uses `FSS_E2E_LOG_DIR` set
to a temp dir so it never pollutes target/.
1. A passing step (`true`) and a failing expectation. The failing case runs in a subshell, and
   the test checks that the summary verdict is fail and the exit code is 1.
2. JSON-field expectation over a canned JSON document.
3. A redaction case: a command that prints `Authorization: Basic abc` must not appear in the log.
   Assert this by grepping the log file.
4. An excerpt cap case: a command printing 1 MiB yields an excerpt of 4 KiB or less and the
   correct full-stdout sha256.
5. A missing-binary case: `e2e_bin nonexistent` fails with the documented message.
6. Determinism: two runs produce identical logs, modulo the ts field, which the test strips before
   comparing.

The script writes its own detailed log (all of the above) and ends with a summary line.
Optionally add `tests/test_e2e_lib.py`, a Python unittest that invokes selftest.sh and parses the
JSON lines, so the policy lane's Python test discovery covers the harness.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Blocked by (must finish first):
  - fss-2h5zq.1: CAP- e2e harness: scripts/e2e/lib.sh structured JSON-lines logging and runner
  - fss-2h5zq.1: CAP- e2e harness: scripts/e2e/lib.sh structured JSON-lines logging and runner
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.63: CAP- QUALIFY: whole-bridge verification on green main (rust+policy lanes, all CAP e2e scripts) and honest status/doc update

## Refinement round 1 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
The self-test adds these cases. Stub rch and cargo with PATH shims in the temp dir (the shims print
canned output and exit codes), so the self-test needs no build.
7. CAPLOG ingestion from canned stdout that contains ANSI colour codes, a malformed CAPLOG line
   (fails closed) and a non-CAPLOG line (ignored).
8. validate_log.py accepts the self-test's own logs and rejects each planted bad record: a missing
   verdict, an excerpt over 4 KiB, a key named authorization, and a non-JSON line.
9. The 10 MiB cap: a run that would exceed it ends with a fail summary that names the cap.
10. e2e_tmpdir is removed on success and kept, with its path logged, on failure.
11. Determinism that ignores ts and duration_ms.
12. `--only` and `--list`.

tests/test_e2e_lib.py is now required, not optional, so the policy lane's Python discovery runs the
harness self-test on every wave. The dependency map above lists fss-2h5zq.1 twice; that is
cosmetic.

## Shared rules for every CAP- bead (repeated so this bead stands alone)

Context: parent epic "CAP- Capability bridge: file-ingest-first end-to-end" (fss-2h5zq), created
2026-09-13 from the Phase-1 reality check at main 474931d and the owner's binding steering
decisions. The epic holds the full background; the essentials are repeated here.

- Constitution (AGENTS.md): Rust 2024 on nightly-2026-08-31. `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` in every
  crate, target, test, example and helper, with no exception path. Zero third-party crates: the
  dependency closure is fss-* only, and DEP-EXCEPTION-001 admits nothing. This bridge also adds
  ZERO new workspace crates. New code lands as modules in existing crates, mainly fss-reference and
  fss-cli. Moving the code into the planned L3/L4 crates (fss-codec-mjpeg, fss-container,
  fss-device-core, fss-model-runtime, fss-kernel-cpu, fss-coverage) is a later owner decision,
  because a new member trips the crate_topology and member-count pins (see fss-1bd1l).
- Do NOT edit crates/fss-packet/** (the owner's crate). Use its public API as-is:
  RtpPacket::parse, SequenceTracker, H264Depacketizer, NalUnit, SenderReportClock and
  JitterEstimator. Any change that needs fss-packet edits goes to an owner bead and is never
  assigned to an agent.
- No device I/O: no camera, USB, V4L2 or socket code; no `std::net` or `TcpStream`. Inputs are
  recorded files and recorded transcripts only. Every file read goes through an explicit I/O
  authority value, following the ReplayIoAuthority/ReplayCx pattern in
  crates/fss-reference/src/adapter_replay.rs, with cooperative cancellation checkpoints
  (request -> drain -> finalize). Asupersync `Cx` is NOT admitted yet (owner decision
  fss-x4a.8.1). Do not add Tokio or any other runtime.
- Security boundary: fixtures are synthetic and generated first-party. No third-party footage, no
  identifiable people, no captured network addresses. Never handle credentials: RTSP auth headers
  are detected and refused, never computed or stored. No scanning. Logs never contain secrets or
  private media bytes; they carry digests and byte spans only.
- Truth discipline:
  - A decoded frame is not retained evidence without source custody.
  - File import has no live continuity, so it never certifies absence. Negative reads stay
    unknown or not_observable.
  - File mtime is not capture time. Use ClockBasis::Estimated with an explicit, wide
    CaptureInterval unless the stream itself carries timing.
  - One camera's model score is never "corroborated".
  - unknown, not_observable, stale and indeterminate are never flattened to null, low confidence
    or omission.
- Registration, done in the same commit as the code:
  1. Every new .rs module under crates/fss-core or crates/fss-reference gets a
     `module_declarations` entry in architecture/semantic_plane_registry.json with its plane
     (authority | cognition | effect | support | ambiguous).
     scripts/semantic_plane_checker.py audits exactly those two crates and fails otherwise.
  2. Every new canonical digest or encoding domain tag gets a row in registries/DIGEST_DOMAINS.md
     (ID SCHEMA-DOMAIN-<NAME>-001, domain fss.<name>.v1, scope, authority, invariant rule).
     Bump ALL THREE pinned domain counts in the same commit: the two digestDomainCount
     assertions in tests/test_schema_validate.py AND the domain_count assertion (and its
     message) in crates/fss-model-ir/tests/model_ir_contract.rs:420 (45 at main 7168075;
     verified in refinement round 3). Count from the value on HEAD at commit time, because several CAP
     beads add domains in parallel.
  3. Every new or changed source path gets a row in MANIFEST.delta.sha256 per ADR-0013. Never
     edit the MANIFEST.sha256 base. Check with `python3 scripts/manifest_audit.py`.
  4. New crate dependency edges must point downward in architecture/crate_topology.json. Layers:
     L2 ledger/object/publication, L3 fss-packet, L4 tensor/model-ir/geometry, L6 fss-cli,
     L7 fss-reference. fss-cli -> fss-reference is the one waived inversion. Check with
     `python3 scripts/dependency_dag_checker.py`.
  5. New CLI error and exit identities get rows in registries/ERRORS.md, and the operation
     crosswalk (architecture/operation_crosswalk.json and crates/fss-cli/src/crosswalk.rs) stays
     consistent.
- Verification (remote only):
  - `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- cargo test -p <crate> --all-targets --no-fail-fast --locked --offline`
  - `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets --keep-going --locked --offline -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo fmt --check`
  - `scripts/qualify.sh --lane policy`
  - `--all-targets` does NOT run doctests. When the crate has doc examples, also run
    `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- cargo test -p <crate> --doc --no-fail-fast --locked --offline`.
  - Launch rch from the repo directory with `--base <sha>`. Decide pass or fail by exit code (rch
    output is ANSI-coloured; strip ANSI before counting diagnostics). Re-run Python checkers and
    e2e scripts on a fresh `git worktree add --detach` checkout, never only in the shared tree.

  Main is currently red for reasons outside this bead (fss-kr9n3, fss-1bd1l, fss-lc2r1). Until
  those land, report "no new findings attributable to this bead's files". Never weaken a gate.
- E2E convention: every test bead ships scripts/e2e/cap_<name>.sh using the shared helpers in
  scripts/e2e/lib.sh (see the "CAP- e2e harness" bead).
  - Logs are JSON lines under ${FSS_E2E_LOG_DIR:-target/e2e-logs}/<name>/. The first record is an
    env record (git sha, bead id, binary sha256s, host triple, FSS_* settings); then one record per
    step: {ts, script, bead, step, cmd, exit, duration_ms, expected, observed, digest,
    stdout_sha256, stdout_excerpt, stderr_excerpt, verdict, repro}. Rust tests feed the log by
    printing one-line `CAPLOG {json}` records under --nocapture; lib.sh ingests them (ANSI
    stripped) through e2e_cargo_test. scripts/e2e/validate_log.py checks every record.
  - The final record is {"step":"summary","verdict":"pass"|"fail","steps":N,"failures":[...]}.
  - Scripts exit non-zero on any mismatch. They are deterministic (fixed seeds, no wall clock
    inside digests) and bounded in size, and they print a one-line reproduction command.
- Known gotchas (verified at main 8b96911, refinement round 1):
  - scripts/dependency_audit.py (DEP-AUD-022) scans every .rs file, tests and examples included,
    for the bare word unsafe. Comments are masked but string literals are NOT, so never put that
    word in a string literal or a guard-test pattern. The only allowed occurrence is
    #![forbid(unsafe_code)].
  - The workspace has 11 members since the twin merge (f9004ef, f5ed038). fss-twin (L4,
    "implemented") depends on fss-geometry. Treat crates/fss-twin/** and crates/fss-geometry/**
    as owner-authored upstream code, like fss-packet: use their public API and record API gaps in
    notes instead of editing them.
  - Shared hot files (edit only your own rows or lines; stage with `git add -p`):
    registries/DIGEST_DOMAINS.md, tests/test_schema_validate.py,
    crates/fss-model-ir/tests/model_ir_contract.rs (the third domain-count pin),
    architecture/semantic_plane_registry.json, MANIFEST.delta.sha256, registries/ERRORS.md,
    crates/fss-reference/src/lib.rs, crates/fss-reference/Cargo.toml and
    crates/fss-cli/src/lab_cmd.rs.
  - LocalRootPublisher::open and StagingSpool::open create directories and take exclusive lock
    files, so they are not read-only. Read-only inspection goes through fss-2h5zq.66.
- Swarm hygiene:
  - One bead per commit, with the bead id in the subject.
  - Commit only files you own. Never `git add -A`. Never reset, amend or rebase main.
  - Commit only what compiles against committed HEAD, and commit type changes together with all
    their users.
  - Record final paths and evidence with `br update <id> --append-notes`. Never use --notes,
    which overwrites the field.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `bash scripts/e2e/selftest.sh; echo $?` prints 0, and the final log line has "verdict":"pass"
- [ ] The negative cases (failing expectation, missing binary) are proven to fail closed
- [ ] The log contains no 'Authorization' text; the excerpt is 4 KiB or less for 1 MiB of output
- [ ] Two runs give identical logs after stripping ts
- [ ] tests/test_e2e_lib.py runs selftest.sh (with rch/cargo PATH shims) and the validate_log.py cases and passes under the policy lane's Python discovery

title: CAP- INGEST: bounded MJPEG/JPEG frame splitter (marker-aware SOI..EOI, stuffing and RST handling) with exact spans
description:
## What and why
MJPEG recordings are concatenated JPEG images. A naive search for FFD9 breaks on stuffed data and
on APPn payloads, so the splitter must walk markers. This is the ingest half. Pixel decode is
DECODE1 (P2); here we only find frames with custody spans so capsules can be built without
decoding.

## Build
`crates/fss-reference/src/ingest/mjpeg.rs`: `split_jpeg_stream(bytes, limits, cx) ->
Result<JpegScan, JpegSplitError>`.
- At SOI, walk the marker segments: for every marker with a length, read the u16 length and skip,
  with bounds checks; SOFn records width, height, components and process (baseline, progressive,
  other) without decoding.
- At SOS, skip the entropy-coded segment, treating FF00 as stuffing, FFD0-FFD7 as RST, and any
  other FFxx as the end of the segment. Continue until EOI.
- Per frame: span, sof info, restart interval, has_eoi.
- Bytes between frames are recorded as omission spans (garbage_between_frames).
- A final frame without EOI is recorded as a truncated frame span with a typed finding. Its bytes
  are still custody, but it is flagged undecodable.
- Limits: max_input_bytes, max_frame_bytes, max_frames, max_marker_segments_per_frame,
  max_dimension (reject width or height > 16384 at the SOF read, before any decode allocation).
- A single .jpg is a stream of one frame.
- Typed errors: NoSoi, MarkerLengthOverflow, TooManyFrames, FrameTooLarge, DimensionLimit, and so
  on. Unsupported processes (progressive SOF2, arithmetic SOF9 and friends, 12-bit) are NOT
  errors at split time: they are recorded, and the decoder refuses them later with a typed
  Unsupported.

## Registration
module_declarations for ingest/mjpeg.rs -> "support"; MANIFEST.delta rows.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.22: CAP- INGEST MJPEG splitter (tests): manifest equality, stuffing/RST edge cases, mutation no-panic, e2e
  - fss-2h5zq.23: CAP- INGEST: FileIngestAdapter (ADP-FILE-001 reference slice): file -> SensorCapsules with source custody -> root-last publication -> ledger batch

## Refinement round 1 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
Acceptance is split as in fss-2h5zq.19.
- This bead is proven on hand-built vectors: FF00 stuffing, RSTn, APPn and COM segments containing
  FF D9, garbage between frames, a missing EOI, zero-length segments, and a SOF with 0 components.
- Equality with every FIXJPEG manifest is proven in fss-2h5zq.22.
- Frames whose dimensions change mid-stream are legal. Each frame records its own SOF info.

## Shared rules for every CAP- bead (repeated so this bead stands alone)

Context: parent epic "CAP- Capability bridge: file-ingest-first end-to-end" (fss-2h5zq), created
2026-09-13 from the Phase-1 reality check at main 474931d and the owner's binding steering
decisions. The epic holds the full background; the essentials are repeated here.

  crate, target, test, example and helper, with no exception path. Zero third-party crates: the
  dependency closure is fss-* only, and DEP-EXCEPTION-001 admits nothing. This bridge also adds
  ZERO new workspace crates. New code lands as modules in existing crates, mainly fss-reference and
  fss-cli. Moving the code into the planned L3/L4 crates (fss-codec-mjpeg, fss-container,
  fss-device-core, fss-model-runtime, fss-kernel-cpu, fss-coverage) is a later owner decision,
  because a new member trips the crate_topology and member-count pins (see fss-1bd1l).
- Do NOT edit crates/fss-packet/** (the owner's crate). Use its public API as-is:
  RtpPacket::parse, SequenceTracker, H264Depacketizer, NalUnit, SenderReportClock and
  JitterEstimator. Any change that needs fss-packet edits goes to an owner bead and is never
  assigned to an agent.
- No device I/O: no camera, USB, V4L2 or socket code; no `std::net` or `TcpStream`. Inputs are
  recorded files and recorded transcripts only. Every file read goes through an explicit I/O
  authority value, following the ReplayIoAuthority/ReplayCx pattern in
  crates/fss-reference/src/adapter_replay.rs, with cooperative cancellation checkpoints
  (request -> drain -> finalize). Asupersync `Cx` is NOT admitted yet (owner decision
  fss-x4a.8.1). Do not add Tokio or any other runtime.
- Security boundary: fixtures are synthetic and generated first-party. No third-party footage, no
  identifiable people, no captured network addresses. Never handle credentials: RTSP auth headers
  are detected and refused, never computed or stored. No scanning. Logs never contain secrets or
  private media bytes; they carry digests and byte spans only.

    unknown or not_observable.

    or omission.

- No device I/O: no camera, USB, V4L2 or socket code; no `std::net` or `TcpStream`. Inputs are
  recorded files and recorded transcripts only. Every file read goes through an explicit I/O
  authority value, following the ReplayIoAuthority/ReplayCx pattern in
  crates/fss-reference/src/adapter_replay.rs, with cooperative cancellation checkpoints
  (request -> drain -> finalize). Asupersync `Cx` is NOT admitted yet (owner decision
  fss-x4a.8.1). Do not add Tokio or any other runtime.
- Security boundary: fixtures are synthetic and generated first-party. No third-party footage, no
  identifiable people, no captured network addresses. Never handle credentials: RTSP auth headers
  are detected and refused, never computed or stored. No scanning. Logs never contain secrets or
  private media bytes; they carry digests and byte spans only.
- Truth discipline:
  - A decoded frame is not retained evidence without source custody.
  - File import has no live continuity, so it never certifies absence. Negative reads stay
    unknown or not_observable.
  - File mtime is not capture time. Use ClockBasis::Estimated with an explicit, wide
    CaptureInterval unless the stream itself carries timing.
  - One camera's model score is never "corroborated".
  - unknown, not_observable, stale and indeterminate are never flattened to null, low confidence
    or omission.
- Registration, done in the same commit as the code:
  1. Every new .rs module under crates/fss-core or crates/fss-reference gets a
     `module_declarations` entry in architecture/semantic_plane_registry.json with its plane
     (authority | cognition | effect | support | ambiguous).
     scripts/semantic_plane_checker.py audits exactly those two crates and fails otherwise.
  2. Every new canonical digest or encoding domain tag gets a row in registries/DIGEST_DOMAINS.md
     (ID SCHEMA-DOMAIN-<NAME>-001, domain fss.<name>.v1, scope, authority, invariant rule).
     Bump ALL THREE pinned domain counts in the same commit: the two digestDomainCount
     assertions in tests/test_schema_validate.py AND the domain_count assertion (and its
     message) in crates/fss-model-ir/tests/model_ir_contract.rs:420 (45 at main 7168075;
     verified in refinement round 3). Count from the value on HEAD at commit time, because several CAP
     beads add domains in parallel.
  3. Every new or changed source path gets a row in MANIFEST.delta.sha256 per ADR-0013. Never
     edit the MANIFEST.sha256 base. Check with `python3 scripts/manifest_audit.py`.
  4. New crate dependency edges must point downward in architecture/crate_topology.json. Layers:
     L2 ledger/object/publication, L3 fss-packet, L4 tensor/model-ir/geometry, L6 fss-cli,
     L7 fss-reference. fss-cli -> fss-reference is the one waived inversion. Check with
     `python3 scripts/dependency_dag_checker.py`.
  5. New CLI error and exit identities get rows in registries/ERRORS.md, and the operation
     crosswalk (architecture/operation_crosswalk.json and crates/fss-cli/src/crosswalk.rs) stays
     consistent.
- Verification (remote only):
  - `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- cargo test -p <crate> --all-targets --no-fail-fast --locked --offline`
  - `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets --keep-going --locked --offline -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo fmt --check`
  - `scripts/qualify.sh --lane policy`
  - `--all-targets` does NOT run doctests. When the crate has doc examples, also run
    `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- cargo test -p <crate> --doc --no-fail-fast --locked --offline`.
  - Launch rch from the repo directory with `--base <sha>`. Decide pass or fail by exit code (rch
    output is ANSI-coloured; strip ANSI before counting diagnostics). Re-run Python checkers and
    e2e scripts on a fresh `git worktree add --detach` checkout, never only in the shared tree.

  Main is currently red for reasons outside this bead (fss-kr9n3, fss-1bd1l, fss-lc2r1). Until
  those land, report "no new findings attributable to this bead's files". Never weaken a gate.
- E2E convention: every test bead ships scripts/e2e/cap_<name>.sh using the shared helpers in
  scripts/e2e/lib.sh (see the "CAP- e2e harness" bead).
  - Logs are JSON lines under ${FSS_E2E_LOG_DIR:-target/e2e-logs}/<name>/. The first record is an
    env record (git sha, bead id, binary sha256s, host triple, FSS_* settings); then one record per
    step: {ts, script, bead, step, cmd, exit, duration_ms, expected, observed, digest,
    stdout_sha256, stdout_excerpt, stderr_excerpt, verdict, repro}. Rust tests feed the log by

    stripped) through e2e_cargo_test. scripts/e2e/validate_log.py checks every record.
  - The final record is {"step":"summary","verdict":"pass"|"fail","steps":N,"failures":[...]}.
  - Scripts exit non-zero on any mismatch. They are deterministic (fixed seeds, no wall clock
    inside digests) and bounded in size, and they print a one-line reproduction command.
- Known gotchas (verified at main 8b96911, refinement round 1):
  - scripts/dependency_audit.py (DEP-AUD-022) scans every .rs file, tests and examples included,
    for the bare word unsafe. Comments are masked but string literals are NOT, so never put that
    word in a string literal or a guard-test pattern. The only allowed occurrence is
    #![forbid(unsafe_code)].
  - The workspace has 11 members since the twin merge (f9004ef, f5ed038). fss-twin (L4,
    "implemented") depends on fss-geometry. Treat crates/fss-twin/** and crates/fss-geometry/**
    as owner-authored upstream code, like fss-packet: use their public API and record API gaps in
    notes instead of editing them.
  - Shared hot files (edit only your own rows or lines; stage with `git add -p`):
    registries/DIGEST_DOMAINS.md, tests/test_schema_validate.py,
    crates/fss-model-ir/tests/model_ir_contract.rs (the third domain-count pin),
    architecture/semantic_plane_registry.json, MANIFEST.delta.sha256, registries/ERRORS.md,
    crates/fss-reference/src/lib.rs, crates/fss-reference/Cargo.toml and
    crates/fss-cli/src/lab_cmd.rs.
  - LocalRootPublisher::open and StagingSpool::open create directories and take exclusive lock
    files, so they are not read-only. Read-only inspection goes through fss-2h5zq.66.
- Swarm hygiene:
  - One bead per commit, with the bead id in the subject.
  - Commit only files you own. Never `git add -A`. Never reset, amend or rebase main.
  - Commit only what compiles against committed HEAD, and commit type changes together with all
    their users.
  - Record final paths and evidence with `br update <id> --append-notes`. Never use --notes,
    which overwrites the field.

title: CAP- INGEST: FileIngestAdapter (ADP-FILE-001 reference slice): file -> SensorCapsules with source custody -> root-last publication -> ledger batch
description:
## What and why
This is top-10 gap #4, "first real bytes". ADP-FILE-001 ("bounded media import", tier T0/T4,
promotion gate GATE-010, registries/DEVICE_ADAPTERS.md) exists only as a registry row
(fss-x4a.30.89.2 "Realize registry row", not reshaped here). This bead delivers the vertical
slice: bytes from a recorded file become immutable SensorCapsules with source custody, published
root-last and anchored in the canonical EvidenceDeltaBatch ledger.

## Build
`crates/fss-reference/src/ingest/file_adapter.rs`, `FileIngestAdapter`:
- Input: `FileIngestRequest { path, format_hint, limits, sensor_id, stream_id, capture_hint:
  Option<CaptureHint{start_ns, uncertainty_ns, assumed_fps}> }`, plus `&ReplayCx`, whose
  ReplayIoAuthority is the explicit I/O capability, and `&mut ReferenceDeployment` (LAB1).
- Steps:
  1. Stat the file, then refuse non-regular files, symlinks and sizes over the limit (typed).
  2. Read bounded (a single buffer), computing sha256 as the file-custody digest.
  3. Sniff the format from the bytes: an Annex-B start code, `#!rtpplay1.0` (routed to INGEST5
     once it exists), or a JPEG SOI. A hint that conflicts with the sniff is a typed
     FormatConflict, never a silent override.
  4. Split with INGEST1 or INGEST2.
  5. For each segment (an access unit or a JPEG frame), build
     `fss_core::SensorCapsule::from_source_bytes(SensorSourceBytesSpec{ capsule_id, sensor_id,
     stream_id, sequence, capture, receive_time, clock_basis, source: segment bytes,
     frame_count: 1, gap_before })`.
  6. Stage the whole file as the root custody object, and each segment object, via
     stage_and_publish. Publish one import manifest root last, per import.
  7. Append one EvidenceDeltaBatch that carries the capsule metadata digests, the import-manifest
     root, and the acquisition transition records from INGEST4.
- The import manifest `FileImportManifest` holds input sha256, bytes, format, detector evidence,
  segment spans, omission spans, capsule ids, limits, and the adapter id/generation. It is
  canonically encoded under a NEW digest domain: register SCHEMA-DOMAIN-FILE-IMPORT-MANIFEST-001
  `fss.file_import.manifest.v1` in registries/DIGEST_DOMAINS.md and bump digestDomainCount.
- Time truth: files carry no trusted capture clock.
  - Without a capture_hint, CaptureInterval is the full "unknown" window the core type permits,
    with ClockBasis::Estimated, and the report says capture_time: unknown.
  - With a hint, the per-frame interval is [start + i/fps - u, start + i/fps + u], still
    ClockBasis::Estimated, labeled operator_assumption.
  - receive_time comes from the VirtualClock/ReplayCx, never the host wall clock.
  - Check whether CaptureInterval can express "unknown". If it cannot, record that as a finding
    and use the widest representable interval with a knowledge flag. Never fake precision.
- gap_before is true after any omission span or truncated segment.
- Coverage: file import emits NO ContinuityWitness and NO CoverageWitness that certifies absence.
  A test must prove that an absence query over an imported interval returns not certifiable.
  Also look at open bug fss-3qlsa (first matching witness wins); do not rely on its behaviour.

## Adapter identity
Use fss_core AdapterIdentity / AdapterKind for ADP-FILE-001 with a generation string. If
architecture/device_adapters.json needs a status change from "specified", that is a registry
edit. Do it only if scripts/device_adapter_checker.py requires it, and never mark it beyond
"reference implemented, not qualified".

## Registration
module_declarations: ingest/file_adapter.rs -> "authority" (it produces capsules and ledger
batches). The new digest domain row plus the count pin. MANIFEST.delta rows.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Blocked by (must finish first):
  - fss-2h5zq.19: CAP- INGEST: bounded H.264 Annex-B elementary-stream splitter with exact source spans and access-unit grouping
  - fss-2h5zq.21: CAP- INGEST: bounded MJPEG/JPEG frame splitter (marker-aware SOI..EOI, stuffing and RST handling) with exact spans
  - fss-2h5zq.9: CAP- LAB: ReferenceDeployment composition in fss-reference (spool + root-last publication + durable ledger + effects + situation)
- Related existing beads (context only, not blocking; this bead does not close them): fss-x4a.30.89.2, fss-x4a.30.89.1, fss-3qlsa
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.17: CAP- LAB: `fss-lab ingest --input <file> --root <dir>` runs the file-ingest adapter on the real stack and prints an import report
  - fss-2h5zq.24: CAP- INGEST FileIngestAdapter (tests): custody digests, time-truth labels, no-absence proof, crash/cancel mid-import, e2e
  - fss-2h5zq.25: CAP- INGEST: drive AcquisitionSession through a file session (request -> auth(None) -> ack -> first frame -> explicit no-continuity or continuity -> quiescence)
  - fss-2h5zq.27: CAP- INGEST: rtpdump recorded-RTP reader feeding fss-packet (RtpPacket::parse -> SequenceTracker -> H264Depacketizer) into capsules
  - fss-2h5zq.31: CAP- INGEST gauntlet (tests): malformed-media, limit, crash and cancel campaign across Annex-B, MJPEG, file adapter and lifecycle
  - fss-2h5zq.41: CAP- DECODE: decode receipt and source-to-tensor lineage (capsule source digest -> decoder generation -> tensor digest) published beside the capsule
  - fss-2h5zq.59: CAP- STATUS: `fss status --json --root <dir>` reports sensors, streams, capsules, events and obligations from the real ledger (never implying unsupported readiness)

## Refinement round 1 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- Adapter identity: fss_core::AdapterKind::FileArchive (identity.rs:309), with AdapterIdentity, for
  ADP-FILE-001. architecture/device_adapters.json lists ADP-FILE-001 with currentState
  "specified". Leave it unless scripts/device_adapter_checker.py requires a change, and never mark
  it beyond "reference implemented, not qualified".
- Capture time: TimestampNs is an i128, and CaptureInterval::new(earliest, latest) only requires
  earliest <= latest. So "unknown" can be represented as an explicit maximal window. Still carry an
  explicit knowledge label (capture_time: unknown) in the manifest and report, because a wide
  interval alone is not a label.
- Import identity and idempotency (decided here, tested in fss-2h5zq.31):
  - import identity = digest(input sha256, detected format, limits digest, adapter generation,
    sensor id, stream id);
  - a second import with the same identity into the same root returns the existing import-manifest
    root as `idempotent_existing` and appends no batch;
  - the same bytes under a different file name have the same identity.
- Storage: do not store every byte twice.
  - Default: stage the whole file once as the custody object. Record each segment in the import
    manifest as (file object digest, span, segment sha256).
  - Decode and status fetch the span and verify sha256(span) == capsule.source_digest before using
    it.
  - Stage per-segment objects only if the publication limits or the object model require it. Record
    the decision and its storage cost in notes.
- Ledger batch content, with every payload staged as a batch child (see the family table of
  fss-2h5zq.9):
  - "sensor_capsule", one per capsule; the payload is the capsule's canonical bytes;
  - "file_import_manifest"; the payload is the manifest;
  - "acquisition_transition", from fss-2h5zq.25.
  Publication goes through ReferenceDeployment's LedgeredRootPublisher wrapper, so the root and the
  batch are linked by the existing reconcile() machinery.
- Deterministic ids: capsule_id, sensor_id and stream_id are derived from the import identity and
  the segment index, so fresh roots give identical digests.

## Refinement round 2 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- Verified capacity facts:
  - one spool object is at most 64 MiB (fss_object::MAX_OBJECT_BYTES, lib.rs:40);
  - the spool's default max_total_bytes is 512 MiB;
  - a manifest holds at most 16,384 children;
  - a ledger batch holds at most 16,384 deltas and 16,384 children;
  - a journal record payload is at most 16 MiB.
  The round-1 plan, "stage the whole file once", fails for any file over 64 MiB, and one batch per
  import fails beyond 16,384 capsules.
- Chunked custody:
  - The file is staged as consecutive chunk objects of a fixed size: default 16 MiB, never above
    MAX_OBJECT_BYTES, and at least max_nal_bytes and max_frame_bytes, so a segment crosses at most
    one chunk boundary.
  - The import manifest records the whole-file sha256 and the ordered chunk digests. A segment is
    (first chunk index, offset, len, segment sha256).
  - Readers reassemble the span from one or two chunks, and verify sha256(span) ==
    capsule.source_digest before any use.
  - A file smaller than one chunk is a single object, exactly the round-1 design.
  - The chunk size is recorded in the manifest and in the import identity.
- Batching:
  - If one import's deltas or children would exceed 16,384, or the encoded batch would exceed
    MAX_RECORD_PAYLOAD_BYTES, write K capsule batches (sensor_capsule and acquisition_transition
    deltas) followed by ONE final batch that holds the file_import_manifest delta.
  - An import is complete only when its manifest batch exists. Capsule batches without it are an
    incomplete import. Doctor and status report it (fss-2h5zq.57, .59); it is never hidden.
  - Re-importing completes it idempotently: the deterministic ids append no duplicate delta.
- Capacity is checked before reading: file size plus the spool's occupied_bytes against
  max_total_bytes gives a typed refusal that names the limit.

## Refinement round 3 (2026-09-13, verified against main 7168075)
A review of the round-2 chunking and batching design against fss-object, fss-publication and
fss-ledger found steps the code does not support. These rules replace the conflicting round-1 and
round-2 text.
- Read (replaces step 2): read the file once into one bounded buffer of at most min(--max-bytes, the
  splitter's max_input_bytes) while hashing with fss_core::Sha256Hasher. Chunk objects are slices of
  that buffer; nothing is read twice.
- Chunks: fixed size C, at most limits.spool.max_object_bytes (which may be configured below
  MAX_OBJECT_BYTES). There is no chunk type: the custody object is an ObjectManifest whose children
  are the DEDUPLICATED chunk digests, because ObjectManifest::new rejects duplicate children and sorts
  them (manifest.rs:41-56). FileImportManifest keeps the ordered chunk list, repeats included.
  Identical chunks dedupe in the spool (StageOutcome::AlreadyPresent).
- Segments: a segment is (file_offset, len, segment_sha256). A reader fetches chunks floor(offset/C)
  through floor((offset+len-1)/C), which may be any number of chunks, and verifies
  sha256(span) == capsule.source_digest. The round-2 claim "a segment crosses at most one chunk
  boundary" is dropped: an H.264 capsule is a whole access unit and the splitter has no AU byte limit.
- Commits (replaces "append one EvidenceDeltaBatch"): every import commits at least two batches,
  because LedgeredRootPublisher's batch is fixed to one local_root_reachability delta whose children
  are the root's whole closure (ledger.rs:9-24; commit_prepared :794-808). Order:
  1. stage and verify every object (chunks, capsule payloads, transition payloads, manifests);
  2. capsule batch(es) through AuthorityPublisher::prepare_batch/append; the first also creates the
     import object (family "file_import", generation 1 = in_progress);
  3. publish_and_commit(import slot);
  4. a final batch that moves the import object to generation 2 (complete; payload =
     FileImportManifest) and carries the file_import_manifest delta, with the import root among its
     children.
  Complete means: the import object is at generation 2 and the import slot is RootLedgerState::Ledgered
  with the expected root. Readers (status, decode, situation, capstone) use only capsules of complete
  imports; this predicate comes from ledger state alone.
- Deterministic partition and resume: batch ids are batch:file-import:<identity hex>:c<k> and
  batch:file-import:<identity hex>:manifest (at most 128 bytes). The deltas-per-batch bound and the
  chunk size are part of the import identity (through the limits digest), so a resumed import
  reproduces the same partition. For each planned batch, look it up in
  DurableReferenceLedger::batches() by id: identical deltas and children -> skip; different ->
  typed ImportPlanConflict; absent -> prepare at the current head. Never re-prepare a committed delta
  (GenerationConflict, evidence.rs:715-729; DuplicateBatchId; BatchIdConflict). The root reuses
  publish_and_commit's AlreadyLedgered. After a reopen, staged objects are Staged again, so a resume
  re-verifies them before any prepare or publish.
- Split a batch at the first of: 16,384 deltas, 16,384 children, or encode_batch(..).len() >
  MAX_RECORD_PAYLOAD_BYTES. Bound delta ids at 128 bytes.
- Reachability: every object the import stages is reachable from a durable ledgered root, otherwise
  LocalRecoveryReport.unreferenced_objects is non-empty and doctor is never clean
  (local/mod.rs:504, :514-520). One root's closure is at most min(max_children, 16,384) objects.
  Above that, publish part slots fi-<id>-p<k>, one per capsule batch, that are NOT children of the

  because a new member trips the crate_topology and member-count pins (see fss-1bd1l).

  assigned to an agent.

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Ingesting each clean FIXH264/FIXJPEG fixture produces one capsule per AU or frame whose source_digest equals sha256(segment bytes), plus a whole-file custody object; the import manifest is published root-last and referenced from the import's final (manifest) batch
- [ ] Without a capture_hint, capture time is reported unknown (ClockBasis::Estimated); with a hint, intervals carry the stated uncertainty and are labeled operator_assumption
- [ ] An absence query over the imported window is not certifiable; no ContinuityWitness is emitted for annexb or mjpeg
- [ ] Non-regular files, symlinks, oversize input and format conflicts give typed errors; the digest domain is registered and the count pin bumped
- [ ] A second import of the same bytes (same or different file name) into the same root returns idempotent_existing with no new batch; the import manifest records whole-file custody plus per-segment spans and sha256s; the storage decision is recorded in notes
- [ ] Files larger than one chunk are stored as ordered chunk objects whose concatenation hashes to the file sha256, and a span crossing a chunk boundary verifies; an import whose deltas exceed one batch is written as capsule batches plus a final manifest batch, and an import without its manifest batch is reported incomplete, never shown as complete
- [ ] Every import commits capsule batch(es), the ledgered import root and a final batch that moves the import object to generation 2; complete means generation 2 plus a Ledgered import slot, and readers use only complete imports
- [ ] Resume and re-import skip committed batches by deterministic id (typed ImportPlanConflict on a mismatch), repeated chunks are deduplicated in the custody manifest but kept in order in FileImportManifest, a span may cover any number of chunks, and after a complete import unreferenced_objects is empty
- [ ] The exact capacity check runs after hashing and before the first stage; a refusal leaves occupied_bytes and object_count unchanged; CaptureHintAfterReceive is typed

title: CAP- INGEST FileIngestAdapter (tests): custody digests, time-truth labels, no-absence proof, crash/cancel mid-import, e2e
description:
## Tests (crates/fss-reference/tests/file_ingest_contract.rs)
- Custody: for each fixture, recompute sha256 over each capsule's span from the original file and
  compare it with capsule.source_digest. The whole-file object digest equals sha256 of the file.
- The ledger batch references the import-manifest root; the manifest decodes canonically, and
  re-encoding it is byte-identical.
- Time truth, both with and without a hint.
- Absence is not certifiable over the imported window.
- Crash injection at each PublishCutPoint during an import: reopen shows orphaned staging, no
  visible partial import, and a re-import that is idempotent (same digests, no duplicate batch).
- Cancellation mid-scan and mid-publication: drain completed, no ledger batch.
- Symlink, directory and oversize input.

## E2E (scripts/e2e/cap_ingest_file_adapter.sh)
Uses `fss-lab ingest` once LAB5 exists; until then, the test binary. Per fixture, log the
capsule count, the root, the time-truth label and the absence-query result. Then run a
crash-injection round and log the recovery state.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Blocked by (must finish first):
  - fss-2h5zq.23: CAP- INGEST: FileIngestAdapter (ADP-FILE-001 reference slice): file -> SensorCapsules with source custody -> root-last publication -> ledger batch
  - fss-2h5zq.1: CAP- e2e harness: scripts/e2e/lib.sh structured JSON-lines logging and runner
  - fss-2h5zq.3: CAP- fixtures: deterministic synthetic H.264 Annex-B and rtpdump (RTP/RFC 6184) fixture generator
  - fss-2h5zq.5: CAP- fixtures: first-party deterministic baseline JPEG and MJPEG fixture encoder
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.63: CAP- QUALIFY: whole-bridge verification on green main (rust+policy lanes, all CAP e2e scripts) and honest status/doc update

## Refinement round 1 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- Test idempotency: the same file, and the same bytes under a different name.
- Tamper with a byte inside a segment span of the stored whole-file object. Reading that span then
  gives CustodyMismatch.
- Assert deterministic ids across roots, and the LedgerCutPoint::AfterRootDurable crash during
  import.
- Print CAPLOG lines per fixture and per fault.

## Refinement round 2 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- Multi-chunk: use a tiny chunk-size knob (for example 4 KiB) so small fixtures produce several
  chunks. Assert that the chunk digests concatenate to the file sha256. Tamper with a byte in a span
  that straddles a chunk boundary and expect CustodyMismatch.
- Multi-batch: with a tiny batch knob, assert the capsule batches plus the final manifest batch.
  Crash between the last capsule batch and the manifest batch: the import is reported incomplete,
  and a re-import completes it with no duplicate deltas.
- A capacity refusal (spool total) happens before the file is read.

## Refinement round 3 (2026-09-13, verified against main 7168075)
- Custody: sha256 of the concatenated chunk bytes in manifest order equals
  FileImportManifest.input_sha256 and sha256(file); a single-chunk file's chunk digest equals
  sha256(file). This replaces "the whole-file object digest equals sha256 of the file" and "chunk
  digests concatenate to the file sha256".
- Tamper (replaces the round-1/2 CustodyMismatch expectations): StagingSpool::read rehashes every
  object (spool/mod.rs:653, :1033-1050), so a byte flipped in a stored chunk gives a typed
  CustodyUnavailable{chunk, SpoolError::Corrupt} in-session and a BrokenRoot after reopen. This
  holds for the straddling span too. CustodyMismatch is tested by corrupting span metadata (a
  test-built capsule with a wrong source_digest or span).
- Crash at each PublishCutPoint (replaces "reopen shows orphaned staging"): AfterChildrenVerified and
  AfterManifestBody leave unreferenced objects; AfterRootTempWrite leaves an orphaned root temp;
  AfterRootRename leaves a durable root whose slot is PendingLedger, and a re-import commits it.
  Orphaned staging comes only from spool stage faults (FaultInjectingSpoolIo).
- Cancellation before the first batch appends nothing; cancellation after capsule batch k leaves an
  incomplete import (import object at generation 1) that status and doctor report, and a re-import
  completes it with no duplicate delta.
- New cases: an indeterminate append on each batch (fail_journal_after_phase) followed by
  reconcile_ledger_append; a re-import with a different chunk or batch knob gets a new identity, never
  BatchIdConflict; a file made of two identical chunks; a capacity refusal leaves occupied_bytes and
  object_count unchanged; re-importing an already-staged file larger than the remaining capacity
  succeeds; after a complete import, unreferenced_objects is empty and reconcile().is_clean() holds.

title: CAP- INGEST: drive AcquisitionSession through a file session (request -> auth(None) -> ack -> first frame -> explicit no-continuity or continuity -> quiescence)
description:
## What and why
Vision goal #6: fss_core::AcquisitionSession (crates/fss-core/src/acquisition.rs:2436, a 158 KB
state machine) and its witnesses are PARTIAL because "no adapter drives it and no real bytes". The
witnesses are AcquisitionRequest, AuthReceipt, AdapterAck, FirstFrameWitness, ContinuityWitness,
DegradationEvidence, FailureWitness, QuiescenceReceipt and IndeterminateWitness, each with its
fss.acquisition.* digest domain already registered. The file adapter is the first real driver.

## Build
`crates/fss-reference/src/ingest/file_session.rs`:
- Map a file import onto the lifecycle:
  1. AcquisitionSession::new(AcquisitionRequest), with source, device and adapter identities for
     ADP-FILE-001 and the requested capability "file_import".
  2. authenticate(AuthReceipt with CredentialMethod::None). There is no secret, and the receipt
     stays secret-free.
  3. accept(AdapterAck).
  4. observe_first_frame(FirstFrameWitness over the first capsule: timing, format,
     decode_state DecodeState::NotAttempted until DECODE runs, source_custody
     SourceCustody::Retained, explicit_omission ExplicitOmission::None, frame digest).
  5. Continuity:
     - annexb/mjpeg: do NOT call verify_continuity. A file has no packet sequence. Record an
       explicit typed "continuity not observable for file source". If the core model has no such
       state, use degrade(DegradationEvidence{lost dimension: continuity/coverage, invalidated
       claims: absence}) and record the gap between model and reality as a finding.
     - rtpdump: verify_continuity is driven by INGEST6.
  6. At EOF: cancel(QuiescenceReceipt{zero tasks, zero open descriptors, drained buffers}, now)
     -> Cancelled. There is no Quiesced or Reconciled state kind; reconcile(resolved_state, note,
     now) is legal only from Indeterminate (acquisition.rs:3080).
  7. An I/O error or a malformed stream mid-file goes to fail(FailureWitness) or
     mark_indeterminate, depending on whether capsules were already published.
- The transition records (AcquisitionTransitionRecord) are appended in the SAME ledger batch as
  the capsules (INGEST3), so history and evidence are one ordered universe.
- check_absence_claim_allowed must return an error for file sessions. Test it.

## Considerations
- The transitions allowed by get_transition_rule/is_allowed_transition may not fit a file source
  well: for example, continuity may be mandatory before a Streaming-like state. Do NOT widen the
  core state machine silently. If a transition is missing, file a design finding bead against
  fss-core and use the nearest honest path (degrade), documenting why.
- Registration: module_declarations ingest/file_session.rs -> "authority". MANIFEST.delta rows.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Blocked by (must finish first):
  - fss-2h5zq.23: CAP- INGEST: FileIngestAdapter (ADP-FILE-001 reference slice): file -> SensorCapsules with source custody -> root-last publication -> ledger batch
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.17: CAP- LAB: `fss-lab ingest --input <file> --root <dir>` runs the file-ingest adapter on the real stack and prints an import report
  - fss-2h5zq.26: CAP- INGEST file acquisition lifecycle (tests): transition histories per outcome, witness digests, absence refusal, e2e
  - fss-2h5zq.29: CAP- INGEST: RTP continuity -> ContinuityWitness -> AcquisitionSession (verified, degraded or new stream generation)
  - fss-2h5zq.31: CAP- INGEST gauntlet (tests): malformed-media, limit, crash and cancel campaign across Annex-B, MJPEG, file adapter and lifecycle

## Refinement round 1 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- The state kinds at acquisition.rs:87 are Requested, Authenticated, AdapterAccepted,
  FirstFrameObserved, ContinuityVerified, Degraded, Failed, Cancelled and Indeterminate.
- The transition table allows FirstFrameObserved -> Degraded. So the honest file path is:
  Requested -> Authenticated -> AdapterAccepted -> FirstFrameObserved -> Degraded (continuity not
  observable for a file source; invalidated claim: absence) -> Cancelled (QuiescenceReceipt at EOF).
- A model gap to record as a finding bead against fss-core (do not widen the core here): the core
  has no "end of source" terminal kind, so a normally finished file ends as Cancelled. The report
  labels that ending `end_of_file_source`, never an operator cancel.
- A mid-file failure:
  - before any capsule is published: fail(FailureWitness) -> Failed;
  - when the publication outcome is unknown (a crash between root durable and batch):
    mark_indeterminate(IndeterminateWitness) -> Indeterminate. After ReferenceDeployment reconciles,
    call reconcile(resolved_state, note, now).
- check_absence_claim_allowed returns an error for Degraded and Cancelled file sessions. Assert the
  exact AcquisitionError variant.

title: CAP- INGEST: rtpdump recorded-RTP reader feeding fss-packet (RtpPacket::parse -> SequenceTracker -> H264Depacketizer) into capsules
description:
## What and why
This is the FIRST real consumer of fss-packet (vision goal #7: "no consumer crate"). A recorded
RTP capture in rtptools rtpdump format is the file analogue of a live RTSP/RTP session, so it
exercises the owner's packet kernel on real bytes without any socket.

## Build
`crates/fss-reference/src/ingest/rtpdump.rs`:
- A bounded rtpdump reader:
  - The text header `#!rtpplay1.0 <addr>/<port>\n`. The address is opaque: never parsed as a
    network address, never logged (privacy), only length-checked.
  - The RD_hdr_t, 16 bytes.
  - Records: an RD_packet_t (u16 length, u16 plen, u32 offset_ms) followed by the packet.
    plen == 0 means a non-RTP record and is skipped with an omission span.
  - Limits on records, record size and total bytes. A truncated final record is a typed finding.
- Per record:
  1. `fss_packet::RtpPacket::parse(bytes, PacketLimits::default())`.
  2. `SequenceTracker::observe(...)`, using a StreamKey{ingress, generation} per SSRC and a new
     generation on an SSRC change or RestartRequired.
  3. `H264Depacketizer::new(key, 96, H264Mode::<non-interleaved>, H264Limits)` and
     `.push(key, extended_sequence, packet, now_ns)`, where now_ns comes from offset_ms through
     the VirtualClock. Also `.expire(now_ns)` and `.finish()` at EOF.
- NalUnits (with NalSourceSpan back into the file records) are grouped into access units by RTP
  timestamp and marker bit. Each AU becomes a capsule via the same capsule path as INGEST3, whose
  adapter routes `#!rtpplay1.0` here.
- Timing: the RTP 90 kHz timestamps give intra-stream relative timing, a real improvement over
  Annex-B. The absolute capture time remains unknown unless RTCP SR is present
  (SenderReportClock). Use ClockBasis::DeviceMonotonic for relative timing only if the core
  semantics allow it; otherwise Estimated. Record the choice.
- FragmentDiscard / H264Failure outcomes become typed omission and degradation findings with
  source spans. Nothing is dropped silently.

## Gating (why this bead is blocked)
- crate_topology.json lists fss-packet as "planned" although it is a workspace member. A new
  fss-reference -> fss-packet edge would add policy findings until the owner resolves fss-1bd1l
  (mark present, or remove from the workspace).
- fss-kr9n3 tracks fss-packet's red clippy and fmt and its failing RTCP SDES test. It is the
  owner's crate, so the orchestrator may not fix it.
- Both are blocking dependencies. This bead must NOT edit crates/fss-packet/**. If an API gap is
  found (for example, no public way to build a NalUnit from bytes), record it on the owner bead
  "CAP- OWNER fss-packet ..." and work around it in fss-reference.

## Registration
- The Cargo edge fss-reference -> fss-packet (L7 -> L3, downward), plus Cargo.lock and
  MANIFEST.delta.
- module_declarations ingest/rtpdump.rs -> "support" (a parser); the capsule construction stays
  in file_adapter.

  - fss-1bd1l: (existing bead)
  - fss-kr9n3: (existing bead)

  - fss-2h5zq.29: CAP- INGEST: RTP continuity -> ContinuityWitness -> AcquisitionSession (verified, degraded or new stream generation)

- StreamKey has three fields at 8b96911:
  - ingress: u128, nonzero and owner-issued. Derive it from the canonical FSS stream identity, never
    from the SSRC.
  - generation: u64, a nonzero epoch.

title: CAP- INGEST: RTP continuity -> ContinuityWitness -> AcquisitionSession (verified, degraded or new stream generation)
description:
## What and why
Top-10 gap #5, "connect fss-packet to acquisition truth". With a recorded RTP stream we CAN
observe continuity, so the file session can honestly reach a continuity-verified state, which is
impossible for Annex-B or MJPEG. A gap or reset must drive degradation or a new stream generation.
Coverage then follows from real packet evidence, not assumption.

## Build
`crates/fss-reference/src/ingest/rtp_continuity.rs`:
- Consume the SequenceStats/SequenceObservation stream from INGEST5 per window of N packets.
- Clean window: build fss_core::ContinuityWitness { adapter_id, device_id, source_id,
  window_start_seq, window_end_seq, window_start_pts_ns, window_end_pts_ns, frames_observed,
  discontinuities: 0, packet_loss: 0, observed_jitter_ns (from fss_packet::JitterEstimator over
  offset_ms arrivals), max_jitter_threshold_ns, coverage_witness }.
  - The coverage_witness covers ONLY the recorded interval and the observed domain of this one
    camera stream. It is never a site-wide claim.
  - Then call AcquisitionSession::verify_continuity(...).
- Loss or discontinuity: DegradationEvidence (lost dimensions: continuity; invalidated claims:
  absence over the gap interval), then degrade(...). The coverage witness is marked gap for that
  interval.
- SSRC change or RestartRequired: a new StreamGeneration, and reconnect(...) or the documented
  path for a new generation. Capsules after it carry gap_before = true.
- Negative-read test: an absence query over a window with a gap must not certify absence. Beware
  fss-3qlsa: event_store evaluate_coverage_for_absent uses the FIRST matching witness, so a later
  gap can be ignored. Add a test that registers the certifying witness first and the gapped one

title: CAP- fixtures: deterministic synthetic H.264 Annex-B and rtpdump (RTP/RFC 6184) fixture generator
description:
## What and why
File ingest needs real, valid bitstreams, and nothing in the repo provides them. fss-reference
encoded_fixture.rs (FSS-014) generates seeded frame fixtures bound to SensorCapsuleV1, but its
payloads are not real codec syntax, and the fss-packet example uses an inline RTP fixture.
Ingest must never depend on third-party footage (security boundary), so we generate syntactically
valid streams first-party. The target is NAL-level ingest, not pixel decode: the H.264 payloads
need correct NAL headers, SPS/PPS/AUD/IDR/non-IDR structure, emulation-prevention bytes and
correct first_mb_in_slice. The macroblock data does not need to decode to a meaningful picture.
The fixture manifest must say "structurally valid, not decodable pictures" so nobody overclaims.

## Build (proposed paths; record the final ones in notes)
- `crates/fss-reference/src/media_fixture/h264.rs`: a deterministic generator with a seed and
  parameters (GOP length, frame count, NAL sizes, sizes that force emulation-prevention 0x000003
  insertion, optional AUD, 3-byte and 4-byte start codes).
  - Output: an Annex-B elementary stream `Vec<u8>` plus a manifest of expected NAL spans
    (offset, len, type, is_idr, access-unit index).
- `crates/fss-reference/src/media_fixture/rtpdump.rs`: packetizes the same NALs into RTP per
  RFC 6184: single NAL unit mode, STAP-A for SPS+PPS, FU-A for NALs larger than the MTU. It uses
  payload type 96, clock 90 kHz, a fixed SSRC and a seeded initial sequence number that includes
  a wrap case at 65535 -> 0. It serializes to the rtptools rtpdump format:
  - a text line `#!rtpplay1.0 0.0.0.0/0\n` (a zero address, never a real one);
  - a 16-byte RD_hdr_t (start sec/usec, source, port, all zero or deterministic);
  - per packet, an 8-byte RD_packet_t (u16 length incl. header, u16 plen, u32 offset_ms), then
    the packet.
  - Variants: clean, loss (drop listed sequence numbers), reorder (swap pairs), duplicate,
    ssrc_reset (new SSRC mid-stream = new stream generation), and truncated_last_record.
- `crates/fss-reference/src/media_fixture/mod.rs`: `FixtureManifest { name, generator,
  generator_version, seed, params, sha256, expected: ... }`, rendered canonically.
- Committed fixture bytes under `tests/fixtures/media/h264/` and `tests/fixtures/media/rtp/`
  (a few KiB each) plus per-family `tests/fixtures/media/h264/fixture_manifest.json` and
  `tests/fixtures/media/rtp/fixture_manifest.json`, which list each file with
  its sha256, generator and seed. A unit test regenerates each fixture and asserts it is
  byte-identical to the committed file, so fixtures can never drift silently.
- An optional lab-only oracle cross-check: if `ffprobe` exists on the host, the companion test may
  record the NAL counts it sees as a lab-oracle observation (DEP-LAB-001: sealed lab only, never
  a production path). If it is absent, log a skipped step, not a failure.

## Registration
- semantic_plane_registry.json module_declarations: the media_fixture/* modules are "support".
- MANIFEST.delta rows for the sources and fixtures.
- Adding a new digest domain is not needed unless the manifest is canonically digested. If it is,
  register SCHEMA-DOMAIN-MEDIA-FIXTURE-MANIFEST-001 `fss.media_fixture.manifest.v1`.

## Consumers
CAP- INGEST Annex-B splitter, rtpdump reader, RTP continuity, RTSP transcript fixture,
malformed-media gauntlet, fss-lab ingest.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Related existing beads (context only, not blocking; this bead does not close them): fss-x4a.28.4
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.4: CAP- fixtures H.264/rtpdump (tests): regeneration identity, structure checks, e2e manifest verification
  - fss-2h5zq.7: CAP- fixtures: recorded RTSP/1.0 interleaved-TCP session transcript (no credentials) for the sans-IO parser
  - fss-2h5zq.18: CAP- LAB ingest command (tests): CLI integration per format, determinism, degraded paths, e2e ingest script
  - fss-2h5zq.20: CAP- INGEST Annex-B splitter (tests): manifest equality, malformed corpus, property/no-panic, e2e
  - fss-2h5zq.24: CAP- INGEST FileIngestAdapter (tests): custody digests, time-truth labels, no-absence proof, crash/cancel mid-import, e2e
  - fss-2h5zq.28: CAP- INGEST rtpdump -> fss-packet (tests): NAL equivalence with Annex-B, loss/reorder/wrap/ssrc variants, e2e
  - fss-2h5zq.30: CAP- INGEST RTP continuity (tests): witness construction, degrade and new-generation paths, gap absence refusal, e2e
  - fss-2h5zq.31: CAP- INGEST gauntlet (tests): malformed-media, limit, crash and cancel campaign across Annex-B, MJPEG, file adapter and lifecycle
  - fss-2h5zq.60: CAP- STATUS (tests): per-root assertions after lab, ingest and rtpdump runs, readiness guard, e2e
  - fss-2h5zq.62: CAP- CAPSTONE pipeline (tests): digest-chain verification, fault injections, idempotent rerun, doctor/status cross-check, e2e

## Refinement round 1 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- Probation (crates/fss-packet/src/continuity.rs, verified). SequenceTracker admits a stream only
  after two sequential packets. The first packet of every SSRC generation is classified Probation
  with extended_sequence None, and it must never reach H264Depacketizer.
  - So the rtpdump generator starts each generation (the clean start, and the segment after
    ssrc_reset) with one sacrificial packet: a repeated SPS+PPS STAP-A, as real cameras repeat
    parameter sets.
  - The manifest lists, per packet, the expected SequenceClass (Probation, Baseline, Advanced,
    Reordered, Duplicate, BeforeBaseline, DiscontinuitySuspected, RestartRequired), and whether its
    NALs are expected to be delivered. NAL equivalence with the Annex-B fixture is then exact over
    the delivered packets.
- Add the rtpdump variant `large_gap`: a forward jump above the tracker's 3,000-packet dropout
  bound, giving DiscontinuitySuspected and, on consecutive jumps, RestartRequired.
- The Annex-B content must include at least one AU with two slices (the second slice has
  first_mb_in_slice > 0), an SEI NAL, trailing_zero_8bits before a start code, and both start-code
  lengths, so AU grouping is really exercised.
- Per-family manifests: tests/fixtures/media/h264/fixture_manifest.json and
  tests/fixtures/media/rtp/fixture_manifest.json share one schema. They replace the single shared
  tests/fixtures/media/fixture_manifest.json, so the H.264, JPEG and RTSP fixture beads can land in
  parallel without conflicting on one JSON file. Every later mention of "fixture_manifest.json"
  means the family manifest.
- Keep the generators pure (no I/O inside media_fixture/*): they return bytes, and the caller
  writes files. Record in notes exactly how the committed bytes were produced (command and
  sha256). The regeneration test is the authority, and fixtures are never hand-edited.

    crates/fss-cli/src/lab_cmd.rs.

title: CAP- INGEST gauntlet (tests): malformed-media, limit, crash and cancel campaign across Annex-B, MJPEG, file adapter and lifecycle
description:
## What and why
AGENTS.md workflow step 8: "Add failures first: cancellation, packet gaps, clock skew, corrupt
data, ... partial archive publication, duplicate requests". Hostile bytes are the default for any
importer. This is a cross-cutting campaign over the P1 ingest path. It is a test bead in its own
right and seeds the later registered proof family TEST-MEDIA-MALFORMED-001 (fss-x4a.28.4),
without claiming to complete it.

## Build
- `crates/fss-reference/tests/ingest_gauntlet.rs`, a table-driven corpus.
  - The corpus is generated in-test from FIXH264/FIXJPEG plus deterministic mutations: truncation
    at every 64th byte, bit flips, start-code injection, length-field overflow, zero-length NAL,
    forbidden bit, a huge SOF dimension, a missing EOI, 1 GiB claimed lengths.
  - A sparse file is created in a temp dir with set_len, never filled, to test the size limit
    without disk use.
  - Duplicate import of the same file into the same root.
  - The same file under two names: the same custody digest, and a second import is idempotent or
    typed-duplicate by policy. Decide which and document it.
  - Cancel at every checkpoint.
  - A crash at every PublishCutPoint.
- Invariants asserted for every case:
  - no panic;
  - no allocation beyond the limit (use the limit knobs and assert typed LimitExceeded before the
    read);
  - either Ok with every published capsule digest matching its span, or a typed error with ZERO
    ledger batches;
  - no half-visible import after reopen;
  - obligations terminal.
- `scripts/e2e/cap_ingest_gauntlet.sh` runs the gauntlet with --nocapture, turns each case into a
  JSON log step (case id, mutation, expected class, observed class, error id, ledger batches
  before and after), and summarizes counts per class.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Blocked by (must finish first):
  - fss-2h5zq.23: CAP- INGEST: FileIngestAdapter (ADP-FILE-001 reference slice): file -> SensorCapsules with source custody -> root-last publication -> ledger batch
  - fss-2h5zq.25: CAP- INGEST: drive AcquisitionSession through a file session (request -> auth(None) -> ack -> first frame -> explicit no-continuity or continuity -> quiescence)
  - fss-2h5zq.3: CAP- fixtures: deterministic synthetic H.264 Annex-B and rtpdump (RTP/RFC 6184) fixture generator
  - fss-2h5zq.5: CAP- fixtures: first-party deterministic baseline JPEG and MJPEG fixture encoder
  - fss-2h5zq.1: CAP- e2e harness: scripts/e2e/lib.sh structured JSON-lines logging and runner
- Related existing beads (context only, not blocking; this bead does not close them): fss-x4a.28.4
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.63: CAP- QUALIFY: whole-bridge verification on green main (rust+policy lanes, all CAP e2e scripts) and honest status/doc update

## Refinement round 1 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- The idempotency policy is now fixed by fss-2h5zq.23. The same identity gives idempotent_existing
  with no new batch; the same bytes under a different name have the same identity. Test both.
- Add LedgerCutPoint::AfterRootDurable to the crash cases.
- After every failed import, assert that only orphaned staging remains, and that it is classified
  by CAP- DOCTOR0's spool::inspect if that has landed (otherwise by reopen).
- The rtpdump mutation families live in fss-2h5zq.28.
- Print CAPLOG lines per case family.

## Refinement round 2 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- Add the chunked-custody and multi-batch families from fss-2h5zq.23, with tiny chunk and batch
  knobs. Include a crash at every point between the first capsule batch and the manifest batch.
  Assert that the incomplete import is reported and that a re-import completes it.

## Refinement round 3 (2026-09-13, verified against main 7168075)
- Invariants (replace "a typed error with ZERO ledger batches" and "no half-visible import after
  reopen"): every case ends in one of
  - Ok, with every published capsule digest matching its span;
  - a typed error before the first batch, with zero new batches;
  - a typed error after it, leaving an import whose import object is at generation 1: status and
    doctor report it incomplete, no reader counts or decodes it, and a re-import completes it with
    zero duplicate deltas.
- "LimitExceeded" is not an existing type: assert the fss-2h5zq.23 adapter error variants. Spool
  refusals (SpoolError::ByteQuotaExceeded, ObjectCountLimit) must be mapped by the adapter before
  staging, so none may surface from a stage call.
- Crash points between batches: after each capsule batch, after each part publish,
  LedgerCutPoint::AfterRootDurable on the import slot, and an indeterminate append on every batch.
- Tamper expectations follow fss-2h5zq.24 round 3 (CustodyUnavailable in-session).

title: CAP- RTSP: sans-IO RTSP/1.0 message and SDP parser (bounded, no sockets, auth challenges detected and refused)
description:
## What and why
Top-10 gap #8 notes that RTSP/RTP over TCP-interleaved is the first physical-sensor path
reachable in safe Rust. The socket part is blocked on owner decision fss-x4a.8.1 (Asupersync
`Cx`) and on a device-I/O substrate ADR. The protocol part is pure parsing and can be built and
proven now against recorded transcripts. It is sans-IO: the parser takes bytes and returns
events. It never reads from anything.

## Build
`crates/fss-reference/src/rtsp/message.rs` and `rtsp/sdp.rs`:
- An RTSP/1.0 message parser:
  - Request line `METHOD rtsp-URI RTSP/1.0` or status line `RTSP/1.0 NNN reason`.
  - Headers with a line limit, a count limit and case-insensitive names. Recognized headers:
    CSeq, Content-Length, Content-Type, Session (with timeout=), Transport
    (RTP/AVP/TCP;unicast;interleaved=a-b, and RTP/AVP;unicast;client_port for completeness,
    parsed but unused), Range, RTP-Info, Public.
  - A body by Content-Length, with a limit.
  - Incremental parsing across record boundaries: feed(bytes) -> Vec<RtspEvent>.
- An interleaved-frame recognizer: `$`, channel u8, length u16, payload, emitted as
  RtspEvent::Interleaved{channel, span}.
- Minimal SDP: v=, o= (opaque, never logged), s=, c= (opaque), m=video/audio, a=rtpmap,
  a=fmtp with packetization-mode and sprop-parameter-sets (a bounded base64 decoder written
  first-party, no crate), a=control. Audio m-lines are recorded and ignored (audio is off by
  default: plan GOAL-009 privacy).
- Credential boundary: a 401 with WWW-Authenticate becomes RtspEvent::AuthRequired{scheme}. The
  challenge parameters are NOT stored. There is no code path that constructs an Authorization
  header. A test asserts that the crate source contains no "Authorization:" string builder.
- Typed errors: MalformedStartLine, HeaderLimit, BadContentLength, BodyLimit, BadTransport,
  BadInterleavedLength, BadBase64, and so on. No panic.

## Registration
module_declarations rtsp/message.rs and rtsp/sdp.rs -> "support". MANIFEST.delta rows.

## Related
fss-x4a.12.10 (FSS-111, RTSP parser/session state machine, P0) is the production owner. This bead
is the reference vertical slice and cites it; it does not close it. See also fss-x4a.11.5
(FSS-047, RTSP auth/session state; blocked by design here: no credentials) and fss-x4a.28.6
(TEST-RTSP-001).

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Related existing beads (context only, not blocking; this bead does not close them): fss-x4a.12.10, fss-x4a.28.6
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.33: CAP- RTSP parser (tests): transcript event sequences, incremental splits at every byte, no-credential guard, e2e
  - fss-2h5zq.34: CAP- RTSP: sans-IO session state machine over recorded transcripts; interleaved RTP handed to the fss-packet ingest path

## Refinement round 1 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
Acceptance is split so this bead stays ready while the transcript fixture (fss-2h5zq.7) lands.
- This bead is proven on hand-built byte vectors:
  - each method's request and response;
  - a 401 with WWW-Authenticate;
  - an interleaved frame split across feeds;
  - a bad Content-Length;
  - a hand-built SDP.
- Transcript event sequences and equality with the FIXH264 SPS/PPS are proven in fss-2h5zq.33.
- GET_PARAMETER (keepalive) is parsed. ANNOUNCE, RECORD, REDIRECT and SET_PARAMETER give a typed
  Unsupported{method}.
- The guard test for "no Authorization builder" may contain the literal "Authorization:", but never
  the word unsafe.

## Refinement round 2 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- SDP: recognize a=rtcp-rsize (RFC 5506) on the media level and surface it as
  rtcp_reduced_size: bool. The session uses it to choose RtcpMode (fss-2h5zq.34).

## Shared rules for every CAP- bead (repeated so this bead stands alone)

Context: parent epic "CAP- Capability bridge: file-ingest-first end-to-end" (fss-2h5zq), created

  because a new member trips the crate_topology and member-count pins (see fss-1bd1l).

  RtpPacket::parse, SequenceTracker, H264Depacketizer, NalUnit, SenderReportClock and
  JitterEstimator. Any change that needs fss-packet edits goes to an owner bead and is never
  assigned to an agent.
- No device I/O: no camera, USB, V4L2 or socket code; no `std::net` or `TcpStream`. Inputs are
  recorded files and recorded transcripts only. Every file read goes through an explicit I/O
  authority value, following the ReplayIoAuthority/ReplayCx pattern in
  crates/fss-reference/src/adapter_replay.rs, with cooperative cancellation checkpoints
  (request -> drain -> finalize). Asupersync `Cx` is NOT admitted yet (owner decision

    unknown or not_observable.

    CaptureInterval unless the stream itself carries timing.

    or omission.

     `module_declarations` entry in architecture/semantic_plane_registry.json with its plane
     (authority | cognition | effect | support | ambiguous).
     scripts/semantic_plane_checker.py audits exactly those two crates and fails otherwise.
  2. Every new canonical digest or encoding domain tag gets a row in registries/DIGEST_DOMAINS.md
     (ID SCHEMA-DOMAIN-<NAME>-001, domain fss.<name>.v1, scope, authority, invariant rule).

     assertions in tests/test_schema_validate.py AND the domain_count assertion (and its
     message) in crates/fss-model-ir/tests/model_ir_contract.rs:420 (45 at main 7168075;
     verified in refinement round 3). Count from the value on HEAD at commit time, because several CAP
     beads add domains in parallel.
  3. Every new or changed source path gets a row in MANIFEST.delta.sha256 per ADR-0013. Never
     edit the MANIFEST.sha256 base. Check with `python3 scripts/manifest_audit.py`.
  4. New crate dependency edges must point downward in architecture/crate_topology.json. Layers:
     L2 ledger/object/publication, L3 fss-packet, L4 tensor/model-ir/geometry, L6 fss-cli,
     L7 fss-reference. fss-cli -> fss-reference is the one waived inversion. Check with
     `python3 scripts/dependency_dag_checker.py`.
  5. New CLI error and exit identities get rows in registries/ERRORS.md, and the operation
     crosswalk (architecture/operation_crosswalk.json and crates/fss-cli/src/crosswalk.rs) stays
     consistent.
- Verification (remote only):
  - `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- cargo test -p <crate> --all-targets --no-fail-fast --locked --offline`
  - `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets --keep-going --locked --offline -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo fmt --check`
  - `scripts/qualify.sh --lane policy`
  - `--all-targets` does NOT run doctests. When the crate has doc examples, also run
    `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- cargo test -p <crate> --doc --no-fail-fast --locked --offline`.
  - Launch rch from the repo directory with `--base <sha>`. Decide pass or fail by exit code (rch
    output is ANSI-coloured; strip ANSI before counting diagnostics). Re-run Python checkers and
    e2e scripts on a fresh `git worktree add --detach` checkout, never only in the shared tree.

  Main is currently red for reasons outside this bead (fss-kr9n3, fss-1bd1l, fss-lc2r1). Until
  those land, report "no new findings attributable to this bead's files". Never weaken a gate.
- E2E convention: every test bead ships scripts/e2e/cap_<name>.sh using the shared helpers in
  scripts/e2e/lib.sh (see the "CAP- e2e harness" bead).
  - Logs are JSON lines under ${FSS_E2E_LOG_DIR:-target/e2e-logs}/<name>/. The first record is an
    env record (git sha, bead id, binary sha256s, host triple, FSS_* settings); then one record per
    step: {ts, script, bead, step, cmd, exit, duration_ms, expected, observed, digest,

    stripped) through e2e_cargo_test. scripts/e2e/validate_log.py checks every record.

    inside digests) and bounded in size, and they print a one-line reproduction command.

    #![forbid(unsafe_code)].

    "implemented") depends on fss-geometry. Treat crates/fss-twin/** and crates/fss-geometry/**
    as owner-authored upstream code, like fss-packet: use their public API and record API gaps in
    notes instead of editing them.
  - Shared hot files (edit only your own rows or lines; stage with `git add -p`):
    registries/DIGEST_DOMAINS.md, tests/test_schema_validate.py,
    crates/fss-model-ir/tests/model_ir_contract.rs (the third domain-count pin),
    architecture/semantic_plane_registry.json, MANIFEST.delta.sha256, registries/ERRORS.md,
    crates/fss-reference/src/lib.rs, crates/fss-reference/Cargo.toml and
    crates/fss-cli/src/lab_cmd.rs.
  - LocalRootPublisher::open and StagingSpool::open create directories and take exclusive lock
    files, so they are not read-only. Read-only inspection goes through fss-2h5zq.66.
- Swarm hygiene:
  - One bead per commit, with the bead id in the subject.
  - Commit only files you own. Never `git add -A`. Never reset, amend or rebase main.
  - Commit only what compiles against committed HEAD, and commit type changes together with all
    their users.
  - Record final paths and evidence with `br update <id> --append-notes`. Never use --notes,
    which overwrites the field.

title: CAP- RTSP parser (tests): transcript event sequences, incremental splits at every byte, no-credential guard, e2e
description:
## Tests (crates/fss-reference/tests/rtsp_parser_contract.rs)
- Per transcript, the expected events.
- Incremental robustness: split the S2C stream at EVERY byte offset and feed in two parts; the
  events must be identical.
- 10k-mutation no-panic.
- A limit test.
- A source-grep guard test: rtsp/*.rs contains no Authorization-header construction.

## E2E (scripts/e2e/cap_rtsp_parser.sh)
Per transcript, log the event-kind histogram, the SDP summary (PT, clock, has_sps_pps; never o=
or c=) and the error ids.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Blocked by (must finish first):
  - fss-2h5zq.32: CAP- RTSP: sans-IO RTSP/1.0 message and SDP parser (bounded, no sockets, auth challenges detected and refused)
  - fss-2h5zq.1: CAP- e2e harness: scripts/e2e/lib.sh structured JSON-lines logging and runner
  - fss-2h5zq.7: CAP- fixtures: recorded RTSP/1.0 interleaved-TCP session transcript (no credentials) for the sans-IO parser
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.63: CAP- QUALIFY: whole-bridge verification on green main (rust+policy lanes, all CAP e2e scripts) and honest status/doc update

## Refinement round 1 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- This bead now owns two checks moved from fss-2h5zq.32: the transcript event sequence for every
  FIXRTSP variant (including sr_absent and get_parameter_keepalive), and equality of the SDP's
  SPS/PPS with the FIXH264 parameter sets.
- Print CAPLOG lines per transcript.

## Refinement round 2 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- Include the rtcp_rsize transcript (fss-2h5zq.7) in the per-variant event sequences, and assert
  its rtcp_reduced_size flag.
