title: CAP- RTSP: sans-IO session state machine over recorded transcripts; interleaved RTP handed to the fss-packet ingest path
description:
## What and why
A session state machine (Init -> OptionsDone -> Described -> SetUp -> Playing -> TearingDown ->
Closed, plus AuthRequired as a terminal-blocked state and Failed) driven purely by RtspEvents
from RTSP1. It turns a recorded TCP-interleaved session into RTP packets for the exact same
pipeline as rtpdump (INGEST5 and INGEST6). The first live camera path later only swaps the byte
source, once the owner admits a substrate.

## Build
`crates/fss-reference/src/rtsp/session.rs`:
- `RtspSession::on_event(event) -> Vec<SessionAction>`.
- Actions are data, e.g. ExpectResponse{cseq}, DeliverRtp{channel, span}, DeliverRtcp,
  SessionTimeout{secs}, Stop{reason}. They are never I/O.
- CSeq pairing between requests and responses.
- Session-id binding: a mismatch is a typed error.
- The Transport interleaved channel map (RTP 0, RTCP 1).
- A Session timeout header is recorded as an obligation for a future keepalive, and flagged
  not_applicable for recordings.
- RTP channel payloads go to fss_packet::RtpPacket::parse and then the INGEST5 path; RTCP goes to
  RtcpCompound::parse and SenderReportClock, which gives absolute capture-time evidence when an
  SR exists. That is an improvement over rtpdump without SR.
- AuthRequired stops the session. The report says "credentialed sessions are out of scope
  (security boundary; owner decision)".
- A transcript reader: `#!fss-rtsp-transcript v1` records (from FIXRTSP) are replayed in order,
  with offset_ms driving the VirtualClock.

## Gating
It uses fss-packet (RtpPacket, RtcpCompound), so it depends on INGEST5, which carries the
fss-1bd1l/fss-kr9n3 gates.

## Registration
module_declarations rtsp/session.rs -> "support". If a session record is canonically digested,
add SCHEMA-DOMAIN-RTSP-SESSION-RECORD-001 `fss.rtsp_session_record.v1`.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Blocked by (must finish first):
  - fss-2h5zq.32: CAP- RTSP: sans-IO RTSP/1.0 message and SDP parser (bounded, no sockets, auth challenges detected and refused)
  - fss-2h5zq.27: CAP- INGEST: rtpdump recorded-RTP reader feeding fss-packet (RtpPacket::parse -> SequenceTracker -> H264Depacketizer) into capsules
- Related existing beads (context only, not blocking; this bead does not close them): fss-x4a.12.10, fss-x4a.28.6
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.35: CAP- RTSP session (tests): state traces per transcript, RTP equivalence with rtpdump path, no-socket guard, e2e
  - fss-2h5zq.36: CAP- RTSP: `fss-lab ingest --rtsp-transcript <file>` routes recorded sessions through capsules, continuity and the ledger

## Refinement round 1 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- RTCP: RtcpCompound::parse(bytes, PacketLimits, RtcpMode). Read rtcp.rs for the RtcpMode variant
  that matches the transcript.
- Sender reports: SenderReportClock::new(key, 90_000, report, received_ns, uncertainty_ns,
  max_distance_ticks), with the uncertainty taken from the transcript's offset resolution. Its
  estimates are sender assertions, not physical capture truth, so ClockBasis stays Estimated unless
  a disciplined basis is proven.
- Probation handling per generation is as in fss-2h5zq.27.
- sr_absent keeps capture time unknown.

## Refinement round 2 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- RtcpMode choice (variants verified at rtcp.rs:7):
  - Compound by default (RFC 3550 §6.1);
  - ReducedSize only when the SDP negotiated a=rtcp-rsize (fss-2h5zq.32 surfaces the flag).
  A report that fails the selected mode, such as an SR without CNAME under Compound, becomes a
  typed RTCP finding with its record span. The session continues, and capture time for that
  interval stays unknown.
- SenderReportClock::new(key, 90_000, report, received_ns, uncertainty_ns, max_distance_ticks)
  (timing.rs:70) refuses:
  - key.ingress or key.generation equal to 0, and max_distance_ticks outside 1..0x8000_0000
    (Configuration);
  - report.ssrc != key.ssrc (StreamMismatch);
  - a zero NTP timestamp (NoSenderReport).
  Map each ContinuityError to a typed finding.
- fss-kr9n3's failing SDES wire-contract test means RtcpCompound::parse may still change for SDES.
  Pin the expectations to RFC 3550, and record any disagreement on fss-kr9n3.
- The report states the RTCP mode used.

description:

gains an `rtsp` section: state trace, SDP summary and SR presence. Continuity comes from INGEST6,
so a clean transcript can reach continuity-verified; a transcript with loss degrades.

## Build
- Extend LAB5's command: `--format rtsp-transcript` (sniffed from `#!fss-rtsp-transcript v1`).
- Wire it to RTSP2's output, then the INGEST5/INGEST6 pipeline, then FileIngestAdapter capsule
  publication.
- The report also carries acquisition states and the continuity witness digest.

  - fss-2h5zq.29: CAP- INGEST: RTP continuity -> ContinuityWitness -> AcquisitionSession (verified, degraded or new stream generation)
  - fss-2h5zq.17: CAP- LAB: `fss-lab ingest --input <file> --root <dir>` runs the file-ingest adapter on the real stack and prints an import report

title: CAP- BLOCKED on owner decision fss-x4a.8.1: networked RTSP/RTP client over sockets (placeholder; do not start)
description:
## Status: BLOCKED on owner decision fss-x4a.8.1. DO NOT START; DO NOT ASSIGN.

This is the ONE placeholder for the networked-RTSP area, per the owner's steering decision #2
(2026-09-13): "Device I/O stays blocked ... networked RTSP and Asupersync (fss-x4a.8.1) remain
owner decisions: at most ONE placeholder bead per blocked area."

## Why it is blocked
- AGENTS.md: "Asupersync only for asynchronous orchestration; no Tokio adapters", and "`Cx` or an
  equivalent explicit authority reaches every I/O, time, sleep, lock, network ... boundary".
  fss-x4a.8.1 (FSS-021, integrate Asupersync `Cx` and the region hierarchy, P0) waits on the
  owner.
- RTSP over `std::net` is technically possible in safe std Rust, but it would bypass the
  `Cx`/Asupersync mandate.
- There is also no ADR naming the admitted device-I/O substrate. The reality check found "no ADR
  or DEP bead" for it.
- Security boundary: owner-authorized cameras only, no credential handling. RTSP digest or basic
  auth would require SecretHandle leases (SEC-003; there is no implementation bead) and so is out
  of scope even after unblocking, unless the owner decides otherwise.

## What it would do once unblocked (so the future self does not re-derive it)
- Replace the transcript byte source of RTSP2 with a `Cx`-authorized TCP connection to ONE
  owner-configured camera URL.
- No discovery or scanning (ONVIF WS-Discovery is a separate item).
- Bounded reconnect with typed backoff; no unbounded retry.
- Request -> drain -> finalize cancellation.
- Keepalive per the Session timeout.
- Every byte recorded into a transcript for replayable custody.
- The same pipeline: RTSP2 -> INGEST5/6 -> capsules -> ledger.
- Tests: TEST-RTSP-001 (fss-x4a.28.6) against a local test server lab fixture, GATE-030.

## Unblock checklist
1. The owner decides fss-x4a.8.1, or an ADR explicitly admits a sans-Asupersync interim.
2. A device-I/O substrate ADR.
3. A secret-free first camera, or a SecretHandle design.
4. RTSP3 is done.

title: CAP- DECODE: safe baseline JPEG decoder (SOF0, Huffman, integer IDCT, 4:4:4/4:2:0) into a u8 HWC fss_tensor::Tensor
description:
## What and why
Top-10 gap #6, "first pixels", and the first real caller of fss-tensor (vision goal #15: "no
consumer"). FSS-117 (fss-x4a.12.16, "safe JPEG/MJPEG reference decoder vertical slice", P0) is
the production item. It is blocked in the tracker by FSS-113 and FSS-054 and is not reshaped
here. This bead is the capability slice that makes pixels exist, and it cites FSS-117.

## Build
`crates/fss-reference/src/decode/jpeg.rs`. The location respects "zero new crates"; the planned
L3 crate fss-codec-mjpeg is the eventual home, which is an owner decision.
- `decode_baseline_jpeg(bytes, limits: JpegDecodeLimits, cx) -> Result<DecodedImage,
  JpegDecodeError>`.
- Supported: SOF0 baseline, 8-bit, 1 or 3 components, sampling (1x1) and (2x2 luma with 1x1
  chroma), i.e. 4:4:4 and 4:2:0 (add 4:2:2 if trivial); DQT (8-bit tables); DHT (up to 4 DC and
  4 AC tables); DRI and RSTn resync; APPn and COM skipped.
- Refused with a typed Unsupported{process}: progressive SOF2, extended 12-bit, lossless,
  arithmetic coding, 16-bit DQT, multi-scan, CMYK or Adobe transforms.
- Pipeline:
  1. Huffman decode with a bounded bit reader handling FF00 stuffing.
  2. DC prediction and restart.
  3. Dequantize.
  4. A deterministic INTEGER IDCT: fixed-point, the classic islow algorithm structure written
     from the spec, not copied code. Integer arithmetic makes output bit-identical across hosts.
  5. Chroma upsampling by replication (simple, deterministic; document it).
  6. JFIF YCbCr -> RGB in fixed point with clamping.
- Output: `fss_tensor::Tensor` with DType::U8 and shape [H, W, C], C = 1 or 3, built with
  Tensor::from_values and a Generation identifying the decoder generation
  (`decoder:fss-reference-jpeg-baseline@1`), plus `DecodedImage { tensor, width, height,
  components, sampling, decoder_generation }`.
- Limits, checked BEFORE allocation using checked multiplication: max_width, max_height (default
  8192), max_pixels (default 33_554_432), max_tensor_bytes (respect fss_tensor
  MAX_STORAGE_BYTES), max_huffman_symbols, max_restart_intervals. Cancellation checkpoint per MCU
  row.
- Errors: typed and stable, with no panic. Truncated entropy data is a typed Truncated{mcu_row}.
  Partial output is NOT returned as a valid image.

## Truth
A decoded tensor is DERIVED from custody bytes. It is not evidence by itself (AGENTS.md
prohibited shortcut). Lineage is DECODE2.

## Registration
- module_declarations decode/jpeg.rs -> "support" (codec utility). The tensor digest uses the
  already-registered fss.tensor.v1 domain.
- A new Cargo edge fss-reference -> fss-tensor (L7 -> L4, downward). fss-tensor is "implemented"
  in the topology, so this is not gated.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Related existing beads (context only, not blocking; this bead does not close them): fss-x4a.12.16, fss-x4a.28.4
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.40: CAP- DECODE JPEG (tests): PSNR vs source truth, pinned tensor goldens, unsupported/limit/truncation, mutation no-panic, e2e
  - fss-2h5zq.41: CAP- DECODE: decode receipt and source-to-tensor lineage (capsule source digest -> decoder generation -> tensor digest) published beside the capsule

## Refinement round 1 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- New blocking dependency: the fixture encoder (fss-2h5zq.5). The decoder's acceptance is defined
  against encoder ground truth.
- DType::U8 exists (dtype.rs, value 9). Build the tensor with Tensor::from_values(Shape [H,W,C],
  &[u8], Generation); read tensor.rs for the Shape and Generation constructors.
- Also expose the luma plane: `DecodedImage::luma() -> &[u8]` returns the Y samples before colour
  conversion, shape [H, W]; for grey images it is the only plane. DecodedImage also carries the
  luma sha256. fss-twin's GrayImage takes exactly such u8 luma bytes (CAP- TWIN, fss-2h5zq.68).
- fss_tensor::MAX_STORAGE_BYTES is 256 MiB, so the decoder's max_tensor_bytes default must not
  exceed it.

## Refinement round 3 (2026-09-13, verified against main 7168075)
- Generation: fss_tensor's Generation is fss_core::Generation(u64), so the string
  decoder:fss-reference-jpeg-baseline@1 cannot be the tensor's generation. The tensor gets a declared
  constant Generation(n). DecodedImage.decoder_generation carries the string
  decoder:fss-reference-jpeg-baseline:v1, which satisfies the subsystem-generation grammar (no '@').
- luma() contract: tightly packed, row-major, exactly W x H, cropped from the MCU-padded plane, full
  range; the exact post-IDCT, level-shifted, clamped Y samples that feed the colour converter; never
  re-derived from RGB.
- Two digests: luma_sha256 = ContentDigest::sha256(luma) (equal to fss-twin's pixels/storage value
  when row_stride = width) is distinct from tensor.content_digest(), which uses the fss.tensor.v1
  domain prefix (tensor.rs:362-364).
- 1-component scans are non-interleaved (T.81 A.2.2): the MCU is one 8x8 block whatever the declared
  H/V, and the block grid is ceil(W/8) x ceil(H/8).
- 3-component 4:2:0: a 16x16 MCU, chroma planes of ceil(W/2) x ceil(H/2), replication at (x/2, y/2)
  before cropping. Luma is unaffected by chroma upsampling.
- Output shapes: greyscale [H,W,1], byte-identical to luma(); colour [H,W,3] RGB.

title: CAP- fixtures H.264/rtpdump (tests): regeneration identity, structure checks, e2e manifest verification
description:
## Unit tests (crates/fss-reference/tests/media_fixture_h264_contract.rs)
- Regenerate every committed fixture and compare it byte for byte.
- Parse the generated Annex-B with an independent minimal start-code scan written in the test,
  not the production splitter, and check it against the manifest's expected spans.
- Emulation prevention: no 0x000000/0x000001/0x000002 inside NAL payloads, and 0x000003 inserted
  where needed.
- rtpdump: the header line is `#!rtpplay1.0 0.0.0.0/0`; record lengths sum to the file size; each
  RTP header has version 2 and PT 96. The wrap and ssrc_reset variants appear where the manifest
  says they do.
- The loss variant is missing exactly the listed sequence numbers.

## E2E (scripts/e2e/cap_fixtures_h264.sh)
- Recompute the sha256 of each file in tests/fixtures/media/{h264,rtp} and compare it with
  fixture_manifest.json, one JSON log step per file.
- If ffprobe is present, log its packet and NAL counts as a lab-oracle observation. If it is
  absent, log a skip.

title: CAP- DECODE: `fss-lab decode --input <mjpeg|jpeg> --root <dir>` ingests, decodes and prints per-frame tensor digests
description:
## What
A user-runnable decode: `fss-lab decode --input f.mjpeg --root D [--json]` runs LAB5's ingest,
then DECODE2 per capsule, and prints `fss.lab.decode_report.v1`:
- frames[] with capsule_id, source_digest, outcome, shape, tensor_digest and receipt_digest;
- totals by outcome;
- decoder_generation.

Never print pixel data. An optional `--dump-pgm <dir>` writes decoded frames as PGM/PPM (a
trivial first-party writer) for human eyeballing. It is off by default, and the report says the
dumped files are derived artifacts, not evidence.

title: CAP- EXEC: deterministic scalar reference executor over fss_model_ir::ModelIrGraph (Conv2d, Relu, Add, MaxPool2d, Sigmoid, MatMul, Reshape, Softmax)
description:
## What and why
Top-10 gap #7, "first inference", and the first real caller of fss-model-ir (vision goal #17:
execution NOT_STARTED; only fss-reference's scripted MockModelExecutor exists). FSS-139
(fss-x4a.14.10, "scalar operator executor for first detector graph", P0) is blocked in the
tracker by FSS-137 (IR v1, fss-x4a.14.8, in progress) and FSS-138 (package importer). This bead
is the capability slice and cites FSS-139 without closing it.

## Build
`crates/fss-reference/src/scalar_executor.rs`. The planned home is fss-model-runtime /
fss-kernel-cpu, which is an owner decision.
- `ScalarExecutor::run(graph: &ModelIrGraph, inputs: &[(port, Tensor)], budget: ExecBudget, cx)
  -> Result<ExecOutcome, ExecError>`.
- Validate first with fss_model_ir::GraphValidator. Check shapes with infer_operator_outputs
  against the actual inputs; a mismatch is a typed ShapeMismatch.
- Execute nodes in the graph's canonical topological order. The order is fixed by the IR's
  canonical digest ordering, so execution is deterministic.
- Kernels, all f32 unless the IR says otherwise, with a FIXED accumulation order for bit
  reproducibility:
  - Conv2d NCHW with the stride/padding/dilation/groups attributes exactly as declared in
    fss-model-ir op.rs OperatorSpec. Read the spec; do not invent attribute names.
  - Relu, Sigmoid (a documented, deterministic formula).
  - Add, Sub, Mul, Div with broadcasting via fss_model_ir::broadcast_shapes.
  - MaxPool2d, MatMul, Reshape, Softmax (max-subtraction, fixed reduction order).
  - Every other OpCode (Gelu, Silu, Tanh, Transpose, Squeeze, Unsqueeze, Concat, Slice,
    LayerNorm, RMSNorm, Embedding) returns a typed UnsupportedOperator{op} BEFORE execution
    starts. Never partial execution.
- Budget: MACs and bytes are computed from the inferred shapes before running. Over budget gives a
  typed BudgetExceeded without executing. Cancellation checkpoint per node, request -> drain ->
  finalize; no partial outputs escape.
- u8 HWC decoder tensors are converted by an explicit, recorded preprocessing node or function
  (u8 -> f32 scale 1/255, HWC -> NCHW). Preprocessing identity is part of the receipt (EXEC2),
  never implicit.

## Considerations
- fss-x4a.14.8 is still in progress and may change the IR API. Pin to the current API, keep the
  adapter layer thin, and re-check its status before starting. If it is mid-refactor, coordinate
  via agent mail.
- Registration: module_declarations scalar_executor.rs -> "cognition" (model execution produces
  cognition). New Cargo edges fss-reference -> fss-model-ir and fss-tensor (downward, L7 -> L4).

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Related existing beads (context only, not blocking; this bead does not close them): fss-x4a.14.10, fss-x4a.14.8
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.46: CAP- EXEC scalar executor (tests): hand-computed goldens per kernel, determinism, unsupported/budget/cancel, e2e
  - fss-2h5zq.47: CAP- EXEC: model invocation receipt bound to graph digest, input/output tensor digests, preprocessing and executor generation (model_execution_receipt.v1)

## Refinement round 1 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- Weights: fss-model-ir v1 has no constant or initializer nodes at 8b96911 (graph.rs, node.rs and
  port.rs define none). Every weight therefore enters as a named graph input. ScalarExecutor::run
  binds weight tensors by input port name; the activity package (fss-2h5zq.49) supplies them from
  verified blobs.
- Attribute names come from OperatorSpec in op.rs. Conv2d uses strides, padding, dilations and
  groups; MaxPool2d uses kernel_size, padding and strides. Read OperatorSpec for the exact types.
- Execution order: GraphValidator::validate, then GraphValidator::topological_sort
  (validator.rs:273), which is the IR's own order. The graph digest is compute_model_ir_digest
  (domain fss.model_ir.v1).
- The OpCode set has 22 opcodes: Add, Sub, Mul, Div, Relu, Gelu, Silu, Sigmoid, Tanh, MatMul,
  Reshape, Transpose, Squeeze, Unsqueeze, Concat, Slice, LayerNorm, RMSNorm, Softmax, Conv2d,
  MaxPool2d and Embedding. Dispatch with an exhaustive match (no wildcard arm), so a new opcode is a
  compile error, never a silent pass.
- fss-x4a.14.8 (FSS-137) is still in progress at 8b96911. Re-check its notes before starting.

## Refinement round 2 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- OperatorSpec attribute types and defaults (op.rs, verified):
  - Conv2d takes 2 to 3 inputs (X, W, optional bias B). Attributes:
    - dilations: IntList, default [1,1];
    - groups: Int, default 1;
    - padding: IntList, default [0,0,0,0], ordered [top, left, bottom, right]
      (shape_inference.rs:1279);
    - strides: IntList, default [1,1].
  - MaxPool2d takes 1 input. Attributes: kernel_size (IntList, required), ceil_mode (Bool, default
    false), padding (IntList, default [0,0,0,0]; each pad must be strictly less than the kernel
    extent), strides (IntList, default [1,1]).
  - Softmax: axis, Int, default -1.
  - Reshape: shape (IntList, required) and allowzero (Bool, default false).
  - Add, Sub, Mul, Div, Relu, Sigmoid and MatMul take no attributes.
  - AttrValue is {Bool, Int(i64), Float(f64), String, IntList(Vec<i64>), FloatList(Vec<f64>),
    DType, Shape}. Read attributes with AttrValue::as_usize_list, as_int and as_bool, and apply the
    OperatorSpec default when an attribute is absent.
- dtypes: shape inference rejects non-float inputs to float ops with DTypeMismatch (expected F32).
  The executor runs F32 only and refuses anything else with a typed UnsupportedDType before
  execution.
- Shapes are concrete (fss_tensor::Shape of usize), so a graph has one fixed input shape. Take every
  output shape from fss_model_ir::infer_operator_outputs and never re-derive it. This matters: the
  fss-x4a.14.8 candidate a20fa6c (NOT on main) changes Reshape so that a 0 dimension copies the input
  dimension unless allowzero is set.
- a20fa6c API deltas, to absorb only if it lands first:
  - ModelIrVersion::Unsupported now wraps UnsupportedVersion, and ModelIrVersion::unsupported(n)
    returns a Result;
  - verify_operator_table_digest and order_independent_num_elements are new exports;
  - Concat's axis becomes optional, with negative axes;
  - GraphValidator::topological_sort moves from validator.rs:273 to :292.
  Keep version handling behind one helper so either signature is a one-line change, and never match
  on the Unsupported payload.
- Transcendentals: f32::exp calls the platform libm, which is not bit-identical across hosts.
  Sigmoid and Softmax use a first-party deterministic exp: range reduction plus a fixed polynomial,
  using only IEEE +, -, * and /, and documented with its maximum relative error. Never call
  mul_add.
- Weight inputs are graph inputs, so they must carry the graph generation (GraphValidator's
  generation-uniformity rule).
- Preprocessing is outside the IR, which has no cast or resize op. It covers u8 HWC -> f32 NCHW,
  luma selection, and any resize to the fixed input shape. It is a canonical PreprocessProgram value
  whose digest goes into the receipt (fss-2h5zq.47).

## Refinement round 3 (2026-09-13, verified against main 7168075)
fss-x4a.14.8 is closed. Its round-5 commits (6a2791e, 7168075) are on main, so the round-2
"a20fa6c, absorb only if it lands" block is superseded by these verified facts:
- Versions: parse only with ModelIrVersion::from_u32 (graph.rs:72; anything but 1 is
  VersionMismatch). UnsupportedVersion is opaque (private field, graph.rs:14-38): use as_u32() or
  is_supported(), never match on its payload.
- verify_operator_table_digest(&expected, &actual) is pure (op.rs:791); verify_operator_table_frozen()
  (op.rs:811) recomputes and compares with OPERATOR_TABLE_FREEZE_DIGEST. GraphValidator::validate
  re-verifies the freeze on every call (validator.rs:85) and compute_model_ir_digest validates
  internally, so call each once per run.
- Order: GraphValidator::topological_sort(graph, &producer_map) is pub at validator.rs:292. Build the
  ProducerId map exactly as canonical.rs:66-77 does, so execution order equals digest order.
- infer_operator_outputs(node_id, op, &[&TensorPort], &output_names, &attrs, generation)
  (shape_inference.rs:68); order_independent_num_elements (validator.rs:48) is exported.
- Defaults: OperatorSpec.default_value is free text pinned by the freeze digest (op.rs:98; for example
  "[1, 1]" or "none"). Never parse it. Mirror the defaults hard-coded in infer_operator_outputs and
  canonical.rs::normalize_attributes (148-327). Read groups with as_usize. Never read Reshape's shape
  with as_usize_list: it may contain -1, and the Shape-for-IntList pin (op.rs:106-124) admits an
  AttrValue::Shape for the attributes named shape and normalized_shape only. Take Reshape's output
  shape from infer_operator_outputs, which follows ONNX: -1 is inferred, 0 copies the input dim
  unless allowzero, and allowzero with a 0 dim fails validation with ShapeMismatch
  (shape_inference.rs:309-475).
- Padding order [top, left, bottom, right]: shape_inference.rs:1337-1347 (Conv2d) and 1497-1507
  (MaxPool2d); the round-2 citation :1279 is stale. MaxPool2d honours the ceil_mode last-window clamp
  (1547-1588): a window that would start at or past the input plus the left pad is dropped, and
  window positions in the padding are skipped, never read as 0.
- dtypes: the IR requires a float input only for unary activations, the norms and Softmax, and admits
  F16, BF16 and F64 there; Add, Sub, Mul, MatMul, Conv2d and MaxPool2d accept integer dtypes
  (dtype.rs:96-97; shape_inference.rs:153, 248, 1438). The executor's F32-only gate is therefore the
  only dtype guard, and it runs before execution.
- Generations: weight inputs carry the graph generation, which is fss_core::Generation(u64)
  (ids.rs:360), not the ModelGeneration string of the package (fss-2h5zq.49).

title: CAP- EXEC scalar executor (tests): hand-computed goldens per kernel, determinism, unsupported/budget/cancel, e2e
description:
## Tests (crates/fss-reference/tests/scalar_executor_contract.rs)
- A per-kernel golden with small hand-computed tensors: 3x3 conv on 5x5 with padding 1 and
  stride 2, broadcasting Add [1,C,1,1] + [N,C,H,W], MaxPool2d, MatMul, and so on.
- Metamorphic checks: conv with a delta kernel equals the input; Relu is idempotent; Softmax sums
  to 1 within 1e-6 and is invariant to adding a constant.
- Bit-identical repeated runs.
- A graph with Gelu gives UnsupportedOperator and zero executed nodes.
- Budget and cancellation cases.

## E2E (scripts/e2e/cap_exec_scalar.sh)
Per kernel case, log the graph canonical digest, input and output tensor digests versus the
goldens, MACs and the outcome.

- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Blocked by (must finish first):
  - fss-2h5zq.45: CAP- EXEC: deterministic scalar reference executor over fss_model_ir::ModelIrGraph (Conv2d, Relu, Add, MaxPool2d, Sigmoid, MatMul, Reshape, Softmax)
  - fss-2h5zq.1: CAP- e2e harness: scripts/e2e/lib.sh structured JSON-lines logging and runner
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.63: CAP- QUALIFY: whole-bridge verification on green main (rust+policy lanes, all CAP e2e scripts) and honest status/doc update

- Test weight-input binding. A missing weight port gives a typed error before any execution.
- Cover each unsupported opcode explicitly.
- Print CAPLOG lines per kernel case.

## Refinement round 2 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- Add goldens for:
  - MaxPool2d with ceil_mode true and false;

  - Conv2d with a bias input, and with groups > 1.
- The exp routine: check vectors against an f64 reference within the documented bound, and pin its
  bit patterns.
- A non-F32 input is refused before execution.
- The version helper is covered.
- A Reshape case whose output shape comes from infer_operator_outputs, so the test holds on both
  main and a20fa6c.

- Reshape goldens (replace "holds on both main and a20fa6c"): shape [0,-1] with allowzero false

  graph built with unsupported(2)? is refused by validate.
- ceil_mode equality-boundary cases, where the clamp drops the last window, for height and width
  (mirroring the tests 7168075 added to the IR contract test).
- dtype refusal uses an F16 Relu graph and an I32 Add graph; both pass IR validation, which proves
  the executor gate is the one refusing them.

operatorTraceDigest, decisionPathDigest and shadowComparison. Nothing produces it.

## Build
`crates/fss-reference/src/model_receipt.rs`: `ModelInvocationReceipt` populates the schema fields
that the scalar path can honestly fill:
- inputRoots = DECODE2 receipt or tensor digests;
- modelPackageRoot = EXEC3's package root, or "none: inline test graph";
- executionPlanDigest = the canonical fss.model_ir.v1 graph digest plus the node order;
- backend = "scalar-reference";
- numericPolicyDigest = the documented f32 and accumulation-order policy;
- budget and usage (MACs, bytes);
- outcome, errorId, outputRoot, operatorTraceDigest (a hash chain over per-node output digests).

Fields that cannot be filled (shadowComparison, activationGeneration without an activation
system) are set to explicit not_applicable or unknown values the schema allows. If the schema
lacks a representation, record a schema finding; never omit or null silently.
- Canonical binary encoding: if a digest domain for model execution receipts is not yet
  registered in registries/DIGEST_DOMAINS.md, add SCHEMA-DOMAIN-MODEL-EXECUTION-RECEIPT-001
  `fss.model_execution_receipt.v1` and bump the count.
- The receipt is staged and published and referenced from the ledger, like decode receipts.

## Refinement round 2 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
Verified schema facts (schemas/model_execution_receipt.v1.json; additionalProperties is false at
every level):
- Every digest field uses sensor_capsule.v1.json#/$defs/digest, whose pattern is
  ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*:[0-9a-f]{32,}$. ContentDigest's Display, "sha256:<64 hex>", matches.
  Placeholder strings such as "none: inline test graph" or "not_applicable" do NOT validate, and
  required digests cannot be null.
- Required fields:
  - schema, the const "fss.model_execution_receipt.v1";
  - jobId, 1 to 256 characters;
  - inputRoots, 1 to 4096 digests;
  - the digests modelPackageRoot, activationGeneration, preprocessProgram, postprocessProgram,
    operatorRegistryGeneration, executionPlanDigest, numericPolicyDigest and decisionPathDigest;
  - backend {id (≤128), implementation (≤256), hardware (≤512), featureSet (≤128 strings)};
  - budget and usage, each {inputBytes, outputBytes, peakBytes, workUnits, wallNs}, integers ≥ 0;
  - outcome, one of ok, error, cancelled, panicked, oom, budget_exhausted, indeterminate.
  Optional: batch, cancelReason, errorId, outputRoot and operatorTraceDigest (each also nullable),
  and shadowComparison.
Field mapping (deterministic; document it in model_receipt.rs):
- jobId: "exec:" + a hex prefix of sha256 over (the capsule id or test-case id, the model
  generation, the input roots).
- inputRoots: decode-receipt digests in the pipeline; input tensor digests in unit tests.
- modelPackageRoot: the verified package root from fss-2h5zq.49. For inline test graphs, a
  sentinel (defined below).
- activationGeneration: always the sentinel "unactivated_reference_run", because no activation
  system exists.
- preprocessProgram and postprocessProgram: digests of the canonical PreprocessProgram and
  PostprocessProgram descriptors. An identity postprocess has its own descriptor; it is not a
  sentinel.
- operatorRegistryGeneration: fss_model_ir::OPERATOR_TABLE_FREEZE_DIGEST, parsed with
  ContentDigest::parse.
- executionPlanDigest: sha256 over a domain-separated encoding of (compute_model_ir_digest(graph),
  the topological node-id order, the bound input port names).
- numericPolicyDigest: the digest of the numeric-policy descriptor (F32, fixed accumulation order,
  the exp routine's version, no FMA, virtual wall time).
- decisionPathDigest: the digest of the ordered per-node dispatch record (node id, opcode, kernel
  variant id, resolved attributes). It is the path the executor actually took.
- backend: {id "scalar-reference", implementation "fss-reference scalar_executor@1", hardware
  "host-independent-scalar", featureSet ["f32", "fixed-order", "no-fma"] plus one
  "sentinel:<field>=<reason>" entry per sentinel}.
- budget and usage:
  - workUnits is MACs, budgeted and used;
  - byte counts come from the inferred shapes;
  - wallNs is ReplayCx VirtualClock time, so it is deterministic.
  Host wall time appears only in logs (duration_ms), never in a receipt.
- outcome:
  - ok;
  - error, for UnsupportedOperator, UnsupportedDType, ShapeMismatch or a missing weight, with
    errorId = the stable error id;
  - budget_exhausted;
  - cancelled, with cancelReason = the ReplayCx stage.
  The scalar path never produces panicked, oom or indeterminate; document why.
- outputRoot and operatorTraceDigest are set on ok and null otherwise. shadowComparison is null.
Sentinels:
- A required digest with no honest value is sha256 over the domain-separated text
  "fss.model_execution_receipt.v1/sentinel/<field>/<reason>".
- It is listed in backend.featureSet and in the Rust receipt's explicit sentinel list.
- Record a schema finding for the owner: the schema cannot express not_applicable for a required
  digest. Do not edit the schema.
Instance validation:
- No repository tool validates JSON instances. scripts/schema_validate.py checks schema documents
  and the registry constitution only.
- This bead therefore adds scripts/json_instance_validate.py, stdlib only, a strict Draft 2020-12
  subset:
  - keywords: type (including type arrays), const, enum, required, properties,
    additionalProperties (false or a schema), pattern, minLength and maxLength, minimum, minItems
    and maxItems, items, anyOf, and $ref across files in schemas/;
  - it REFUSES any keyword it does not implement, instead of ignoring it.
  fss-2h5zq.48 tests it.
- MODEL-RECEIPT-001 (architecture/model_runtime_registry.json) names fss-model-runtime (planned) as
  owner, with status "specified". This reference producer does not change that row.

## Refinement round 3 (2026-09-13, verified against main 7168075)
Corrections from a review of the round-2 receipt design against the schema, fss-core and the
policy lane:
- Superseded: the round-0 Build lines modelPackageRoot = "none: inline test graph" and "explicit
  not_applicable or unknown values the schema allows". The schema admits neither.
- modelPackageRoot is VerificationReceipt.manifest_digest (fss-object model_package.rs:855-865);
  fss-object has no "package root". operatorRegistryGeneration: call verify_operator_table_frozen()
  (op.rs:811) before emitting OPERATOR_TABLE_FREEZE_DIGEST. compute_model_ir_digest already binds the
  operator-table digest, the u64 generation and the canonical order, so adding the node order to
  executionPlanDigest is redundant but harmless. jobId uses the ModelGeneration string (for example
  model:fss-activity:v1).
- Sentinels use a DISTINCT scheme, never sha256:. A sentinel is "fss-na:" followed by the 64-hex
  sha256 of the declared text "fss.model_execution_receipt.v1/sentinel/<field>/<reason>". The schema
  pattern accepts it, a reader sees it in the field itself, and ContentDigest::parse refuses it
  (digest.rs:208-230 accepts only sha256 and blake3 with 64 hex), so no Rust consumer can mistake it
  for content. A sha256:-form sentinel would disguise "not applicable" as a real digest, which
  AGENTS.md prohibits. In Rust the field is an enum such as ReceiptDigest::{Content(ContentDigest),
  NotApplicable{field, reason}}, never a bare ContentDigest. The featureSet entry
  sentinel:<field>=<reason> stays, at most 128 characters.
- Evidence rule: a receipt with any fss-na: field is never activation-backed model evidence
  (MODEL-RECEIPT-001: "Only a valid output root and execution receipt can become model-derived
  evidence"). activationGeneration is a sentinel on every reference receipt, so publication and
  ledger consumers label these receipts reference-only.
- Schema nuance: additionalProperties is false at every level EXCEPT shadowComparison.metrics
  (schema-valued {"type":"number"}, lines 244-249).
- Validator (scripts/json_instance_validate.py) semantics, replacing the round-2 keyword list:
  - accept the annotation and container keywords $schema, $id, title, description, $comment and $defs
    without asserting anything;
  - refuse unknown keywords only in subschemas statically reachable from the root through properties,
    items, anyOf, additionalProperties and $ref. sensor_capsule.v1.json itself uses allOf, if/then/else
    and not, so a whole-file scan would refuse every receipt;
  - a type-specific keyword applies only when the instance has that type (maxLength on a null
    cancelReason; properties on a null shadowComparison);
  - bool is neither integer nor number; const and enum compare type-strictly (in Python 1 == True and
    1 == 1.0);
  - parse with parse_constant rejecting NaN and Infinity and an object_pairs_hook rejecting duplicate
    keys, matching the Rust capsule decoder;
  - pattern uses ECMA-style end anchoring: Python's $ also matches before a trailing newline, so
    anchor with \Z (or fullmatch);
  - resolve $ref against the $id base by reusing schema_validate.SchemaCatalog loading
    (scripts/schema_validate.py:193, :840-918), unescape ~0 and ~1 in JSON pointers, and refuse targets
    outside schemas/.
- Digest domains: the receipt uses several domain-separated encodings (jobId derivation, execution
  plan, numeric-policy descriptor, decision path, pre/postprocess descriptors, trace chain, sentinel
  text). Register ONE row, SCHEMA-DOMAIN-MODEL-EXECUTION-RECEIPT-001, whose invariant lists the fixed
  sub-tags fss.model_execution_receipt.v1/<part>. The count delta is +1 from HEAD.
- Policy lane: qualify.sh lists its Python tests explicitly (scripts/qualify.sh:226-260). Add a run
  line for tests/test_json_instance_validate.py and a py_compile entry for the validator;
  scripts/qualify.sh is a shared hot file (edit only your lines).
- The receipt objects are reachable from a durable ledgered root (fss-2h5zq.23 round-3 rule), so
  doctor stays clean.

## Shared rules for every CAP- bead (repeated so this bead stands alone)

Context: parent epic "CAP- Capability bridge: file-ingest-first end-to-end" (fss-2h5zq), created
2026-09-13 from the Phase-1 reality check at main 474931d and the owner's binding steering
decisions. The epic holds the full background; the essentials are repeated here.

- Constitution (AGENTS.md): Rust 2024 on nightly-2026-08-31. `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` in every
  crate, target, test, example and helper, with no exception path. Zero third-party crates: the
  dependency closure is fss-* only, and DEP-EXCEPTION-001 admits nothing. This bridge also adds
  ZERO new workspace crates. New code lands as modules in existing crates, mainly fss-reference and
  fss-cli. Moving the code into the planned L3/L4 crates (fss-codec-mjpeg, fss-container,
  fss-device-core, fss-model-runtime, fss-kernel-cpu, fss-coverage) is a later owner decision,
  because a new member trips the crate_topology and member-count pins (see fss-1bd1l).
- Do NOT edit crates/fss-packet/** (the owner's crate). Use its public API as-is:
  RtpPacket::parse, SequenceTracker, H264Depacketizer, NalUnit, SenderReportClock and
  JitterEstimator. Any change that needs fss-packet edits goes to an owner bead and is never
  assigned to an agent.
- No device I/O: no camera, USB, V4L2 or socket code; no `std::net` or `TcpStream`. Inputs are
  recorded files and recorded transcripts only. Every file read goes through an explicit I/O
  authority value, following the ReplayIoAuthority/ReplayCx pattern in
  crates/fss-reference/src/adapter_replay.rs, with cooperative cancellation checkpoints
  (request -> drain -> finalize). Asupersync `Cx` is NOT admitted yet (owner decision
  fss-x4a.8.1). Do not add Tokio or any other runtime.
- Security boundary: fixtures are synthetic and generated first-party. No third-party footage, no
  identifiable people, no captured network addresses. Never handle credentials: RTSP auth headers
  are detected and refused, never computed or stored. No scanning. Logs never contain secrets or
  private media bytes; they carry digests and byte spans only.
- Truth discipline:
  - A decoded frame is not retained evidence without source custody.
  - File import has no live continuity, so it never certifies absence. Negative reads stay
    unknown or not_observable.
  - File mtime is not capture time. Use ClockBasis::Estimated with an explicit, wide
    CaptureInterval unless the stream itself carries timing.
  - One camera's model score is never "corroborated".
  - unknown, not_observable, stale and indeterminate are never flattened to null, low confidence
    or omission.
- Registration, done in the same commit as the code:
  1. Every new .rs module under crates/fss-core or crates/fss-reference gets a
     `module_declarations` entry in architecture/semantic_plane_registry.json with its plane
     (authority | cognition | effect | support | ambiguous).
     scripts/semantic_plane_checker.py audits exactly those two crates and fails otherwise.
  2. Every new canonical digest or encoding domain tag gets a row in registries/DIGEST_DOMAINS.md
     (ID SCHEMA-DOMAIN-<NAME>-001, domain fss.<name>.v1, scope, authority, invariant rule).
     Bump ALL THREE pinned domain counts in the same commit: the two digestDomainCount
     assertions in tests/test_schema_validate.py AND the domain_count assertion (and its
     message) in crates/fss-model-ir/tests/model_ir_contract.rs:420 (45 at main 7168075;
     verified in refinement round 3). Count from the value on HEAD at commit time, because several CAP
     beads add domains in parallel.
  3. Every new or changed source path gets a row in MANIFEST.delta.sha256 per ADR-0013. Never
     edit the MANIFEST.sha256 base. Check with `python3 scripts/manifest_audit.py`.
  4. New crate dependency edges must point downward in architecture/crate_topology.json. Layers:
     L2 ledger/object/publication, L3 fss-packet, L4 tensor/model-ir/geometry, L6 fss-cli,
     L7 fss-reference. fss-cli -> fss-reference is the one waived inversion. Check with
     `python3 scripts/dependency_dag_checker.py`.
  5. New CLI error and exit identities get rows in registries/ERRORS.md, and the operation
     crosswalk (architecture/operation_crosswalk.json and crates/fss-cli/src/crosswalk.rs) stays
     consistent.
- Verification (remote only):
  - `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- cargo test -p <crate> --all-targets --no-fail-fast --locked --offline`
  - `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets --keep-going --locked --offline -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo fmt --check`
  - `scripts/qualify.sh --lane policy`
  - `--all-targets` does NOT run doctests. When the crate has doc examples, also run
    `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- cargo test -p <crate> --doc --no-fail-fast --locked --offline`.
  - Launch rch from the repo directory with `--base <sha>`. Decide pass or fail by exit code (rch
    output is ANSI-coloured; strip ANSI before counting diagnostics). Re-run Python checkers and
    e2e scripts on a fresh `git worktree add --detach` checkout, never only in the shared tree.

  Main is currently red for reasons outside this bead (fss-kr9n3, fss-1bd1l, fss-lc2r1). Until
  those land, report "no new findings attributable to this bead's files". Never weaken a gate.
- E2E convention: every test bead ships scripts/e2e/cap_<name>.sh using the shared helpers in
  scripts/e2e/lib.sh (see the "CAP- e2e harness" bead).
  - Logs are JSON lines under ${FSS_E2E_LOG_DIR:-target/e2e-logs}/<name>/. The first record is an
    env record (git sha, bead id, binary sha256s, host triple, FSS_* settings); then one record per
    step: {ts, script, bead, step, cmd, exit, duration_ms, expected, observed, digest,
    stdout_sha256, stdout_excerpt, stderr_excerpt, verdict, repro}. Rust tests feed the log by
    printing one-line `CAPLOG {json}` records under --nocapture; lib.sh ingests them (ANSI
    stripped) through e2e_cargo_test. scripts/e2e/validate_log.py checks every record.
  - The final record is {"step":"summary","verdict":"pass"|"fail","steps":N,"failures":[...]}.
  - Scripts exit non-zero on any mismatch. They are deterministic (fixed seeds, no wall clock
    inside digests) and bounded in size, and they print a one-line reproduction command.
- Known gotchas (verified at main 8b96911, refinement round 1):
  - scripts/dependency_audit.py (DEP-AUD-022) scans every .rs file, tests and examples included,
    for the bare word unsafe. Comments are masked but string literals are NOT, so never put that
    word in a string literal or a guard-test pattern. The only allowed occurrence is
    #![forbid(unsafe_code)].
  - The workspace has 11 members since the twin merge (f9004ef, f5ed038). fss-twin (L4,
    "implemented") depends on fss-geometry. Treat crates/fss-twin/** and crates/fss-geometry/**
    as owner-authored upstream code, like fss-packet: use their public API and record API gaps in
    notes instead of editing them.
  - Shared hot files (edit only your own rows or lines; stage with `git add -p`):
    registries/DIGEST_DOMAINS.md, tests/test_schema_validate.py,
    crates/fss-model-ir/tests/model_ir_contract.rs (the third domain-count pin),
    architecture/semantic_plane_registry.json, MANIFEST.delta.sha256, registries/ERRORS.md,
    crates/fss-reference/src/lib.rs, crates/fss-reference/Cargo.toml and
    crates/fss-cli/src/lab_cmd.rs.
  - LocalRootPublisher::open and StagingSpool::open create directories and take exclusive lock
    files, so they are not read-only. Read-only inspection goes through fss-2h5zq.66.
- Swarm hygiene:
  - One bead per commit, with the bead id in the subject.
  - Commit only files you own. Never `git add -A`. Never reset, amend or rebase main.
  - Commit only what compiles against committed HEAD, and commit type changes together with all
    their users.
  - Record final paths and evidence with `br update <id> --append-notes`. Never use --notes,
    which overwrites the field.

## Tests (crates/fss-reference/tests/model_receipt_contract.rs)
- Per outcome, a receipt is produced and emitted as JSON. A small Python test in tests/ validates
  the emitted JSON against the schema with the repo's validator.
- The trace-digest chain recomputes.
- Determinism.

## E2E (scripts/e2e/cap_exec_receipt.sh)
Run the executor cases and log the receipt digests and schema-validation verdicts per case.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Blocked by (must finish first):
  - fss-2h5zq.47: CAP- EXEC: model invocation receipt bound to graph digest, input/output tensor digests, preprocessing and executor generation (model_execution_receipt.v1)
  - fss-2h5zq.1: CAP- e2e harness: scripts/e2e/lib.sh structured JSON-lines logging and runner
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.63: CAP- QUALIFY: whole-bridge verification on green main (rust+policy lanes, all CAP e2e scripts) and honest status/doc update

## Refinement round 2 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- tests/test_json_instance_validate.py (policy-lane discovery) checks:
  - validator positives on every emitted receipt;
  - planted invalid instances: a placeholder string in a digest field, a missing required field, an
    extra property, a bad outcome enum, a negative integer, and inputRoots empty or longer than
    4096;
  - that the validator refuses a schema containing a keyword it does not implement;
  - that a $ref to sensor_capsule.v1.json#/$defs/digest resolves.
- The sentinel digests recompute from their declared texts, and the featureSet lists exactly the
  sentinel fields.
- wallNs is identical across two runs and across two roots.

## Refinement round 3 (2026-09-13, verified against main 7168075)
- Discovery: qualify.sh runs an explicit list, so the test runs because fss-2h5zq.47 adds its line;
  "policy-lane discovery" is not automatic.
- Planted-invalid cases add: a digest with a trailing newline, true in an integer field, NaN in
  metrics, a duplicate key, and null in a required digest.
- The validator refuses a schema that uses oneOf or uniqueItems, and does NOT refuse the receipt
  schema even though sensor_capsule.v1.json contains allOf, if/then/else and not.
- Rust side: every non-sentinel digest round-trips through ContentDigest::parse (the schema accepts
  32 hex, Rust requires 64); every sentinel uses the fss-na: scheme and fails that parse.
- When the third-party jsonschema package happens to be importable, cross-check the verdicts, as
  tests/test_negative_evidence_report_schema.py does, and log a skip otherwise. It is never a
  dependency.

title: CAP- EXEC: first-party 'activity' model graph packaged as an immutable model package and loaded only through the fss-object verifier
description:
## What and why
AGENTS.md prohibits "Downloading 'latest' model weights at runtime". Immutable model generations
are required. fss-object already has a WORKING package verifier (model_package.rs:
import_from_directory, import_package, verify_package, verify_contents; model_license_policy.rs)
that no real model has ever passed through (vision goal #16). This bead makes the executor's
first model a real, first-party, license-clean package.

## Build
- A tiny, hand-specified activity graph:
  1. input: u8 HWC frame, via the recorded preprocessing to f32 NCHW greyscale;
  2. Conv2d with a fixed 3x3 Sobel-like edge kernel;
  3. Relu;
  4. MaxPool2d (coarse);
  5. a MatMul/Add reduction to a scalar;
  6. Sigmoid -> activity score in [0, 1].
- Weights are literal constants in source with a documented derivation. There is no training and
  no external weights, and the license is first-party.
- The package is built by a deterministic builder (`crates/fss-reference/src/activity_model.rs`)
  into a manifest plus tensor blobs in the exact layout fss-object's importer expects. Read
  model_package.rs; do not invent a format.
- The committed package goes under tests/fixtures/models/activity-v1/, with its package root
  digest pinned.
- Load path: executor input graphs come ONLY from a verified package (verify_package OK plus the
  license policy allowing it). An unverified or tampered package gives a typed refusal.
- Model generation id: `model:fss-activity@1`. Scores from different generations are never mixed
  (AGENTS.md).
- Semantics: the score means "pixel-change/edge activity", NOT a person or intrusion detector.
  The label vocabulary passed to the policy must say so, e.g. MockSemanticLabel-equivalent
  "activity" or "unknown motion". Never claim a detection class it cannot support.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Blocked by (must finish first):
  - fss-2h5zq.47: CAP- EXEC: model invocation receipt bound to graph digest, input/output tensor digests, preprocessing and executor generation (model_execution_receipt.v1)
- Related existing beads (context only, not blocking; this bead does not close them): fss-x4a.14.9
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.50: CAP- EXEC activity package (tests): verify/tamper/license, generation isolation, score goldens, e2e
  - fss-2h5zq.51: CAP- EXEC: route the fss-reference mock-model seam through the scalar executor for one lab scenario (executor-backed observations into policy)

## Refinement round 1 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- New blocking dependencies: the decoder (fss-2h5zq.39) and the fixture encoder (fss-2h5zq.5). The
  acceptance pins a score golden for each DECODE fixture.
- Weights are package tensor blobs bound to named graph inputs; the IR has no constants (see
  fss-2h5zq.45).
- The loader API was verified in crates/fss-object/src/model_package.rs:
  - import_from_directory(&mut self, dir, io: &dyn SpoolIo, expected_generation);
  - import_package;
  - verify_package(manifest_digest) -> VerificationReceipt;
  - ModelPackage::verify_contents.
  The license policy is in model_license_policy.rs. Pin expected_generation to
  `model:fss-activity@1`.

## Refinement round 2 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- IR shapes are concrete, so the activity graph declares ONE fixed input: [1,1,32,32] F32 (luma
  only).
- The PreprocessProgram:
  1. selects the luma plane (DecodedImage::luma, fss-2h5zq.39);
  2. resizes deterministically to 32x32: an integer fixed-point box filter when downscaling, and
     nearest replication when upscaling (for example 16x16);
  3. maps u8 to f32 by dividing by 255.
  Its canonical descriptor digest is the receipt's preprocessProgram. Scores from different frame
  sizes are comparable only through this recorded resize, and the builder says so.
- The IR has no reduce op, so the scalar reduction is:
  - Reshape [1,C,H,W] -> [1,K];
  - MatMul with a [K,1] weight of 1/K (a mean);
  - Add a [1,1] bias;
  - Sigmoid.
  Every weight (the conv kernel, the mean vector, the bias) is a package blob bound to a graph input
  that carries the graph generation.
- Score goldens are pinned with the executor's first-party exp (fss-2h5zq.45).

## Refinement round 3 (2026-09-13, verified against main 7168075)
The package layout is now verified against fss-object at 7168075; three round-2 assumptions were
wrong and would have made acceptance impossible.
- Generation id: model:fss-activity@1 is INVALID. ModelGeneration must match
  ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9:+._-]{7,255}$ (fss-core ids.rs:40-55, 620-631), so '@' fails every import. Use
  model:fss-activity:v1, mapped explicitly to the IR's Generation(1).
- A package holds exactly the artifacts {weights_digest} + {license.text_digest} +
  license.artifact_digests (collect_expected_digests, model_package.rs:612-622). There is no graph
  field, tensor table or child manifest, and the manifest has a single weights_digest
  (model_manifest.rs:698-715). license.artifact_digests means upstream provenance, so it must not
  carry extra tensors. The package therefore holds ONE weights artifact: a first-party canonical
  weight bundle (a magic, the pinned compute_model_ir_digest of the activity graph, then named
  tensors, each with name, dtype F32, shape and little-endian f32 bytes). Register its encoding as a
  new digest domain (for example SCHEMA-DOMAIN-REFERENCE-WEIGHT-BUNDLE-001
  fss.reference_weight_bundle.v1) and bump all three count pins. fss-tensor has no canonical tensor
  byte codec (only Tensor::content_digest), so this is an interim reference codec; FSS-138
  (fss-x4a.14.9) owns the real one.
- There is no IR decoder, so the graph cannot come from package bytes. The graph structure is built
  in activity_model.rs; the loader refuses unless its compute_model_ir_digest equals the graph digest
  recorded in the verified weight bundle. This replaces "executor input graphs come ONLY from a
  verified package".
- Load path: StagingSpool::open(scratch root, SpoolLimits) (it creates and locks, so use a scratch
  root, never a deployment root being inspected) -> ModelPackageImporter::new(spool, limits)?
  .with_license_policy(policy) -> import_from_directory(dir, &HostSpoolIo, "model:fss-activity:v1")
  (the license check runs here) -> verify_package(receipt.manifest_digest) (Staged -> Verified) ->
  read weights_digest only after checking that its state is Verified.
- License: the default policy refuses an unlisted identity with UnknownLicense
  (model_license_policy.rs:859-863). Use spdx_or_identity "LicenseRef-FSS-First-Party", admitted
  explicitly with allow_license (model_license_policy.rs:546), with use_approved true, no
  restrictions and text_digest None (setting text_digest would make the license text a required
  artifact).
- Manifest fields: ModelId MOD-FSS-ACTIVITY-001 (MOD- followed by [A-Z0-9-], 5 to 64 characters,
  model_manifest.rs:286-330); input and output SchemaId per fss-core stable_id; CalibrationGeneration
  is required, so use the declared sentinel calib:none:v1 and list it as a sentinel. The target
  schema is schemas/model_manifest.v1.json; schemas/model_package_manifest.v1.json is plan-level
  and not implemented by fss-object.
- Committed fixture: tests/fixtures/models/activity-v1/ holds manifest.json (canonical) plus the
  weight bundle, written with ModelManifestV1 write_to_directory; the manifest digest is pinned.

title: CAP- fixtures: first-party deterministic baseline JPEG and MJPEG fixture encoder
description:
## What and why
MJPEG file ingest (P1) and the baseline JPEG decoder (P2) both need real JPEG bytes whose pixel
truth is known independently of the decoder under test. We cannot use third-party images, and we
may not ship a foreign encoder, so we write a tiny first-party baseline JPEG ENCODER used only to
generate fixtures. An encoder is simpler than a decoder and gives independent ground truth: known
source pixels, a known quantization table, and a bounded reconstruction error.

## Build
- `crates/fss-reference/src/media_fixture/jpeg.rs`: a baseline sequential DCT encoder.
  - 8-bit samples; JFIF APP0; one DQT (luma, plus chroma for colour) at a fixed quality; SOF0
    with 1 component (grey) or 3 components (YCbCr) at sampling 1x1 (4:4:4) and 2x2 (4:2:0).
  - The standard Annex K Huffman tables in DHT; one SOS; an optional DRI plus RSTn markers;
    correct 0xFF00 byte stuffing; EOI.
  - Forward DCT in f64 with a fixed evaluation order, then quantization with rounding. The output
    is deterministic.
- Source images: deterministic synthetic patterns (horizontal and vertical gradients, a
  checkerboard, a flat field, a colour bars image). Sizes: 16x16, 33x17 (odd, forces edge MCUs),
  64x48.
- An MJPEG stream: the concatenation of N JPEG frames, each of which is a complete SOI..EOI.
  Variants: clean, truncated_last (no EOI), garbage_between_frames, zero_length.
- Committed outputs under tests/fixtures/media/jpeg/ and tests/fixtures/media/mjpeg/ with rows in
  their per-family tests/fixtures/media/{jpeg,mjpeg}/fixture_manifest.json. Each entry holds the
  sha256 of the file and the
  sha256 of the source RGB/grey pixel buffer, so the decoder bead can compare against source truth
  with a tolerance.
- An optional lab oracle: if `djpeg` or `ffmpeg` exists, the companion test records its decoded
  pixel digest as a lab observation only.

## Registration
- module_declarations: "support".
- MANIFEST.delta rows.
- No production path may call the encoder. Put a `//! fixture generation only` doc and a test that
  greps that no non-test module imports it outside fss-lab fixture commands.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.6: CAP- fixtures JPEG/MJPEG (tests): marker structure, stuffing, regeneration identity, e2e manifest check
  - fss-2h5zq.18: CAP- LAB ingest command (tests): CLI integration per format, determinism, degraded paths, e2e ingest script
  - fss-2h5zq.22: CAP- INGEST MJPEG splitter (tests): manifest equality, stuffing/RST edge cases, mutation no-panic, e2e
  - fss-2h5zq.24: CAP- INGEST FileIngestAdapter (tests): custody digests, time-truth labels, no-absence proof, crash/cancel mid-import, e2e

## Shared rules for every CAP- bead (repeated so this bead stands alone)

Context: parent epic "CAP- Capability bridge: file-ingest-first end-to-end" (fss-2h5zq), created
2026-09-13 from the Phase-1 reality check at main 474931d and the owner's binding steering
decisions. The epic holds the full background; the essentials are repeated here.

- Constitution (AGENTS.md): Rust 2024 on nightly-2026-08-31. `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` in every
  crate, target, test, example and helper, with no exception path. Zero third-party crates: the
  dependency closure is fss-* only, and DEP-EXCEPTION-001 admits nothing. This bridge also adds
  ZERO new workspace crates. New code lands as modules in existing crates, mainly fss-reference and
  fss-cli. Moving the code into the planned L3/L4 crates (fss-codec-mjpeg, fss-container,
  fss-device-core, fss-model-runtime, fss-kernel-cpu, fss-coverage) is a later owner decision,
  because a new member trips the crate_topology and member-count pins (see fss-1bd1l).
- Do NOT edit crates/fss-packet/** (the owner's crate). Use its public API as-is:
  RtpPacket::parse, SequenceTracker, H264Depacketizer, NalUnit, SenderReportClock and
  JitterEstimator. Any change that needs fss-packet edits goes to an owner bead and is never
  assigned to an agent.
- No device I/O: no camera, USB, V4L2 or socket code; no `std::net` or `TcpStream`. Inputs are
  recorded files and recorded transcripts only. Every file read goes through an explicit I/O
  authority value, following the ReplayIoAuthority/ReplayCx pattern in
  crates/fss-reference/src/adapter_replay.rs, with cooperative cancellation checkpoints
  (request -> drain -> finalize). Asupersync `Cx` is NOT admitted yet (owner decision
  fss-x4a.8.1). Do not add Tokio or any other runtime.
- Security boundary: fixtures are synthetic and generated first-party. No third-party footage, no
  identifiable people, no captured network addresses. Never handle credentials: RTSP auth headers
  are detected and refused, never computed or stored. No scanning. Logs never contain secrets or
  private media bytes; they carry digests and byte spans only.
- Truth discipline:
  - A decoded frame is not retained evidence without source custody.
  - File import has no live continuity, so it never certifies absence. Negative reads stay
    unknown or not_observable.
  - File mtime is not capture time. Use ClockBasis::Estimated with an explicit, wide
    CaptureInterval unless the stream itself carries timing.
  - One camera's model score is never "corroborated".
  - unknown, not_observable, stale and indeterminate are never flattened to null, low confidence
    or omission.
- Registration, done in the same commit as the code:
  1. Every new .rs module under crates/fss-core or crates/fss-reference gets a
     `module_declarations` entry in architecture/semantic_plane_registry.json with its plane
     (authority | cognition | effect | support | ambiguous).
     scripts/semantic_plane_checker.py audits exactly those two crates and fails otherwise.
  2. Every new canonical digest or encoding domain tag gets a row in registries/DIGEST_DOMAINS.md
     (ID SCHEMA-DOMAIN-<NAME>-001, domain fss.<name>.v1, scope, authority, invariant rule).
     Bump BOTH pinned digestDomainCount assertions in tests/test_schema_validate.py in the same
     commit (45 at main 8b96911). Count from the value on HEAD at commit time, because several CAP
     beads add domains in parallel.
  3. Every new or changed source path gets a row in MANIFEST.delta.sha256 per ADR-0013. Never
     edit the MANIFEST.sha256 base. Check with `python3 scripts/manifest_audit.py`.
  4. New crate dependency edges must point downward in architecture/crate_topology.json. Layers:
     L2 ledger/object/publication, L3 fss-packet, L4 tensor/model-ir/geometry, L6 fss-cli,
     L7 fss-reference. fss-cli -> fss-reference is the one waived inversion. Check with
     `python3 scripts/dependency_dag_checker.py`.
  5. New CLI error and exit identities get rows in registries/ERRORS.md, and the operation
     crosswalk (architecture/operation_crosswalk.json and crates/fss-cli/src/crosswalk.rs) stays
     consistent.
- Verification (remote only):
  - `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- cargo test -p <crate> --all-targets --no-fail-fast --locked --offline`
  - `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets --keep-going --locked --offline -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo fmt --check`
  - `scripts/qualify.sh --lane policy`
  - `--all-targets` does NOT run doctests. When the crate has doc examples, also run
    `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- cargo test -p <crate> --doc --no-fail-fast --locked --offline`.
  - Launch rch from the repo directory with `--base <sha>`. Decide pass or fail by exit code (rch
    output is ANSI-coloured; strip ANSI before counting diagnostics). Re-run Python checkers and
    e2e scripts on a fresh `git worktree add --detach` checkout, never only in the shared tree.

  Main is currently red for reasons outside this bead (fss-kr9n3, fss-1bd1l, fss-lc2r1). Until
  those land, report "no new findings attributable to this bead's files". Never weaken a gate.
- E2E convention: every test bead ships scripts/e2e/cap_<name>.sh using the shared helpers in
  scripts/e2e/lib.sh (see the "CAP- e2e harness" bead).
  - Logs are JSON lines under ${FSS_E2E_LOG_DIR:-target/e2e-logs}/<name>/. The first record is an
    env record (git sha, bead id, binary sha256s, host triple, FSS_* settings); then one record per
    step: {ts, script, bead, step, cmd, exit, duration_ms, expected, observed, digest,
    stdout_sha256, stdout_excerpt, stderr_excerpt, verdict, repro}. Rust tests feed the log by
    printing one-line `CAPLOG {json}` records under --nocapture; lib.sh ingests them (ANSI
    stripped) through e2e_cargo_test. scripts/e2e/validate_log.py checks every record.
  - The final record is {"step":"summary","verdict":"pass"|"fail","steps":N,"failures":[...]}.
  - Scripts exit non-zero on any mismatch. They are deterministic (fixed seeds, no wall clock
    inside digests) and bounded in size, and they print a one-line reproduction command.
- Known gotchas (verified at main 8b96911, refinement round 1):
  - scripts/dependency_audit.py (DEP-AUD-022) scans every .rs file, tests and examples included,
    for the bare word unsafe. Comments are masked but string literals are NOT, so never put that
    word in a string literal or a guard-test pattern. The only allowed occurrence is
    #![forbid(unsafe_code)].
  - The workspace has 11 members since the twin merge (f9004ef, f5ed038). fss-twin (L4,
    "implemented") depends on fss-geometry. Treat crates/fss-twin/** and crates/fss-geometry/**
    as owner-authored upstream code, like fss-packet: use their public API and record API gaps in
    notes instead of editing them.
  - Shared hot files (edit only your own rows or lines; stage with `git add -p`):

  - One bead per commit, with the bead id in the subject.
  - Commit only files you own. Never `git add -A`. Never reset, amend or rebase main.

- Builder determinism (the rebuilt package equals the committed one).
- verify_package OK; tamper refused; license-policy denial path.
- Score goldens per fixture frame.
- A generation-mixing guard: comparing scores across two generation ids gives a typed error
  (reuse fss-reference compare_model_scores semantics).

## E2E (scripts/e2e/cap_exec_activity_package.sh)
Log the package root, the verify verdict, the tamper verdict and per-frame scores versus the
goldens.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Blocked by (must finish first):
  - fss-2h5zq.49: CAP- EXEC: first-party 'activity' model graph packaged as an immutable model package and loaded only through the fss-object verifier
  - fss-2h5zq.1: CAP- e2e harness: scripts/e2e/lib.sh structured JSON-lines logging and runner
  - fss-2h5zq.5: CAP- fixtures: first-party deterministic baseline JPEG and MJPEG fixture encoder
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.63: CAP- QUALIFY: whole-bridge verification on green main (rust+policy lanes, all CAP e2e scripts) and honest status/doc update

## Refinement round 1 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- Tamper with a weight blob and assert the refusal.
- Print CAPLOG lines per frame.

- Preprocessing goldens per fixture size: 16x16 (upscale), 33x17 (box filter with remainders),
  64x48 and 96x96.
- The PreprocessProgram digest is stable.
- The resize output stays within ±1 LSB of an in-test f64 reference.

## Refinement round 3 (2026-09-13, verified against main 7168075)
- Tamper, per stage with the exact expected errors: a weight file edited in the directory is re-hashed
  on read, so import fails in verify_contents with MissingArtifact or ExtraArtifact (not
  ArtifactDigestMismatch); an object tampered in the spool after staging fails verify_package with a
  spool error. Test both.
- License denial: a policy without the first-party identity gives UnknownLicense wrapped in
  ModelPackageError at import.
- Generation strings use model:fss-activity:v1; a manifest carrying model:fss-activity@1 is refused
  by the ModelGeneration grammar (test it). compare_model_scores (model.rs:1212) refuses mixing
  generations.
- A graph whose compute_model_ir_digest differs from the bundle's recorded digest is refused before
  execution.

title: CAP- EXEC: route the fss-reference mock-model seam through the scalar executor for one lab scenario (executor-backed observations into policy)
description:
## What and why
The reality check's step for gap #7 says to route the mock-model seam through the executor for
one scenario. Today every lab and reference flow uses MockModelExecutor / execute_mock_model
(crates/fss-reference/src/model.rs, scripted outcomes). One path must use real computation over
real decoded pixels so that model result -> event is not scripted.

## Build
- An executor-backed model source that yields ReferenceModelObservation (the type
  policy::evaluate_unknown_presence consumes) from EXEC3 scores with a DOCUMENTED threshold
  policy. The threshold is policy configuration with its own generation, not a hidden constant.
  Outputs:
  - score above the threshold -> an "unknown activity" observation;
  - below -> no-activity, which is NOT absence (coverage still governs);
  - an executor failure -> abstention, never "no detection".
- A new lab scenario `file-activity`, used by the capstone. Alternatively, a flag on an existing
  scenario that swaps MockModelExecutor for the executor path. Keep the six mock scenarios intact
  because they test policy semantics.
- A single camera means the result can never be "corroborated" (AGENTS.md prohibited shortcut).
  Assert this in the test.
- Receipts: the observation carries the ModelInvocationReceipt digest (EXEC2) and the
  DecodeReceipt digest (DECODE2), so the event revision is digest-linked to the source bytes.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Blocked by (must finish first):
  - fss-2h5zq.49: CAP- EXEC: first-party 'activity' model graph packaged as an immutable model package and loaded only through the fss-object verifier
  - fss-2h5zq.41: CAP- DECODE: decode receipt and source-to-tensor lineage (capsule source digest -> decoder generation -> tensor digest) published beside the capsule
  - fss-2h5zq.11: CAP- LAB: port the six fss-lab scenarios onto ReferenceDeployment (real crates) with an explicit --root and report schema v2
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.52: CAP- EXEC mock-seam routing (tests): observation mapping, no-corroboration guard, abstention on failure, e2e
  - fss-2h5zq.61: CAP- CAPSTONE: `fss-lab pipeline --input <file> --root <dir>`: file -> capsules -> decode -> executor -> policy -> event -> prepared alert -> receipt -> situation -> handoff

## Refinement round 1 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- Verified at 8b96911: the policy input fss_reference::ReferenceModelObservation (policy.rs:21)
  holds `result: MockModelResult` {generation_id, sensor_id, model_spec_digest,
  input_capture_root, continuity_digest, outcome: MockModelOutcome}.
  - An executor result cannot honestly be a MockModelResult.
  - A file source has no continuity witness to put in continuity_digest.
- Required change: generalize the observation's result into an explicit enum, for example
  `ReferenceModelResult::{Mock(MockModelResult), ScalarExecutor(ExecutorModelResult)}`. This is a
  type change in fss-reference; commit it together with every user.
  - ExecutorModelResult binds the ModelInvocationReceipt digest, the DecodeReceipt digest, the
    model generation, the threshold-policy generation and the capsule source digest.
  - It carries `continuity: NotObservable{reason: file_source}`, never a zero or fabricated digest.
  - Give it its own canonical encoding and domain, SCHEMA-DOMAIN-EXECUTOR-MODEL-RESULT-001
    `fss.executor_model_result.v1`, and bump the count.
  - evaluate_unknown_presence's object_digest-based dedup and failure-domain accounting must work
    for both variants.
- Regression guard: the `fss-lab matrix` stdout of the six mock scenarios stays byte-identical to
  the fss-2h5zq.12 baseline (`lab_matrix_baseline_sha256`), and every existing policy test passes
  unchanged.

## Refinement round 3 (2026-09-13, verified against main 7168075)
- The activity model generation string is model:fss-activity:v1 (fss-2h5zq.49 round 3; '@' is invalid
  under the ModelGeneration grammar).
- Executor model-result payloads are reachable from a durable ledgered root (fss-2h5zq.23 round-3
  rule), so doctor stays clean.
- Receipts with fss-na: sentinels (fss-2h5zq.47 round 3) are reference-only: the observation carries
  that label and is never treated as activation-backed model evidence.

title: CAP- GEO: geometric visibility for coverage using fss-geometry (frustum and mesh occlusion per zone sample) feeding CoverageWitness observed domains
description:
## What and why
fss-geometry (pinhole projection, TriangleMesh ray hits, PnP, route forecasts; merged from
upstream in f6a5591, BTI-01/03/07) has zero consumers. The plan puts geometry in the
coverage/visibility chain: plan §14.8-14.9, FSS-098 (fss-x4a.18.4, "visibility/coverage map and
validation", P2), GOAL-006 and INV-016. The coverage map is NOT_STARTED (vision goal #28). This
bead gives geometry its first honest caller: a camera can only contribute coverage for zone
points that are geometrically visible to it.

## Build
`crates/fss-reference/src/geometry_coverage.rs`:
- Inputs: a TriangleMesh (with GeometryBasis property and revision), per-camera
  (PinholeIntrinsics, RigidPose), and per-zone sample points (world coordinates), under a
  WorkBudget with cancellation.
- Per (camera, sample):
  1. Project into the image (camera.project). Outside the image or behind the camera gives
     out_of_frustum.
  2. Otherwise cast a ray from the camera centre (RigidPose::ray / Ray::new) and take the first
     mesh SurfaceHit. A hit closer than the sample (with epsilon) gives occluded; otherwise
     visible.
- Output: `GeometricVisibility { camera, zone, visible_fraction, per_sample states, basis
  (mesh revision, pose and intrinsics digests), work_used }`, canonically encoded under a NEW
  domain SCHEMA-DOMAIN-GEOMETRIC-VISIBILITY-001 `fss.geometric_visibility.v1` (registered, count
  pin bumped).
- Semantics: geometric visibility is NECESSARY, not sufficient, for coverage. Health, duty cycle,
  lighting and continuity are separate. A CoverageWitness observed domain for a camera may
  include only zones with visible_fraction above a stated threshold. A zone with no visible
  camera is structurally uncovered and can never be certified absent.
- Budget: an exceeded WorkBudget gives typed partial results that are marked unknown, never
  visible.

fss-geometry is "planned" in crate_topology.json (fss-1bd1l, owner decision), so the new edge
fss-reference -> fss-geometry (L7 -> L4) waits on it. Its clippy missing_docs (fss-kr9n3 area)
is not ours to fix unless the owner says so.

fss-x4a.18.4 (FSS-098), fss-3qlsa (coverage-for-absence first-witness bug), BTI units (no beads
exist; see docs/BLENDER_TWIN_IMPLEMENTATION_TASKS.md).

title: CAP- GEO: lab 'sneaky' scenario derives its coverage gap from geometry (occluded zone) instead of a hard-coded gap
description:
## What and why
The toy lab's `sneaky` scenario produced "protected_residual plus a probe affordance and a
coverage_gap warning" from a scripted gap. With GEO1, the gap becomes physically derived: the
intruder path crosses a zone that the property mesh occludes from cam-side and that is outside
cam-front's frustum. The protected residual world then exists for a real, inspectable reason.

## Build
- A small scene fixture: a mesh of the property (ground plane, a house box, a fence segment) and
  two camera poses matching cam-front and cam-side. It is defined in code or as a tiny committed
  fixture with a manifest.
- The sneaky scenario computes GeometricVisibility. The CoverageWitness observed domains come from
  visible zones only. The report gains `geometric_coverage` (per-zone states, basis digest), and
  the probe affordance names the uncovered zone.
- The other scenarios keep full coverage (the scene has no occlusion on their path), so their
  outputs are unchanged.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Blocked by (must finish first):
  - fss-2h5zq.53: CAP- GEO: geometric visibility for coverage using fss-geometry (frustum and mesh occlusion per zone sample) feeding CoverageWitness observed domains
  - fss-2h5zq.11: CAP- LAB: port the six fss-lab scenarios onto ReferenceDeployment (real crates) with an explicit --root and report schema v2

  fss-cli. Moving the code into the planned L3/L4 crates (fss-codec-mjpeg, fss-container,
  fss-device-core, fss-model-runtime, fss-kernel-cpu, fss-coverage) is a later owner decision,
  because a new member trips the crate_topology and member-count pins (see fss-1bd1l).
