  RtpPacket::parse, SequenceTracker, H264Depacketizer, NalUnit, SenderReportClock and
  JitterEstimator. Any change that needs fss-packet edits goes to an owner bead and is never
  assigned to an agent.
- No device I/O: no camera, USB, V4L2 or socket code; no `std::net` or `TcpStream`. Inputs are
  recorded files and recorded transcripts only. Every file read goes through an explicit I/O
  authority value, following the ReplayIoAuthority/ReplayCx pattern in
  crates/fss-reference/src/adapter_replay.rs, with cooperative cancellation checkpoints
  (request -> drain -> finalize). Asupersync `Cx` is NOT admitted yet (owner decision
  fss-x4a.8.1). Do not add Tokio or any other runtime.
- Security boundary: fixtures are synthetic and generated first-party. No third-party footage, no
  identifiable people, no captured network addresses. Never handle credentials: RTSP auth headers
  are detected and refused, never computed or stored. No scanning. Logs never contain secrets or
  private media bytes; they carry digests and byte spans only.
- Truth discipline:
  - A decoded frame is not retained evidence without source custody.
  - File import has no live continuity, so it never certifies absence. Negative reads stay
    unknown or not_observable.
  - File mtime is not capture time. Use ClockBasis::Estimated with an explicit, wide
    CaptureInterval unless the stream itself carries timing.
  - One camera's model score is never "corroborated".
  - unknown, not_observable, stale and indeterminate are never flattened to null, low confidence
    or omission.
- Registration, done in the same commit as the code:
  1. Every new .rs module under crates/fss-core or crates/fss-reference gets a
     `module_declarations` entry in architecture/semantic_plane_registry.json with its plane
     (authority | cognition | effect | support | ambiguous).
     scripts/semantic_plane_checker.py audits exactly those two crates and fails otherwise.
  2. Every new canonical digest or encoding domain tag gets a row in registries/DIGEST_DOMAINS.md
     (ID SCHEMA-DOMAIN-<NAME>-001, domain fss.<name>.v1, scope, authority, invariant rule).
     Bump ALL THREE pinned domain counts in the same commit: the two digestDomainCount
     assertions in tests/test_schema_validate.py AND the domain_count assertion (and its
     message) in crates/fss-model-ir/tests/model_ir_contract.rs:420 (45 at main 7168075;
     verified in refinement round 3). Count from the value on HEAD at commit time, because several CAP
     beads add domains in parallel.
  3. Every new or changed source path gets a row in MANIFEST.delta.sha256 per ADR-0013. Never
     edit the MANIFEST.sha256 base. Check with `python3 scripts/manifest_audit.py`.
  4. New crate dependency edges must point downward in architecture/crate_topology.json. Layers:
     L2 ledger/object/publication, L3 fss-packet, L4 tensor/model-ir/geometry, L6 fss-cli,
     L7 fss-reference. fss-cli -> fss-reference is the one waived inversion. Check with
     `python3 scripts/dependency_dag_checker.py`.
  5. New CLI error and exit identities get rows in registries/ERRORS.md, and the operation
     crosswalk (architecture/operation_crosswalk.json and crates/fss-cli/src/crosswalk.rs) stays
     consistent.
- Verification (remote only):
  - `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- cargo test -p <crate> --all-targets --no-fail-fast --locked --offline`
  - `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets --keep-going --locked --offline -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo fmt --check`
  - `scripts/qualify.sh --lane policy`
  - `--all-targets` does NOT run doctests. When the crate has doc examples, also run
    `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec -- cargo test -p <crate> --doc --no-fail-fast --locked --offline`.
  - Launch rch from the repo directory with `--base <sha>`. Decide pass or fail by exit code (rch
    output is ANSI-coloured; strip ANSI before counting diagnostics). Re-run Python checkers and
    e2e scripts on a fresh `git worktree add --detach` checkout, never only in the shared tree.

  Main is currently red for reasons outside this bead (fss-kr9n3, fss-1bd1l, fss-lc2r1). Until
  those land, report "no new findings attributable to this bead's files". Never weaken a gate.
- E2E convention: every test bead ships scripts/e2e/cap_<name>.sh using the shared helpers in
  scripts/e2e/lib.sh (see the "CAP- e2e harness" bead).
  - Logs are JSON lines under ${FSS_E2E_LOG_DIR:-target/e2e-logs}/<name>/. The first record is an
    env record (git sha, bead id, binary sha256s, host triple, FSS_* settings); then one record per
    step: {ts, script, bead, step, cmd, exit, duration_ms, expected, observed, digest,
    stdout_sha256, stdout_excerpt, stderr_excerpt, verdict, repro}. Rust tests feed the log by
    printing one-line `CAPLOG {json}` records under --nocapture; lib.sh ingests them (ANSI
    stripped) through e2e_cargo_test. scripts/e2e/validate_log.py checks every record.
  - The final record is {"step":"summary","verdict":"pass"|"fail","steps":N,"failures":[...]}.
  - Scripts exit non-zero on any mismatch. They are deterministic (fixed seeds, no wall clock
    inside digests) and bounded in size, and they print a one-line reproduction command.
- Known gotchas (verified at main 8b96911, refinement round 1):
  - scripts/dependency_audit.py (DEP-AUD-022) scans every .rs file, tests and examples included,
    for the bare word unsafe. Comments are masked but string literals are NOT, so never put that
    word in a string literal or a guard-test pattern. The only allowed occurrence is
    #![forbid(unsafe_code)].
  - The workspace has 11 members since the twin merge (f9004ef, f5ed038). fss-twin (L4,
    "implemented") depends on fss-geometry. Treat crates/fss-twin/** and crates/fss-geometry/**
    as owner-authored upstream code, like fss-packet: use their public API and record API gaps in
    notes instead of editing them.
  - Shared hot files (edit only your own rows or lines; stage with `git add -p`):
    registries/DIGEST_DOMAINS.md, tests/test_schema_validate.py,
    crates/fss-model-ir/tests/model_ir_contract.rs (the third domain-count pin),
    architecture/semantic_plane_registry.json, MANIFEST.delta.sha256, registries/ERRORS.md,
    crates/fss-reference/src/lib.rs, crates/fss-reference/Cargo.toml and
    crates/fss-cli/src/lab_cmd.rs.
  - LocalRootPublisher::open and StagingSpool::open create directories and take exclusive lock
    files, so they are not read-only. Read-only inspection goes through fss-2h5zq.66.
- Swarm hygiene:
  - One bead per commit, with the bead id in the subject.
  - Commit only files you own. Never `git add -A`. Never reset, amend or rebase main.
  - Commit only what compiles against committed HEAD, and commit type changes together with all
    their users.
  - Record final paths and evidence with `br update <id> --append-notes`. Never use --notes,
    which overwrites the field.

title: CAP- DOCTOR: `fss doctor --json --root <dir>` inspects the real deployment (journal tail, orphaned staging, broken roots, indeterminate obligations)
description:
## What and why
Vision goal #34: `fss doctor` returns a hard-coded string
(crates/fss-cli/src/fss_cmd.rs: {"schema":"fss.doctor.v1","verdict":"design_only",...}) and
inspects nothing. GATE-010 requires "doctor detects staged, orphaned, and indeterminate state".
Top-10 gap #9 gives the first step: open the ledger and spool and report tail state, orphaned
staging, pending roots and indeterminate obligations.

## Build
- The `fss doctor` parser (parse_json_only_subcommand in fss_cmd.rs) gains an optional
  `--root <dir>`. Without --root, the existing honest design_only output is kept unchanged, so
  scripts relying on it still work.
- With --root, a READ-ONLY inspection. Doctor must not mutate. The companion test proves this
  with a directory tree digest taken before and after. Checks:
  - `ledger.journal`: fss_ledger::inspect(path) (RecoveryReport) gives clean, incomplete_tail
    {bytes}, foreign_trailing_bytes or corrupt. Never open with Truncate. Repair belongs to the
    audited LEDGER-REPAIR path (fss-x4a.9.21, closed), which doctor names as the next affordance.
  - `objects.staging`: orphaned staging entries, and corrupt or foreign entries (the
    SpoolRecoveryReport and LocalRecoveryReport data).
    - Read-only mode may be missing today: LocalRootPublisher::open or StagingSpool::open may
      discard orphaned temps or otherwise mutate. If so, add a read-only inspection function in
      the owning crate (fss-object/fss-publication, NOT fss-packet) with its own tests. Record
      the choice.
    - Visible roots, broken roots (BrokenRootReason) and tombstones.
  - `effects.obligations`: DurableEffectJournal replay counts of terminal, pending and
    indeterminate obligations. Indeterminate ones are listed by id with their reconcile
    affordance.
  - `deployment.layout`: the LAYOUT version from ReferenceDeployment (LAB1). An unknown layout
    gives not_a_deployment.
- Output: `fss.doctor.v1` (SCHEMA-DOCTOR-001: "bounded and secret-free"). A verdict of healthy |
  attention_required | not_a_deployment | unreadable; checks[] with {id, status, counts,
  evidence digests, next_affordance}. The output is bounded: at most N ids listed per check, and
  the rest become a count plus a continuation hint.
- Exit codes: 0 for healthy, a distinct registered code for attention_required, and one for
  not_a_deployment. The error and exit identities go in registries/ERRORS.md, and the crosswalk
  entry for doctor (operation_crosswalk.json, fss-cli crosswalk.rs; AOP-014 fss-x4a.30.83.30)
  stays consistent.
- The help text in fss_cmd.rs is updated. Its sentence "No camera, drone, model, archive, or
  alert operation is implemented yet" stays true and is kept.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Blocked by (must finish first):
  - fss-2h5zq.9: CAP- LAB: ReferenceDeployment composition in fss-reference (spool + root-last publication + durable ledger + effects + situation)
- Related existing beads (context only, not blocking; this bead does not close them): fss-x4a.30.55, fss-x4a.30.83.30, fss-x4a.5.13, fss-x4a.2.2
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.58: CAP- DOCTOR (tests): crash-matrix corpus detection, read-only proof, bounded output, exit codes, e2e
  - fss-2h5zq.61: CAP- CAPSTONE: `fss-lab pipeline --input <file> --root <dir>`: file -> capsules -> decode -> executor -> policy -> event -> prepared alert -> receipt -> situation -> handoff

## Refinement round 1 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- Read-only is a hard requirement, and the existing opens cannot meet it because they create
  directories and take locks.
  - Use the non-mutating inspection APIs from CAP- DOCTOR0 (fss-2h5zq.66, a new blocking
    dependency): spool::inspect, local::inspect, the read-only root-ledger linkage check and
    DurableEffectJournal::inspect.
  - Use fss_ledger::inspect(path) for the ledger.
- fss_ledger::RecoveryReport exposes records(), committed_len(), incomplete_tail() and last_root().
  Fully present corruption and foreign trailing bytes surface as JournalError variants. Doctor maps
  them to `corrupt` and `foreign_trailing_bytes`; the next affordance is the audited LEDGER-REPAIR
  path (fss-x4a.9.21).
- The checks include:
  - RootLedgerReconciliation: pending roots, unbacked ledger claims and slot conflicts;
  - concurrent_writer (lock held), reported with possibly_stale.
- This bead's acceptance is proven on roots built with ReferenceDeployment helpers. The crash-matrix
  sub-root sweep is the acceptance of fss-2h5zq.58.

## Refinement round 2 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- Journals: read ledger/journal.fssj and effects/journal.fssj bounded (check the file length against
  a limit first). fss_ledger::inspect and doctor_path read whole files with no bound. Then run
  fss_ledger::doctor(bytes) (repair.rs:164, pure), which gives committed_len, last_root,
  records_count, incomplete_tail and foreign_range in one pass.
- The ledger's semantic replay (batches, snapshot, root claims) comes from fss-2h5zq.66's
  fss_ledger::inspect_durable, using site_lineage from LAYOUT.
- next_affordance names the exact explicit recovery command from fss-2h5zq.15:
  - `fss-lab recover --root <dir> --truncate-incomplete-tail ledger|effects`;
  - `--plan-ledger-repair` then `--apply-ledger-repair <plan-digest>`, for foreign trailing bytes
    (doctor prints the same plan digest);
  - `--reconcile-effects`, for indeterminate obligations (simulated provider only).
  Doctor itself never repairs.
- Writer state comes from fss-2h5zq.66's probe: writer_state none | concurrent_writer |
  not_probed, plus the probe method. The LOCK files (<root>/objects/LOCK and
  <root>/objects/spool/LOCK, not fss.local_publication.lock) persist after a writer exits, so their
  presence alone says nothing.
- An incomplete import (capsule batches without their manifest batch, fss-2h5zq.23) is an attention
  check, `imports.incomplete`.

## Refinement round 3 (2026-09-13, verified against main 7168075)
Corrections from a review of the round-2 recover and inspection design:
- Superseded: the round-1 bullet "Use fss_ledger::inspect(path) for the ledger" (inspect is unbounded,
  recovery.rs:96-101). Use inspect_durable and doctor_bounded from fss-2h5zq.66.
- corrupt versus foreign: run recover_bytes and fss_ledger::doctor over the same bounded bytes. Report
  foreign_trailing_bytes only when no structurally valid record header lies inside the foreign range;
  otherwise report corrupt_history, whose next_affordance is an owner action, never
  --apply-ledger-repair. fss_ledger::doctor alone reports any invalid record as foreign to the end of
  the file, which would make corrupt unreachable.
- Repair sidecars: list <digest-hex>.quarantine files (informational, with the quarantined digest) and
  leftover <digest-hex>.tmp.<pid>.<n> files (attention; rerun the apply) under ledger/ and effects/
  (repair.rs:624-645).
- next_affordance table, extending round 2: orphaned root temps -> --discard-orphaned-temps;
  orphaned staging -> --discard-orphaned-staging; effect-journal foreign bytes ->
  --plan-effects-repair then --apply-effects-repair; a Committed operation without a provider record
  -> --reconcile-effects; a pending root -> rerun the producing command (explicit commit is an owner
  decision); corrupt_history -> owner action.
- The plan digest doctor prints equals recover's only for the same file: it binds the canonical
  absolute path, dev and inode (repair.rs:388-411).
- Unreferenced objects (LocalRecoveryReport.unreferenced_objects) are reported with a count and a
  bounded id list. With the round-3 reachability rule in fss-2h5zq.11/.23, a complete deployment has
  none; whether a non-empty set is attention_required or informational is an owner decision, and the
  default here is attention_required.
- Writer state uses fss-2h5zq.66 round 3: held | not_observed | not_held | unknown{reason} |
  not_probed, replacing concurrent_writer and none. An incomplete tail seen while a writer is held
  or not_observed is possibly_in_flight, not a fault. Whether a present writer changes the exit code
  is an owner decision; the default is that writer presence alone does not, and the output is
  marked possibly_stale.
- An exceeded limit gives the check status over_budget naming the limit, never a crashed or partial
  check.
- Read-only is proven with fss-2h5zq.67's recording capability, not only by tree digest.

title: CAP- DOCTOR (tests): crash-matrix corpus detection, read-only proof, bounded output, exit codes, e2e
description:
## Tests (crates/fss-cli/tests/doctor_real_root.rs)
- Build roots with LAB1 helpers: clean, incomplete tail, orphaned staging, broken root, lost ack
  (indeterminate), an empty dir, a random dir (not_a_deployment), and an unreadable file.
- Per root, assert the verdict, the checks and the exit code.
- The read-only proof by tree digest.
- Bounded output with 10k orphaned entries: truncated to N plus a count.
- The no-root legacy output is unchanged.

## E2E (scripts/e2e/cap_doctor.sh)
Run `fss-lab crash-matrix` into a root. Then run `fss doctor --json --root` on every sub-root and
log expected versus observed per check. Log the tree digest before and after each call.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Blocked by (must finish first):
  - fss-2h5zq.57: CAP- DOCTOR: `fss doctor --json --root <dir>` inspects the real deployment (journal tail, orphaned staging, broken roots, indeterminate obligations)
  - fss-2h5zq.1: CAP- e2e harness: scripts/e2e/lib.sh structured JSON-lines logging and runner
  - fss-2h5zq.15: CAP- LAB: fss-lab crash-matrix subcommand (kill at every publish cut point and journal phase, reopen, report recovery)
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.63: CAP- QUALIFY: whole-bridge verification on green main (rust+policy lanes, all CAP e2e scripts) and honest status/doc update

## Refinement round 1 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- Add cases for concurrent_writer, a pending root (LedgerCutPoint::AfterRootDurable) and foreign
  trailing bytes.
- Check every crash-matrix sub-root by its slug name.
- Print CAPLOG lines per root.

## Refinement round 2 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- For each crash-matrix slug: doctor reports attention; the named recover action runs; doctor then
  reports healthy.
- Foreign trailing bytes: the plan digest in the doctor output equals the one recover applies.
- An oversize journal against a small limit gives a typed limit error.
- An incomplete import (a crash between the capsule batches and the manifest batch) is reported.

## Refinement round 3 (2026-09-13, verified against main 7168075)
- The doctor -> action -> doctor loop uses the action each slug names in the round-3 table of
  fss-2h5zq.15. The four append.reconcile_* slugs are not_applicable. Pending-root and
  unreferenced-object slugs (publish.after_root_rename, ledger.after_root_durable,
  publish.after_children_verified, publish.after_manifest_body) are resolved by rerunning the
  producing command, then doctor reports healthy.
- The plan-digest equality check runs on the same file (plan digests bind path, dev and inode), never
  on a copy.
- After an apply, the tree-digest comparison expects the quarantine sidecar; every other doctor call is
  still byte-identical before and after.
- Add a corrupt_history case: a bad record followed by valid ones gives corrupt_history with an owner
  action, never --apply-ledger-repair.
- Two limits (replacing the 10k line): a hard scan limit, where exceeding it gives over_budget with
  no count; and an output list limit, which truncates to N plus an exact count. The 10k-orphan case
  sets the scan limit above 10k and asserts the truncated list plus the exact count; a second case
  sets it below and asserts over_budget.
- The lock-held root uses a writer in the same process or a child process (not a container), and
  asserts held through /proc/locks.

title: CAP- STATUS: `fss status --json --root <dir>` reports sensors, streams, capsules, events and obligations from the real ledger (never implying unsupported readiness)
description:
## What and why
`fss status` returns a hard-coded {"phase":"architecture_constitution","sensors":[],...}.
SCHEMA-STATUS-001 (`fss.status.v1`, "CLI output", authority: product boundary) has the rule
"status fields cannot imply unsupported readiness".

## Build
- An optional `--root <dir>`. Without it the legacy output is kept.
- With --root, read-only (like DOCTOR). Report:
  - the ledger anchor (sequence, anchor root digest, site lineage);
  - sensors and streams seen, from capsule deltas (sensor_id, stream_id, generations, capsule
    count, first and last capture interval with clock_basis);
  - per stream: continuity knowledge (verified / degraded / not_observable_file_source);
  - imports (count, last import-manifest root);
  - events (count by disposition), obligations (terminal, pending, indeterminate), last situation
    and handoff digests if present;
  - `degraded[]` (e.g. no_live_continuity for file sources, coverage_gap zones,
    indeterminate_effects);
  - `capabilities_exercised` limited to what this root actually contains (e.g.
    "reference_file_import", "baseline_jpeg_decode", "scalar_executor").
- It never reports device_acquisition, live streaming or alerts-to-real-providers as available.
- Keep `fss capabilities --json` honest: if it is updated, it lists reference-only capabilities
  under a separate `reference_implemented` key and keeps the not_implemented entries for anything
  not real (device_acquisition, archive_upload, real alerts). It never moves them to
  "implemented".
- Bounded output with continuation hints, error ids registered, crosswalk consistent.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Blocked by (must finish first):
  - fss-2h5zq.9: CAP- LAB: ReferenceDeployment composition in fss-reference (spool + root-last publication + durable ledger + effects + situation)
  - fss-2h5zq.23: CAP- INGEST: FileIngestAdapter (ADP-FILE-001 reference slice): file -> SensorCapsules with source custody -> root-last publication -> ledger batch
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.60: CAP- STATUS (tests): per-root assertions after lab, ingest and rtpdump runs, readiness guard, e2e
  - fss-2h5zq.61: CAP- CAPSTONE: `fss-lab pipeline --input <file> --root <dir>`: file -> capsules -> decode -> executor -> policy -> event -> prepared alert -> receipt -> situation -> handoff

## Refinement round 1 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- New blocking dependency: CAP- DOCTOR0 (fss-2h5zq.66). Status reads through the same non-mutating
  inspection layer as doctor, never through LocalRootPublisher::open or StagingSpool::open.
- Sensors, streams and imports are read from ledger deltas by family: "sensor_capsule",
  "file_import_manifest", "acquisition_transition", "decode_receipt" and
  "model_invocation_receipt" (see the family table of fss-2h5zq.9). Each payload object is decoded
  by its payload_digest.
- The acceptance root is one produced by a FileIngestAdapter import (fss-2h5zq.23). The
  `fss-lab ingest` CLI (fss-2h5zq.17) is not a dependency.

## Refinement round 2 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- Read the ledger through fss-2h5zq.66's fss_ledger::inspect_durable, using site_lineage from

description:

- Regeneration is byte-identical.

- Every 0xFF inside entropy-coded data is followed by 0x00 or RSTn.
- SOF0 dimensions and sampling match the parameters.
- The MJPEG variant frame counts match the manifest.

- Verify each fixture sha256 against the manifest.

  and the PSNR against the manifest's source pixels, which must be at least 30 dB at the fixture
  quality. This is a lab observation only; absence of the tool is a logged skip.

description:
## What and why
This is the epic's target end state, and the honest successor to the toy walking skeleton
(vision goal #40). One command takes a recorded file through every real crate. The command:

    fss-lab pipeline --input <mjpeg|jpeg|h264|rtpdump|rtsp-transcript> --root <dir> [--json] [--inject <fault>]

## Build
- An orchestration in fss-lab over the existing pieces:
  1. LAB5 ingest (capsules, acquisition lifecycle, continuity when available).
  2. DECODE2 per JPEG capsule. H.264 has no decoder: those capsules get an explicit
     not_decodable_no_h264_decoder outcome, and the pipeline continues with coverage and
     knowledge only. The first H.264 decoder is FSS-124, fss-x4a.12.23.
  3. EXEC3/EXEC4 activity scores per decoded frame, with receipts.
  4. evaluate_unknown_presence (single source, so it is never corroborated).
  5. publish_reference_event -> event revision.
  6. Alert prepare -> dispatch via the simulated provider -> observe -> reconcile.
  7. compile_reference_situation.
  8. seal_reference_handoff.
- The report `fss.lab.pipeline_report.v1` holds the digest chain file sha256 -> capsule digests ->
  decode receipts -> model receipts -> event revision digest -> effect receipt -> situation digest
  -> handoff digest, plus every knowledge label (capture time unknown/assumed, continuity,
  absence not certifiable, not corroborated).
- `--inject lost-ack|crash:<cut point>|cancel:<stage>` reuses the LAB4 fault hooks. The report and
  a following `fss doctor --root` show the resulting terminal or indeterminate state.
- Idempotency: re-running the same input on the same root must not duplicate effects. It returns
  the existing operation (GATE-010: "duplicate intent/commit does not duplicate an effect").

- New blocking dependency: the crash-matrix bead (fss-2h5zq.15). `--inject` reuses its fault hooks

## Tests (crates/fss-cli/tests/lab_pipeline.rs)
- For the MJPEG, JPEG, Annex-B and (when available) rtpdump fixtures, run the pipeline. Then
  independently re-verify every link of the digest chain by opening the root with the library
  types: recompute the capsule digests from the file, decode again, re-run the executor, compare.

  output for each.
- An idempotent rerun.
- Determinism across roots.

1. Build info (bin paths and sha256).
2. Per fixture: pipeline; a step per stage with digests; then doctor, status, and an idempotent

title: CAP- OWNER (needs owner, do not assign): fss-packet Annex-B byte-stream splitter and a public NalUnit-from-bytes constructor, to unify file and RTP NAL paths
description:
## Status: NEEDS OWNER. DO NOT ASSIGN TO AGENTS. crates/fss-packet/** is the owner's crate.

## Why this exists
File ingest (INGEST1) had to put an Annex-B splitter in fss-reference, because fss-packet only
reconstructs NALs from RTP. Its NalUnit type has a private constructor ("reconstructed NAL bytes
without an invented Annex-B start code"). The result is two NAL representations: fss-packet's
NalUnit with NalSourceSpan, and fss-reference's Annex-B spans. Both feed capsules. This is
tolerable for a reference slice, but the plan's media narrow waist (WP-060, fss-x4a.12) wants ONE
packet/NAL truth.

## Options for the owner
- (A) Add `annexb` scanning to fss-packet: a sans-IO splitter with the same limits discipline,
  plus a public constructor or conversion producing NalUnit (or a shared NalRef {bytes span,
  source kind}) from a byte-stream source. fss-reference then migrates to it and deletes its
  splitter.
- (B) Keep the Annex-B splitter outside fss-packet by design ("packet" means transport packets
  only). Then move the fss-reference splitter to the planned fss-container or fss-codec-h264
  crate later.
- (C) Defer.

Also pending on the owner in the same crate: fss-kr9n3 (clippy/fmt, the RTCP SDES test at
crates/fss-packet/tests/wire_contract.rs:255, topology status).

## If the owner chooses A
Write concrete implementation and test beads then. Acceptance would be: INGEST1's contract tests
pass against the fss-packet implementation, and the fss-reference splitter is deleted.

- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq

title: CAP- DOCTOR0: non-mutating inspection of a deployment root (spool, local publication, root-ledger linkage, effect journal) without locks, directory creation or repair
description:
## What and why
`fss doctor --root` and `fss status --root` must prove "tree digest unchanged", and they must work
while a writer holds the lock. The existing opens cannot do that. Round 2 re-verified each one at
main 8b96911:
- fss_publication::LocalRootPublisher::open (local/mod.rs:567, then open_through:589):
  - it calls create_dir_all, and takes an exclusive try_lock on <root>/LOCK (LOCAL_LOCK_FILE,
    mod.rs:107; the doc comment at mod.rs:563 still says fss.local_publication.lock, which is
    stale);
  - it creates roots/ and tombstones/, opens the owned spool at <root>/spool, and fsyncs;
  - recover() (mod.rs:1653) deletes a root temp file whenever its target record already exists,
    and fsyncs roots/ and tombstones/. Roots are reported Durable only if that fsync succeeded.
- fss_object::StagingSpool::open_with_io (spool/mod.rs:352):
  - it creates the root, objects/ and staging/, and takes an exclusive try_lock on <spool>/LOCK;
  - it creates holds/ on a fresh spool, and fsyncs;
  - recover() (mod.rs:1086) classifies. A spool without holds/ ("legacy") is migrated by
    migrate_holds, which writes and renames.
- fss_ledger::DurableReferenceLedger::open (durable.rs:239) and
  fss_reference::DurableEffectJournal::open (durable_effect.rs:199) both run a read-only preflight
  (inspect plus a private replay_report), then Journal::open for append.
- Read-only today: fss_ledger::inspect(path) (recovery.rs:96), recover_bytes, and
  fss_ledger::doctor(bytes) and doctor_path (repair.rs:164, :383). inspect and doctor_path read the
  whole file without a bound.
Round 1 suggested passing a write-refusing SpoolIo through open_with_io. That cannot work: the first
calls of open_with_io create directories and open the lock file for writing. Each owning crate must
instead split a read-only classifier out of its open, so that open and inspect share it.

## Build
Refactor, never copy. Behaviour of the existing opens is unchanged.
- fss-object (spool):
  - Extract the read-only part of recover() and recover_holds() into a classifier that only lists,
    stats and reads (scan_directory, symlink_metadata, read_object_file) and returns a
    SpoolClassification.
  - open_with_io still creates, locks, migrates holds and fsyncs, then consumes that same
    classification.
  - New `pub fn inspect(root, limits) -> Result<SpoolInspection, SpoolError>`:
    - it never creates, locks, renames, removes or fsyncs;
    - missing objects/ or staging/ are reported as missing_layout, not created;
    - a spool without holds/ is reported holds_migration_pending=true, classified exactly as open
      classifies it before migration;
    - it embeds the SpoolRecoveryReport that open would produce.
- fss-publication (local):
  - The same split for recover(), recover_tombstones() and recover_roots().
  - New `pub fn inspect(root, limits) -> Result<LocalInspection, LocalPublicationError>` returns the
    LocalRecoveryReport that open would produce, plus two extras:
    - redundant_temps: the root temp files open would delete because their target record exists.
      open deletes them silently, so they never appear in LocalRecoveryReport;
    - the durability basis ObservedOnDisk: inspect never fsyncs, so a record found on disk counts as
      durable for classification, labelled durability_not_resynced.
  - Fix the stale lock-name doc comment at mod.rs:563.
- fss-publication (ledger linkage):
  - Move LedgeredRootPublisher::classify (ledger.rs:911) and ledger_claims (ledger.rs:591) into free
    functions over a small read-only root view (visible root, broken slot, root closure) and a
    ledger view (batches, current snapshot).
  - reconcile() calls them with unchanged behaviour.
  - New `pub fn inspect_linkage(&LocalInspection, &LedgerInspection) ->
    RootLedgerReconciliation` calls the same functions, so it equals reconcile() by construction.
  - It reports LedgerReconciliationRequired when the ledger has an incomplete tail, exactly as
    require_no_pending_append would.
- fss-ledger: new `pub fn inspect_durable(path, site_lineage, limits) -> Result<LedgerInspection,
  DurableLedgerError>`:
  - a bounded read (the file length is checked against limits before reading), then recover_bytes;
  - then the existing private replay_report(&report, site_lineage) (durable.rs:420), the same
    replay that open runs;
  - it returns batches, the current LedgerSnapshot, committed_len, last_root and incomplete_tail,
    plus foreign_range from fss_ledger::doctor over the same bytes.
  Also add a bounded `doctor_bounded(path, max_bytes)`.
- fss-reference: new `DurableEffectJournal::inspect(path, limits) ->
  Result<EffectJournalInspection, DurableEffectError>`:
  - a bounded read, recover_bytes, then the existing private replay_report (durable_effect.rs:873);
  - it returns obligation counts (terminal, pending, indeterminate), each indeterminate id with its
    reconcile affordance, incomplete_tail and foreign_range.
- Writer detection (read-only by default):
  - LOCK files persist after a writer exits, so their existence is not evidence of a writer.
  - Default on Linux: read /proc/locks (read-only, non-interfering) and match its FLOCK entries
    against the inodes of <root>/objects/LOCK and <root>/objects/spool/LOCK.
  - Fallback where /proc/locks is unavailable: an explicit opt-in shared try_lock probe, released
    at once. It changes no bytes, but while it is held a starting writer's exclusive try_lock fails
    with the typed, retryable Locked / deployment_locked error. So it is opt-in and documented.
  - Output: writer_state none | concurrent_writer | not_probed, plus probe_method. With
    concurrent_writer the snapshot is still returned, marked possibly_stale.
  - Never block, and never break a lock.
- Bounds: every function takes limits (entries, bytes, journal bytes) and returns a typed
  LimitExceeded. No symlink is followed out of the root. Outputs are secret-free.

## Registration
- scripts/semantic_plane_checker.py audits only crates/fss-core and crates/fss-reference, so the
  fss-object, fss-publication and fss-ledger code needs no module_declarations. If the fss-reference
  inspection becomes a new module rather than living in durable_effect.rs, add a
  module_declarations entry (plane "support" or "effect", with the reason).
- MANIFEST.delta rows for every changed or new file. No new crate edges: fss-publication and
  fss-reference already depend on fss-ledger and fss-object (verified in their Cargo.toml files).

## Consumers
CAP- DOCTOR (fss-2h5zq.57), CAP- STATUS (fss-2h5zq.59), ReferenceDeployment::layout_report
(fss-2h5zq.9) and the ingest gauntlet (fss-2h5zq.31).

## Refinement round 2 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
This bead's What, Build and acceptance were rewritten in round 2. The round-1 version proposed a
write-refusing SpoolIo, which cannot work, used the wrong lock name, reported a meaningless
writer_lock_present, left fss-ledger's replay out, and ignored redundant temps, legacy spools and
fsync-based durability.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)

## Refinement round 3 (2026-09-13, verified against main 7168075)
The three-crate classifier split is sound and the named functions exist (local recover :1653,
recover_tombstones :1702, recover_roots :1769; spool recover :1086, migrate_holds :1208,
recover_holds :1239, scan_directory :1354, read_object_file :1381; ledger classify :911,
ledger_claims :591). Corrections:
- inspect_linkage never returns LedgerReconciliationRequired. require_no_pending_append reads
  in-memory state (ledger.rs:904-909), which is always None after open (durable.rs:280); an
  incomplete tail makes open(Reject) fail instead. inspect_linkage classifies the committed prefix and
  sets the documented extra ledger_tail_incomplete{offset}.
- Refactor over views: ledger_claims takes &DurableReferenceLedger, so change it to
  (&[EvidenceDeltaBatch], &LedgerSnapshot). closure() counts only Durable roots (local/mod.rs:1191),
  so inspect feeds its ObservedOnDisk basis in as Durable; otherwise every root classifies as
  not_durable and the differential cannot pass.
- Legacy spool (replaces "classified exactly as open classifies it before migration"): report
  holds_migration_pending=true and synthesize the hold set migrate_holds would create, so the embedded
  SpoolRecoveryReport equals open's. A partial holds-migration directory from a crashed migration is
  accepted as open accepts it (spool/mod.rs:1092).
- Bounded reads: "length checked before reading" races with an appender. Read with a limit+1 cap and
  report over_budget naming the limit if exceeded. A missing journal is absent, never created
  (Journal::open creates, journal.rs:74). Scan bounds are the fixed ROOT_SCAN_BOUND (64) and
  TOP_LEVEL_SCAN_BOUND (16) plus max_scan_entries; when open itself would fail with EntryLimit,
  inspect reports the same typed limit as a check status.
- Read-only object read: add a lock-free read_verified(digest, max_bytes) beside local::inspect that
  rehashes the object and never creates, locks or holds. fss-2h5zq.59 needs it to decode payloads by
  payload_digest.
- Writer detection (replaces the round-2 paragraph). Verified by experiment: the locks are flock
  (std File::try_lock = flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) on Linux, macOS and the BSDs), held for the lifetime
  of the LocalRootPublisher / StagingSpool value; /proc/locks prints major:minor in HEX; flock
  conflicts across open file descriptions even inside one process; POSIX locks do not interact with
  flock; a reader in another pid namespace (a container) sees none of a host writer's entries; a
  replaced LOCK file hides the holder. Algorithm:
  1. symlink_metadata(LOCK) through the authority: NotFound -> no_lock_file; non-regular ->
     invalid_layout (the class acquire_lock reports).
  2. Decode st_dev: major = ((dev>>8)&0xfff) | ((dev>>32)&!0xfff); minor = (dev&0xff) |
     ((dev>>12)&!0xff).
  3. Read /proc/locks through an injected LockTableSource capability, capped (for example 1 MiB).
  4. Parse each line with split_whitespace, strip "->" (a blocked waiter), and parse hex:hex:decimal.
  5. FLOCK WRITE on (major, minor, ino) -> held (the pid is a hint and may be stale); FLOCK READ ->
     shared_holder (for example another doctor's probe); an inode match with a device mismatch ->
     unknown(device_mismatch).
  6. Re-stat LOCK; a changed (dev, ino) -> unknown(lock_file_replaced).
  7. Check <root>/objects/LOCK, <root>/objects/spool/LOCK and ledger/journal.fssj (repair apply
     flocks it).
  writer_state is one of held{basis, pid_hint}, not_observed{basis: proc_locks, scope:
  this_host_this_pid_namespace} (NEVER "none"), not_held{basis: shared_try_lock} (only from the
  opt-in probe), unknown{reason: no_lock_table | unreadable | parse_error | over_budget |
  device_mismatch | lock_file_replaced}, or not_probed. The round-2 names none and
  concurrent_writer are replaced.
- Opt-in probe: open the publication LOCK with open_read (O_RDONLY, no create, capability.rs:139);
  never create a missing LOCK; probe only <root>/objects/LOCK (a probe on the spool LOCK would make a
  starting writer fail after it created roots/ and tombstones/, with a different error). While the
  probe is held, a starting writer gets LocalPublicationError::Locked{path} (local/mod.rs:2108);
  deployment_locked is fss-2h5zq.9's mapping and not yet registered, and nothing marks either error
  retryable. Any new SpoolIo method needs a default body (SpoolIo is implemented outside its crate).
- Same-process callers see their own lock as held, so every entry point takes a self_holds_lock
  input and refuses the probe in that case (ReferenceDeployment::layout_report is such a caller).
- An incomplete tail observed while writer_state is held or not_observed is reported as
  possibly_in_flight, not as a fault.
- Platform and authority: /proc/locks and the journal reads go through injected capabilities; the
  detector is cfg(target_os = "linux"); other targets report unknown(no_lock_table), or not_probed
  without the probe. Release builds include macOS and Windows.

## Shared rules for every CAP- bead (repeated so this bead stands alone)

  dependency closure is fss-* only, and DEP-EXCEPTION-001 admits nothing. This bridge also adds

  fss-cli. Moving the code into the planned L3/L4 crates (fss-codec-mjpeg, fss-container,
  fss-device-core, fss-model-runtime, fss-kernel-cpu, fss-coverage) is a later owner decision,
  because a new member trips the crate_topology and member-count pins (see fss-1bd1l).

  RtpPacket::parse, SequenceTracker, H264Depacketizer, NalUnit, SenderReportClock and
  JitterEstimator. Any change that needs fss-packet edits goes to an owner bead and is never
  assigned to an agent.

  recorded files and recorded transcripts only. Every file read goes through an explicit I/O
  authority value, following the ReplayIoAuthority/ReplayCx pattern in

  identifiable people, no captured network addresses. Never handle credentials: RTSP auth headers
  are detected and refused, never computed or stored. No scanning. Logs never contain secrets or
  private media bytes; they carry digests and byte spans only.

title: CAP- DOCTOR0 inspection (tests): differential against the mutating open, tree-digest read-only proof, lock-held snapshot, limits, e2e
description:
## Tests
Test files:
- crates/fss-object/tests/spool_inspect_contract.rs;
- crates/fss-publication/tests/local_inspect_contract.rs (including inspect_linkage);
- crates/fss-ledger/tests/durable_inspect_contract.rs;
- crates/fss-reference/tests/effect_journal_inspect_contract.rs.

Cases:
- Differential. Build each fault corpus, copy the root, run the mutating open (or reconcile()) on
  one copy and inspect on the other, and assert equal classifications. The corpora:
  - clean;
  - each PublishCutPoint via inject_crash_at;
  - LedgerCutPoint::AfterRootDurable via LedgeredRootPublisher::inject_crash_at (a pending root);
  - a ledger claim without a durable root (an unbacked claim);
  - each fss_ledger AppendPhase via fail_journal_after_phase;
  - a corrupt object byte, a foreign file and a symlink;
  - a redundant root temp (the temp and its target record both present);
  - a legacy spool (holds/ removed);
  - missing objects/;
  - foreign trailing bytes appended to each journal;
  - a lost-ACK effect.
  The documented extras (redundant_temps, holds_migration_pending, durability_not_resynced) are
  asserted explicitly.
- Read-only proof:
  - A tree digest over (relative path, size, mode, sha256) is equal before and after every inspect
    call, and no LOCK file is created where none existed.
  - Also run every inspection on a copy whose directories are made read-only, and assert success.
    If the test process can still create a file there (it runs privileged), log the case as skipped
    with that reason; never count it as a pass.
- Writer detection:
  - with a LocalRootPublisher holding the locks: concurrent_writer through /proc/locks;
  - after it is dropped: none;
  - the opt-in probe race: while a test hook holds the shared probe lock, LocalRootPublisher::open
    returns the typed Locked error, and it succeeds after release.
- Limits:
  - 10k orphaned entries against a small limit give a typed LimitExceeded, never unbounded output;
  - an oversize journal against a small journal-byte limit gives the typed limit before any read.
- Enumerate the cut-point and phase enums with an exhaustive match that has no wildcard arm.
- Each corpus prints one-line CAPLOG records for the e2e script.

## E2E (scripts/e2e/cap_inspect.sh)
Run the four contract tests through e2e_cargo_test. Log one step per corpus: the mutating-open
classes, the inspect classes, the extras, the writer_state, and the tree digest before and after.

## Refinement round 2 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
Rewritten in round 2 to match the new fss-2h5zq.66: the fss-ledger test file; the redundant-temp,
legacy-spool, missing-layout, foreign-tail, oversize-journal and unbacked-claim corpora; the
read-only-copy proof; and the /proc/locks and probe-race writer cases.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Blocked by (must finish first): fss-2h5zq.66, fss-2h5zq.1
- Created in refinement round 1 (2026-09-13).

## Refinement round 3 (2026-09-13, verified against main 7168075)
- Binding read-only proof: a recording SpoolIo (and an equivalent journal-read capability) that fails
  on any call outside {read_dir, next_dir_entry, entry_file_type, metadata, symlink_metadata,
  open_read, read}. The call-recording pattern exists in root_publication_review568.rs:230-340. A
  tree digest cannot see an fsync or a transient lock, so it is supplementary: it now includes
  directory mtimes (nanoseconds), which catches a temp file created and removed.
- The read-only-copy case: detect privilege by attempting create_new of a sentinel file. If it
  succeeds, emit a CAPLOG record with verdict skip and reason privileged, and restore permissions in
  a drop guard. The recording-capability proof is the one acceptance relies on.
- Differential for append phases: the mutating side cannot open with Reject on an incomplete tail.
  Compare the offset with open(Reject)'s IncompleteTail{offset}, and the prefix classification with
  open(Truncate) + reconcile() on a second copy.
- Writer cases: expect held (not concurrent_writer) and, after drop, not_observed. The probe race
  expects LocalPublicationError::Locked{path: <root>/objects/LOCK}. Add: a replaced LOCK file ->
  unknown(lock_file_replaced), never not_observed; an in-process self-held case; a missing lock
  table (injected LockTableSource) -> unknown(no_lock_table); a waiter line with "->" parses.
- More corpora: an interrupted holds migration; LOCK as a symlink or a directory (invalid_layout,
  matching acquire_lock); a missing journal (reported absent, not created); scan-limit parity
  (EntryLimit from both open and inspect).
- The parser for /proc/locks is unit-tested on recorded lines, including hex device numbers, FLOCK
  READ and WRITE, POSIX and OFDLCK entries (ignored), and "->" waiter lines.

title: CAP- TWIN: first fss-twin consumer: a recorded JPEG frame is decoded and its luma plane localizes the camera through fss_twin::localize_gray_frame (decode-vs-raw differential)
description:
## What and why
fss-twin (BTI-001..008) was merged from upstream in f9004ef and f5ed038, after the reality check.
It is an "implemented" L4 crate:
- it imports a property twin (import_twin);
- it builds and archives localization atlases (atlas_archive);
- it localizes a camera from a grayscale frame, either pinhole or distorted (rectification).
Nothing in the workspace consumes it, so it is a new island, like the four crates this epic
connects. BTI-001..009 have no beads.

The CAP DECODE track produces the grayscale frames the twin needs. Wiring recorded file -> decode ->
twin localization gives the twin its first product-path caller, and turns vision goal #27 ("register
cameras 2D->3D automatically") into something a recorded file can drive.

## Scope check (escalated to the owner in refinement round 1)
fss-twin post-dates the owner's 2026-09-13 steering decision and is still being authored upstream.
Before starting, confirm two things with the owner (agent mail or bead notes): that a consumer in
fss-reference is wanted now, and that the localization API is stable. Never edit
crates/fss-twin/** or crates/fss-geometry/**; API gaps go to notes.

## Verified facts (round 2, main 8b96911)
- There are two public localization paths:
  - Pinhole: fss_twin::localization::native::localize_gray_frame(atlas, twin, &GrayImage,
    LocalizationCamera{intrinsics, image_domain}, ImageLocalizationOptions, &mut WorkBudget)
    (native.rs:290).
    - GrayImage::new(ImageIdentity{exposure, pixels, image_domain, dimensions}, pixels, allowed,
      budget) checks sha256(pixels) == identity.pixels (BasisMismatch otherwise) and a 0/1 mask of
      the same size, and allows at most 4096x4096.
    - Every identity digest must be nonzero, and the camera's intrinsics dimensions and
      image_domain must equal the image's.
  - Raw (distorted): fss_twin::rectification::localize_raw_frame(atlas, twin, &RectificationPlan,
    &RawGrayFrame, options, budget) (rectification/localize.rs:55).
    - The plan is RectificationPlan::compile(RectificationSpec{source, target, distortion,
      maximum_radius, source_domain, calibration, range}).
    - The frame is RawGrayFrame::new(RawFrameIdentity{exposure, storage, allowed_mask,
      image_domain, calibration, dimensions, row_stride, range}, storage, allowed, budget).
    - Errors: RawLocalizationError::{Rectification, Localization}.
  - Both refuse a query whose exposure equals an atlas reference exposure
    (LocalizationError::ReferenceExposure).
- crates/fss-twin/tests/fixtures/brown_luma_96x96.gray is NOT a pinhole image:
  - It is the owner's Brown-Conrady-distorted rendering of a synthetic LCG texture: radial [-0.1,
    0.001, 0.0001], tangential [0.001, -0.001], source = target =
    PinholeIntrinsics::new(96,96,80.0,80.0,48.0,48.0), maximum_radius 1.0, LumaRange::Full.
  - Its only user, rectified_localization_contract.rs, goes through the raw path. The rectified
    pixels hash to sha256:7e31c6e153dded00386436ef3b1bdc98dba5a8dd9049c3fb65bb6ce68bd20e98 and
    localize to the identity pose with rms < 1e-4.
  - Round 1 fed it to localize_gray_frame, which would test the wrong camera model.
- That test builds its atlas in-test from the undistorted texture: seed 1973_u32,
  state = state*1664525+1013904223, sample 20+((state>>16)%180), reference exposure [1;32]. No atlas
  is committed.
- crates/fss-twin/examples/localize_atlas.rs (present at 8b96911) is the owner's reference
  composition: import_twin + atlas_archive::decode_atlas(bytes, twin,
  ArchiveExpectation{package, provenance, descriptor: native::descriptor_domain()}) + either path.
- fss-twin re-exports no fss-geometry types. WorkBudget, PinholeIntrinsics and PoseSolverOptions are
  named only through fss-geometry, so fss-reference needs a direct fss-geometry edge. That edge is
  gated by fss-1bd1l, like CAP- GEO.
- JFIF luma is full range, so decoded luma uses LumaRange::Full.

## Build
`crates/fss-reference/src/twin_localization.rs`. Its module_declarations plane is "cognition", or
"support" with a stated reason.
- `localize_decoded_frame(decoded: &DecodedImage, receipt: &DecodeReceipt, atlas:
  &LocalizationAtlas, twin: &PropertyTwin, mode: TwinImageMode, options: ImageLocalizationOptions,
  budget, cx) -> Result<TwinLocalizationReceipt, TwinLocalizationError>`, where
  `TwinImageMode::{Pinhole(LocalizationCamera), Raw(&RectificationPlan)}`.
- Luma: DecodedImage::luma() from fss-2h5zq.39, the Y samples before colour conversion, shape
  [H, W].
- Identity:
  - exposure = sha256 over a domain-separated encoding of (the capsule id, the capsule source
    digest). It is never an atlas reference exposure.
  - pixels, or storage in raw mode, = sha256(luma bytes).
  - image_domain comes from the camera or the rectification spec; calibration from the spec.
  - row_stride = width.
  - The allowed mask is all ones unless a privacy mask is configured; its digest is recorded.
- The receipt binds:
  - the capsule source digest, the decode receipt digest and the luma digest;
  - the mode, and in raw mode the rectification map digest and output-domain digest;
  - the atlas digest (LocalizationAtlas::digest) and the twin digest (PropertyTwin::digest);
  - the selection statistics (selected, omitted) and the matched-landmark count;
  - the outcome: localized{candidates with pose and rms} | insufficient_matches |
    geometric_failure | refused{reason};
  - the work used.
- Register SCHEMA-DOMAIN-TWIN-LOCALIZATION-RECEIPT-001 `fss.twin_localization_receipt.v1` and
  bump the count. Add the ledger delta family "twin_localization_receipt" to the family table of
  fss-2h5zq.9.
- Truth: a pose from one frame is a pose candidate, not a calibration certificate. It never
  upgrades an ExtrinsicsCertificate and never widens coverage on its own, and the report says so.
- Budget and cancellation: fss_geometry::WorkBudget::cancellable, bridged to ReplayCx.
- Cargo edges: fss-reference -> fss-twin (L7 -> L4; fss-twin is "implemented", not gated) and
  fss-reference -> fss-geometry (L7 -> L4; gated by fss-1bd1l).

## Fixture
- The two JPEG encodings of brown_luma from fss-2h5zq.5:
  - brown_luma_q100 (an all-ones DQT) is the strict differential;
  - brown_luma_qfix (normal quality) is observational.
- The atlas: rebuild the owner's in-test atlas in the CAP test from the same LCG texture, citing
  the owner test. Also round-trip it through atlas_archive::encode_atlas and decode_atlas, so the
  archive path that fss-2h5zq.61's --twin-atlas uses is exercised. Nothing is written into
  crates/fss-twin/**.

## Refinement round 2 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
Rewritten in round 2:
- the raw (rectification) path replaces localize_gray_frame for the distorted brown_luma fixture;
- a two-quality differential replaces a single, likely flaky one;
- the fss-geometry edge makes this bead depend on fss-1bd1l;
- the exposure-laundering refusal is added.

- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Blocked by (must finish first): fss-2h5zq.41, fss-2h5zq.5, fss-1bd1l (round 2: the direct fss-geometry edge)
- Created in refinement round 1 (2026-09-13).

## Refinement round 3 (2026-09-13, verified against main 7168075)
- Identity: set pixels (pinhole) or storage (raw) from the decode receipt's RECORDED luma digest,
  after a CAP pre-check that sha256(luma()) equals it (typed LumaCustodyMismatch). Recomputing the
  digest from the bytes being passed would make fss-twin's BasisMismatch check vacuous, so the
  tamper case could never fire.
- 3-component inputs always use luma(), never RGB converted to Y from the tensor.
- Refuse frames larger than fss-twin's limits before calling it: GrayImage allows at most
  4096 x 4096 (4,194,304 pixels) and row_stride at most 65,536; the decoder default allows 8192.
- Preconditions: row_stride = width holds only because luma() is tight and cropped; the raw-mode mask
  length is W x H.
- Fixture ids: brown_luma_q100 and brown_luma_qfix (fss-2h5zq.5 round-3 note; its worktree currently
  has one q90 encoding named gray_96x96_brown_luma).
- The receipt objects are reachable from a durable ledgered root (fss-2h5zq.23 round-3 rule).

title: CAP- TWIN (tests): decode-vs-raw localization differential, tamper/budget refusals, determinism, e2e
description:
## Tests (crates/fss-reference/tests/twin_localization_contract.rs)
- Raw-path differential:
  - localize the owner's raw brown_luma_96x96 bytes and the decoded brown_luma_q100 luma through
    RawGrayFrame and localize_raw_frame, with the owner's rectification spec and LumaRange::Full;
  - assert outcome equality and the recorded pose tolerance;
  - on the raw input, reproduce the owner's rectified-pixel sha256 (7e31c6e1...), proving the setup
    matches.
- Observational qfix case: log the outcome, the matched-landmark count and the pose error. Assert
  only that there is no confident wrong pose.
- Pinhole path: encode the owner's undistorted texture in-test with the CAP fixture encoder at q100,
  decode it, rotate it as the owner's native test does, and localize with localize_gray_frame.
  Assert the rotated pose within the tolerance.
- Refusals, each typed and with no pose:
  - one flipped luma byte gives BasisMismatch;
  - a wrong image domain;
  - a wrong calibration (raw mode) gives a Rectification error;
  - wrong dimensions;
  - exposure [1;32], the reference exposure (the laundering guard);
  - WorkBudget::new(1) and a set cancellation flag.
- Archive: encode_atlas followed by decode_atlas preserves the atlas digest, and the stage works
  from the decoded archive.
- Determinism: repeated runs give identical receipt digests.
- Truth guard: the receipt never carries a certificate or a coverage claim.
- Print CAPLOG records per case.

## E2E (scripts/e2e/cap_twin_localization.sh)
For each case, log the mode, the luma digest, the rectification map digest (raw mode), the atlas and
twin digests, the outcome, the pose, the residual RMS and the tolerance check.

## Refinement round 2 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
Rewritten in round 2 to match fss-2h5zq.68: the raw path for brown_luma, the q100/qfix split, the
pinhole case on the undistorted texture, the exposure-laundering refusal and the archive round
trip.

title: CAP- fixtures: recorded RTSP/1.0 interleaved-TCP session transcript (no credentials) for the sans-IO parser
description:
## What and why
The sans-IO RTSP parser (P2) is tested against a RECORDED session transcript, never a socket. We
synthesize the transcript first-party so it contains no real host, no credentials and no
third-party server quirks we cannot license.

## Build
- `crates/fss-reference/src/media_fixture/rtsp.rs`: builds a byte transcript of a client/server
  exchange in a documented container format. Each record is `direction (C2S|S2C) u8`,
  `offset_ms u32`, `len u32`, then `bytes`, with a text header `#!fss-rtsp-transcript v1\n`.
  - Exchange: OPTIONS, DESCRIBE (with an SDP body: m=video 0 RTP/AVP 96, a=rtpmap:96 H264/90000,
    a=fmtp:96 packetization-mode=1;sprop-parameter-sets=<base64 SPS>,<base64 PPS>,
    a=control:trackID=1), SETUP (Transport: RTP/AVP/TCP;unicast;interleaved=0-1), PLAY
    (Range: npt=0-), then S2C interleaved frames `$ 0x00 len16 <RTP packet>` built from the
    FIXH264 RTP packetizer, a few RTCP SRs on channel 1, and TEARDOWN.
  - URL host is `rtsp://fixture.invalid/stream` (the .invalid TLD by RFC 2606). There is never an
    IP address.
  - Variants: clean; `auth_required` (the server answers 401 with a WWW-Authenticate challenge;
    the transcript stops there because the client never answers with credentials);
    `interleave_split` (an interleaved frame split across TCP records); `bad_content_length`;
    `session_timeout_header`.
- Committed under tests/fixtures/media/rtsp/ with manifest rows.

## Registration
module_declarations "support"; MANIFEST.delta rows.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Blocked by (must finish first):
  - fss-2h5zq.3: CAP- fixtures: deterministic synthetic H.264 Annex-B and rtpdump (RTP/RFC 6184) fixture generator
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.8: CAP- fixtures RTSP transcript (tests): record framing, SDP sanity, no-credential guard, e2e
  - fss-2h5zq.33: CAP- RTSP parser (tests): transcript event sequences, incremental splits at every byte, no-credential guard, e2e
  - fss-2h5zq.35: CAP- RTSP session (tests): state traces per transcript, RTP equivalence with rtpdump path, no-socket guard, e2e
  - fss-2h5zq.37: CAP- RTSP lab ingest (tests): CLI integration per transcript variant and e2e script

## Refinement round 1 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- The interleaved RTP comes from the FIXH264 packetizer, so each SSRC generation in a transcript
  also starts with the sacrificial probation packet (see fss-2h5zq.3). The manifest lists the
  expected per-packet SequenceClass.
- Add the variants `sr_absent` (no RTCP SR, so capture time stays unknown) and
  `get_parameter_keepalive` (C2S GET_PARAMETER).
- Use a per-family manifest: tests/fixtures/media/rtsp/fixture_manifest.json.
- The RTCP SR packets must parse with fss_packet::RtcpCompound::parse(bytes, PacketLimits, RtcpMode)
  and bind with SenderReportClock::new(key, 90_000, report, received_ns, uncertainty_ns,
  max_distance_ticks) (verified signatures). The manifest records each SR's NTP and RTP timestamps.

## Refinement round 2 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- RtcpMode (crates/fss-packet/src/rtcp.rs:7, verified) has exactly two variants:
  - `Compound`: the first packet must be an SR (200) or RR (201), and an SDES CNAME item for that
    sender must appear; otherwise parse returns PacketError::Compound.
  - `ReducedSize`: independently framed reports (RFC 5506); negotiation belongs to the session
    owner.
- Every SR on channel 1 in the default variants is a compound packet: the SR, then an SDES with one
  chunk for the SR's SSRC.
  - The chunk carries CNAME "fss-fixture@fixture.invalid" (synthetic; no address).
  - Encode it exactly per RFC 3550 §6.5: an item list ended by a null item, and the chunk padded to
    a 32-bit boundary.
  - fss-kr9n3 tracks a failing fss-packet SDES test
    (source_description_must_terminate_and_match_chunk_count). Follow the RFC, not what today's
    parser accepts, and record any disagreement on fss-kr9n3.
- SR contents must satisfy SenderReportClock::new (timing.rs:70):
  - the SR SSRC equals the RTP SSRC of that generation (otherwise StreamMismatch);
  - the NTP timestamp is nonzero (zero means NoSenderReport).
  The manifest records each SR's NTP seconds and fraction, RTP timestamp, and packet and octet
  counts.
- New variant `rtcp_rsize`: the SDP m-line carries a=rtcp-rsize, and the SRs are sent reduced-size
  (SR only, no SDES). CAP- RTSP session (fss-2h5zq.34) selects ReducedSize only when a=rtcp-rsize
  was negotiated.
- Mutations (an SR without CNAME, a mismatched SR SSRC, a zero NTP) are built in fss-2h5zq.35's
  tests, never committed.

title: CAP- fixtures RTSP transcript (tests): record framing, SDP sanity, no-credential guard, e2e
description:
## Unit tests (crates/fss-reference/tests/media_fixture_rtsp_contract.rs)
- Regeneration is byte-identical.
- Record framing sums to the file length.
- Every C2S request has CSeq.
- Guard test: no record contains 'Authorization:' and no fixture contains an IPv4 or IPv6
  literal (regex).
- The base64 SPS/PPS in the SDP decode to the same bytes as the FIXH264 SPS/PPS.

## E2E (scripts/e2e/cap_fixtures_rtsp.sh)
Run the manifest sha256 check and the no-credential grep over tests/fixtures/media/rtsp, one
logged step per file.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Blocked by (must finish first):
  - fss-2h5zq.7: CAP- fixtures: recorded RTSP/1.0 interleaved-TCP session transcript (no credentials) for the sans-IO parser
  - fss-2h5zq.1: CAP- e2e harness: scripts/e2e/lib.sh structured JSON-lines logging and runner

  crate, target, test, example and helper, with no exception path. Zero third-party crates: the
  dependency closure is fss-* only, and DEP-EXCEPTION-001 admits nothing. This bridge also adds

  fss-cli. Moving the code into the planned L3/L4 crates (fss-codec-mjpeg, fss-container,

  because a new member trips the crate_topology and member-count pins (see fss-1bd1l).

  RtpPacket::parse, SequenceTracker, H264Depacketizer, NalUnit, SenderReportClock and
  JitterEstimator. Any change that needs fss-packet edits goes to an owner bead and is never
  assigned to an agent.

  recorded files and recorded transcripts only. Every file read goes through an explicit I/O
  authority value, following the ReplayIoAuthority/ReplayCx pattern in

title: CAP- LAB: ReferenceDeployment composition in fss-reference (spool + root-last publication + durable ledger + effects + situation)
description:
## What and why
This is the first step of top-10 gap #1, "make the one runnable demo use the real crates". The
real composition exists only inside cargo tests:
- crates/fss-reference/tests/situation_invariants_contract.rs, durable_effect_contract.rs,
  context_selection_inv092_contract.rs and meaningful_delta_invariants.rs build a
  DurableReferenceLedger;
- they then call policy::evaluate_unknown_presence / publish_reference_event, alert.rs,
  durable_effect::DurableEffectJournal, situation::compile_reference_situation and
  seal_reference_handoff.

fss-lab cannot call test code. Lift that composition into ONE library type that the lab, the
file-ingest adapter, the doctor and the capstone pipeline all share, so there is exactly one
place where "a deployment root on disk" is defined.

## Build
`crates/fss-reference/src/reference_deployment.rs` defines `ReferenceDeployment`:

- `open(root: &Path, site_lineage, cx: &ReplayCx) -> Result<Self, ReferenceError>` creates or
  reopens a fixed layout under root:
  - `root/ledger/journal.fssj`: fss_ledger::DurableReferenceLedger::open(path, lineage,
    IncompleteTailPolicy::Reject). Reject is used on open; repair is the doctor's job, never
    silent.
  - `root/objects/`: fss_publication::LocalRootPublisher::open(root, LocalPublicationLimits),
    which owns the fss_object StagingSpool.
  - `root/effects/journal.fssj`: fss_reference::DurableEffectJournal.
  - `root/LAYOUT`: a small canonical layout-version file.
- `stage_and_publish(slot, objects: &[&[u8]]) -> LocalPublicationReceipt`: stage children, stage
  the manifest, and publish root-last (child-first), with cancellation through the
  PublishCancellation trait bridged to ReplayCx.
- `append_batch(deltas) -> LedgerSnapshot`: prepare_batch + append on the durable ledger. Every
  batch carries the publication root digest, so ledger <-> object custody is digest-linked.
  GATE-010 needs "source bytes, model result, event revision, and receipt are digest-linked".
- Thin pass-throughs for the policy, alert/effect and situation entry points used by the tests,
  so callers never reach into three crates.
- `layout_report() -> DeploymentLayout`, a read-only description reused by `fss doctor`.
- Determinism: every digest reported must be independent of the absolute root path and of the
  wall clock. All times come from the VirtualClock or ReplayCx. Assert this in tests by opening
  two different roots.

## Where it connects
- It depends only on crates fss-reference already depends on (fss-core, fss-ledger, fss-object,
  fss-publication). No new crate edges.
- Consumers: LAB2 (scenarios), INGEST file adapter, DOCTOR/STATUS, CAPSTONE.
- Related existing beads: GATE-010 fss-x4a.2.2 (walking skeleton), fss-x4a.28.41 (e2e scripts),
  fss-x4a.24.40 (FSS-240 rehearsal). This bead does not close them.

## Failure semantics to preserve
- Crash between stage and publish leaves orphaned staging, which the LocalRecoveryReport and
  SpoolRecoveryReport surface on reopen.
- An incomplete journal tail is refused on open with a typed error that names the doctor
  (`fss doctor --root`) as the next affordance.
- A lost ACK leaves the effect indeterminate. It never becomes silently verified.

## Registration
- module_declarations entry: "ambiguous". It bridges authority storage and effect wiring, so this
  classification is honest; the checker reports it as a finding without guessing. Alternatively
  split it into support-only glue if the checker requires it; record the decision in notes.
- A new domain SCHEMA-DOMAIN-REFERENCE-DEPLOYMENT-LAYOUT-001 `fss.reference_deployment.layout.v1`,
  only if the LAYOUT file is canonically digested.
- MANIFEST.delta rows.

## Dependency map (resolved ids)
- Parent epic: fss-2h5zq
- Related existing beads (context only, not blocking; this bead does not close them): fss-x4a.2.2, fss-x4a.28.41, fss-x4a.24.40
- Unblocks:
  - fss-2h5zq.10: CAP- LAB ReferenceDeployment (tests): reopen, digest linkage, crash cut points, path independence, e2e
  - fss-2h5zq.11: CAP- LAB: port the six fss-lab scenarios onto ReferenceDeployment (real crates) with an explicit --root and report schema v2
  - fss-2h5zq.23: CAP- INGEST: FileIngestAdapter (ADP-FILE-001 reference slice): file -> SensorCapsules with source custody -> root-last publication -> ledger batch
  - fss-2h5zq.57: CAP- DOCTOR: `fss doctor --json --root <dir>` inspects the real deployment (journal tail, orphaned staging, broken roots, indeterminate obligations)
  - fss-2h5zq.59: CAP- STATUS: `fss status --json --root <dir>` reports sensors, streams, capsules, events and obligations from the real ledger (never implying unsupported readiness)

## Refinement round 1 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- Use the existing ledger-linked publication rather than a bespoke linkage. The type is
  fss_publication::LedgeredRootPublisher::new(&mut LocalRootPublisher, &mut DurableReferenceLedger)
  (crates/fss-publication/src/ledger.rs:685).
  - It provides publish_and_commit, prepare_root_batch, commit_prepared, reconcile() ->
    RootLedgerReconciliation, and the crash hook inject_crash_at(LedgerCutPoint::AfterRootDurable).
  - `stage_and_publish` and `append_batch` above become thin wrappers over it, so the ledger <->
    object custody linkage is the one fss-publication already tests.
- Opening:
  - DurableReferenceLedger::open(path, site_lineage, IncompleteTailPolicy::Reject);
  - LocalRootPublisher::open(root.join("objects"), LocalPublicationLimits);
  - DurableEffectJournal::open(path, IncompleteTailPolicy::Reject).
  LocalRootPublisher::open creates directories and takes an exclusive lock on
  fss.local_publication.lock. So a second concurrent open of one root is a typed `deployment_locked`
  error, and doctor and status never use open; they use CAP- DOCTOR0 (fss-2h5zq.66).
- Situation: route through fss_reference::compile_reference_situation_with_durable_journal(request,
  &DurableEffectJournal, &DurableReferenceLedger), then seal_reference_handoff. Both are exported
  from situation_guard.rs. There are two compile_reference_situation functions: the one in
  situation.rs is private, and the one in situation_guard.rs is exported.
- Ledger delta families. EvidenceDelta.family is a free string.
  - Define pub const family names in this module. Reuse the families fss-reference already writes:
    "sensor_capsule", "event_revision" and "alert_effect_outcome".
  - Later beads add their families to the same table: file_import_manifest,
    acquisition_transition, decode_receipt, model_invocation_receipt, executor_model_result and
    twin_localization_receipt.
  - Stage every delta's payload object as a child of its batch, so doctor and status can fetch and
    decode it by payload_digest.
- Export `pub const DEPLOYMENT_CANCEL_STAGES: &[&str]`, listing every ReplayCx checkpoint stage name,
  so the crash matrix can enumerate its cancellation points.

## Refinement round 2 (2026-09-13, verified against main 8b96911)
- Lock facts (verified):
  - The publication lock is <publication root>/LOCK (LOCAL_LOCK_FILE = "LOCK",
    fss-publication local/mod.rs:107).
  - The owned spool has its own <publication root>/spool/LOCK (SPOOL_LOCK_FILE,
    fss-object spool/mod.rs:79).
  - The doc comment on LocalRootPublisher::open (local/mod.rs:563) still says
    fss.local_publication.lock. That is stale; CAP- DOCTOR0 fixes it. Every CAP text that says
    fss.local_publication.lock means <root>/objects/LOCK.
- Open order: fss_ledger::Journal::open takes no lock. So open LocalRootPublisher (root/objects)
  FIRST; it takes the only locks. Only then open DurableReferenceLedger and DurableEffectJournal. A
  second opener fails with the typed, retryable deployment_locked before it touches either journal.
- Capacity:
  - LocalPublicationLimits has no Default.
  - Spool defaults: max_object_bytes 64 MiB (fss_object::MAX_OBJECT_BYTES), max_total_bytes 512 MiB,
    max_objects 65,536.
  - A manifest holds at most 16,384 children (MAX_MANIFEST_CHILDREN).
  - An fss-ledger batch holds at most 16,384 deltas and 16,384 children (batch_codec.rs), and a
    journal record payload is at most 16 MiB (MAX_RECORD_PAYLOAD_BYTES).
  ReferenceDeployment takes an explicit DeploymentLimits (publication, spool, ledger) and records
  its digest in LAYOUT. Every capacity refusal is typed and names the limit.
- LAYOUT (canonical) records the layout version, site_lineage, the relative component paths
  (ledger/journal.fssj, objects/, effects/journal.fssj) and the limits digest. doctor and status read
  site_lineage from LAYOUT to replay the ledger read-only (fss-2h5zq.66). A root without LAYOUT is
  not_a_deployment.
- Recovery is explicit, never silent. Doctor is read-only and never repairs. Add
  `ReferenceDeployment::open_for_recovery(root, RecoveryAction, cx)`, with RecoveryAction:
  - TruncateIncompleteLedgerTail and TruncateIncompleteEffectTail reopen that journal with
    IncompleteTailPolicy::Truncate. Per journal.rs:18 it "truncates exactly the incomplete suffix
    after validating every committed record".
  - ApplySealedLedgerRepair{plan_digest} uses the audited fss_ledger repair path (doctor, plan,
    SealedRepairPlan::apply; repair.rs; fss-x4a.9.21). It applies only if the recomputed plan digest
    matches.
  Each action returns a typed receipt: bytes removed or quarantined, committed_len and last_root
  before and after. The CLI is `fss-lab recover` (fss-2h5zq.15).
- The family table gains the rule from fss-2h5zq.23: an import is complete only when its final
  "file_import_manifest" batch exists.

title: Bug: tombstone rename indeterminate state flattened; cleanup errors replace original; weak review568 child-root test
description:
Found by the orchestrator's 7.6 gate-fix pass (worktree commit 47f3595), outside that bead's G1-G3 scope.

1. crates/fss-publication/src/local/mod.rs record_tombstone: a tombstone rename that takes effect but reports failure (fail-after-apply) still returns a plain Io::Rename error and does not poison the publisher. The tombstone is then on disk but absent from memory, and a reopen admits it, which can break roots published in between. This is the same indeterminate-flattening class as 7.6 G1. It needs the same treatment: remove plus fsync rollback, and on rollback failure a durable indeterminate marker, poisoning, and a typed RootVisibilityIndeterminate-style error.
2. Several paths do `self.remove_temp(..)?; return Err(original)`, so a cleanup failure replaces the original error. Nothing becomes visible in those cases, but the original cause is lost; carry both.
3. tests/root_publication_review568.rs test_publish_rejects_child_root_that_is_only_visible_not_durable: slot A fails only because the publisher is already poisoned, so the "Visible child blocks publish" assertion proves nothing. Reopen a fresh publisher over a visible-not-durable child and assert the specific typed refusal.

Acceptance: failing-first tests for each item using the deterministic FaultInjectingSpoolIo; workspace test and clippy green via rch.

title: Perception: generate real MJPEG frames in VirtualCameraSpec instead of PRNG payloads
description: The virtual camera generates pseudorandom payload bytes from a seed, not actual image data. This means the entire downstream pipeline (MJPEG decode, foreground detection, luma analysis) has no real pixel data to work with. Fix: generate deterministic but structurally valid MJPEG frames (each packet contains a fragment of a synthetic JPEG image) so the MJPEG codec can decode them to real luma pixels. The frames should show controlled change between captures (e.g. a moving rectangle on a static background) so the foreground detector produces meaningful regions. Requires: image generation in VirtualCameraSpec (synthetic JPEG via fss-codec-mjpeg encode), packet framing that carries JPEG fragments, and a test that verifies decoded luma matches the synthetic pattern.

comments.author: IvoryOsprey
comments.text: Root cause established by instrumented child runs (fd-table + kernel probes): at _finish_streams the raw write(1) raises BrokenPipeError (parent read end closed, sole holder = child), yet stream.flush() returned True - a bare flush is not evidence of delivery, and a zero-byte write does not detect a readerless pipe either (probe: succeeds). Check only turns success into failure; non-pipe descriptors keep the flush verdict. Both failing tests now pass (3 passed incl /dev/full full-device case); full suite 469 passed + 720 subtests, zero failures. No other behavior changed.

title: Scalar executor throughput: profile-driven kernels (im2col/GEMM tiling) with tolerance-certified agreement to the scalar reference

Per PURE_RUST_MODEL_RUNTIME.md, add optimized kernels (Conv2d via im2col plus cache-tiled GEMM, packed weights, fused activation) alongside the scalar reference, never replacing it, each with a tolerance-certified contract against the scalar kernel, safe Rust only. Profile first (per-op time on YOLOX-Nano), predeclare the target and a countermetric, and report before/after with the same inputs. YOLOX conformance vs onnxruntime must still hold.
close_reason: Landed in main 7d6c625 (b16d5bc, subagent; rebased by the orchestrator). The optimized CPU executor (packed 3x3 conv register tiles, 1x1 as GEMM, row-wise depthwise, fused bias+SiLU) is BIT-IDENTICAL to the scalar reference (certified tolerance 0 ULP by randomized differential tests; YOLOX conformance vs onnxruntime unchanged). YOLOX-Nano graph execution drops from a median 3085.4 ms to 193.2 ms per 416x416 inference (16.0x; release, one noisy shared AMD EPYC worker, 15 samples; docs/PERF_LEDGER.md PERF-001). Kernel generation is bound into model identity, and --kernels scalar-reference forces the oracle. Orchestrator gates at 7d6c625 via rch: workspace tests exit 0 (5846), doc tests exit 0, clippy exit 0, fmt exit 0. Not measured: arm64, multi-threading.

title: Privacy masks at decode: owner-drawn masked regions removed before any analysis, export or hydration (GOAL-009)
description: GOAL-009 privacy by architecture has no implementation. Add an owner-declared, per-sensor privacy mask policy (polygons or rectangles in image coordinates, versioned, digest-bound, approval-gated like zones) applied inside retained decode (JPEG/MJPEG/H.264/H.265) BEFORE frames reach foreground, detector, tracker, PGM output or any agent hydration. Masked pixels become a fixed fill; the decode receipt binds the mask-policy digest; coverage witnesses mark masked zone area as not_observable (never absence); events and agent outputs record privacy_transform. Unmasked access to masked pixels needs an explicit, separately authorized capability and is refused by default. Tests: masked regions never influence detections (planted motion inside a mask gives no candidate), receipt binding, coverage honesty, refusal of unmasked export.
close_reason: Landed in main eb4d2e2 (9c21e87 by subagent; merged onto geometric coverage by a second subagent, which fixed a real leak: tolerant decode served unmasked frames). Owner-declared per-sensor rectangle mask policies are retained approval-gated as authority family privacy_mask_policy and applied inside every retained decode (JPEG, H.264, H.265, RGB) before any consumer. Receipts bind the policy; masked zones are not_observable (privacy_masked), never absence; unmasked access is refused with no override. No-policy outputs stay byte-identical (golden pins). Orchestrator split gates at eb4d2e2 via rch: rest 2801/0, fss-reference 0 failures, fss-cli 378/0, doc 32/0, clippy exit 0; fmt, policy, planes and registry checks pass. GOAL-009 still lacks: masks on live capture paths, deletion closure, retention schedules, masking at export or cloud boundaries.

description: crates/fss-reference/src/agent_session/* (~13k lines: durable session store, checkpoint journal, workspace revisions, disclosure, hydration, handoff) and situation handoff sealing are tested but have no surface. The fss/1 protocol requires session.open (AOP-001), session.resume (AOP-002) and handoff (AOP-012), and AGENTS.md forbids mission state existing only in conversation. Add fss CLI commands backed by the existing durable stores in a deployment root: open a mission-scoped session (mission and objective contract, principal, budgets), record workspace revisions, publish a root-last handoff capsule, and resume it, enumerating assumptions invalidated since the handoff anchor (reusing orient/follow anchors).
