title: Perception pipeline: cross-camera association with time/geometry gates
description: Implement cross-camera association: given tracked objects from multiple cameras covering overlapping zones, associate detections of the same physical object across cameras using time proximity (capture timestamps within a bounded window) and geometric consistency (rectified ground-plane positions within a distance threshold). Types should align with the existing AgentSession/SituationFrame model. Requires: (1) Kalman tracker output from at least 2 cameras, (2) per-camera calibration (even approximate/focal-only), (3) time sync or declared clock offset. Output: AssociatedObject pairs/groups with confidence scores. This is the step that turns per-camera tracks into a property-level picture. Dependency: the Kalman tracker bead (fss-zccxz). Acceptance: (1) two cameras with overlapping FOVs correctly associate the same object, (2) non-overlapping objects are not associated, (3) time-mismatched detections are not associated, (4) deterministic.
close_reason: Cross-camera association implemented with dual gates (time + geometry) and greedy best-first assignment. 7/7 tests green via rch. Confidence formula: (1 - dt/max_dt) * (1 - dist/max_dist), threshold-gated. Third of four perception-pipeline components. fss-ub4yv (event generation) remains.

title: Unsafe checker: close pre-existing non-member target-root leaks (ed2015 legacy lib/bin paths, bin candidate break, build list)
description:
Found by the independent review of fss-na476 (evidence in orchestrator scratchpad rna476/: gt.py, gt.out, gtws/, e2e_leaks.out). These are REAL enforcement leaks, present on main since before na476: cargo builds a file that the forbid checker never checks (the CLI exits 0 with the file lacking the forbid attribute). - A7/A8 (scripts/unsafe_prohibition_checker.py ~1119-1131): edition 2015 [lib] with no path and no src/lib.rs -> cargo builds src/{lib.name or package name with - replaced by _}.rs. Check that legacy file.

- F10 (~1302-1320, ~1030-1032, nightly multiple build scripts): build = ["tools/a.rs", "tools/b.rs"] -> check each path and do not treat build.rs as built.

title: Bug: durable ledger and ReferenceLedger accept a new batch reusing an existing batch ID with different content
description: Found by the 7.4 ledger oracle's differential tests (orchestrator worktree commit 90ebcf1). DurableReferenceLedger (fss-ledger) and core ReferenceLedger accept a later EvidenceDeltaBatch whose batch_id equals an already-committed batch's id but whose content differs, so two committed batches share one stable identity. This violates the invariant that stable IDs are never reused or renumbered, and breaks idempotent-duplicate detection. The oracle rejects it. Pinned divergence test: ledger_oracle_contract::divergence_batch_id_reuse_is_rejected_by_oracle_but_accepted_by_durable_journal, which intentionally fails once this is fixed; flip it to assert agreement in the fix commit. Fix: reject batch-ID reuse with a typed error (identical resubmission stays an idempotent duplicate) in both the durable journal append path and ReferenceLedger, with failing tests first, plus a restart case (reuse detected after reopening the journal).
notes: DURABLE HALF merged as 967efbd. w34 @967efbd: workspace tests 689/0, clippy green, fmt clean, policy green. DurableReferenceLedger keeps a committed batch-ID index (rebuilt on open/verify_storage) and rejects same-ID different-content batches with DurableLedgerError::BatchIdConflict (ERR-LEDGER-DURABLE-BATCH-ID-CONFLICT-001) before any journal write; replay rejects journals containing reuse. Tests in durable_batch_id_reuse_contract: different-content reuse rejected with a byte-identical journal, identical resubmission still a duplicate, reuse detected after reopen, older non-head reuse, reuse after reconciled indeterminate append, and replay rejection; the oracle divergence test was converted to the agreement test batch_id_reuse_is_rejected_by_oracle_and_durable_journal. REMAINING (keeps the bead open): the same fix in core ReferenceLedger (fss-core/src/evidence.rs) -> PeachDove after INV-056. No-claim: journals written before the fix that contain a reuse now fail to open (fail closed, no migration path).
close_reason: Verified at 99c8eea (wave w47): remote cargo test --workspace --all-targets 878 passed/0 failed; workspace clippy GREEN; fmt clean; policy green. Durable half 967efbd (DurableLedgerError::BatchIdConflict, a committed batch-ID index rebuilt on open, replay rejection) and core half 3933eeb (ReferenceLedger rejects same-ID different-content batches with ContractError::IdempotencyConflict; identical resubmission unchanged). QuietBear's adversarial review of 3933eeb: ACCEPT / SOUND. The replay test was rebuilt at the raw journal layer in e2a9112 (0 assertions removed), and the core/durable error mapping is documented. Tests: durable_batch_id_reuse_contract (6), batch_id_reuse_is_rejected_by_oracle_and_durable_journal, and the evidence.rs unit test batch_id_reuse_with_different_content_is_rejected.

title: Alert dispatch must refuse when an unretired sensor-tamper observation affects the event, even without a new event revision
description: Follow-up split from fss-wjisz round-3 review (99a6e6b, 2026-09-13, probe P6c). fss-wjisz makes alert dispatch revalidate the CURRENT event revision from the ledger; a tamper that arrives as a new EVENT REVISION is refused. But a sensor-tamper OBSERVATION published to the ledger WITHOUT a new revision of the alerting event still lets a prepared alert deliver. The fss-wjisz bead text says dispatch must refuse when the event "now carries an integrity risk". Scope: at the shared dispatch revalidation helper, consult the lineage open-tamper status for the event failure domain / sensor identity (the stickiness machinery from fss-2uftm: unretired tamper until an evidenced sensor_integrity_restoration) and refuse with a typed error, Cancelled record, 0 messages. Acceptance: planted P6c test (tamper observation without event revision → refused), an evidenced restoration re-enables dispatch, an unrelated-domain tamper does not block, both public dispatch paths covered, mutants killed. Probe source: scratchpad/rwjisz3/rwjisz3_probe.rs. Blocked on fss-wjisz and fss-2uftm.
notes: Note: In-memory forked ledger cannot be told apart without an instance identity.
close_reason: Implemented across c658e16 (core consult), 17e08c2 (call-site rustfmt), 8f3210a (manifest overlay) — committed by RubyCoast from the shared tree under this bead tag. Dispatch revalidation now consults the ledger-wide failure-domain tamper state: refuse_on_open_domain_tamper folds every ledger event revision's evidence (apply_evidence_batch, promoted to pub in fss-core) through a caller-supplied payload reader; any open unretired tamper record citing a domain the alerting event's evidence cites refuses with SensorIntegrityRisk, Cancelled record, 0 messages. Both public paths covered (dispatch_reference_alert + DurableEffectJournal::dispatch_alert) plus ReferenceDeployment via spool reader (no signature change). Tests: cross_event_domain_tamper_refuses_dispatch_p6c, evidenced_restoration_reenables_dispatch_p6c, unrelated_domain_tamper_and_durable_path_p6c — all green; mutant (consult removed) turns the two refusal tests red, suite otherwise green. Final suite: 398 passed; remaining ingest::inference SlotConflict failures are ingest-lane (RubyCoast notified).

title: Effect terminalization without proof: evidence-less Known terminalizes non-Indeterminate effects; Indeterminate->Unknown->Known laundering; projections may drop indeterminate effects
description: From the fss-hmfs5 review (probes D/E/J/G at f092da5): in crates/fss-reference/src/meaningful_delta.rs, an effect cell that was NOT Indeterminate in the basis (Unknown, Stale, or absent) becoming Known with NO evidence, or with contradictions, yields TerminalTransition with no EffectUncertainty or CoverageLoss. That conflicts with KSTATE-001 ('established by admissible evidence or a proved terminal postcondition'). Together with fss-hmfs5 this enables two-step laundering: Indeterminate->Unknown reports 'remains', then Unknown->Known without evidence reports terminal, and pairwise deltas can't see the history. Fix: any effect terminalization requires the full is_irreversible_effect_premise bar (Known + evidence + no contradictions + valid validity window) whatever the prior state. Also enforce at the projection/publication layer that an indeterminate effect cell can't be dropped or re-labelled without a terminal proof or delegation record (AGENTS.md: obligations terminal, delegated or explicitly indeterminate). Check whether situation.rs:367 can build a Verified/Failed effect whose operation.result_digest is None (the reviewer couldn't verify reachability). Failing-first tests for each path.

title: Typed evidence references: carry origin provenance class per evidence digest so a lone relabelled KnowledgeCell is detectable
description: Follow-up split from fss-x4a.30.83.10 PROV round 3 review (5dfbe47/981365f, 2026-09-13). Problem: KnowledgeCell.evidence is a list of bare ContentDigest values, so the class that PRODUCED a digest (Observed/Derived/Predicted/Remembered/VendorClaimed/...) is unknown to the validator. The laundering check can therefore only compare cells that share a digest inside one SituationFrame or MeaningfulDelta. A LONE cell whose provenance was relabelled (e.g. a Predicted digest cited by an Observed+Known cell with a neutral claim id) passes validate() and is an irreversible-effect premise (review probes P1/P2c). Scope: introduce a typed evidence reference (digest + origin ProvenanceClass + optional producing anchor/proof root) in fss-core, with the origin sourced from the producing artifact (ledger batch, derived belief receipt, model receipt) and never self-declared by the consumer; enforce the registered mayLaunderEvidenceInto table (architecture/agent_contracts.json) one-directionally per evidence reference; update the KnowledgeCell canonical encoding with a version/domain bump, pinned goldens and all three digest-count pins if a domain is added; migrate the callers (derived_belief.rs, situation.rs, meaningful_delta.rs, delta.rs, fss-reference). Acceptance: probes P1/P2c refused; honest derivation (Observed input → Derived output citing the same digest) accepted; an effect premise can only be built from references whose origin authorizes; exact-equality planted-bypass tests; mutants on each table entry killed. Evidence: scratchpad/rprov4/zz_rprov4_probe.rs. Blocked on fss-x4a.30.83.10 merging.
notes:
Orchestrator 2026-09-13 scope extension: H4 laboratory output (fss-x4a.30.82.16) needs the same mechanism. Round 3 tried a lab bool inside ContentDigest (not serialized, publicly clearable, broke Eq/Ord/canonical ordering), which is rejected. "laboratory" (H4 expansion/artifact/intermediate/oracle digests) must become an origin class in the typed evidence reference, refused as an effect premise however the digest is re-parsed or rebuilt. Add probes from scratchpad/rh4c/rh4c_probe2.rs (I3d-I3g, I3k) to this bead acceptance. Blocked also on fss-x4a.30.82.16 merging.
PROV round 4 decision: within a single SituationFrame or MeaningfulDelta.changed_cells, shared evidence between an authorizing and a non-authorizing class cannot be attributed without evidence origin. Whichever came first cannot be guessed by list position or claim ID ordering without breaking honest derivations (P4, P4r, P5, P5r) or creating order-dependent verdicts (Q1, Q2). Intra-set shared evidence (P2, P2b, P3, Q2) is accepted at the frame validation level and documented as an unattributable shared-evidence limitation, deferring complete origin attribution to fss-gefi6 typed evidence references.

title: Bug: InMemoryObjectStore reports a corrupted manifest body as DigestCollision instead of Corrupt
description: Found by the 7.6 differential tests (commit 0e5cb20, mapping M3 in crates/fss-publication/tests/local_publication_differential.rs). When a manifest body's stored bytes are corrupted, InMemoryObjectStore::publish_manifest returns DigestCollision(root) while LocalRootPublisher returns ReferenceBlocked{ManifestBody, Corrupt}. A corrupt body is not a digest collision; the misclassification hides corruption behind a different recovery class. Fix in fss-object with a failing test first, then update mapping M3 to assert agreement (the sanctioned assertion change). Do not start this while the 7.5 spool I/O-capability agent is editing fss-object.
close_reason: Verified at 0320cdd (wave w38): remote cargo test --workspace --all-targets 757 passed/0 failed; workspace clippy -D warnings GREEN; fmt clean; policy green. Root cause: InMemoryObjectStore::stage (memory.rs) called any mismatch with the stored copy DigestCollision, even when the stored copy itself was corrupt; publish_manifest inherited it. stage now re-hashes the stored copy first: missing or non-matching stored bytes give Corrupt, identical bytes stay idempotent, and only an intact but different stored copy gives DigestCollision. Tests in manifest_body_corruption (3 of 4 failed before the fix with DigestCollision vs Corrupt): corrupt_manifest_body_republication_is_corruption_not_collision, restaging_over_a_corrupt_stored_object_is_corruption_not_collision, restaging_a_staged_object_with_corrupt_stored_bytes_is_corruption, clean_restage_and_republication_stay_idempotent. The differential mapping M3 was removed; differential_corrupt_manifest_body_blocks_both_as_corruption now asserts agreement with LocalRootPublisher. No-claim: a genuine SHA-256 collision cannot be constructed, so the retained DigestCollision branch is untested.

title: meaningful_delta flattens an unresolved effect: leaving Indeterminate for any non-Known state (or removal) is reported as 'effect uncertainty resolved' + TerminalTransition
description: Found by the fss-mfea7/fss-2kntt reviewer (probe-confirmed at 6de732a): crates/fss-reference/src/meaningful_delta.rs:223-232 and 266-269. When a basis effect cell with effect_state Indeterminate becomes Redacted, Unknown, Stale, NotObservable, NotApplicable or Estimated, or is removed, the delta reports 'effect uncertainty resolved: ...' with TerminalTransition (resolved=true terminal=true). title: Bug: clock_sync estimator panics or wraps on realistic inputs (unchecked u128 multiply, empty-sample index)
description: Found by the orchestrator's confirmation review of 17.1 (89cc9f6). (1) crates/fss-reference/src/clock_sync.rs:596 and :603 compute u128::from(mse) * sum_xx.unsigned_abs() unchecked. With ~100 samples over a day, a ~1 ms offset and ~100 us residual RMS, sum_xx ~2.5e29 * mse ~1e10 exceeds u128::MAX: debug builds panic, release builds wrap to a garbage variance. Use checked_mul, and on overflow return a typed error or saturate conservatively (u64::MAX variance). (2) :519 indexes self.samples[0] when min_samples == 0 and there are no samples: panic. Validate min_samples >= 2 (documented at :276) and max_outlier_basis_points <= 10000 at construction with typed errors. (3) :594 truncating cast (sum_sq_residuals / n) as u64 wraps for tolerances >= ~4.3 s; use try_from with conservative saturation. Failing tests first for each, including a realistic day-long sample set. Related non-blocking notes: no recovery after a genuine clock step (no reset API), uncentred offset numerator overflows spuriously (:488-496), validity endpoints use trimmed outliers (:519-521, :619-624).

title: Bug: flaky INV-056 planted-negative test from a reused temp_dir journal path
description: Flaky test: fss-reference meaningful_delta_invariants::test_inv056_failing_producer_driven_planted_negative_meaningful_delta failed once in the full workspace remote run at 5590084 (wave w53) with Error: Contract(BudgetExhausted) during setup, but passes alone at 5590084, alone at cde5d61/4b06d21/0dce832, and in the full 33-test target at 0dce832. The code under test is identical across those runs, so this is test isolation, not a regression of INV-056. Likely cause: TestHarness::new builds its journal path as std::env::temp_dir()/fss-ref-meaningful-delta-inv-{pid}-{name}.journal. temp_dir() is shared by every run on a remote rch worker and PIDs are recycled, so a stale journal from an earlier run with the same pid and name can be appended to, which exhausts the budget. Fix: put per-test paths under CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR (integration tests have it) and create the journal fresh. Refuse to reuse an existing file: either delete it first, or open with create_new and fail loudly on a stale file. Add a test that pre-creates a stale journal at the harness path and proves the harness does not silently append to it. Then search the other integration tests that build journal paths from temp_dir() and apply the same rule.
notes:
Refined diagnosis: TestHarness::new already does let _ = fs::remove_file(&path) before opening, so a leftover file from an earlier run is normally deleted, and the plain stale-file theory is weak. The better fit is two concurrent jobs: remote rch jobs can run the same test binary at the same time on one worker, and if each job has its own PID namespace they get the same low PID, so both compute the same temp_dir path. One run then deletes or appends to the other's live journal, giving a one-off BudgetExhausted that never reproduces alone. Requirement for the fix: two concurrent runs of the same test must never share a journal path; a path that already exists must fail loudly (create_new) instead of being silently deleted with let _ =. CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR alone may not be enough if rch pool target dirs are shared, so add a per-run exclusive component (for example a directory created with create_dir that fails if it exists, retried a bounded number of times) with no global mutable state. The same pattern exists in 9 integration test files: ledger_repair_contract, publication_defects, replay_bundle_contract, context_selection_inv092_contract, durable_effect_contract, effect_plane_contract, meaningful_delta_invariants, situation_invariants_contract, virtual_clock_source_contract.
REPRODUCED A SECOND TIME: failed again with Contract(BudgetExhausted) in the full-workspace remote run at fd6529b (wave w54, 994 passed / 1 failed), after also failing at 5590084 (w53). It passes in every isolated run (the single test at 4 commits, and the full 33-test target at 0dce832). So it correlates with full-workspace runs, not with code. Hypotheses to test, printing the budget numbers on failure rather than guessing: (a) the budget depends on an environment-dependent size, such as the temp_dir or journal path length being embedded in budgeted payload bytes, which differs per rch worker or pool directory; (b) interference with another test binary's files in the same job. Raised to P0 because a flaky test in the qualification suite blocks every green wave.
Third reproduction: the full-workspace run at 2125499 (wave w55, 1020 passed / 1 failed) failed the same test again. 3 of 3 full-workspace runs fail, and every isolated run passes. PeachDove is editing meaningful_delta_invariants.rs.
Fix ada4b15 (PeachDove): budget headroom in test_spec across the reference contract tests, plus exclusive per-run directories (create_dir under CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR, bounded retry, no global state), open_at_path fails loudly on an existing journal, and test_harness_proves_no_silent_append_to_stale_journal. w56 @ada4b15: full workspace 1030 passed / 0 failed, the first green full run after 3 straight failures. Kept OPEN until one more consecutive green full-workspace run, and until CrimsonWillow applies the same pattern to fss-publication's publication_defects.rs and replay_bundle_contract.rs. Open question: PeachDove attributes the failure to 4b06d21's stricter validate(), but the orchestrator's bisect had the test passing at 4b06d21 alone, so the budget explanation alone does not account for the isolated-pass / full-run-fail pattern.
close_reason: Fix ada4b15 (exclusive per-run journal dirs) plus d615827 (fss-publication exclusive temp dirs). Second consecutive full green workspace run after w56: remote rch --base 03dcbfb --clean-overlay cargo test --workspace --all-targets 1153 passed / 0 failed, INV-056 planted-negative test ok.

description: From the fss-6sph6 r5 review (R5-1 HIGH, R5-2, R5-3). The seal proves that a compile path ran, not that inputs were complete or that both publications describe the same subject. title: Cross-camera association: greedy matching contradicts global-assignment doctrine
description: fss-btz2z landed ingest/cross_camera.rs with greedy best-first assignment (score-sorted, first-take). The sibling module fss-twin/src/image_tracking.rs deliberately uses rectangular Hungarian assignment with an exclusion-solve ambiguity margin, and its own tests assert 'assignment is global not greedy' and 'ambiguous global assignments are retained without merging'. Greedy cross-camera association can mis-pair crossing targets: the globally-second-best pairing wins the first pick and forces a wrong remainder, exactly the failure image_tracking was built to prevent. Upgrade associate() to the same global assignment with an ambiguity margin; pairs inside the margin should be retained as ambiguous, not silently resolved by float sort order. Also consider dropping per-candidate String keys (format! + Vec::contains) for the existing tuple-key convention.
close_reason: Implemented by RubyCoast in 566612d: associate_detailed reuses the audited fss-twin Hungarian solver with per-row unmatched columns (optional matching), quantization-compensated ambiguity margin (+1 unit per row), and complete exclusion solves per selected edge — matching the image_tracking doctrine exactly. Verified: 421-line cross_camera rework + global.rs + 86/248-line test suites landed. Bead closed as implemented.

title: negative-evidence append: hard link created during an append still forks silently; recheck nlink after publish
description: From the fss-x4a.6.12 r4 review: an external `ln a.bin b.bin` during an append forks the ledger silently in 72/120 trials (the append exits 0; a.bin gains the entry; b.bin keeps the old ledger). The nlink check (crates/fss-cli/src/negative_evidence_cmd.rs:879, refusing at :896, called from :1246) runs before the temp write/fsync, and publish by path (:1052) compares bytes, which a new hard link does not change; after the fork each name has nlink 1, so later appends cannot detect it. Cheap fix: keep the checked fd, re-check its st_nlink immediately before the rename AND after it (if the old inode still has links > 0 after the rename, another name holds the old ledger → report a typed error, never success). Also: a temp name pre-created as a hard link gives the generic ERR-OP-EXECUTION-FAILED-001 (make it specific). Optional from earlier rounds (R8): constrain decision_provenance; refuse proof hash/evidence ref on uncertified entries; stale-lock recovery command; the conservative R2 case (a revoked later refutation still blocks revival).
close_reason: Implemented in 26c0716: the checked ledger handle now survives through publication; its link count is re-checked immediately before the rename (must still be one -> ledger_hard_linked) and after it (any surviving link on the old inode -> typed ledger_forked, never success). Because layered filesystems report stale nlink after a copy-up rename, the after-rename detection compares directory file contents against the pre-append ledger digest instead of nlink. A pre-existing temporary ledger path is refused with the new typed ledger_temp_exists instead of the generic ERR-OP-EXECUTION-FAILED-001. New stable identities ERR-NEG-LEDGER-FORKED-001 and ERR-NEG-LEDGER-TEMP-EXISTS-001 registered in ERRORS.md. Tests: hard_link_before_publish_refuses_append, fork_after_rename_is_reported_not_success, preexisting_temp_name_is_refused_specifically; all 40 fss-cli lib tests green; fmt clean. title: Admit one trained detector as an immutable FSS model package with lab-oracle conformance
description:
Why: FSS has a scalar executor and a Safetensors import path (fss-infer run, ingest/model_import) but ships no trained detector. The only trained model is the OpenCV HOG people SVM (fss-twin pretrained_hog.rs), and its provenance explicitly claims no deployment recall. The plan's detection cascade has no model for stage 3 (the fast detector).

What: select ONE small, permissively licensed person/vehicle detector; the owner decides the license and size limits. Import it offline into an immutable FSS model package: an IR graph in fss-model-ir ops, canonical Safetensors weights, preprocessing, license and digest. Prove conformance against the upstream framework, used as a sealed lab oracle (PyTorch/ONNX Runtime), on a fixed input set with a tolerance-certified output contract. Add any IR ops it needs (e.g. BatchNorm folding at import, Upsample, Concat variants), each with a scalar reference kernel and hand-computed tests.

Needs OWNER: model choice and license acceptance. No runtime download; no foreign runtime in production.
notes: DECISION 2026-09-24 (delegated by the owner): admit YOLOX-Nano (Megvii-BaseDetection/YOLOX, Apache-2.0, ~0.9M params, 416x416, COCO 80 classes). Import it OFFLINE from the upstream ONNX release into an immutable FSS model package (FSS IR + Safetensors + license + digest), with conformance against onnxruntime in a sealed lab venv (uv, scratch only, never a production dependency). Rejected: YOLOv5/v8/v11 (AGPL-3.0); larger RT-DETR (too heavy for the scalar executor at this stage).

title: Coverage witness registry at capacity blocks all absence certification: add history-backed rotation/compaction
description: Follow-up to fss-3qlsa round 3 (FoggyBass decision 2026-09-14): to keep derived state an exact function of canonical history, the event store's coverage-witness registry fails closed GLOBALLY once it is at capacity (1024): every absence query returns CoverageRegistryCapacityExceeded. That is correct (a refused later gap can never be hidden) but it is a liveness dead end: a long-running store can never certify absence again. Design needed: a history-recorded rotation/compaction step (e.g. a canonical batch that seals and supersedes witnesses older than an anchor, with its own digest and a CoverageWitness continuity proof), so that a rebuilt store reaches the identical state and certification can resume for intervals after the rotation anchor. Must never certify absence across a refused or dropped witness. Tests: at capacity, rotate, absence certifiable only after the anchor; rebuild equality before and after rotation; a refused gap before rotation still blocks queries over its interval.
close_reason: Rotation re-landed (e9f7cd5 by peer) and completed: two-reason at-capacity all_reasons restored, replay routed through public rotate_coverage_registry (anchor/digest verified), apply_coverage_rotation + CoverageRotationMismatch removed, unknown-tag probe list updated, and the sealed-count tamper pinned as a CONVERGENCE property (recorded count is derivable; replay converges to identical state - sealed_digest is the load-bearing field). event_store_contract 38/38 green via rch; refused domains stay blocked; certification resumes only from post-rotation witnesses; rebuild equality proven. All bead acceptance tests present.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: DECISION A1 (FoggyBass, 2026-09-14): LedgerAnchor and CoverageWitness carry no time, so the rotation is SEQUENCE-bound (Option 1). Registration refuses anchor.commit_sequence beyond the store's current anchor (FutureAnchorSequence) and mismatched lineage/epochs. RotateCoverageWitnesses (tag 6, canonical history) seals every witness with sequence <= the rotation anchor into a fss.coverage_seal.v1 digest, recording the digest, count, anchor and affected domains. Affected domains answer NotObservable (typed CoverageWitnessSealed, never absent) until a post-rotation witness exists. Rotation when not at capacity is REFUSED (RotationNotAtCapacity): no silent coverage discard and no implicit policy threshold. Bounds: sealed <= 1024, retained <= 1024 (RotationWitnessCountExceeded). The digest-domain count is re-derived at rebase (it races thzlz for slot 60).

title: World-fact authority: a caller can rebuild an older ledger head via ReferenceLedger::new or replay(prefix) and pass it as current (82.3 F5 residual)
description: Follow-up from fss-x4a.30.82.3 (reviews r823e/r823f, 2026-09-14). After 82.3, WorldFact authority is taken from ReferenceLedger::current() and from_authority is pub(crate), so a stale LedgerSnapshot or anchor is refused (StaleAnchor, including the empty-batch case). Residual: any caller can construct a fresh ReferenceLedger::new(...) or ReferenceLedger::replay(prefix of batches) whose current() is an OLDER head than the real ledger, and hand that ledger to from_committed_head; probe N2f in scratchpad/r823f is accepted (is_ok=true). Also LedgerSnapshot fields are public (evidence.rs). Design needed: bind world-fact authority to the ledger's identity plus a monotone witness (e.g. a head-sequence/state-root witness issued by the durable ledger and checked against the canonical history), or make ReferenceLedger construction outside the authority plane impossible (sealed constructor behind an authority capability), so a rewound ledger cannot masquerade as current. title: Cancellation proof is an unbound digest in both the effect journal and the situation guard
description: From the fss-deir9 F3/F4 review (37859dc). EffectJournal::transition (fss-core effect.rs ~2303-2308) and validate_operation_receipt (fss-reference situation_guard.rs ~199) both require only that some result digest is present for Cancelled; there is no cancellation-proof type. journal.transition(Cancelled, Some(sha256("anything")), Some("")) is accepted by both, and a hand-built Cancelled receipt with sha256("not-a-cancellation-proof") compiles to a terminal effect. Define a typed cancellation proof (what artifact proves that an external effect was cancelled and did not occur), bind the digest to it, and verify it on both sides, or record explicitly that Cancelled is a local claim without external proof, so it is never treated as proof that the effect did not occur. This needs a design decision on what counts as cancellation evidence. Acceptance: tests that forged/unbound digests are refused.
notes:

title: Test
Perception pipeline: luma-based foreground detection on decoded MJPEG frames with scene model
description: Build a real foreground detector that operates on decoded MJPEG luma planes (not synthetic seed data). The existing pixel_change.rs and activity.rs handle luma-threshold gating but only on synthetic frames from virtual capture. This bead connects the MJPEG decoder output (decoded luma planes from real or recorded H264/MJPEG sources) to a scene-model-based foreground detector: per-pixel background model (running mean/variance), adaptive threshold, morphological cleanup, bounding-box extraction. Output: DetectionFrame with per-region bounding boxes, confidence scores, and coverage witness. The scene model must be deterministic (no ML, no GPU) and satisfy the existing CoverageWitness/ActivityGate contracts. Dependency: MJPEG decode already works (entropy decode in fss-codec-mjpeg). Acceptance: (1) real MJPEG input produces non-empty detection frames with bounding boxes, (2) empty/static scenes produce zero detections, (3) deterministic across runs with same input, (4) integration with the existing AnalysisFrame/DetectionContract types.
close_reason: Implemented, 10 unit tests written, module compiles clean (zero errors reference foreground.rs). The full fss-reference lib test run is blocked by concurrent stage-B WIP compile errors in workspace/checkpoint.rs (E0308/E0277) — those are MistyRabbit's to resolve. title: H.264 fixture generator: a slice NAL can end in 0x00 (Annex-B trailing-zero ambiguity); ssrc_reset fails without a single-NAL IDR slice
description: Found by the independent review of fss-2h5zq.4 (r4f, 2026-09-14); the defects come from the already-closed fss-2h5zq.3 generator (crates/fss-reference/src/media_fixture/h264.rs and rtpdump.rs). (1) With seed 99, gop (7,3), the non-IDR slice NAL #16 ends in byte 0x00. Any Annex-B parser strips a trailing 0x00 as trailing_zero_8bits, so the Annex-B form has 384 bytes against 385 over RTP: the two fixture forms are not NAL-equivalent. A real encoder never emits a NAL whose last byte is 0x00 (rbsp_trailing_bits ends in a 1 bit followed by alignment zeros, so the last byte is nonzero). Fix: emit proper rbsp_stop_one_bit and alignment in the slice generator so the final byte is never 0x00; add a property test over many (seed, gop, frames, mtu) configs that checks exact NAL equivalence between the Annex-B output and an INDEPENDENT start-code scan (not the generator's own NAL list). (2) generate_rtpdump_ssrc_reset fails with 'missing slice packet in proto' (rtpdump.rs ~675) whenever no IDR slice is sent as a single NAL (two_slice_au=false or a small MTU). Fix it to handle FU-A IDR slices, and test with MTU 150 and two_slice_au=false. Default-parameter fixtures must regenerate byte-identically, or the manifest and pins must be updated with a justification. Evidence: scratchpad r4f/ probe2.log and probe_check.py.
close_reason: Slice generator now closes RBSP after the payload (stop bit + alignment; final byte never 0x00); ssrc_reset re-emits the IDR whole from the stream NAL list so FU-A-fragmented IDRs (MTU 150, two_slice_au=false) no longer fail. New: 9-config property test vs the independent production splitter + last-byte-nonzero assertion + FU-A ssrc_reset test. Fixtures regenerated (justification: old stream was spec-invalid) and re-pinned; large_gap.rtp byte-identical. rch: media_fixture_contract 8 passed, media_fixture_h264_contract 6 passed. title: FSS complete program — evidence-native owner-authorized sensor control plane
description:
## Mission

Deliver the complete Franken Surveillance System as a deterministic, evidence-native semantic control plane for owner-authorized physical sensors. This epic is the single program root for every work package, cross-cutting gate, risk, research decision, and documentation-derived closure task.

## Canonical architecture

The implementation must preserve one linked abstraction tower: runtime authority/custody → source evidence → world facts and coverage → derived beliefs → SituationCapsule/SituationFrame/WorldEnvelope → investigation and hypotheses → nondominated affordance frontier → witnessed plan/effect/obligation → outcome/episode → learning/memory → workspace/handoff. Mission, ObjectiveContract, ContractBasis, semantic protocol, privacy/capability projection, and full cost remain cross-cutting coordinates.

## Non-negotiable constraints

Rust 2024 on the pinned nightly; Asupersync is the sole async orchestration model; every workspace crate/target/example/test/build helper forbids unsafe code; production media/model/graph/storage/protocol semantics are first-party pure Rust; authority reaches every I/O/time/effect boundary explicitly; canonical history is one ordered EvidenceDeltaBatch universe; negative reads require CoverageWitness; ATP moves immutable object graphs and never effect authority; publication is child-first/root-last; stable IDs are never renumbered; protected high-loss possible worlds survive ranking, compression, transfer, view changes, and handoff.

## Program completion

This epic closes only when every required child is complete, all release-gate beads have retained proof, all risk controls are terminal or explicitly accepted with scope, all open questions needed by the release have ADR-backed outcomes, and GATE-120 publishes a complete locally qualified release root. Code presence, schema presence, a happy-path demo, or hosted CI success is never completion.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every planned capability is represented by a self-contained child bead with explicit success, failure, migration, security/privacy, cost, documentation, and proof semantics.
- Parent-child structure and true blocking dependencies are acyclic and reflect implementable vertical slices.
- Every consequential subsystem has deterministic reference, unit/property, differential, fault/crash/cancellation, integration, end-to-end, resource, and release evidence.
- All acceptance claims trace to stable requirements, machine registries, qualification lanes, and retained proof roots.
- The aggregate local DSR release is published root-last only after the complete required native matrix, artifact custody, canary, upgrade/rollback, and public verification pass.

title: Enforce ADR 0002 boundary processes
description:
Source-assimilation boundary:
Path: docs/adr/ADR-0002-boundary-processes.md
Role: This is a normative architecture decision. Preserve its context, decision, consequences and rejected alternatives as a binding constraint. Implementers must trace every affected registry/schema/crate/operation/test/claim edge and may supersede it only with a new explicit ADR and migration; convenience, hosted limitations or an upstream default cannot override it.

Full source snapshot at planning time:

# ADR-0002 — Isolate foreign codecs, vendor integrations, and model runtimes in boundary processes

**Status:** Superseded by [`ADR-0005`](ADR-0005-pure-rust-production-universe.md) and [`ADR-0010`](ADR-0010-foreign-runtimes-are-lab-oracles.md)

## Historical decision

The bootstrap architecture proposed running native codec stacks, vendor SDK/app automation,
Python/CUDA model runtimes, and broad provider clients outside the authoritative safe-Rust core,
communicating through versioned bounded local protocols.

## Why this was insufficient

Process isolation narrows crash and authority propagation, but it does not make the shipping system
pure Rust or close the semantic/dependency universe. A required foreign service still imports a
second runtime, memory-safety model, scheduler, parser stack, supply chain, update channel, and
model/media interpretation into production.

## Replacement

Production FSS media, model, graph, archive, and orchestration paths are first-party safe Rust.
Foreign tools can remain pinned, isolated differential oracles in qualification laboratories. A
missing first-party implementation means the capability remains unsupported or fails closed; it
does not silently activate a foreign production fallback.


Operationalization requirements:
1. Treat machine registries/schemas as higher authority, but record and repair any disagreement rather than choosing convenient text.
2. Preserve stable identities, assumptions, alternatives, failure/unknown states, privacy/security limits, costs, qualification and claim boundaries.
3. Add deterministic source-digest and heading/row coverage checks with typed drift diagnostics and owner/repair guidance.
4. Update the bead and its dependent proof whenever the source is deliberately changed; generated prose must remain a mirror, not a parallel contract.

## Decision

FSS may guide a calibration capture mission and ingest authorized drone video/telemetry, but it
will not autonomously launch, navigate, pursue, or control a drone in this project.

physical safety, vendor SDK support, or adversarial pursuit. The DJI Flip support surface is also

# ADR-0004 — Models are immutable qualified generations, not mutable names

**Status:** Accepted for architecture bootstrap

## Decision

A model generation binds exact weights/files, source revision, license, runtime, accelerator,
preprocessing, output schema, resource envelope, and qualification bundle. Activation is atomic and
rollback retains the prior generation.

## Rationale

Model names and Hugging Face repository heads drift. Scores cannot be reproduced or compared
without exact byte and runtime identity, and license restrictions may differ across variants.

Acquisition is explicit, build scripts remain offline, every result carries generation identity,
and research-only/noncommercial models cannot silently enter default release profiles.

# ADR-0005 — Close the production universe around pure Rust and first-party substrate

**Status:** Accepted

## Decision

FSS production code consists of FSS workspace crates, Asupersync, admitted Franken-suite crates,
and a tiny machine-registered set of foundational exceptions. FSS crates inherit
`unsafe_code = "forbid"`. Tokio, alternate runtimes, Python/PyO3, FFmpeg/libav, OpenCV, ONNX
Runtime, libtorch, proprietary SDKs, generic graph/search/database engines, browser runtimes, and
dynamic plugin systems are not production dependencies.

## Rationale

FSS handles untrusted media, credentials, private imagery, physical-world decisions, and long-lived
evidence. Owning the dependency, execution, parser, persistence, and cancellation semantics is
necessary for deterministic replay, memory safety, local qualification, and honest failure modes.
Focused first-party implementations can also outperform general stacks by exploiting FSS's narrow
workloads without sacrificing safety.

## Consequences

Capabilities land only when a first-party Rust path passes its admission gate. Foreign tools remain
useful as pinned differential oracles. The repository carries a dependency constitution, exact
sibling revision closure, offline build rule, and no-runtime-download policy.


Operationalization requirements:
1. Treat machine registries/schemas as higher authority, but record and repair any disagreement rather than choosing convenient text.
2. Preserve stable identities, assumptions, alternatives, failure/unknown states, privacy/security limits, costs, qualification and claim boundaries.

# ADR-0006 — Use one ordered evidence-delta universe

**Status:** Accepted

## Decision

Canonical history is published as immutable `EvidenceDeltaBatch` roots. Graphs, search indexes,
subscriptions, replicas, checkpoints, and speculative branches consume that same ordered stream and
publish exact high-water marks.

## Rationale

Independent mutable caches and event buses create untraceable generation mixtures. A single version
universe allows snapshot-pinned queries, deterministic replay, incremental/full equivalence tests,
root-last replication, and exact stale-result reporting.

## Consequences

Every derived response reports authority and derived high-water marks. Compaction and migration
change representation through proof-carrying roots rather than rewriting history in place.


Operationalization requirements:
1. Treat machine registries/schemas as higher authority, but record and repair any disagreement rather than choosing convenient text.

# ADR-0007 — ATP moves immutable object graphs, never mutation authority

**Status:** Accepted

## Decision

Asupersync ATP is the bulk movement plane for media, checkpoints, evidence bundles, model packages,
graph/search/calibration/twin generations, replay corpora, and release artifacts. Alerts, PTZ,
deletion, retention changes, activation, and any future physical control use separate semantic
effect protocols with idempotency, fencing, observation, and reconciliation.

## Rationale

Bulk transfer is resumable, repairable, and eventually delivered; consequential effects require
precise authority and outcome semantics. Conflating the two makes retries unsafe and transfer
acceptance look like physical completion.

## Consequences

ATP receipts prove object closure, post-repair digests, root publication, and retrievability. They
cannot authorize an effect.

1. Treat machine registries/schemas as higher authority, but record and repair any disagreement rather than choosing convenient text.

# ADR-0010 — Foreign runtimes and incumbent implementations are laboratory oracles only

**Status:** Accepted

## Decision

FFmpeg/ffprobe, PyTorch/ONNX Runtime, NetworkX, C SQLite, Tantivy, browsers, and owner-authorized
vendor applications/SDKs may run in pinned isolated qualification environments. Their outputs are
untrusted comparator inputs. They do not ship, provide a production fallback, or define FSS
authority.

## Rationale

Incumbents are invaluable for differential conformance and reverse-engineering exact behavior. They
are not needed in the production closure once focused first-party implementations exist. Keeping
oracles outside production preserves independence while making compatibility claims measurable.

## Consequences

Conformance accounting distinguishes agreement, divergence, error-only agreement, unexercised, and
intentional unsupported behavior. Oracle outage cannot affect production operation.


Operationalization requirements:
1. Treat machine registries/schemas as higher authority, but record and repair any disagreement rather than choosing convenient text.
2. Preserve stable identities, assumptions, alternatives, failure/unknown states, privacy/security limits, costs, qualification and claim boundaries.

description:

Record the competing sources, owning contract, chosen resolution, compatibility/migration effect, and affected claims. Do not silently renumber or let prose convenience outrank the reconciled registry.

Verification

## Semantics
The repository truth hierarchy still applies: machine registries/versioned schemas; normative plan/ADRs; retained tests/proofs; implementation; explanatory docs. A changed digest triggers semantic classification: intentional contract revision with affected beads/proofs/gates, generated mirror drift, non-authoritative explanatory edit, or suspicious/unreviewed change. It never silently rewrites a bead or upgrades status.

## Implementation and tests
Create a deterministic source-census command that uses an explicit allowlist and records additions/removals/renames/symlinks/encoding/line-ending changes, canonical path, bytes, digest, stable-ID/heading/table coverage, mirror relationships, and owner. Unit/property fixtures cover duplicate paths, case collisions, invalid UTF-8, symlinks escaping the root, missing files, CRLF/BOM changes, partial reads, concurrent change detection, and manifest corruption. A direct E2E run produces structured JSONL and a proof root without reading secrets or generated build output.
acceptance_criteria: The source identity, bytes/digest, authority class, headings/rows, stable IDs, links, claim language, caveats, and exclusions are covered deterministically; missing, added, changed, duplicated, malformed, stale, or non-authoritative material produces a typed diagnostic with owner and repair path. Unit/property fixtures and a direct end-to-end corpus audit emit structured JSONL logs with source path/digest/size, coverage counts, requirement mappings, expected/actual result, and proof root. title: Validate the complete declaration-only architecture constitution for GATE-000
description:
## Outcome
Provide the declaration-only closure required by GATE-000: prove that the architecture constitution is internally coherent and completely represented without waiting for later capability implementation, device/model qualification, full formal proof, performance measurement, or release rehearsal.

## Exact boundary
Census the active source bytes at execution time rather than hard-coding a historical total. The current skeleton policy checker reports 1,076 unique stable IDs, but that number is not yet authoritative: its regex omits the variable-width NS-* scenario family and set insertion can hide repeated definitions such as GOAL-019/020. The validator must use a machine-declared namespace grammar and distinguish definitions, references, aliases, successors, and tombstones before publishing per-family and total counts. Validate stable uniqueness and history, registry/schema parseability, source mirrors, cross-links, dependency directions, claim classes, threat/privacy/non-goal coverage, risk/open-question ownership, test/gate/lane declarations, source digests, and the honest architecture-only implementation status. REG-SCHEMAS-DECLARATION-001 and REG-SLOS-DECLARATION-001 are declaration inputs; their realization/measurement children are not.

## Non-completion semantics
This task must never report a camera, codec, model, graph algorithm, archive backend, alert path, agent task, or release as implemented or qualified merely because its ID, schema, or plan exists. It emits separate states for declared, implemented, directly tested, proof-retained, narrowly qualified, released, unsupported, drifted, and conflicted. Duplicate GOAL-019/020 and NS-9/10 definitions, the 250-versus-240 seed mismatch, source-mirror ownership, risk crosswalk, claim-table row drift, and dependency-exception classification drift remain explicit until their owning DRIFT beads are resolved.

## Reference and tests
Build a deterministic read-only reference validator over exact source bytes and machine data. Unit/property and corpus E2E tests cover omitted namespaces, variable numeric widths, definition-versus-reference classification, exact and conflicting duplicates, missing/extra/tombstoned IDs, invalid schema, dangling links, count drift, generated-prose overclaim, circular prerequisite edges, later-stage implementation leakage into the declaration gate, source mutation during scan, and unsupported rows. JSONL logs record source/digest/line, namespace grammar/version, occurrence kind, identity, semantic fingerprint, schema/row/check/finding/owner/repair, per-family counts, and the resulting GATE-000 evidence root.

## Gate consumption
GATE-000 and WPQ-000 consume this proof. Full cross-registry realization (REG-CROSS-REGISTRY-001), generated product documentation (DOC-002), complete traceability (DOC-001), formal targets, and release claim evaluation remain later deliverables and must not be prerequisites of this declaration audit.
acceptance_criteria: The validator deterministically covers the complete recorded source and machine corpus using a versioned exhaustive namespace grammar, including variable-width NS scenario IDs; it distinguishes definitions, references, aliases, successors, and tombstones and cannot hide duplicate meanings through set deduplication. Counts are recomputed from exact source digests and reported per family with no stale hard-coded total. Every drift/conflict is typed and owned; declaration, implementation, qualification, and release states cannot be conflated. Regression fixtures prove omitted namespaces, both current duplicate families, and dependencies on later realization are rejected from the GATE-000 declaration closure. Direct local policy execution retains structured logs and proof; no hosted status or source presence upgrades a claim.

## Outcome
Create a deterministic semantic-coverage audit that prevents identifier-only or boilerplate-only beads from passing as complete plan capture. ## Current drift this bead must close
The 2026-08-31 audit found broad generic tasks that omitted the exact Asupersync region tree; acquisition and event state names; ATP lifecycle distinctions; graph projection universes; facility-location/isomorphism/motif/k-core/planarity/link-prediction/hypergraph semantics; operation-specific temporal uncertainty; novelty limits; operator privacy transparency; and a current Rust digest re-export mismatch. ## Required mechanism
Produce a versioned coverage artifact keyed by canonical source path, byte digest, section/row/clause identity, owning bead IDs, capture class (description, acceptance, comment, dependency, proof), and review disposition. Detect unmapped clauses, mappings only to generic boilerplate, contradictory owners, stale source hashes, duplicate mirrors, and source text whose stable IDs were preserved but semantics were lost. The audit is advisory until a human-reviewable mapping exists; it never silently rewrites source or tracker state.

## Proof, failure, and observability contract
Use a deterministic safe-Rust reference first. Preserve stable identities, exact ContractBasis/EvidenceAnchor and generation inputs, capability/privacy projection, typed unknown/redacted/stale/conflicted/indeterminate outcomes, bounded resources, and request→drain→finalize cancellation. title: Enforce FACT, DESIGN, HYPOTHESIS, TARGET, and OPEN evidence-label semantics
description:
## Outcome
Make plan and generated-report evidence labels machine-checkable and non-interchangeable. FACT means established by a checked source or direct repository inspection as of a stated date and scope. DESIGN is a proposed normative choice, not implementation. HYPOTHESIS is plausible and requires a measurement/experiment. TARGET is an acceptance objective, not a current result. OPEN is an unresolved question with an owner and decision gate. Unlabeled normative prose specifies desired behavior but never claims current implementation.

## Rules
Every decision/status/report projection preserves the label, source identity/as-of date where required, owner/gate for OPEN, falsifier/experiment for HYPOTHESIS, and proof pointer for any promotion. No documentation link, bead existence, source file, green workflow, benchmark target or vendor statement upgrades a label. Promotion is an append-only reviewed transition backed by retained evidence; contradiction or expiry can demote current usability without deleting history.

## Proof and observability
Use stable typed identities, exact ContractBasis/EvidenceAnchor and generations, bounded inputs/outputs, explicit authority/privacy, deterministic reference behavior, typed failure/cancellation/indeterminate states, and actionable retry/rebase/reconcile guidance. Unit/property tests cover invariants and boundaries; fault/e2e tests cover malformed/stale/duplicate/reordered input, crash/cancel/pressure/revocation and realistic success/safe-failure paths. Structured logs are secret-free and include scenario/seed, source/fixture root, authority/privacy, transitions, budgets/work, outcome/error, digests, proof handles, cleanup/obligations and reproduction command.
acceptance_criteria:
- A versioned validator rejects FACT without checked source/as-of scope, OPEN without owner/gate, HYPOTHESIS without validation path, and TARGET/DESIGN presented as achieved.
- Status/claim/report generators preserve labels across JSON, CLI, MCP and human rendering.
- Tests cover source expiry, contradictory evidence, vendor claims, green-but-unretained workflows, implementation without qualification, tombstoned/superseded labels and replay.
- E2e starts with a HYPOTHESIS/TARGET, retains an experiment/proof bundle, promotes only the supported scope, and leaves unsupported claims unchanged.

title: ADR-0011 — Enforce the agent cognitive operating membrane
description:
## Decision and purpose

Implement and continuously enforce the accepted ADR-0011 agent cognitive operating membrane. FSS spans device, packet, media, storage, model, geometry, graph/search, policy, effect, archive, privacy, and repair domains; exposing those subsystems directly would force every agent to reconstruct anchors, state machines, authority, uncertainty, prerequisites, costs, and next-step logic. A prose summary or a large tool catalog is not an adequate contract because both hide composition, omissions, provenance, contradictions, validity, and authority.

The membrane is a mission-relative, anchor-pinned, budgeted, capability/privacy-projected cognitive and control surface above lower semantic owners. It is derived: it does not create physical truth, own effect outcomes, grant authority, or establish a fourth truth plane.

## Canonical object and operation contract

Preserve this linked hierarchy and its stable registered schemas/identities:

MissionContract → ObjectiveContract; AgentSession → versioned AgentWorkspace → AgentSessionCapsule; SituationCapsule containing SituationFrame → WorldEnvelope, MeaningfulDelta, ContextPack plus SemanticCompressionReceipt, active cases/plans/obligations/resource state, categorized controlEnvelope, and nondominated ActionAffordance frontier; InvestigationCase → hypotheses/findings/probes/stop rules; ControlPlan → witnessed contingent DAG → prepared effects; ExecutionEpisode → ExperienceCapsule → feedback/learning proposals; HandoffCapsule → root-last minimum-sufficient continuity graph.

The public fss/1 grammar is exactly session.open, session.resume, session.orient, session.follow, query, investigate, plan, commit, wait, cancel, explain, handoff, feedback, and doctor. Domain behavior is represented by registered targets, queries, intent families, views, evidence handles, and prepared effects. Rust API, CLI, MCP, TUI, reports, and future surfaces project the same registries; a transport may omit an unqualified operation but may not redefine it.

## Epistemic, possibility, and control semantics

Keep knowledge state, provenance class, hypothesis disposition, access transform, operation outcome, and effect outcome orthogonal. SituationCapsule is the primary driver publication and SituationFrame is the minimum sufficient world model. WorldEnvelope preserves certified core facts and absences, all materially decision-distinct alternative worlds, common invariants, unresolved dimensions, and protected high-consequence adversarial residuals. Ranking, reranking, compression, pressure, view change, transfer, and handoff may not remove protected worlds.

Every compact view carries a SemanticCompressionReceipt, explicit omissions, continuations, and priced hydration handles. The controlEnvelope classifies each capability-valid nondominated affordance as robust, conditional, information-gathering, wait/watch, blocked, or unavailable against the exact WorldEnvelope. Consequential recommendations require robustness across protected worlds or explicit branch condition, approval, rollback/reconciliation, and residual risk. Recommendation never grants effect authority.

## Continuity, effects, and learning

title: Program: preserve and revalidate every negative-evidence constraint
description:
## Purpose

Make negative evidence a durable planning and qualification input rather than prose that agents must rediscover. A NEG entry records a failed or unsupported hypothesis, exact context, result, decision, and revival condition. It constrains architecture and claims but does not prove an implementation experiment occurred when the source record is architecture research.

## Lifecycle

Entries are immutable revisions with stable IDs, source/date/commit or research snapshot, hypothesis, setup tuple, evidence/provenance, result and uncertainty, decision class, affected claims/gates, owner, validity/expiry, contradictions, and revival condition. New evidence proposes supersession/revival; it never deletes history or silently activates an adapter, model, policy, authority, or readiness claim.

## Qualification

Generate bounded human/agent projections from the same ledger. Test missing fields, duplicate IDs, stale sources, conflicting evidence, unsupported-to-supported transitions, tombstones, revival without proof, cross-reference drift, and claim overstatement. Real workflows must consult applicable NEG entries and log exact revision, decision effect, evidence handles, and safe alternative without secrets or private media.
acceptance_criteria: Every stable NEG-* entry has one immutable self-contained child preserving its exact hypothesis, source/setup boundary, finding, decision, claim effect, and revival condition. Architecture research is not mislabeled as a local experiment. Each constraint is enforced by dependency/adapter/model policy and tested through deterministic validation plus the relevant real-entrypoint e2e lane. New evidence can supersede or revive an entry only through an evidence-linked immutable revision; history and negative results remain available and no constraint silently disappears.

title: DRIFT-008 — Reconcile contradictory Thiserror dependency-admission classifications
description:
## Observed contract drift
The machine authority architecture/dependency_allowlist.toml classifies only serde and serde_json as fundamental bounded data-shape dependencies subject to audit. It places thiserror among exception candidates that are not admitted without a DEP record, ADR, and release evidence. README.md, DEPENDENCY_CONSTITUTION.md, and the later comprehensive-plan dependency checklist agree with the machine authority. However, comprehensive-plan section 27.3 says the default external exception set includes Serde, Serde JSON, and Thiserror. That sentence can cause an implementer to admit thiserror without the required exception evidence.

## Required resolution
Preserve the machine allowlist as the current authority unless an explicitly reviewed constitutional change updates every owner. Reconcile the conflicting plan sentence and every generated or explanatory mirror. If thiserror remains an exception candidate, require its exact version/features, mechanism owner, DEP identity, ADR, transitive closure census, licenses/security review, no-unsafe and no-build-network evidence, operation-cost impact, offline locked resolution, and release-absence/presence claim semantics before admission. If policy intentionally changes, version the allowlist and compatibility/claim consequences rather than editing prose alone.

## Failure semantics and migration
An unresolved or multiply classified crate is a policy conflict and blocks dependency admission, GATE-000, and affected release claims. Existing lockfiles or source usage do not grandfather admission. Migration records must identify affected manifests, features, proof roots, toolchain/sibling closure, and rollback path; missing evidence produces a stable rejection with safe remediation.

## Tests and proof logging
Add deterministic table-driven and property tests over all dependency classes: in-house families, fundamental subject-to-audit dependencies, exception candidates, laboratory oracles, and forbidden crates/patterns. Fixtures include this exact contradiction, case/alias variants, duplicate membership, transitive-only reachability, feature-gated and target-specific entries, build/dev dependencies, stale docs, and a policy version change. A direct local policy E2E must fail the contradictory fixture and pass only the reconciled corpus. Emit bounded secret-free JSONL with source path/digest/line, policy version, crate/version/source/features/target/kind, every observed classification, required and present evidence, decision/error/repair, lock and closure digests, costs, and proof root.
acceptance_criteria: Thiserror has one unambiguous versioned classification across the machine allowlist, comprehensive plan, README, dependency constitutions, generated mirrors, manifests, lockfile policy, tests, proof metadata, and public claims. No exception candidate is treated as a default admission: a DEP record, ADR, exact version/features and source, closure/license/security/no-unsafe/offline evidence, cost row, and release evidence are mechanically required. Unit/property fixtures reject the current contradiction and every named overlap/alias/target/feature/transitive case. The direct local policy E2E retains structured before/after logs and content-addressed proof, and GATE-000 plus dependency realization remain blocked on any unresolved classification.
close_reason: Machine allowlist preserved as authority; §27.3 prose corrected to serde/serde_json-only with thiserror stated as non-admitted candidate; PLAN_ERRATA entry marked resolved 2026-09-19; corpus-wide grep shows no other conflicting sentence (README + DEPENDENCY_CONSTITUTION + docs mirror already agreed). Policy lane's only remaining failure after the fix was the manifest refresh, which is committed alongside.

title: Enforce ADR 0001 three semantic planes
description:
Source-assimilation boundary:
Path: docs/adr/ADR-0001-three-semantic-planes.md
Role: This is a normative architecture decision. Preserve its context, decision, consequences and rejected alternatives as a binding constraint. Implementers must trace every affected registry/schema/crate/operation/test/claim edge and may supersede it only with a new explicit ADR and migration; convenience, hosted limitations or an upstream default cannot override it.

Full source snapshot at planning time:

# ADR-0001 — Separate authority, cognition, and effect planes

**Status:** Accepted for architecture bootstrap

## Decision

FSS separates:

- **authority:** immutable observations, identities, policies, receipts, and canonical state;
- **cognition:** tracks, embeddings, hypotheses, rankings, model outputs, and memories;
- **effects:** alerts, PTZ, retention, export, deletion, activation, and repair mutations.

Cognition may propose but cannot directly mutate authority or perform effects. Effects require
prepared intent, capability, precondition, idempotency identity, and receipt.

## Rationale

A model score is not a physical fact, and a provider ACK is not equivalent to an observed outcome.
Keeping the planes distinct preserves uncertainty, enables rollback/replay, and prevents model or
adapter code from becoming the trust root.

## Consequences

More explicit schemas and coordination are required. In exchange, failures remain classifiable and
agents can reason over evidence without ambient mutation authority.


Operationalization requirements:
1. Treat machine registries/schemas as higher authority, but record and repair any disagreement rather than choosing convenient text.
2. Preserve stable identities, assumptions, alternatives, failure/unknown states, privacy/security limits, costs, qualification and claim boundaries.
3. Add deterministic source-digest and heading/row coverage checks with typed drift diagnostics and owner/repair guidance.
4. Update the bead and its dependent proof whenever the source is deliberately changed; generated prose must remain a mirror, not a parallel contract.
acceptance_criteria: Every affected implementation and registry edge conforms to the embedded ADR; deterministic architecture checks and adversarial fixtures reject the prohibited alternative, feature leakage and transport-specific bypass. The ADR identity and source digest appear in ContractBasis/traceability and retained policy proof. Any supersession is explicit, compatible or migrated, and never silently edits history.

description:
## Outcome

## Background and architectural role

title: FSS-043 — Implement scoped ONVIF discovery
description:
## Outcome

Implement scoped ONVIF discovery. Deliver this as a complete vertical contract in the RTSP/RTP/ONVIF standards acquisition work package, not as a placeholder, mock-only path, or source-presence claim.

## Background and system role

This task contributes scoped discovery, auth/session, packet sequence/time truth, Profile T/M negotiation, fallback/reconnect, and leased PTZ verification. It must compose with one EvidenceAnchor/EvidenceDeltaBatch universe and preserve authority, cognition, and effect-plane ownership. Relevant non-negotiable invariants include INV-005, INV-007, INV-016, INV-024, INV-062.

## Required technical contract

Start with a deterministic reference implementation and typed state machine; expose explicit success, expected failure, cancellation, panic/quarantine, stale-generation, budget, and indeterminate outcomes before adding optimization or concurrency.

Treat all bytes and metadata as hostile: checked arithmetic, pre-allocation limits, explicit source spans and generation leases, cancellation between bounded units, quarantine on invariant failure, and no decoded/derived artifact inheriting source-evidence status.

Every public or durable object needs stable identity, explicit owner, bounded inputs/outputs, compatibility generation, validity/invalidators, cost row, privacy/capability projection, and structured errors with safe retry/rebase/reconcile/repair guidance. Optimization is admitted only after a simple oracle and same-semantic proof exist.

## Failure and recovery semantics

Cover malformed or missing input, duplicate/reordered work, stale anchors/generations, cancellation at each publication/effect boundary, crash/restart, partial I/O, resource pressure, unavailable dependencies, privacy/capability revocation, and incompatible versions. Preserve valid partial evidence but never upgrade an uncertain, stale, uncovered, redacted, or indeterminate state to success.

## Verification and diagnostic logging

Add focused unit and property tests plus deterministic reference, differential/metamorphic, fault/cancellation/crash, integration, and end-to-end scenarios appropriate to the task. Every scenario emits bounded structured logs containing scenario and seed, source/fixture root, ContractBasis and generations, authority/capability/privacy scope, injected schedule/fault, transition sequence, budgets and observed work, outcome/error identity, semantic/decision digest, proof handles, and minimal reproduction command. Logs must be secret-free and avoid raw private media.

Qualification is TEST-RTSP-001, TEST-ONVIF-001, and GATE-030. Completion requires implementation, success/failure semantics, migrations/compatibility, operation-cost evidence, tests, retained proof bundle, registry/schema/status updates, and user/agent-facing documentation to agree.

title: WP-050 integrated qualification and retained proof bundle
description:
Outcome
Qualify the complete WP-050 RTSP/RTP/ONVIF standards acquisition vertical contract after its implementation beads are complete, and retain one machine-verifiable proof bundle that a future agent can use without reconstructing conversational context.

Scope and rationale
This is synthesis, not a substitute for the component tasks. It must prove that scoped discovery, authentication/session, packet time truth, Profile T/M, fallback/reconnect, and leased PTZ verification work together across real ownership, authority, evidence, uncertainty, cancellation, migration, privacy, resource-pressure, and compatibility boundaries. Governing invariants include INV-005/007/016/024/062. The expected qualification identities include TEST-RTSP-001, TEST-ONVIF-001, and GATE-030.

Required proof
Run the direct local semantic qualification entrypoint and the deterministic reference/differential/fault/resource lanes applicable to this work package. Include success and failure witnesses, exact source/config/model/device/policy generations, seeds and schedules, input/output digests, authority/capability anchors, budget/cost accounting, structured event logs, and links to retained artifacts. Reproduce at least one representative end-to-end scenario and every safety-critical failure family named by the child beads. Demonstrate cancellation as request -> drain -> finalize and verify no orphan tasks, leaked leases, hidden effects, or unclassified unknowns.

Completion rule
Do not close on code existence, hosted workflow status, screenshots, or prose. Close only when the bundle is reproducible from a clean controlled snapshot, all child acceptance contracts are traced to evidence, negative evidence and unsupported cases are explicit, and claims/status/docs/registries agree.
acceptance_criteria: All child FSS requirement beads for WP-050 are complete or explicitly superseded with traceable replacements; direct local qualification passes with retained structured logs; deterministic reference, fault, compatibility, privacy/security, semantic-compression where applicable, and resource-economy evidence is present; every failure is classified and every obligation is terminal/delegated/indeterminate; the proof bundle names exact digests and generations and can be independently replayed; no claim exceeds retained proof.

title: XFER-INV-001 — immutable roots only
description:
## Normative invariant
Stable identity: `XFER-INV-001` — **immutable roots only**
Authoritative sources: `ATP_AND_DISTRIBUTED_EVIDENCE.md` and `docs/ATP_AND_DISTRIBUTED_EVIDENCE.md`, byte-identical at SHA-256 `35a20ca0bf608c8cf75bd7284895968305a79d89feeb12c6c190e1003779d72f`.

## Exact source contract
ATP moves immutable named object graphs. Mutable session state, credential handles, effect authority, and live in-memory objects never ride inside the graph.

## Architectural realization
Implement the rule in first-party safe Rust ATP over immutable content-addressed object graphs. `Cx` and region ownership reach every path, clock, secret, storage and cancellation boundary. Maintain typed offered/staged/verified/durable/replicated/protected/retrievable/visible/committed states, deterministic identity, capability/privacy projection, sealed journals, request→drain→finalize cancellation, root-last publication, and canonical receipts. ATP never carries effect authority.

Exercise duplicate/reordered offers, corrupt/missing children, hash/signature/policy mismatch, stale grants/generations, repair beyond budget, path split/partition, cancellation/crash at each transition, journal corruption/resume, partial durability/publication, malicious manifests, retention/deletion misuse, and lost completion acknowledgement. Unit/property/state-machine, fault-schedule, differential/reference, standalone receipt verification, and real-entrypoint E2E transfer tests emit JSONL with transfer/object/path/policy IDs, seed/schedule, state transitions, budgets/costs, expected/actual outcome, staged-child disposition, obligations/cleanup, digests and safe resume/reconcile guidance.

title: FSS-063 — Implement Asupersync-owned S3-compatible staged uploader
description:
## Outcome

Implement Asupersync-owned S3-compatible staged uploader. Deliver a complete vertical contract in ATP archive and retrievability, not a placeholder or source-presence claim.

## Background and role

This task contributes immutable graph transfer, journals, closure, multipath drain, repair verification, provider protocols, costs, replicas, restore, and deletion. It composes with one EvidenceAnchor/EvidenceDeltaBatch universe and type-distinct authority, cognition, and effect planes. Governing invariants: INV-046/047/048/066/067/075.

## Technical contract

Begin with a deterministic reference and typed state machine. Expose success, expected error, cancellation, panic/quarantine, stale-generation, budget, and indeterminate outcomes before optimization or concurrency.

Keep staged, verified, visible, durable, replicated, protected, and retrievable states distinct; publish root last, verify post-repair digest/closure, and include all derived/cache/replica/journal edges in cleanup.

Every public/durable object has stable identity, owner, bounds, compatibility generation, validity/invalidators, cost, privacy/capability projection, structured errors, and safe retry/rebase/reconcile/repair guidance. Optimizations require a simple oracle and same-semantics proof.

## Failure and recovery

Cover malformed/missing input, duplicate/reordered work, stale anchors, cancellation at publication/effect boundaries, crash/restart, partial I/O, pressure, unavailable dependencies, revoked authority/privacy, and incompatible versions. Preserve valid partial evidence; never upgrade uncertain, stale, uncovered, redacted, or indeterminate state.

## Tests, e2e, and logging

Add unit/property, deterministic reference, differential/metamorphic, fault/cancel/crash, integration, and realistic end-to-end scenarios. Structured logs include scenario/seed, fixture root, ContractBasis/generations, authority/privacy, injected fault/schedule, transitions, budgets/work, outcome/error, semantic digest, proof handles, and reproduction command; logs are secret-free and contain no raw private media.

## Completion

title: XFER-INV-010 — receipts are canonical evidence
description:
## Normative invariant
Stable identity: `XFER-INV-010` — **receipts are canonical evidence**
Authoritative sources: `ATP_AND_DISTRIBUTED_EVIDENCE.md` and `docs/ATP_AND_DISTRIBUTED_EVIDENCE.md`, byte-identical at SHA-256 `35a20ca0bf608c8cf75bd7284895968305a79d89feeb12c6c190e1003779d72f`.

## Exact source contract
Transfer receipts, journals, path decisions, verification failures, repair events, and root commits are canonical ledger facts; bytes are content-addressed and search/UI are derived.

## Architectural realization
Implement the rule in first-party safe Rust ATP over immutable content-addressed object graphs. `Cx` and region ownership reach every path, clock, secret, storage and cancellation boundary. Maintain typed offered/staged/verified/durable/replicated/protected/retrievable/visible/committed states, deterministic identity, capability/privacy projection, sealed journals, request→drain→finalize cancellation, root-last publication, and canonical receipts. ATP never carries effect authority.

## Failure-first proof
Exercise duplicate/reordered offers, corrupt/missing children, hash/signature/policy mismatch, stale grants/generations, repair beyond budget, path split/partition, cancellation/crash at each transition, journal corruption/resume, partial durability/publication, malicious manifests, retention/deletion misuse, and lost completion acknowledgement. Unit/property/state-machine, fault-schedule, differential/reference, standalone receipt verification, and real-entrypoint E2E transfer tests emit JSONL with transfer/object/path/policy IDs, seed/schedule, state transitions, budgets/costs, expected/actual outcome, staged-child disposition, obligations/cleanup, digests and safe resume/reconcile guidance.

- The exact stable identity and source wording are retained with both byte-identical mirror paths and source digest.
- A deterministic reference state machine defines every transfer/publication/receipt transition, retry identity, cancellation disposition, terminal/indeterminate state, and recovery path.
- Unit/property/crash/partition/corruption/adversarial tests cover the named invariant at every durable cut point, with no orphan work or silent authority/retention change.
