title: Reconcile and implement canonical ATP transfer, path, and archive lifecycles
description:
## Outcome
Reconcile the normative ATP documents into one registered transfer vocabulary without erasing their distinct layers. The semantic transfer lifecycle is Proposed → Reserved → Offered → Receiving → ChildrenVerified → GraphClosed → DurabilitySatisfied → RootCommitted → ReceiptSealed, with Rejected, Aborted, Quarantined, Indeterminate, and Superseded terminals. Archive publication additionally distinguishes manifest validation, fetching/staging, object verification, root publication, replication-policy satisfaction, retrievability verification, completion, scrubbing, and retirement. Path state is separately Discover → Candidate → Probing → Active → Suspect → Draining → Closed.

## Non-collapse rules
Offered, received, verified, graph-closed, durable, committed, published, replicated, retrievable, protected, and complete are never synonyms. Root visibility is last and requires verified child closure, post-repair canonical digests, authorization, and publication fence. Indeterminate means remote semantic commit may have occurred and lookup cannot resolve; it owns a durable reconciliation obligation. Cancellation drains all losing/in-flight paths and leaves a checksummed resumable journal. Delivery of bytes/path never grants retention, indexing, activation, or effect authority.

## Proof, failure, and observability contract
Use a deterministic safe-Rust reference first. Preserve stable identities, exact ContractBasis/EvidenceAnchor and generation inputs, capability/privacy projection, typed unknown/redacted/stale/conflicted/indeterminate outcomes, bounded resources, and request→drain→finalize cancellation. Unit and property tests cover every transition and invariant. Fault tests cover malformed inputs, duplicates/reordering, stale anchors/generations, cancellation at every boundary, crash/restart, partial I/O, pressure, authority/privacy revocation, and incompatible versions. A realistic end-to-end script must exercise success plus safe failure through the public semantic surface and retain secret-free structured logs with scenario/seed, fixture/source root, authority/privacy, transition sequence, injected schedule/fault, budgets/observed work, outcome/error identity, decision/output digests, proof handles, cleanup/obligation state, and an exact reproduction command. No log may contain raw private media, credentials, or unbounded payloads.

Legacy/cross-document state spellings retained for reconciliation include ManifestVerified, ObjectVerified, GraphClosureVerified, ExposureReady, RootPublished, ReplicaQualified and RetrievabilityVerified. They must map to a layer-qualified canonical state or remain a distinct registered state; no spelling is silently discarded.
acceptance_criteria:
- Machine registries/schemas define layer-qualified canonical states and an explicit crosswalk for legacy document names; no transport invents aliases.
- Deterministic reducers reject skipped publication, root-before-child, stale fence, receipt-before-commit, path-close-with-live-work, and archive-complete-without retrievability.
- Crash/cancel tests cut every journal/publication/path state and prove resume equivalence, idempotency, cleanup, cost accounting, and exact terminal obligations.
- Provider simulators cover partial listing, eventual consistency, duplicate delivery, repair, quota pressure, revocation, lost ACK, and unresolved remote commit.
- E2e transfer/archive scripts log both semantic and path transitions, digests, fences, object counts/bytes, provider tuple, proof-of-retrievability, and reproduction command.

title: OBJECT-TOMBSTONE-001 — object store refuses to serve or publish tombstoned objects
description: PeachDove review of crates/fss-object (finding F8, left out of fss-x4a.9.20): fss-core defines TombstoneRecord and IdentityLifecycleRegistry, but InMemoryObjectStore has no tombstone state. acceptance_criteria: Positive: InMemoryObjectStore::tombstone(digest, TombstoneRecord) moves a Verified object to a Tombstoned state that keeps the record and the digest but releases the payload bytes and their quota; read_verified returns a typed Tombstoned error; publish_manifest and verify_closure fail with a typed error naming the tombstoned child; published manifests whose closure contains a tombstoned child are reported by a closure query. title: MODEL-INV-001 — immutable model generation
description:
## Normative model-runtime invariant
Stable identity: `MODEL-INV-001` — **immutable model generation**
Authoritative sources: `PURE_RUST_MODEL_RUNTIME.md` and `docs/PURE_RUST_MODEL_RUNTIME.md`, which are byte-identical at SHA-256 `12290ad6c104a642f6c7ef8f9e2f142a7815e923481b0932d3999dba648a609d`.

## Exact source contract
A model generation binds source repository and exact revision; original weight-file identities; imported canonical tensor identities; architecture/config/tokenizer/vocabulary; preprocessing and postprocessing programs; operator semantics and numeric policy; quantization/calibration assets; runtime/kernel generation; license and deployment restrictions; resource envelope; and qualification corpus/results. Any change creates a new generation; the model name is not identity.

## Architectural realization
Implement this invariant in first-party safe Rust with immutable typed generations, explicit `Cx` authority and region ownership at every I/O/time/resource/oracle boundary, request→drain→finalize cancellation, bounded work/output, stable error identities, root-last publication, and receipt-backed activation. Preserve source evidence, derived cognition, and effect authority as distinct planes; unsupported capability degrades explicitly and never downloads or invokes a foreign runtime.

## Failure and compatibility semantics
Exercise malformed and adversarial packages, stale/mixed generations, invalid shapes/layouts/numerics, duplicate/retry, cancellation/crash, OOM/thermal/deadline pressure, corrupt or missing artifacts, oracle disagreement/hang, migration/rollback, and unauthorized capability/privacy paths as applicable. Record unsupported, abstained, stale, conflicted, cancelled, and indeterminate states without flattening them.

## Deterministic proof and logging
Start with scalar/reference behavior and deterministic fixtures. Add unit/property tests, adversarial numeric/resource tests, differential oracle tests, cancellation/crash schedules, package/activation migration tests, event-quality and real-entrypoint E2E scenarios. Structured JSONL logs bind invariant/scenario/step, seed/schedule, input/model/preprocess/operator/kernel/calibration/runtime generations, authority/privacy scope, budgets/counters, expected and actual typed outcomes, decision/output/proof digests, cleanup/obligation state, costs, and safe recovery, while excluding weights, secrets, and protected media.
acceptance_criteria:
- The exact invariant identity and source wording are retained in the machine traceability graph, with both byte-identical source mirrors and their digest recorded.
- The implementation has a deterministic first-party reference and explicit typed success, unsupported, abstention, stale-generation, cancellation, resource-pressure, corruption, and indeterminate semantics.
- Focused unit/property/fault/differential tests cover its named contract and highest-loss violation; nondeterministic or foreign oracles are quarantined and cannot establish correctness alone.
- A real-entrypoint E2E script emits schema-validated JSONL and a standalone-verifiable proof bundle with exact generations, bounds, outcomes, cleanup, artifact hashes, cost, expiry, and repair guidance.
- Production closure contains no foreign runtime, hidden download/code path, ambient authority, unbounded queue/work/output, or secret/protected-byte disclosure.
- Completion is consumed by WP-080, cross-registry validation, local qualification and release claim derivation without treating source presence as proof.

title: FSS-072 — Implement pure-Rust model invocation/receipt protocol
description:
## Outcome

Implement pure-Rust model invocation/receipt protocol. Deliver a complete vertical contract in pure-Rust model runtime, not a placeholder or source-presence claim.

## Background and role

This task contributes immutable packages, typed tensors/IR, scalar and safe optimized kernels, memory plans, receipts, quantization, licenses, and rollback. It composes with one EvidenceAnchor/EvidenceDeltaBatch universe and type-distinct authority, cognition, and effect planes. Governing invariants: INV-002/013/032/044/045/049.

## Technical contract

Begin with a deterministic reference and typed state machine. Expose success, expected error, cancellation, panic/quarantine, stale-generation, budget, and indeterminate outcomes before optimization or concurrency.

Bind results to exact input/package/preprocess/numeric/kernel/memory/calibration generations; failures and abstentions remain derived uncertainty, and production has no foreign-runtime fallback.

Every public/durable object has stable identity, owner, bounds, compatibility generation, validity/invalidators, cost, privacy/capability projection, structured errors, and safe retry/rebase/reconcile/repair guidance. Optimizations require a simple oracle and same-semantics proof.

## Failure and recovery

Cover malformed/missing input, duplicate/reordered work, stale anchors, cancellation at publication/effect boundaries, crash/restart, partial I/O, pressure, unavailable dependencies, revoked authority/privacy, and incompatible versions. Preserve valid partial evidence; never upgrade uncertain, stale, uncovered, redacted, or indeterminate state.

Structured logs include scenario/seed, fixture root, ContractBasis/generations, authority/privacy, injected fault/schedule, transitions, budgets/work, outcome/error, semantic digest, proof handles, and reproduction command; logs are secret-free and contain no raw private media.

## Completion

Qualification is INT-FT-001..005, QL-MODEL-001, TEST-MODEL-HOST-001, and GATE-050. Code, migrations, costs, tests, proof, registries/schemas/status, and user/agent docs must agree.

title: Implement open-set novelty escalation without threat laundering
description:
## Outcome
Add property-, mode-, environment-, and model-generation-specific open-set/embedding novelty as a candidate and investigation signal only. Novelty may raise inspection priority, request a verifier, retrieve similar hard negatives, or create an explicit unknown-object hypothesis. It cannot label novelty as threat, authorize or suppress an effect, rewrite canonical evidence, or compare embeddings across generations. Baselines are drift-monitored, privacy-scoped, and invalidated on deployment/model changes.

## Required distinctions
Preserve unusual object, unusual behavior, out-of-distribution input, low observability, model disagreement, and simply rare-but-benign as different signals. The evaluation corpus includes darkness, IR, compression, blur, tiny/partial/crouched/crawling subjects, dark clothing/masks, weather/foliage, animals including raccoon/cat/deer/bird/insect/spider web, shadows/reflections/displays/replay, camera motion, and resource pressure. “Usually a raccoon” memory may influence retrieval or request verification, never current truth.

## Proof, failure, and observability contract
Use a deterministic safe-Rust reference first. Preserve stable identities, exact ContractBasis/EvidenceAnchor and generation inputs, capability/privacy projection, typed unknown/redacted/stale/conflicted/indeterminate outcomes, bounded resources, and request→drain→finalize cancellation. Unit and property tests cover every transition and invariant. Fault tests cover malformed inputs, duplicates/reordering, stale anchors/generations, cancellation at every boundary, crash/restart, partial I/O, pressure, authority/privacy revocation, and incompatible versions. A realistic end-to-end script must exercise success plus safe failure through the public semantic surface and retain secret-free structured logs with scenario/seed, fixture/source root, authority/privacy, transition sequence, injected schedule/fault, budgets/observed work, outcome/error identity, decision/output digests, proof handles, cleanup/obligation state, and an exact reproduction command. No log may contain raw private media, credentials, or unbounded payloads.
acceptance_criteria:
- Novelty outputs identify embedding/model/index/baseline generations, property/privacy domain, calibration validity, drift status, nearest evidence handles, and typed unknown disposition.
- Generation mixing, baseline reuse after invalidation, identity claims, and direct effect authorization are rejected.
- Unit/property tests cover thresholds, ties, empty/low-quality inputs, drift, privacy TTL, and deterministic replay.
- Held-out/e2e scenarios include novel benign, familiar threat, crawling/raccoon ambiguity, OOD darkness, and model disagreement, proving novelty changes inspection but not truth or authority.
- Logs retain component scores and routing decision without raw identity-bearing embeddings.

title: Qualify verifier independence and shared model failure domains
description:
## Outcome
Define when a second detector, VLM, temporal model, geometry rule or modality provides independent verification rather than a correlated repeat. Independence is analyzed across training data, checkpoint lineage/model family, architecture, preprocessing, modality, source sensors, clocks/networks, calibration and observed failure history. Two sizes or prompts of the same VLM may be highly correlated; deterministic geometry/rules or a genuinely different detector/modality may be stronger.

## Contract
Every claimed corroborator pair/group emits a failure-domain decomposition, conditional-independence assumptions, measured joint-error evidence for the deployment regime, invalidators and an independence class. Unknown or shared domains reduce evidence weight or keep the event single-domain/unconfirmed. The verifier localizes supporting/contradicting evidence and may abstain; it never authorizes an effect or turns a model phrase into numeric confidence.

## Proof and observability
Use stable typed identities, exact ContractBasis/EvidenceAnchor and generations, bounded inputs/outputs, explicit authority/privacy, deterministic reference behavior, typed failure/cancellation/indeterminate states, and actionable retry/rebase/reconcile guidance. Unit/property tests cover invariants and boundaries; fault/e2e tests cover malformed/stale/duplicate/reordered input, crash/cancel/pressure/revocation and realistic success/safe-failure paths. Structured logs are secret-free and include scenario/seed, source/fixture root, authority/privacy, transitions, budgets/work, outcome/error, digests, proof handles, cleanup/obligations and reproduction command.
acceptance_criteria:
- Registry/policy defines independence classes and minimum evidence for corroboration; unknown/shared domains cannot count as independent.
- Tests cover same-family model sizes, shared training/preprocess, two cameras on one network/clock, independent geometry, modality disagreement, regime drift and missing lineage.
- Sealed evaluation measures marginal/joint failures by tactic and observability slice rather than assuming diversity from model names.
- E2e shows a correlated double detection remains unconfirmed while genuinely independent evidence can advance the immutable event revision.

title: Implement calibrated sequential fusion with common-cause and abstention semantics
description:
## Outcome
Build an auditable deterministic fusion reference over calibrated likelihood/evidence intervals, missing data, contradictions, and declared common-cause failure domains. Candidate adaptive lanes may include conformal risk control for set-valued/abstaining output, e-values/e-martingales or other anytime sequential tests, bounded-prior-sensitivity Bayesian/likelihood models, defensible Dempster-Shafer-like evidence, and a learned shadow meta-model. No technique is admitted by elegance or raw score; it must beat the simple reference on sealed event-level evaluation without breaking calibration.

## Policy boundary
Sequential evidence may alert, wait for bounded imminent corroboration, request a better observation, alert with degraded coverage, retain silently, request operator confirmation, or reject. Every wait has deadline and expected value; optional stopping and false-alert exposure are measured. Severity, probability, expected harm, time criticality, reversibility, and false-alert cost remain distinct. Only adaptive routing changes online by default; safety/privacy, deployment, and calibrated decision policy require explicit versioned activation.

## Proof, failure, and observability contract
Use a deterministic safe-Rust reference first. Preserve stable identities, exact ContractBasis/EvidenceAnchor and generation inputs, capability/privacy projection, typed unknown/redacted/stale/conflicted/indeterminate outcomes, bounded resources, and request→drain→finalize cancellation. Unit and property tests cover every transition and invariant. Fault tests cover malformed inputs, duplicates/reordering, stale anchors/generations, cancellation at every boundary, crash/restart, partial I/O, pressure, authority/privacy revocation, and incompatible versions. A realistic end-to-end script must exercise success plus safe failure through the public semantic surface and retain secret-free structured logs with scenario/seed, fixture/source root, authority/privacy, transition sequence, injected schedule/fault, budgets/observed work, outcome/error identity, decision/output digests, proof handles, cleanup/obligation state, and an exact reproduction command. No log may contain raw private media, credentials, or unbounded payloads.

Verifier independence is supplied by MODEL-INDEPENDENCE-001. In particular, two sizes/checkpoints/prompts of the same VLM are not presumed independent; common training, preprocessing, modality and failure history must be accounted before fusion advances corroboration.
acceptance_criteria:
- Reference fusion produces intervals/sets, alternatives, assumptions, invalidators, missing-data reasons, failure-domain accounting, and an abstention/decision fingerprint.
- Conformal/sequential claims name tested exchangeability/coverage/optional-stopping assumptions and fail closed outside them.
- Tests cover correlated cameras/models, contradictory evidence, missing coverage, optional stopping, delayed corroboration, urgent low-probability high-loss events, and high-confidence benign animals.
- Shadow adaptive fusion cannot mutate thresholds/policy and is compared against the reference with event AUPRC, selective risk, calibration, false alerts/property-day, miss confidence bounds, and latency.
- E2e logs show why alert/wait/abstain/reject occurred and what evidence would change it.

title: WP-110 — Time synchronization and calibration

Establish conservative metric/time relationships and invalidate them honestly when the deployment changes.

Point timestamps without justified bounds are forbidden. Low training residual or attractive rendering is not a valid certificate. GATE-060/GATE-070; QL-GEOMETRY-001; TEST-TIME-001 and TEST-CALIBRATION-001; synthetic truth/known rig; held-out views; drift/crop/movement/clock faults; deterministic solver interfaces; activation/rollback; mask-before-egress and coverage-impact e2e.

The work package is complete only when its contracts, reference behavior, optimized/imported behavior, migrations, privacy/security policy, operation-cost rows, tests, proof bundles, compatibility claims, implementation status, and user-facing documentation agree.

title: Enforce operation-specific maximum tolerable time uncertainty
description:
## Outcome
Require every time-sensitive operation to declare a maximum tolerable capture-time uncertainty and a typed response when exceeded. Each source item retains device time/basis, host monotonic receive time, UTC/property mapping, earliest/latest plausible capture time, exposure/rolling-shutter/encoding/buffering/network/vendor-relay/decode-reorder/quantization/offset-drift uncertainty sources, sequence/discontinuity, and clock generation. Evidence degradation can only widen the interval.

## Decision semantics
Temporal association uses interval overlap and feasible transit intervals, not point equality or an ad hoc wider gate. The same 500 ms may be acceptable for a person crossing a yard and fatal for a fast vehicle/drone or closely spaced cameras. Cross-camera identity, geometry-dependent negative evidence, transit impossibility, and coverage conclusions abstain or degrade when their own tolerance is exceeded. A model cannot narrow time without retained synchronization evidence. Clock calibration methods retain ordered evidence strength, failure models, validation residuals, and generation identity.

## Proof, failure, and observability contract
Use a deterministic safe-Rust reference first. Preserve stable identities, exact ContractBasis/EvidenceAnchor and generation inputs, capability/privacy projection, typed unknown/redacted/stale/conflicted/indeterminate outcomes, bounded resources, and request→drain→finalize cancellation. Unit and property tests cover every transition and invariant. Fault tests cover malformed inputs, duplicates/reordering, stale anchors/generations, cancellation at every boundary, crash/restart, partial I/O, pressure, authority/privacy revocation, and incompatible versions. A realistic end-to-end script must exercise success plus safe failure through the public semantic surface and retain secret-free structured logs with scenario/seed, fixture/source root, authority/privacy, transition sequence, injected schedule/fault, budgets/observed work, outcome/error identity, decision/output digests, proof handles, cleanup/obligation state, and an exact reproduction command. No log may contain raw private media, credentials, or unbounded payloads.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every registered time-sensitive operation names its tolerance, consequence of exceedance, and required clock/coverage evidence.
- Interval composition is conservative under clock drift, buffer delay, reorder, reconnect, and missing metadata.
- Tests show the same interval accepted for one operation and rejected for a stricter one; widening never creates stronger identity or absence claims.
- Cross-camera e2e scenarios cover local RTP/UVC and wider time-varying vendor-relay uncertainty with explicit abstention/degradation logs.
- FORMAL-010 and ERR-CLOCK-UNCERTAIN-001 are exercised with retained counterexamples.

title: Prove GATE-040 media/archive resource-pressure behavior without later agent scope
description:
## Outcome
Produce the stage-scoped resource-pressure proof required by GATE-040 for media and archive durability, without making the gate wait for later agent task-quality metrics or the full cross-product resource doctrine.

## Exact scope
Exercise the already-defined typed budgets and pressure propagation through bounded live fan-out, decoded/tensor buffers, malformed media handling, chunk staging, multipart upload/reconciliation, retrieval, provider outage, local safety buffering, archive object sizing/cost, cancellation, and deletion interaction. Bind one exact source/toolchain/config/provider/profile generation and retain the full operation-cost vector for every scenario. This proof does not qualify agent token/context/graph work, release-native matrices, or unrelated later paths; those remain in DOC-029, FSS-198, QL-PERF-001, and GATE-120.

## Failure and degradation semantics
Inject memory/disk/descriptor/queue/bandwidth/request-rate/deadline/provider-price pressure, hostile oversized media, missing cost inputs, upload/list inconsistency, cancellation/crash at every durable transition, and recovery. Verify bounded admission, backpressure, quality ladders, local survival, root-last publication, staged-child disposition, terminal/delegated/indeterminate obligations, and explicit unsupported/not-observable/degraded outcomes. No pressure response may silently weaken custody, retention, privacy, authorization, redundancy, or source evidence.

## Reference, E2E, and logs
Use deterministic single-thread reference fixtures plus property/fault schedules and the real media/archive entrypoints. JSONL records scenario/step/seed, source/profile/provider/policy generations, budgets/reservations/high-water marks, queue/object/work/byte/request/energy/cost counters, injected fault, expected and actual typed transition/outcome, artifact and decision digests, cleanup/obligation state, and bounded repair/resume guidance. The retained proof bundle must be standalone-verifiable and distinguish measurement unavailability from pass.
acceptance_criteria:
- Deterministic reference and real-entrypoint tests cover normal operation and every named pressure/fault class across media, staging, transfer, archive, retrieval, cancellation and deletion interaction.
- Every queue, buffer, task, retry, object count, output and deadline is bounded; observed high-water/cost vectors are retained and compared to the exact profile budget.
- Missing/stale/contradictory resource or price evidence produces a typed non-pass/degraded result, never a fabricated measurement or weaker safety/privacy/custody policy.
- Crash/cancel/outage schedules prove root-last visibility, reusable/quarantined/collectable staged-child classification, and terminal/delegated/indeterminate obligations with safe reconciliation.
- Schema-validated JSONL and content-addressed artifacts can be independently verified from a clean snapshot and contain no secrets or protected media.
- GATE-040 consumes this scoped proof; DOC-029 and later agent/release performance work remain related but are not prerequisites for this stage decision.

title: FSS-100 — Build sealed event-level threat/hard-negative release gauntlet
description:
## Outcome

Build sealed event-level threat/hard-negative release gauntlet. Deliver a complete vertical contract in threat and hard-negative qualification, not a placeholder or source-presence claim.

## Background and role

This task contributes sealed split corpora, adversarial/benign strata, event metrics, calibration, false-alert exposure, preregistration, and bounds. It composes with one EvidenceAnchor/EvidenceDeltaBatch universe and type-distinct authority, cognition, and effect planes. Governing invariants: INV-021/022/028/029/053.

## Technical contract

Produce a sealed repeatable proof artifact—not a presence check—with positive, negative, adversarial, fault, and resource cases; retain raw results, minimized reproducers, exact claim limits, and excluded dimensions.

Use prepare→revalidate→persist-intent→commit/dispatch→observe→verify/reconcile; semantic idempotency conflicts fail, and lost acknowledgement after dispatch stays indeterminate until resolved.

Fail closed on authority/privacy/supply-chain drift; exclude secrets/private media from logs, derive claims from proof roots, and prove the clean offline release contains only admitted components/assets.

Every public/durable object has stable identity, owner, bounds, compatibility generation, validity/invalidators, cost, privacy/capability projection, structured errors, and safe retry/rebase/reconcile/repair guidance. Optimizations require a simple oracle and same-semantics proof.

## Failure and recovery

Cover malformed/missing input, duplicate/reordered work, stale anchors, cancellation at publication/effect boundaries, crash/restart, partial I/O, pressure, unavailable dependencies, revoked authority/privacy, and incompatible versions. Preserve valid partial evidence; never upgrade uncertain, stale, uncovered, redacted, or indeterminate state.

## Tests, e2e, and logging

Add unit/property, deterministic reference, differential/metamorphic, fault/cancel/crash, integration, and realistic end-to-end scenarios. Structured logs include scenario/seed, fixture root, ContractBasis/generations, authority/privacy, injected fault/schedule, transitions, budgets/work, outcome/error, semantic digest, proof handles, and reproduction command; logs are secret-free and contain no raw private media.

Use a deterministic safe-Rust reference first. title: FSS-157 — Implement matching, k-best assignment, and min-cost-flow association
description:
## Outcome

Implement matching, k-best assignment, and min-cost-flow association. Deliver a complete vertical contract in certified graph/search/memory cognition, not a placeholder or source-presence claim.

## Background and role

This task contributes immutable projections, deterministic algorithms/witnesses, incremental equivalence, factorized queries, capability-first expansion, absence, and cautious memory. It composes with one EvidenceAnchor/EvidenceDeltaBatch universe and type-distinct authority, cognition, and effect planes. Governing invariants: INV-035/037/038/039/056/068/069/080.

## Technical contract

Begin with a deterministic reference and typed state machine; expose success, expected error, cancellation, panic/quarantine, stale-generation, budget, and indeterminate outcomes before optimization.

Pin authorized immutable projections; declare exactness, semantics, tie-break/order, complexity/budget witness, high-water mark, and absence boundary; filter before expansion.

Every public/durable object has stable identity, semantic owner, hard bounds, compatibility generation, validity/invalidators, cost, privacy/capability projection, structured errors, and safe retry/rebase/reconcile/repair guidance. Optimization/import requires a simple oracle and same-semantics proof.

## Failure and recovery

Exercise malformed/missing input, duplicate/reordered work, stale anchors/generations, cancellation at publication/effect boundaries, crash/restart, partial I/O, pressure, unavailable dependency, revoked authority/privacy, and incompatible versions. title: FSS-211 — Implement semantic context packs and compression receipts
description:
## Outcome

Implement semantic context packs and compression receipts. Deliver this as a complete vertical contract in the agent cognitive operating membrane; it is not a prose convention, transport-only wrapper, schema-presence claim, or hidden conversational workflow.

## Background and role

The agent membrane must let a cold or resumed driver understand the mission, exact authority basis, current evidence and uncertainty, possible worlds, obligations, resources, and valid next moves without manually reconstructing subsystem state. This task contributes fss/1, durable mission/session/workspace, epistemic cells, SituationCapsule/WorldEnvelope, compression, cases, affordances, plans, obligations, collaboration, learning, and handoff. Governing invariants: INV-083..116.

## Technical contract

Start with a deterministic scalar/reference algorithm and immutable revision state machine. Every publication pins mission/session/workspace, exact authority and derived anchors, capability/privacy projection, budgets, validity/invalidators, and decision digest.

Apply capability/privacy before selection; preserve every contradiction, not-observable domain, hard clamp, protected world, active obligation, and indeterminate effect that could change a consequential action. H0–H4 hydration revalidates authorization and never rebinds an evidence handle.

Every decision-bearing response uses ContractBasis plus AgentRequestEnvelope/AgentResponseEnvelope; SituationCapsule is the primary orientation publication and carries a SituationFrame/WorldEnvelope, MeaningfulDelta, cases/plans/obligations, resources, categorized control envelope, ContextPack, SemanticCompressionReceipt, validity, proof, continuation, and typed affordances or an explicit terminal/blocked/waiting/unauthorized/not-observable reason.

## Failure and recovery

Cover ambiguous/tainted requests, insufficient authority, privacy redaction, missing coverage, stale anchors, incompatible basis, budget exhaustion, model/graph unavailability, concurrent workspace changes, invalidated recommendations, disconnect, cancellation drain, crash, duplicate commit, lost acknowledgement, incomplete handoff, harmful memory, and resnapshot. Preserve useful partial truth and safe next operations without laundering uncertainty or authority.

## Tests, e2e, and diagnostic logging

Add unit/property and exhaustive-small reference tests, sealed possible-world and omission-counterfactual cases, deterministic differential/metamorphic tests, multi-agent schedules, stale/crash/lost-ACK faults, cross-surface transcript equivalence, and end-to-end mission rehearsal. Logs include task/seed, ContractBasis, mission/session/workspace, anchors/high-water marks, WorldEnvelope/control digests, authority/privacy, candidate/selected/omitted items, fault schedule, budgets/full cost, transitions, stable outcome/error, proof handles, continuation, and reproduction command; never secrets or raw private media.

## Completion

Qualification is QL-AGENT-001, all TEST-AGENT-* families, and GATE-115. Task correctness, calibration, unsafe-action rate, evidence use, handoff continuity, operator burden, and full resource vector must meet the retained gate—not merely call/token reduction.
acceptance_criteria:
- FSS-211 has deterministic immutable semantics under fss/1, exact ContractBasis/anchors, capability/privacy projection, budgets, proof, invalidators, and stable recovery-rich outcomes.
- No task-critical contradiction, not-observable domain, protected world, hard clamp, obligation, lease, indeterminate effect, or required next step can disappear into prose or compression.
- Reference/property, adversarial possible-world, omission-counterfactual, stale/crash/lost-ACK, disconnect/cancel, and multi-agent tests pass.
- Equivalent Rust API/CLI/MCP/TUI/report/handoff inputs produce equivalent typed payloads and decision digests where applicable.
- A realistic end-to-end script retains detailed semantic transitions, full resource costs, receipts, proof handles, continuations, and reproduction logs.
- Schemas, registries, robot/human docs, status, and QL-AGENT-001 proof roots agree.

title: DELTA-INVARIANTS-001 — silence certificates, terminal transitions, and plan invalidation in meaningful deltas
description: PeachDove review of crates/fss-reference/src/meaningful_delta.rs and crates/fss-core/src/delta.rs (pre-existing code) found three AGENTS.md prohibited shortcuts: F1 classify_reference_meaningful_delta issues a SilenceCertificate ('complete typed comparison found no decision-relevant change') when basis and result are both Partial/Degraded, so a missing detection during a coverage gap is certified as silence; F4 TerminalTransition is only emitted for Indeterminate->Known effect claims, so event terminalization (Witnessed->Rejected/Resolved), obligation terminal states and effect Failed/Cancelled are MaterialState and coalescible; F5 plan-invalidation detection skips every premise not in KnowledgeState::Known, so plans founded on Estimated premises are never invalidated.
acceptance_criteria: Each of PeachDove's failing tests (F1, F4, F5) added first against the real API, then fixed: no silence certificate unless the result is Complete with no active coverage gap (a degraded-but-unchanged comparison is reported as such, never as certified silence); every terminal lifecycle transition (event, obligation, effect, mission) emits TerminalTransition and is non-coalescible, proven by a coalescing test that keeps it; Estimated and Known premises both trigger PlanInvalidation when they degrade, disappear or conflict. No-claim: does not change situation compilation (see SITUATION-INVARIANTS-001).

title: Expose operator privacy state, overcollection cost, and coverage consequences
description:
## Outcome
Provide an authoritative operator/agent query surface for what is recording and why; enabled zones/audio; effective retention and remote archive state; models that processed an event; identities/embeddings and expiry; evidence access/export; incomplete deletion; and the security-coverage effect of masks, schedules, and privacy pause. Authentication alone does not make overcollection acceptable, and a generic “local” badge must not hide vendor-cloud dependence or model data flow.

## Controls
Support visible recording indicators where applicable, guest/worker temporary privacy modes, indoor disable schedules with explicit coverage impact, a fast privacy pause that records the authority event without retaining private content, selective redacted export, stricter child/neighbor/public-zone defaults, and per-sensor audio opt-in. Every view applies capability/privacy projection before counts or absence. Privacy pause, masking, minimization, deletion lag, provider expiration, cryptographic erasure, replica lag, and unknown third-party copies remain distinct; none may pretend the property stayed fully observed.

## Proof, failure, and observability contract
Use a deterministic safe-Rust reference first. Preserve stable identities, exact ContractBasis/EvidenceAnchor and generation inputs, capability/privacy projection, typed unknown/redacted/stale/conflicted/indeterminate outcomes, bounded resources, and request→drain→finalize cancellation. Unit and property tests cover every transition and invariant. Fault tests cover malformed inputs, duplicates/reordering, stale anchors/generations, cancellation at every boundary, crash/restart, partial I/O, pressure, authority/privacy revocation, and incompatible versions. A realistic end-to-end script must exercise success plus safe failure through the public semantic surface and retain secret-free structured logs with scenario/seed, fixture/source root, authority/privacy, transition sequence, injected schedule/fault, budgets/observed work, outcome/error identity, decision/output digests, proof handles, cleanup/obligation state, and an exact reproduction command. No log may contain raw private media, credentials, or unbounded payloads.

This capability is the normative Operator transparency surface from PRIVACY.md §10 and must remain queryable even when its answer exposes degraded coverage, remote/vendor dependence, incomplete deletion or unknown copies.
acceptance_criteria:
- The public response uses registered envelopes and reports exact authority/privacy/policy generations, redactions, coverage loss, retention/archive/deletion states, evidence handles, and costs.
- Privacy pause retains only its authority/audit event and cannot retain prohibited content or emit false continuity/absence.
- Tests cover hidden-count inference, role/zone projection, audio-off proof, mask reprojection margin, cloud-path disclosure, expiry, incomplete deletion, and revocation mid-query.
- E2e scripts exercise enable/pause/resume/export/delete workflows and verify UI/CLI/MCP semantic equivalence with secret-free structured logs.
- Operator explanations state security tradeoffs without silently changing policy.

title: Program: admit every FrankenSuite mechanism through its exact import gate
description:
Background: architecture/franken_imports.json is the machine-readable admission ledger for mechanisms borrowed from sibling FrankenSuite projects. Each row specifies a source, exact mechanism, admissible mode, owning boundary, substitute prohibition, reference model, failure boundary, and proof gate. A sibling name or aspirational dependency is not implementation authority.

Approach: realize every registry row as an independently reviewable admission bead. Each child must pin exact sibling revision and semantic source, reproduce the mechanism with deterministic fixtures, distinguish reference/laboratory/oracle use from production ownership, verify cancellation/authority/failure behavior, retain differential evidence, and refuse activation until its named gate passes. Preserve first-party pure-Rust production semantics and the pinned sibling-closure requirement.

Why this exists: imported concepts cross the highest-risk architectural boundaries. Explicit per-mechanism admission prevents vague integration claims, accidental foreign-runtime dependencies, semantic drift, and unreviewed substitutes.
acceptance_criteria: All 47 IMP-* registry entries have one self-contained child bead. Each child names source project, mechanism, mode, owner, forbidden substitute, reference model, failure boundary, gate, fixtures, retained evidence, and rollback/deactivation behavior. Dependencies connect each admission to its implementation and qualification consumers. Registry-to-bead audit reports zero missing, duplicate, or status-inconsistent entries.

title: Admit asupersync mechanism: Verified immutable object-graph transfer with path lifecycle, quarantine, journal, resume, repair symbols, and diagnostics
description:
Background: IMP-AS-ATP-001 is the authoritative import-admission row in architecture/franken_imports.json. It permits the asupersync mechanism “Verified immutable object-graph transfer with path lifecycle, quarantine, journal, resume, repair symbols, and diagnostics” only in mode “direct dependency”, owned by fss-transfer. The semantic source is “asupersync ATP architecture and diagnostics”; the required proof gate is INT-AS-001. This bead is the complete admission contract, not a license to import unrelated sibling behavior.

Hard boundaries:
- Forbidden substitute: Treating ATP as a generic RPC/file-upload helper or exposing unverified partial objects.
- Known failure boundary: ATP cannot make a non-idempotent external effect exactly-once.
- Reference model/oracle: Manifest walker, chunk verifier, path-failure simulator, and reconstruction oracle.
- Registry status at planning time: censused.
- Production remains first-party pure Rust, #![forbid(unsafe_code)], explicit-Cx/authority scoped, cancellation-safe, bounded, and deterministic wherever the mechanism crosses those concerns.

Approach:
1. Pin the exact sibling source revision, relevant files/symbols, license, feature set, and registry digest; record the exact-closure identity used by DSR.
2. Build deterministic fixtures around the named reference model and characterize success, malformed input, cancellation, crash/restart, duplicate/replay, stale generation, resource exhaustion, and boundary-specific failures.
3. Implement or integrate only the admitted mechanism inside fss-transfer; preserve local stable IDs, typed planes, canonical encoding, privacy/capability projection, and failure semantics.
4. Differentially compare the local behavior to the reference without shipping a foreign production runtime or allowing a laboratory oracle to acquire ambient authority.
5. Retain a proof bundle containing commands, seeds/schedules, source and toolchain identities, logs, expected/actual semantic digests, cost/resource witnesses, and negative evidence.
6. Provide explicit deactivation, rollback, compatibility, and migration behavior. A failed or unavailable gate leaves the mechanism inactive and the owning claim open.

Reasoning: exact per-mechanism admission prevents a sibling project name from becoming blanket architecture authority. It preserves why the mechanism is useful while keeping FSS ownership, safety, privacy, and release obligations independently verifiable.

Fresh-eyes test, fault, and logging completion:
Use TEST-E2E-HARNESS-001 to test the first-party substitute and, only in the sealed lab, the pinned upstream oracle. title: Assimilate Asupersync authority, region, cancellation, subject and lab-oracle mechanics
description:
Source-assimilation boundary:
Path: docs/deep-dives/ASUPERSYNC.md
Role: This is a research/admission source, not production authority. Extract only explicitly admitted mechanisms through the matching IMP-* beads. Preserve source revision, license, behavioral oracle, substitute prohibition, failure boundary and exact gate. Foreign applications/frameworks remain sealed laboratory or migration oracles; no IPC wrapper, hidden feature, runtime download, foreign allocator/runtime or credential path may become production semantics.

Full source snapshot at planning time:

# Deep dive: `asupersync` as the execution, authority, evidence, and transfer substrate

**Document class:** normative source-to-design audit
**FSS integration gate:** `INT-AS-001`
**Status:** design import; no runtime readiness claim
**Audit basis:** repository architecture, v4 design bible, ATP architecture and DoD, adaptive RaptorQ design, deterministic-lab and evidence surfaces inspected 2026-08-31

## 1. Why this project is load-bearing

The superficial import would be “use Asupersync instead of Tokio.” That would miss almost all of the value. The load-bearing idea is that execution, cancellation, authority, partial effects, evidence, and transfer all share one explicit semantic model:

```text
owned work
+ context-carried authority and budgets
+ request -> drain -> finalize cancellation
+ reserve -> commit effects
+ tracked obligations
+ deterministic schedules and virtual time
+ proof-carrying transfer receipts
= concurrency that can be reasoned about after failure
```

For FSS, this is not an ergonomic preference. A property may have dozens of continuous streams, multiple decode and inference rates, remote archives, live viewers, agent queries, and alerts. The system must remain correct when any one of those is cancelled, delayed, duplicated, corrupted, restarted, or partitioned.

## 2. Mechanism inventory and exact FSS transplants

### 2.1 Region ownership is the lifecycle topology

Every unit of work has one owner. FSS adopts a region tree rather than a collection of services with detached loops:

```text
process-region
├── authority-region
│   ├── ledger-publication
│   ├── policy-registry
│   ├── identity-registry
│   └── evidence-sealer
├── property-region
│   ├── clock-authority
│   ├── coverage-authority
│   ├── archive-supervisor
│   ├── graph/search projectors
│   ├── agent-session regions
│   └── sensor-region*
│       ├── adapter-session
│       ├── packet-receive-pump
│       ├── continuity-monitor
│       ├── source-spool
│       ├── media-stage regions
│       ├── cognition-stage regions
│       └── publication obligations
└── effect-region
    ├── alert-coordinator
    ├── camera-control coordinator
    ├── export/deletion coordinator
    └── reconciliation workers
```

A region cannot report terminal closure while a child still owns a packet, file descriptor, credential lease, model job, archive multipart upload, notification attempt, or unsealed evidence record. Region closure emits a drain receipt naming all completed, cancelled, failed, panicked, and indeterminate children.

### 2.2 `Cx` is not a cancellation token; it is attenuated authority

Every operation that can block, allocate shared capacity, touch a device, publish state, call a model, move an object, or create child work accepts an explicit context. FSS extends the context with domain epochs and scopes:

```text
principal_id
property_id / privacy_domain
request_id / trace_id / replay_id
observation_anchor
sensor and object scopes
capability mask
policy / adapter / model / calibration / schema epochs
deadline and capture-time deadline
poll / CPU / memory / decoded-pixel / network / disk / model-token budgets
alert and external-effect budget
cancellation state and reason chain
pressure vector
```

Authority is narrowed twice. Rust types remove impossible operations from an interface; runtime capability masks and object scopes prevent a component from recovering broader authority through ambient service references. A detector cannot open the credential store. A query worker cannot create an alert coordinator. A model executor cannot choose its own network destination.

### 2.3 Budgets form a compositional resource contract

FSS imports the budget-combination doctrine rather than scattering timeouts and semaphore limits. Child budgets are monotone attenuations of parent budgets. The budget vector includes dimensions that conventional runtimes leave implicit:

- wall-clock and event-latency deadline;
- scheduler polls and cooperative checkpoints;
- CPU work units and SIMD tiles;
- decoded pixels and audio samples;
- resident, pinned, and staged bytes;
- network ingress, egress, and retransmission bytes;
- object-store operations and estimated dollar cost;
- model invocations, tokens, layers, or temporal windows;
- external effects and retries;
- privacy-sensitive materializations.

No subsystem may “recover” from exhaustion by silently switching to an unadmitted path. Degradation follows a registered ladder and emits a receipt.

### 2.4 Four-valued outcomes prevent epistemic flattening

FSS retains the `Ok / Err / Cancelled / Panicked` quadrant at every asynchronous boundary. Domain state adds `Indeterminate` where an external effect or device operation may have occurred but cannot yet be proven. `Indeterminate` belongs in the durable operation state machine, not as a fifth Rust exception accidentally caught by generic retry logic.

Examples:

- `Cancelled`: a model job observed cancellation before publishing output and drained cleanly.
- `Err`: an RTSP server rejected authentication before stream establishment.
- `Panicked`: an internal invariant failed; the worker is quarantined and the panic evidence retained.
- `Indeterminate`: a push notification request crossed the provider boundary, then the connection died before a receipt.

The severity lattice determines default aggregation, but domain policy may not convert a more severe state into a less severe one.

### 2.5 Cancellation is request, drain, and finalization

Dropping futures is forbidden as a shutdown protocol. Each long-running FSS subsystem declares:

1. admission-close behavior;
2. its safe cancellation checkpoints;
3. work that is temporarily masked;
4. obligations that must drain;
5. a nonnegative drain potential;
6. escalation and indeterminacy behavior;
7. finalization evidence.

Representative potential functions:

```text
camera drain potential = queued packets + owned frame buffers + staged capsules + in-flight model windows
archive drain potential = unsealed children + unverified remote parts + resumable journal entries
alert drain potential = undispatched intents + transmitted-unreconciled attempts + unsealed receipts
model drain potential = admitted jobs + active kernels + unpublished outputs + pinned input views
property drain potential = live child regions + active leases + unresolved effects + unsealed roots
```

Progress certificates sample the potential, active regime, expected descent, rebounds, and the reason safe quiescence can or cannot be guaranteed. A timeout is evidence about elapsed time; it is not proof that an effect did not occur.

### 2.6 Reserve/commit and linear obligations protect partial effects

FSS imports two-phase operations wherever cancellation between “started” and “visible” could lose or duplicate work:

- channel sends;
- packet and frame buffer admission;
- ledger sequence allocation;
- evidence-root publication;
- model output publication;
- alert dispatch;
- camera controls;
- archive multipart publication;
- retention and deletion;
- model, adapter, calibration, and policy activation.

The reserve step fixes identity, authority, budget, preconditions, generation, and destination. Commit is a short bounded section that makes the effect visible or dispatches it. Dropping a reservation has explicit abort semantics. Committed obligations remain tracked until terminal proof or durable indeterminacy.

### 2.7 Deterministic laboratory execution is inherited by every boundary

All time, sleeps, retry schedules, jitter, queue selection, leases, deadlines, fault decisions, and scheduler handoffs must be supplied through the runtime abstraction. The laboratory explores:

- cancellation at each registered yield point;
- packet loss, duplication, corruption, delay, and reorder;
- camera disconnect and reconnect at every acquisition transition;
- source-clock steps, drift, wraparound, and contradictory timestamps;
- process death at every reserve/materialize/publish barrier;
- alert lost-ACK and duplicate-callback schedules;
- simultaneous agents preparing overlapping effects;
- archive path failure during chunk, repair, verify, or root publication;
- model crash, OOM, malformed result, and generation rollover;
- restore while stale readers, prepared effects, and derived generations remain alive.

The same semantic scenario must run under production scheduling and LabRuntime. Production-only timers, threads, or hidden randomness are verification escape hatches.

### 2.8 Trace equivalence and canonical replay reduce schedule noise

Asupersync’s Mazurkiewicz-trace and Foata-normal-form work suggests a stronger FSS replay contract. The replay engine records observable dependency labels, not merely one brittle total ordering. Independent actions may commute; dependent actions may not. FSS canonicalizes equivalent schedules into stable parallel layers and records:

```text
trace_class_fingerprint
canonical_schedule_digest
switch_count
independence_policy_epoch
happens-before edges
resource/effect conflicts
```

This matters for multi-camera ingestion: packets from independent cameras may interleave arbitrarily without changing semantics, while two publications to the same event lineage or archive root are dependent. Canonicalization keeps regression diffs human-readable and lets schedule exploration focus on distinct races.

### 2.9 ATP is an immutable object-graph plane, not generic RPC

FSS imports ATP for movement of immutable graphs:

- source-media capsule graphs;
- archive manifests and chunks;
- replay/crashpack bundles;
- model and calibration generations;
- digital-twin geometry and coverage generations;
- graph/search generations;
- qualification corpora and proof bundles;
- read-replica deltas.

An ATP root names a manifest; manifests name typed children; children name chunks and optional repair symbols. The receiver stages bytes, verifies identities, verifies graph closure, records a resumable journal, and publishes the root last. Path candidates may race, but losing paths drain. Post-repair plaintext identity is authoritative; successful erasure decoding is not sufficient by itself.

ATP is explicitly not the transport for non-idempotent camera control, alerts, deletion, or drone effects. Those need request identity, fencing, lookup, reconciliation, and domain-specific terminal predicates.

### 2.10 Transfer receipts become economic and forensic evidence

Every transfer receipt records more than byte count:

- source/destination and capability identity;
- immutable root and graph closure result;
- path set, chosen path, and hedged paths;
- chunk/FEC parameters and repair usage;
- bytes read/sent/retransmitted/staged/discarded;
- resume point and journal identity;
- checksum and post-repair verification;
- queue, CPU, memory, disk, and network pressure;
- object-store request counts and estimated cost;
- cancellation and drain evidence;
- exact reproduction command and implementation identity.

This makes archive strategy auditable and lets FSS distinguish “provider accepted bytes” from “the evidence graph is remotely retrievable.”

### 2.11 Adaptive transfer and scheduling are bounded decisions

The Transfer Brain and adaptive-RaptorQ work contributes a general rule: adaptation selects among safe registered arms; it never defines safety. FSS may adapt:

- chunk size and transfer concurrency;
- path hedging;
- repair-symbol overhead;
- live-preview frame rate;
- model routing and candidate budgets;
- buffer-pool targets;
- archive object sizing;
- witness-refinement effort.

Each adaptive decision has a decision card, safe baseline, clamps, shadow panel, common-random-number evaluation, regime boundaries, minimum evidence, rollback, and negative-evidence record. “The learned policy chose it” is not an explanation.

### 2.12 Capability tokens are suitable for relay and worker isolation

FSS adopts narrow capability tokens for worker and relay operations. A token binds:

```text
actions
destination or object prefix
methods / operation families
byte and cost ceiling
expiry and nonce
required checksums / roots
privacy class
principal and issuing policy epoch
```

Tokens are verified before expensive state allocation. Anti-replay state is bounded and domain-scoped. A model-executor token cannot be repurposed as an archive-upload token; an archive token cannot read arbitrary objects.

### 2.13 Evidence and decision registries are first-class runtime products

The `franken_decision`, `franken_evidence`, and qualification ideas are imported as a cross-cutting substrate. Every optimization, adaptive policy, compatibility promotion, and readiness claim names:

- decision identity and allowed arms;
- invariant owner;
- reference model;
- evidence schema;
- validity and expiry;
- environment and generation tuple;
- positive and negative evidence;
- rollback and revival conditions.

Metrics are not allowed to mutate answers. Missing optional telemetry may reduce confidence in a performance claim; it cannot change the selected event, graph path, or effect outcome.

## 3. FSS semantic owners

| Imported mechanism | Owning FSS component | Replacement prohibition |
|---|---|---|
| Regions, `Cx`, budgets, outcomes | `fss-runtime` | No second async runtime or detached worker model |
| Two-phase channels/effects | `fss-runtime`, `fss-effect` | No “send then hope” mutation path |
| Obligations and leases | `fss-obligation`, `fss-effect` | No untracked committed external work |
| LabRuntime and trace canonicalization | `fss-lab` | No production-only time/randomness path |
| ATP object graphs | `fss-transfer` | No ad hoc multipart uploader as authoritative transfer |
| Adaptive decision cards | `fss-decision` | No opaque online threshold mutation |
| Evidence receipts | `fss-evidence` | No log-line-only readiness claims |

## 4. Superficial imitations that would fail

1. Passing `&Cx` through APIs while adapters recover global credentials or clocks.
2. Using regions for tasks but spawning codec or vendor subprocesses outside ownership.
3. Cancelling by dropping queues and losing which packets/effects were committed.
4. Treating ATP as an RPC bus and sending alert or PTZ commands over eventual delivery.
5. Recording transfer throughput without graph closure or retrievability.
6. Adding FEC without post-repair content verification.
7. Using a learned scheduler before a deterministic safe baseline exists.
8. Running deterministic unit tests while production uses separate timers, random jitter, or native threads.
9. Reporting timeout as cancellation even when a provider or device effect may have happened.
10. Treating telemetry failure as permission to skip safety checks.

## 5. Admission evidence for `INT-AS-001`

Asupersync becomes load-bearing only after all of the following pass:

1. One complete property lifecycle runs under real and laboratory time with identical semantic roots.
2. Region close proves no owned task, descriptor, subprocess, buffer lease, credential lease, or effect obligation survives.
3. Cancellation campaigns cover every registered yield/publication barrier and preserve reason chains.
4. Drain certificates are produced for stream, archive, model, and effect regions; forced termination yields explicit indeterminacy.
5. Authority attenuation is tested statically and dynamically against attempted scope recovery.
6. Two-phase channel and publication paths survive cancellation before reserve, after reserve, during materialization, and after commit.
7. ATP corruption, truncation, reordering, duplicate chunks, path loss, resume, FEC repair, and root-last publication preserve object identity.
8. Relay tokens reject wrong destination, method, root, expiry, nonce, privacy class, and byte ceiling.
9. Adaptive policies cannot select an unregistered arm or cross hard clamps; shadow/revert behavior is deterministic.
10. Schedule-class replay and canonicalization remain stable across repeated runs and expose real dependency changes.
11. Same-binary A/A experiments show the evidence instrumentation does not change semantic outputs.
12. A negative-evidence bundle documents unsupported/noncooperative host-boundary behavior.

## 6. Deliberately rejected imports

- Making pure geometry, parsing, score calibration, or media kernels async merely for consistency.
- Claiming bounded cancellation for noncooperative vendor or operating-system calls without an isolation boundary.
- Using distributed “exactly once” terminology. FSS uses identity, idempotency, leases, receipts, and reconciliation.
- Allowing adaptive pressure control to weaken freshness, coverage, privacy, or evidence requirements.
- Treating ATP repair success as source truth before post-repair digest and graph-closure verification.

## 7. Resulting architectural leap

The deepest import is not a runtime API. It is the ability to make every long-lived FSS operation answer four questions precisely:

1. **Who owns this work?**
2. **What authority and budget does it possess?**
3. **What partial effects or obligations can exist if it stops now?**
4. **What retained evidence proves its terminal state?**

Without those answers, a surveillance system is a pile of best-effort loops. With them, it becomes an inspectable, replayable control plane.


Operationalization requirements:
1. Treat machine registries/schemas as higher authority, but record and repair any disagreement rather than choosing convenient text.
2. Preserve stable identities, assumptions, alternatives, failure/unknown states, privacy/security limits, costs, qualification and claim boundaries.
3. Add deterministic source-digest and heading/row coverage checks with typed drift diagnostics and owner/repair guidance.
4. Update the bead and its dependent proof whenever the source is deliberately changed; generated prose must remain a mirror, not a parallel contract.

Unadmitted ideas remain unavailable. The embedded source can be removed after assimilation without losing rationale or implementation requirements.

Hard boundaries:
- Forbidden substitute: One undifferentiated internal bus where every message pays every invariant or none.
- Known failure boundary: Federation and brokerless mobility remain gated until session/lease semantics are qualified.
- Reference model/oracle: In-memory deterministic subject router with explicit service-class compiler.

description:
Source-assimilation boundary:
Path: docs/deep-dives/FRANKENSQLITE.md
Role: This is a research/admission source, not production authority. Extract only explicitly admitted mechanisms through the matching IMP-* beads. # Deep dive: `frankensqlite` as the multi-version evidence and semantic-transaction substrate

**Document class:** normative source-to-design audit
**FSS integration gate:** `INT-FSQL-001`
**Status:** design import; persistence adapter remains unqualified
**Audit basis:** repository architecture, concurrency contract, critical invariants, recovery and benchmark methodology inspected 2026-08-31

## 1. The non-obvious import

The shallow transplant would be “store FSS metadata in SQLite.” The valuable import is a much stronger model:

```text
immutable versions
+ coherent snapshot anchors
+ witnessed reads, including negative predicates
+ deterministic commit publication
+ SSI-style dangerous-structure detection
+ conservative conflict refinement
+ semantic merge proofs
+ crash-first recovery
= concurrent reasoning without mixing worlds
```

FSS observes a world that changes independently of it. The ledger cannot make the physical world transactional, but it can make the *observation history, derived-generation boundaries, prepared effects, and reconciliation protocol* serializable and auditable.

## 2. One canonical version axis for authoritative facts

Every committed authority-plane change receives a monotonically ordered `CommitSeq`. A query pins a `WorldAnchor`:

```text
deployment_lineage
commit_seq
observation_epoch
object_root
adapter_registry_epoch
model_registry_epoch
calibration_epoch
policy_epoch
privacy_epoch
schema_epoch
```

A reader never combines event revision from one anchor, camera health from another, and calibration from a third unless it explicitly performs a temporal join. Derived graph/search/model generations publish the exact high-water mark they consumed and cannot claim freshness beyond it.

The ledger stores compact authority facts and manifests. Large media, model weights, geometry, and proof artifacts remain content-addressed objects whose roots are referenced transactionally.

## 3. Read witnesses: a plan records what it relied on

A prepared alert, camera control, deletion, export, or activation records semantic read witnesses, not one coarse state hash. FSS witness classes include:

- identity generation and revision;
- field value, field absence, or presence state;
- stream continuity interval and packet-sequence domain;
- source-object existence and custody state;
- event revision and evidence-root membership;
- calibration transform, covariance, and validity region;
- coverage cell/zone version and visibility mask;
- track/association membership and alternative hypotheses;
- policy, privacy, model, adapter, schema, and capability epochs;
- archive publication and retrievability state;
- resource reservation, lease, and fence;
- aggregate quantity plus contributing set;
- graph edge existence/nonexistence and bounded reachability;
- negative predicate over an explicitly covered spatial-temporal domain.

A write witness identifies the semantic domains an effect or publication intends to change. Conflict is defined over semantics, not serialized row bytes.

## 4. Negative reads are first-class predicates

“No person is in the protected yard” is not absence of a detector row. It depends on:

```text
zone geometry
camera coverage generation
effective sensor health
capture interval and continuity
model/detector generation
minimum observable size/contrast
occlusion and privacy masks
queried time range
```

The witness therefore names a bounded domain and coverage certificate. New evidence that introduces a person, invalidates calibration, degrades a camera, or changes the policy conflicts with the negative read. Cache miss is never evidence of absence.

## 5. Hierarchical witnesses permit safe refinement

Witnesses form a hierarchy:

```text
deployment
└── domain (sensor / event / archive / policy / geometry)
    └── sensor-set / zone / time-bucket / entity family
        └── stream generation / spatial cell / event / object root
            └── field / packet range / pixel mask / edge / object child
```

Coarse witnesses are mandatory and sound. Fine witnesses are optional performance accelerators. If two prepared operations conflict coarsely, the coordinator may spend a bounded value-of-information budget to refine. Exhaustion yields a conservative conflict or replan; it never grants permission.

This asymmetry is essential: performance failure may reduce concurrency, but cannot create an undetected race.

## 6. SSI-style dangerous structures for multi-agent and external-world plans

Prepared and recently committed semantic transactions form a dependency graph from read/write antidependencies. The coordinator detects dangerous structures that could create write skew, including phantoms from negative reads.

Examples:

- Agent A reads “rear camera healthy” and prepares suppressing a redundant alert; Agent B concurrently disables that camera for maintenance.
- Two agents each see one free archive budget and both prepare expensive exports.
- A retention change reads “no legal hold” while another operation creates the hold.
- A camera-control plan reads an old calibration/coverage generation while a calibration activation changes the field of view.
- An alert policy reads “no prior alert in cooldown window” while another alert commits into that window.

Passing the ledger gate proves validity at the selected anchor. It does not prove the camera/provider/physical world stayed unchanged forever. The boundary operation still performs a final bounded precondition check and later reconciliation.

## 7. Deterministic commit combining

Planning, decoding, inference, and graph work remain parallel. Completed commit candidates enter one brief deterministic sequencing point. The combiner:

1. orders candidates by registered stable policy;
2. validates transaction, lease, fence, and epoch identity;
3. checks read/write witnesses against the chosen anchor;
4. performs bounded refinement;
5. detects dangerous structures;
6. reserves durable IDs and idempotency rows;
7. stages object/publication references;
8. commits one authority delta batch or returns a precise conflict/replan result.

Callbacks and expensive work happen after releasing the sequencing lock. Drain-then-drop-then-process prevents reentrant deadlocks. Failed speculative workers publish no visible side effects.

## 8. Semantic merge ladder

FSS never resolves semantic conflict with last-writer-wins. The merge ladder is:

1. **Exact intent replay.** Recompile the immutable intent against the new anchor.
2. **Stable-key structural merge.** Merge disjoint fields, object children, spatial masks, annotation edges, or time ranges using canonical order.
3. **Registered commutative composition.** Append-only adjudications, evidence edges, and counters may compose when the registry proves commutativity and identity.
4. **Domain compensation and replan.** Reconcile an external effect before generating a replacement plan.
5. **Reject.** Unknown, ambiguous, or privacy-sensitive semantics do not merge.

An accepted merge emits a certificate naming basis anchors, intents, conflict domains, mechanism, canonical normal form, decision path, and post-merge digest.

Potential safe merge families:

- append-only evidence/adjudication records;
- nonoverlapping media packet ranges in one stream generation;
- nonoverlapping privacy-mask tiles under the same coordinate frame;
- independent archive manifest children before root publication;
- track annotations that target distinct registered fields;
- resource counters with algebraically registered operations.

Threat belief, identity association, effect status, policy priority, and deletion scope never use blind field merges.

## 9. Savepoints map to staged semantic work

Savepoints are useful for bounded batches and agent plans. Rolling back to a savepoint restores transaction-local rows, object references, witness sets, and publication reservations while preserving the outer transaction’s ownership and lock semantics. Release merges child state into its parent deterministically.

FSS uses savepoint-like scopes for:

- one sensor capsule inside a larger ingest batch;
- one model result inside an event revision;
- one provider part inside a multipart archive upload;
- one candidate association inside a k-best hypothesis batch;
- one evidence export rendition inside an all-or-nothing sibling publication.

A savepoint cannot roll back an already dispatched external effect; that belongs to reconciliation/compensation.

## 10. Exact numeric ordering is a correctness surface

Time, sequence numbers, costs, IDs, and model scores cannot rely on lossy or platform-variable comparison. FSS imports the exact-order discipline:

- integer timestamps and sequence values compare exactly in widened integer space;
- floating values have a registered total order, NaN policy, signed-zero policy, and overflow behavior;
- mixed integer/real comparisons never silently cast large integers to imprecise floats;
- score-space identity is part of the key, so values from different model generations are incomparable by default;
- deterministic tie-breaks are explicit stable IDs or insertion sequence, never hash iteration.

This is crucial for replay, top-k alert selection, temporal windows, and archive expiry.

## 11. Recovery is part of the transaction contract

Crash testing covers each publication cut:

```text
before ID reservation
after reservation / before row materialization
after ledger rows / before object staging
after object children / before root seal
after root seal / before root pointer commit
after commit / before client response
after effect intent commit / before dispatch
after dispatch / before provider receipt
after receipt / before observation/reconciliation
```

Recovery distinguishes:

- definitely not committed;
- committed and visible;
- staged but unreachable and eligible for quarantine/GC;
- effect dispatched but outcome unknown;
- object root published but remote retrievability unproven;
- derived generation stale and rebuildable;
- canonical evidence requiring operator repair.

Recovery never infers a successful external effect solely from an intent row.

## 12. Compact conflict summaries must preserve safety history

Pruning old transactions or event history must retain enough summary state to preserve SSI reasoning. Approximate read fingerprints may create false conflicts but cannot create false negatives. Any compact structure used for witness membership has a declared one-sided error contract and reference fallback.

For FSS, summaries retain at least:

- read/write conflict epochs;
- negative-domain coverage roots;
- effect and lease fences;
- event lineage high-water marks;
- archive/deletion obligations;
- dangerous-structure in/out history needed by the selected SSI profile.

## 13. Canonical versus derived data

### Canonical ledger families

- deployment, principal, capability, policy, and privacy generations;
- device/adapter/stream identities and compatibility tuples;
- observation/capsule manifests and time/continuity evidence;
- immutable event revisions and adjudications;
- calibration and coverage certificates;
- model job/result identities and admitted summaries;
- prepared effects, receipts, reconciliation, and obligations;
- archive roots, retention, holds, deletion plans, and proof bundles;
- the ordered `EvidenceDeltaBatch` log.

### Derived/rebuildable families

- decoded frame caches and proxies;
- track acceleration indexes;
- search segments and embeddings;
- graph adjacency representations and centrality scores;
- thumbnails, summaries, context packs, and TUI projections;
- materialized standing queries;
- optimization statistics not required to explain a committed decision.

Derived generations still have identities and high-water marks; rebuildable does not mean untracked.

## 14. FSS semantic owners

| Imported mechanism | FSS owner | Replacement prohibition |
|---|---|---|
| `CommitSeq`, snapshot anchors | `fss-ledger`, `fss-types` | No mutable “latest world” singleton |
| Read/write/negative witnesses | `fss-transaction` | No state-hash-only validation |
| SSI dependency graph | `fss-transaction` | No optimistic commit without phantom handling |
| Deterministic commit combiner | `fss-ledger` | No callback under publication lock |
| Semantic merge certificates | Domain crate + `fss-transaction` | No generic last-writer-wins |
| Crash recovery | `fss-ledger`, `fss-evidence` | No log scraping as source of truth |
| Exact ordering | `fss-types` | No hash order or lossy mixed numeric compare |

## 15. Superficial imitations that would fail

1. Storing rows in FrankenSQLite but letting every subsystem maintain its own mutable epoch.
2. Snapshotting tables without pinning model, calibration, policy, and object roots.
3. Recording a plan state hash rather than the facts and negative predicates it relied on.
4. Using the low-level transaction manager and assuming it provides full SSI semantics automatically.
5. Treating cache misses or no detector row as negative evidence.
6. Refining conflicts with a probabilistic structure that can false-negative.
7. Letting a callback or model run inside the commit critical section.
8. Merging threat belief or effect state by field timestamp.
9. Pruning dependency history needed to detect later dangerous structures.
10. Reporting crash recovery from happy-path database reopen tests only.

## 16. Admission evidence for `INT-FSQL-001`

1. Differential execution against a single-threaded in-memory reference ledger.
2. Snapshot tests prove no query mixes authority epochs or derived high-water marks.
3. Negative-read phantom corpus covers space, time, coverage, continuity, policy, and object domains.
4. Multi-agent dangerous-structure schedules are explored deterministically.
5. Conflict refinement exhaustion produces conservative aborts only.
6. Semantic merge certificates replay byte-for-byte and reject unknown operations.
7. Savepoint rollback/release preserves outer ownership and witness semantics.
8. Exact numeric and tie-order fixtures cover large integers, NaNs, signed zero, time intervals, and model-generation separation.
9. Crash injection at every reserve/materialize/publish/effect boundary yields the registered recovery state.
10. Backup/restore enters a new observation epoch and rejects stale prepared effects.
11. Pruning/compaction preserves SSI summaries and negative-domain roots.
12. Concurrency/performance claims include raw samples, environment, contention shape, aborts, tail latency, and same-binary A/A controls.
13. No persistence readiness claim is made from parser/source presence or rejection-only tests.

## 17. Deliberately rejected imports

- Treating the entire physical world as ACID. Only the observation/effect protocol is transactional.
- Using database triggers or SQL as hidden policy authority.
- Exposing arbitrary SQL to agents.
- Making large media blobs the primary relational payload.
- Requiring advanced native-mode features before a deterministic adapter proves semantics.
- Equating database commit with camera/provider effect completion.

## 18. Resulting architectural leap

The ledger does more than remember events. It lets an agent or operator ask:

> “At exactly which coherent world anchor was this decision valid, what positive and negative facts did it rely on, which concurrent changes could invalidate it, what external effect crossed the boundary, and what can be proven after a crash?”

That is the transaction model FSS actually needs.


Operationalization requirements:
1. Treat machine registries/schemas as higher authority, but record and repair any disagreement rather than choosing convenient text.
2. Preserve stable identities, assumptions, alternatives, failure/unknown states, privacy/security limits, costs, qualification and claim boundaries.
3. Add deterministic source-digest and heading/row coverage checks with typed drift diagnostics and owner/repair guidance.
4. Update the bead and its dependent proof whenever the source is deliberately changed; generated prose must remain a mirror, not a parallel contract.
