title: WP-030 — Canonical ledger and object spool
description:
## Outcome

Implement the authority plane: one ordered multi-version history, semantic transaction witnesses, crash-safe object custody, root-last publication, retention/holds, backup/restore, and graph-complete deletion planning.

## Background and architectural role

Admit only the qualified FrankenSQLite/FrankenFS surfaces behind deterministic traits and reference adapters. Implement EvidenceDeltaBatch ordering, positive/negative/hierarchical read and write witnesses, SSI dangerous-structure checks, semantic merge certificates, staged/visible/durable/replicated/protected states, migrations, rebuild cursors, checkpoints, and new-epoch restore.

## Failure semantics and non-negotiable boundaries

Raw-byte or last-writer-wins merge is forbidden. A database commit is not an external effect; an uploaded child is not a published root; a deleted row is not deletion closure. Crashes at every reserve/materialize/publish/effect cut classify staged, visible, committed, quarantined, recoverable, and indeterminate state exactly.

## Qualification and retained evidence

GATE-040; INT-FSQL-001 and INT-FFS-001; TEST-LEDGER-CRASH-001; phantom/write-skew schedules; reference/optimized differential; kill-point matrix; restore/replay equivalence; deletion reachability adversaries; migration and rollback proof.

## Completion boundary

The work package is complete only when its contracts, reference behavior, optimized/imported behavior, migrations, privacy/security policy, operation-cost rows, tests, proof bundles, compatibility claims, implementation status, and user-facing documentation agree.
acceptance_criteria:
- The epic’s complete contract is represented by granular child beads with explicit owners and true blocking edges.
- Child acceptance covers success and failure semantics, compatibility/migration, privacy/security, performance cost, observability, documentation/status, and retained proof.
- Unit/property, deterministic reference, differential, fault/cancellation/crash, integration, end-to-end, resource-economy, and release lanes are assigned where applicable.
- Closing this epic requires terminal proof for every required child; implementation or schema presence alone is insufficient.

title: Consented real-footage corpus from owner cameras with owner-drawn event labels
description:
Why: every perception result in the repo (foreground, HOG people SVM, Kalman tracking, cross-camera association, zone events) has only ever run on procedural textures or bright squares on black. GOAL-005 (rare-event quality) and GOAL-006 (explicit observability) cannot be measured without real footage. The 2026-09-23 reality check found this is the single biggest proof gap.

What: a small, consented corpus recorded ONLY from the owner's own cameras on the owner's property, for example 20-60 short MJPEG/H.264 clips: empty scene, resident walking, delivery, animal, night, rain or wind-blown foliage, occlusion. Include a label file with per-clip event intervals and zones, drawn by the owner. Store it outside git or as small committed fixtures, per the owner's privacy choice. Add a README describing consent, capture device and firmware, and retention.

Needs OWNER: consent, recording, and the storage/retention decision. Do not synthesize footage or download third-party footage as a substitute. This unblocks the evaluation-harness bead.
notes: DECISION 2026-09-24 (delegated by the owner): recording the OWNER camera corpus requires physical access to the owner property and cameras and cannot be done by an agent. It stays open for the owner. An interim public, permissively licensed clip may be used strictly as labelled LAB evaluation data, never as deployment evidence.

title: Perception pipeline: Kalman constant-velocity tracker with IoU-based track management
description: Implement a real Kalman filter tracker for detected objects. Input: DetectionFrame bounding boxes from the foreground detector. Output: TrackedObject list with stable IDs, Kalman-filtered positions/velocities, track states (Tentative/Confirmed/Lost/Deleted). Uses a constant-velocity motion model with IoU-based data association (nearest-neighbor on bounding-box IoU, not Hungarian — that is a follow-up bead). Track management: new tracks start Tentative, confirmed after N consecutive hits, deleted after M consecutive misses. All arithmetic is f64, no external crates. The tracker must be deterministic across runs with the same input. Types should align with the existing tracking.rs types in fss-reference. Acceptance: (1) single object tracked across frames with smooth Kalman-filtered position, (2) two crossing objects maintain separate IDs through the crossing, (3) missed detections handled (coast on prediction, delete after max_misses), (4) deterministic.

title: Deterministic parallel inference: scoped-thread optimized executor with bit-identical output
description: After fss-bd99t, YOLOX-Nano runs in about 193 ms single-threaded. Parallelize the optimized executor across output channels or rows with std::thread::scope (structured, joined, never detached; AGENTS.md forbids detached threads), with an explicit thread budget carried in the execution context. Output must be bit-identical to the scalar reference regardless of thread count (each output element computed by exactly one thread in the fixed order). The thread count is bound into the kernel-generation identity only if it could affect results (it must not). Measure 1/2/4/8 threads in release via rch; record in PERF_LEDGER.
notes: Landed in main eb4d2e2 (fe90129/fa97613/cb5272c, subagent): deterministic scoped-thread Conv2d, bit-identical for every thread count, --threads N|auto, default 1. PERF-002 honest null: no speedup measured, because every available rch worker was heavily loaded (load avg 70-84 on 16 CPUs; thread spawn about 427 us vs 1-20 ms of work per split conv). Kept OPEN: re-measure on a quiet host; a persistent per-inference worker set may be needed and would be a pool (design decision).

title: Tracker lifecycle: min_hits was dead config; Tentative tracks coasted as Lost
description: Fresh-eyes review of ingest/tracker.rs found the match path set status=Confirmed unconditionally, so min_hits only gated the creation frame (any single rematch confirmed), the step-5 promotion loop was unreachable dead code, and an unmatched Tentative track lingered as Lost until max_misses instead of dying immediately per its own comment. Effect: two-frame flicker noise reached Confirmed status and eventgen emits events for exactly what min_hits exists to suppress. Fix: promotion at match time honouring min_hits (Lost revives on redetection), immediate deletion of unmatched Tentative tracks via post-scan descending swap_remove (safe against assigned-flag displacement), dead promotion loop removed. Three regression tests added.
close_reason: Fixed in 1e1af5e: match-time promotion honours min_hits with Lost revival, unmatched Tentative tracks delete immediately via post-scan descending swap_remove, dead step-5 loop removed; 3 regression tests added (10/10 green).
